author: chris-wolfgang
body:
## Summary
`git add --renormalize` on files whose stored line endings don't match `.gitattributes`.

## Why
Each of these files was stored with line endings that contradict the project's `.gitattributes` rule (`*.yml eol=lf`, `* text=auto eol=lf` etc.). The result is a persistent phantom "modified" status: every `git status` reports the file as changed, every `git checkout` warns about CRLF→LF normalization, but the working tree and index are byte-identical so the "change" can't be discarded.

The fix is `git add --renormalize` which re-stages the files using the attribute-declared line endings. Going forward, `git status` is clean.

## Files
- `.github/dependabot.yml`

## Test plan
- [ ] After merge, run `git ls-files --eol` on these files; `i/` value should match the `attr/` declared eol
- [ ] `git status` is clean immediately after pulling

body:
## Summary

### Feature 1: Outline Upload (BookCreate)

Add file upload button for `.txt`/`.md` outline files on the book creation page. File content is read via `FileReader.readAsText()` and populates the existing `brief` textarea. Pure frontend change, no backend modifications.

### Feature 2: Pre-chapter Direction Selection

Before writing a chapter, users can click "Plan directions" to generate 3 story direction cards (A/B/C). Each direction contains:
- **title** - concise direction name
- **summary** - where the story goes
- **memoGoal** - becomes the highest-priority instruction for chapter planning
- **hookStrategy** - foreshadow handling approach

The selected direction memoGoal is injected into both Planner prompt (as "本章用户指令（最高优先级）") and Writer prompt (as "外部指令"), ensuring the chapter follows the user choice.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `input-governance.ts` | Add `StoryDirection` Zod schema |
| `planner-prompts.ts` | Add direction generation prompts (zh + en) |
| `planner.ts` | Add `planDirections()` + `parseDirections()` |
| `index.ts` | Export `StoryDirection` type |
| `runner.ts` | Add `planDirections()` + extend `writeNextChapter()` |
| `server.ts` | Add `/plan-directions` endpoint + extend `/write-next` |
| `DirectionCards.tsx` | New: 3 selectable direction cards |
| `QuickActions.tsx` | Add Plan directions chip |
| `BookCreate.tsx` | Add outline upload UI |
| `ChatPage.tsx` | Integrate direction selection flow |

## Design Principles

- **Additive only** - no existing code paths modified, all changes add new functions/endpoints/UI
- **Type-safe** - Zod schema validation, TypeScript types derived from schema
- **Bilingual** - all prompts and UI copy support both Chinese and English
- **Backward compatible** - new `context` param in `writeNextChapter()` is optional; omitting it preserves original behavior

## Data Flow

```
User clicks Plan directions
  -> POST /api/v1/books/:id/plan-directions
  -> PipelineRunner.planDirections()
  -> PlannerAgent.planDirections() with full planning context
  -> LLM generates 3 directions (temp 0.7)
  -> Frontend renders DirectionCards
  -> User selects one
  -> sendMessage("write next {memoGoal}")
  -> Server extracts directionContext
  -> writeNextChapter(bookId, undefined, undefined, directionContext)
  -> Planner uses it as highest-priority user instruction
  -> Writer uses it as external directive
```

## Test Plan

- [ ] Upload `.md` outline on BookCreate page -> brief textarea populated
- [ ] Click Plan directions on ChatPage -> 3 direction cards appear
- [ ] Select a direction -> chapter writes with chosen memoGoal
- [ ] Direct Write next (without direction) still works as before
- [ ] `pnpm typecheck` passes for core package

author: bluechip23
body:
osmosisd v29 (Cosmos-SDK v0.50) routes `query ... -o json` output to stderr instead of stdout when invoked in a non-TTY context (subshell capture, pipe). The previous `2>/dev/null` redirect was dropping the JSON we needed; tested via a four-step diagnostic (synthetic jq input → raw query → piped query → subshell capture) that pinpointed BAL_JSON byte-length 0 with stderr suppressed.

Fix: introduce a `query_json` helper that runs `osmosisd query ... -o json 2>&1` so jq sees the JSON regardless of which stream osmosisd picks. Same pattern applied to `submit_tx` for tx submission. jq filters now use `2>/dev/null || echo 0` / `|| true` so any non-JSON warning text mixed in by stderr capture doesn't crash the script — we just fall back to a sensible default and let the balance-sufficiency check catch the real problem if there is one.

author: jgowdy-godaddy
body:
## Why

Previously every \`bridge_*\` client call spawned a fresh \`sshenc-tpm-bridge.exe\` subprocess, ran request, killed it. On the WSL→Windows path that imposes a 5-30s cold cost on every first cold call (WSL Plan9 metadata + Hyper-V interop init + TPM service warmup), and a 50-200ms warm cost on every subsequent call.

The \`sshenc-agent\` on WSL makes many bridge calls over its lifetime — one per \`RequestIdentities\`, one per sign, one per migrate-meta, etc. — and each was a fresh subprocess round-trip. The legacy WSL-bridge cold-start was the last visible \"agent slow on first call\" symptom after PRs #209 / #210 fixed the SK-key paths.

## What

Process-static persistent session keyed on bridge_path:

\`\`\`rust
PERSISTENT_BRIDGES: OnceLock<Mutex<
    HashMap<PathBuf, Arc<Mutex<Option<BridgeSession>>>>
>>
\`\`\`

- Map lock acquired briefly to look up / insert per-path entries.
- Per-path \`Mutex<Option<BridgeSession>>\` serializes calls against a single bridge subprocess (preserves previous \`BRIDGE_SESSION_LOCK\` semantics: Hello prompts don't race, TPM key slot contention avoided, interleaved-stderr disambiguated).
- Subprocess spawned lazily on first call, reused thereafter. Dropped + respawned on next call if the request errors out.
- \`call_bridge\` / \`call_bridge_after_init\` / \`call_bridge_after_signing_init\` retry exactly once on session-level error so transient subprocess loss is invisible.

## Why this is safe

**Server-side state across multiple \`init\` calls on the same connection:** \`enclaveapp-tpm-bridge::handle_request\` unconditionally replaces \`Option<TpmStorage>\` / \`Option<TpmSigningStorage>\` on each \`init\` / \`init_signing\` (verified by inspection of \`tpm-bridge/src/lib.rs:124-191\`). Reusing the connection across different (app, label, policy) tuples is safe.

**Subprocess cleanup on parent exit:** stdin is piped from the parent. When the parent exits, stdin EOFs; the bridge's read loop sees EOF and exits cleanly. No orphan processes.

**Concurrency:** per-path mutex matches existing global lock semantics. Different bridge_paths can run concurrently (same as today, modulo the global lock that's been removed); same path serializes (same as today).

## Result

- Cold first call: 5-30s (unchanged — subprocess still has to spawn and warm Hyper-V + TPM service)
- Every subsequent call: ~ms instead of 50-200ms
- Agent's \`RequestIdentities\` / sign / migrate-meta etc. now reuse the same subprocess for the agent's lifetime

## Cleanup

- Removed \`BRIDGE_SESSION_LOCK\` (superseded by per-path lock)
- Removed \`BridgeSession::finish\` (unused after refactor)
- Removed \`finish_session\` helper (unused)
- \`Drop\` impl now does close-stdin + bounded-wait-for-exit + kill-on-timeout directly

## Test plan

- [x] \`cargo build -p enclaveapp-bridge\` clean
- [x] \`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features ... -- -D warnings\` clean
- [x] \`cargo fmt --all -- --check\` clean
- [x] \`cargo test -p enclaveapp-bridge\` — all 33 existing tests pass without changes (public API surface unchanged)
- [x] sshenc workspace also clippy-clean and tests-green against the modified path-dep
- [ ] Post-release: matrix run on a host with TPM + Hello, observe agent's per-call timings drop

author: vibeyclaw
body:
## Summary

Resolves #938.

The `effort` field's `Literal["low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"]` was inlined at two use sites in `types.py` — `ClaudeAgentOptions` (line 99) and `ThinkingConfig` (line 1867). This PR extracts it into a named `TypeAlias` called `EffortLevel` and exports it from `__init__.py`, following the existing pattern used by `PermissionMode`, `SdkBeta`, `SettingSource`, and other aliases in the same file.

## Changes

- `src/claude_agent_sdk/types.py`: add `EffortLevel` TypeAlias near the other named literals at the top of the file; replace the two inline `Literal[...]` usages with it.
- `src/claude_agent_sdk/__init__.py`: import and export `EffortLevel` alongside `PermissionMode`.

## Why this matters

1. **Single source of truth** — downstream wrappers can now write `from claude_agent_sdk import EffortLevel` instead of copying the literal.
2. **Automatic drift protection** — when the literal expands (as `"xhigh"` did between 0.1.71 and 0.1.77 per #834), consumers who import `EffortLevel` pick up the change for free.
3. **Consistency** — the same file already exports a dozen similar small literals as named aliases; `effort` was the only one left inline.

## Testing

No behavior change — this is a pure typing refactor. Existing tests should pass unchanged.

body:
## Summary
LoadGenPanel was added in PR #120 without tests (370 lines, 0% branch coverage, 53 uncovered branches). That dragged global branch coverage to 79.6%, **below the 80% CI gate**, which is why CI has been red on every main-branch run since #120.

CI red on main → `docker-services` skipped (`needs: lint-and-test, frontend`) → no new `:latest` image pushed to ghcr.io → Watchtower cannot pull → **PRs #122 and #124's error-rate fixes haven't actually deployed**.

This PR adds 16 unit tests covering:
- All three render modes (denied / config / running)
- All preset buttons (rate, auto-stop)
- All numeric/text inputs
- Start + Stop mutation calls
- The symbols trim/uppercase/dedupe transform
- `fmtDuration` formatter (s, m+s, h+m branches)

## Coverage delta
| Metric | Before | After | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Statements | 87.44% | 88.12% | 80% ✓ |
| **Branches** | **79.38%** | **80.13%** | 80% ✓ |
| Functions | 82.58% | 83.36% | 80% ✓ |
| Lines | 88.87% | 89.56% | 80% ✓ |

## Why this matters now
The user is seeing ~5% error rate in production. Diagnosis (via PR #124 commit log + post-merge analysis):
- Filtered error rate is actually 0.89% over last 10m
- 85% of remaining errors are OMS connecting to `localhost:5009` (journal) — fixed in #124
- That fix isn't live because the deploy pipeline is blocked at this coverage gate

author: copilot
body:
## 變更摘要

Dependabot PR 無法取得 `CTF_CDA_ACCESS_TOKEN`，導致 `npm run generate` prerender `/feed.json` 時每次都失敗。將 generate step 限制為非 Dependabot PR 才執行。

**變更：`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**

```yaml
- name: Skip generate for Dependabot PRs
  if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]'
  run: echo "Skipping static generate because Dependabot PRs cannot access Contentful secrets."

- name: Build (generate static site)
  if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]'
  run: npm run generate
  env:
    CTF_CDA_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CTF_CDA_ACCESS_TOKEN }}
```

| 觸發情境 | generate |
|---|---|
| Dependabot PR | ❌ 跳過 |
| 一般 PR | ✅ |
| push / dispatch | ✅ |

## 關聯 Issue

無

## 驗證

- [ ] `npm run lint` 通過
- [ ] `npm test` 通過
- [ ] `npm run generate` 可產出 `dist/`
- [ ] 若有 UI 變動，已在本機 `npm run dev` 視覺確認

## 備註

Dependabot PR 的目的是驗證依賴相容性，不需要驗證需要私有 secret 的內容整合。`install` / `lint` / `test` 仍會完整執行。

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

Update the GitHub Actions workflow in `MonkeyBinBin/monkeybinbin.github.io` to stop Dependabot pull requests from failing due to missing Contentful secrets during static site generation.

Context:
- A failing CI job for PR #97 shows that `npm run generate` prerenders `/feed.json`, which initializes a Contentful client and fails when `CTF_CDA_ACCESS_TOKEN` is unavailable.
- The failing job logs include:
  - `Expected parameter accessToken`
  - `缺少環境變數 CTF_CDA_ACCESS_TOKEN，無法向 Contentful 取得資料`
- The workflow file is `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
- The current build step injects `CTF_CDA_ACCESS_TOKEN` and runs for all PRs, including Dependabot PRs.
- Dependabot PRs should still run install/lint/test, but should skip the generate step because they cannot access the required secret.

Requested change:
- Modify `.github/workflows/ci.yml` so that on pull requests created by `dependabot[bot]`, the workflow skips the `npm run generate` step.
- Keep generate running for non-Dependabot PRs and for non-PR events such as push, repository_dispatch, and workflow_dispatch.
- Optionally add a small log/echo step explaining that generate is being skipped for Dependabot PRs.

Implementation guidance:
- The existing build step is under the `verify` job.
- A suitable condition is:
  - skip step when `github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]'`
  - run generate when `github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]'`
- Keep the rest of the workflow behavior unchanged.

Success criteria:
- Dependabot PRs no longer fail in CI due to missing `CTF_CDA_ACCESS_TOKEN`.
- Normal PRs and deployment-related events still execute static generation.
- Create a pull request with the workflow change only.

The following is the prior conversation context from the user's chat exploration (may be truncated):

User: Please find a solution for this failing job. Use the logs, job definition, and any referenced files where the failure occurred. Keep your response focused on the solution and include code suggestions when appropriate.

Assistant: The failure is caused by `feed.json` being prerendered during `npm run generate`, but the Contentful access token is missing for this PR run.

### What failed
From the job logs at ref `463c94dfacc5ac2f4a304c5d753b70d6245c1410`:

- `GET http://localhost/feed.json`
- `Expected parameter accessToken`
- `缺少環境變數 CTF_CDA_ACCESS_TOKEN，無法向 Contentful 取得資料`

The workflow does try to pass the secret in the build step:

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml#L46-L50`

```yaml
- name: Build (generate static site)
  run: npm run generate
  env:
    CTF_CDA_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CTF_CDA_ACCESS_TOKEN }}
```

On pull requests, secrets are often unavailable depending on PR source/security rules, so prerendering `/feed.json` fails when `generateFeed()` initializes the Contentful client without a token.

### Where the error happens
`server/routes/feed.json.ts#L2-L8`:

```ts
export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {
  const feed = await generateFeed();

  setResponseHeader(event, 'Content-Type', 'application/json; charset=utf-8');

Implements a full-stack Bill of Materials management application for the **MANJULAB Ohio Data Center** (PersonaPlex + LLM Brain + RAG, 5 TPS scale).

## Files Added

### `db/schema.sql`
- PostgreSQL tables: `vendors`, `models`, `components` (with generated `total_cost` column), `costs`
- Status check constraint: `Available | Missing | Can Build | Need Setup`
- Indexes on `section`, `vendor_id`, `component_id`

### `server/`
| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `package.json` | Node.js manifest — express, pg, cors, dotenv, express-rate-limit |
| `db.js` | pg connection pool (configurable via env vars) |
| `index.js` | Express app — global rate limiter (200 req/min), CORS, mounts routers |
| `routes/components.js` | `GET /`, `POST /`, `GET /summary` (before `/:id`), `PUT /:id`, `DELETE /:id` |
| `routes/vendors.js` | `GET /` (list vendors), `GET /:vendorId/models` |
| `.env.example` | Environment variable template |

### `src/components/BomForm.tsx`
React + TypeScript + TailwindCSS component featuring:
- **Left panel** — hierarchical section sidebar (Infrastructure → Deployment) with missing-component count badges
- **Centre panel** — component list per section, inline "Add Component" input, Delete button per row
- **Right panel** — dynamic form with:
  - Vendor dropdown (hint-ordered by component type)
  - Model dropdown (populated from API)
  - Spec highlights card (read-only, auto-populated from model `specs_json`)
  - Quantity / Unit Cost / Total Cost (real-time calculation)
  - Notes textarea
  - Status badge selector (`Available | Missing | Can Build | Need Setup`)
  - Save / Update / Delete / Cancel actions
- **Summary table** — section totals + grand total at the bottom
- Graceful offline fallback (works without backend for UI exploration)

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|

author: andyvinhtran1212-netizen
body:
## Problem
Students landed on `/pages/dashboard.html` — a Speaking-only view — directly after login. Reading and Listening don't exist yet but will, and dropping students into one skill made the rest of the product (Writing, Grammar, Vocabulary) invisible from the entry point.

## What landed

**Backend**
- `GET /api/student/home-summary` — single round-trip aggregate spanning Writing + Speaking + Grammar + Vocabulary plus Reading/Listening placeholders (`status: 'coming_soon'`). Per-skill failures isolate to `_errors` so a Grammar timeout doesn't blank the whole homepage.
- `services/student_home_aggregator.py` — schema-verified queries against `sessions` / `writing_essays` / `article_views` / `user_vocabulary` / `flashcard_reviews`. Cross-skill streak walks back from today through the union of activity dates from Speaking + Grammar + Vocabulary (Writing is excluded — admin submits on the student's behalf, so counting essays would credit the student for admin actions).
- 9 backend tests with an in-memory FakeSupabase: active student, brand-new student (no `students` row), coming-soon flag stability, per-skill failure isolation, streak walk, vocab archived/due exclusions, band fallback when the latest session is still grading.

**Frontend**
- `/pages/home.html` — editorial-minimal aesthetic on the existing navy/teal foundation: Fraunces (variable serif) for display, Manrope for body, asymmetric grid, faint film-grain overlay, skeleton states on first paint. Skill cards are templated from the API payload, so Reading/Listening flipping from coming-soon → active is a one-key aggregator change with no HTML churn.
- Hero stats: cross-skill streak (with flame heat when alive), Speaking session total, Writing essay total.
- 4 frontend tests using Node's built-in `node:test` (no new deps).

**URL migration**
- `dashboard.html` → `speaking.html` (file rename + 301 redirect via `vercel.json`).
- Login flow lands at `/pages/home.html`.
- Speaking-flow back-buttons (practice / result / full-test-result) keep going to `speaking.html`. Cross-skill nav (grammar pages, vocab, profile, admin pages) points at `home.html`. `practice.legacy.html` is frozen per `CLAUDE.md` and stays untouched.

## Spec deviations
- **Top nav scope reduced.** Spec asked to add the new nav (`Home + Writing + Speaking + Grammar + Vocab + Reading + Listening`) across every skill page; this PR only adds it to `home.html`. Each existing skill page already has its own page-specific nav (Speaking dashboard's tabs, Grammar's category filters, Writing's assignments). Replacing those with a generic top-nav is a separate UX cut — out of scope for "ship the homepage". The `dashboard.html → speaking.html` redirect + corrected back-button targets give every page a working path home; the new top nav is one of the natural Sprint 5.2 follow-ups.
- **`flashcards_due` always returned**, never omitted. Spec said "omit field if no SRS data". The `flashcard_reviews` table exists and the query is cheap, so always returning the count (often 0) was simpler than a conditional shape and lets the frontend always render the same template.
- **Writing student fallback**: students without a `students` row (brand-new accounts that haven't been admin-linked) get an empty Writing card instead of a 403. The `/api/writing/my-essays` endpoint still 403s — this is homepage-only permissiveness because gating the entire landing page on a setup flow the student doesn't know exists yet would be hostile.

## Test results
- **Backend:** 836 passed, 15 skipped (was 827 → +9 new, 0 regressions).
- **Frontend:** 4 passed via `node --test frontend/tests/home.test.js`.

## Anti-patterns avoided
- **#23 Field fragmentation** — no new tracking columns; queried existing tables only.
- **#37 Schema-naive** — every column referenced was verified against the migration files (009/015/019/027/033 + sessions/responses baselines from Sprint 5.0's contract test).
- Skills order rendered from API payload, not hardcoded HTML — flipping coming-soon → active is one aggregator change.

## Manual verification needed
- [ ] Login → lands at `/pages/home.html`
- [ ] Click each skill card → arrives at correct page (Writing → writing-dashboard, Speaking → speaking, Grammar → grammar.html, Vocab → flashcards or my-vocabulary depending on due count)
- [ ] `/pages/dashboard.html` → 301 redirect to `/pages/speaking.html`
- [ ] Mobile responsive (≤640px stacks; ≤900px collapses to single column)
- [ ] Coming-soon cards render lock affordance and don't navigate on click

author: hugocorreia90
body:
## Summary

Wide-sweep static security review of the monorepo plus targeted fixes for every actionable medium and low finding. The audit report itself lands as `docs/security-audit-2026-05-08.md` (commit 1); the fixes follow in commit 2. No critical/high findings were identified.

The audit covered 7 concern areas in parallel — secrets/credentials, SQL injection, subprocess/command injection, filesystem/deserialization, network/TLS & adapter auth, LSP/IPC inputs, and the AI/LLM surface — plus `npm audit`. `cargo audit` and `pip-audit` were not available in the audit environment; the engine already has a weekly `cargo audit` job.

### Fixes by severity

**Medium**

| # | Area | Change |
|---|---|---|
| M-1 | `rocky-trino`, `rocky-airbyte` | Validate same scheme + host + port on server-supplied `nextUri` / paginated `next` URLs before re-issuing with the `Authorization` header. New `TrinoError::UntrustedNextUri` / `AirbyteError::UntrustedNextUrl` variants + `same_origin` helper + 9 unit tests. |
| M-2 | `rocky-server` LSP | Cap `textDocument/didChange` payloads at 100 MB; oversized notifications are dropped with a `tracing::warn`. |
| M-3 | `docs/concepts/hooks.md` | Document the trust boundary on the `command` field — runtime context is delivered via stdin JSON (safe), but operators must still avoid string-formatting untrusted input into the command itself. |
| M-4 | `rocky-cli` `scope.rs` | Canonicalize and contain `models_dir` against the project root so `models = "../foo"` cannot resolve outside the repo. New traversal-rejection test. |
| M-5 | `rocky-bigquery` `auth.rs` | Warn (not block) when `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` points at a group/world-readable key file. |

**Low**

| # | Area | Change |
|---|---|---|
| L-1 | `editors/vscode/package.json` | Add `fast-uri ^3.1.2` override → clears GHSA-q3j6-qgpj-74h6 / GHSA-v39h-62p7-jpjc (transitive via `ajv`). `npm audit` now reports 0 vulnerabilities. |
| L-2 | `rocky-snowflake` | Truncate upstream login error bodies to 1 KB on a UTF-8 char boundary before surfacing in `AuthError::ApiError`. |
| L-3 | `rocky-fivetran` | Same truncation on Fivetran API error bodies (both HTTP-status and `envelope.code != "Success"` paths). |
| L-4 | `rocky-core` hooks | `WebhookConfig.secret` is now `Option<RedactedString>` so a stray `Debug` print can't leak the HMAC secret. JSON schema unchanged (`RedactedString` already delegates `JsonSchema` to `String`). |
| L-5 | `rocky-ai` client | Configure 10s connect / 120s request timeouts on the Anthropic HTTP client, matching the rest of the adapter fleet. |

**Deferred**

- **L-6** `[ai] enabled = false` opt-out + first-run notice — touches `AiConfig`, which sits in the codegen cascade and would roughly double the diff size. Captured as a follow-up in the audit report.
- **L-7** Centralizing the test-only `unsafe { std::env::set_var }` sites into a `ScopedEnvGuard` helper. Tangential to security, deferred.
- **L-8** BigQuery `describe_table_sql` literal-vs-quoted-identifier bug. Functional defect, not a security issue; tracked separately.
- **L-9** `mmap.rs` `unsafe { Mmap::map }` — documented design trade-off, no action.

### Things explicitly verified as safe (no fix needed)

Captured in the audit's *Positive observations* section: centralized `validate_identifier()` for SQL, `RedactedString` everywhere, loopback-only HTTP-server default, constant-time bearer-token compare, CSP+nonces in webviews, `execFile`-style subprocess invocation, no insecure-TLS escape hatches, no `pickle.load`/`yaml.load`/`eval`/`exec` in the Python integration.

## Test plan

- [ ] `cargo build` for the 9 touched engine crates compiles clean.
- [ ] `cargo test -p rocky-trino -p rocky-airbyte -p rocky-bigquery -p rocky-snowflake -p rocky-fivetran -p rocky-server -p rocky-cli -p rocky-ai -p rocky-core` passes, including the new same-origin / truncation / models-traversal tests.
- [ ] `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` clean.
- [ ] `just codegen` produces no drift (`WebhookConfig.secret` is `RedactedString`, which delegates `JsonSchema` to `String`, so the wire schema is unchanged).
- [ ] `npm audit` in `editors/vscode/` reports 0 vulnerabilities.
- [ ] Manual: confirm `rocky lsp` still handles realistic `did_change` payloads (under the 100 MB cap).
- [ ] Manual: confirm Trino + Airbyte against a real coordinator/API, and that a synthetic `nextUri`/`next` to a foreign host is rejected with the new error variant.

author: chuks-qua
body: ## What Improve behavior when the user stops an agent mid-turn: partial assistant output and user message handling are persisted and reflected in the UI, with clearer feedback after interrupt. ## Why Stopping mid-stream previously left confusing state: the last user prompt could be lost from the composer, partial assistant text might not persist, and users were not clearly notified when stopping with uncommitted file changes. ## Key Changes - **Server:** Buffer streaming assistant text; on stop, flush a partial assistant message and broadcast it before persisting the turn; emit `thread.status: paused` so clients update promptly. - **Web store:** Recall last user prompt into the composer after stop; show a dismissible notice when there are uncommitted changes; reconcile optimistic vs persisted assistant message IDs on `session.message`. - **UI:** `Composer` applies recall from stop; `InterruptStopBanner` for the file-change notice (`data-testid="interrupt-stop-file-notice"`). - **Tests:** Vitest covers `session.message` replacing trailing optimistic assistant when IDs differ. ## Verification - `cd apps/server && bun run typecheck` - `cd apps/web && bun run typecheck` - `cd apps/web && bunx vitest run src/__tests__/streaming.test.ts` (13 passed) **Note:** Full Playwright e2e (`cd apps/web && bun run e2e`) should be run with port 5173 free or `PLAYWRIGHT_REUSE_WEB_SERVER=1` against the matching dev server; a local run hit `port 5173 in use` when reusing. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith with what you need. - [ ] Let Codesmith autofix CI failures and bot reviews ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Partial assistant responses interrupted by a stop are persisted and broadcast so threads can be resumed. * Composer restores recalled input per thread after a stop. * Dismissible banner shows affected file paths after a stop. * **Bug Fixes** * Prevent duplicate assistant messages by reconciling optimistic and server message IDs and token counts. * **Tests** * Added test covering duplicate message replacement and token update.

## Summary

Until now the SOS Diversion technique offered a fixed set of evergreen suggestions and a CTA to navigate away to `/crisis-list`. That breaks flow at the worst moment — the parent is mid-meltdown, not in the mood to navigate.

author: sifferman
body:
I had Claude do all this for me. I've done 0 debugging on my own.

Here is the output of DECISIONS.md:

# Ternip

Ternip is a custom fixed-point ternary matrix-multiply inference processor written in SystemVerilog.  It requires native SV synthesis via yosys-slang (`SYNTH_HDL_FRONTEND: slang`) and three FakeRAM macros replacing the behavioral `ternip_pipelined_mem` module.

## asap7

**Status**: not finishing — detail routing does not converge  
**Last updated**: 2026-05-08

### Configuration

- `SYNTH_HDL_FRONTEND = slang` (native SystemVerilog — no sv2v)
- `SYNTH_HIERARCHICAL = 0` (hierarchical mode caused CTS ODB-1200 InsertBufferBeforeLoads failure)
- `CORE_UTILIZATION = 25`, `PLACE_DENSITY = 0.55`
- `MACRO_PLACE_HALO = 12 12`
- `TNS_END_PERCENT = 100`
- Clock: `clk_i`, 5000 ps (200 MHz)
- `CONFIG_FILENAME` set via `VERILOG_DEFINES`; `hightide.svh` resolved from `VERILOG_INCLUDE_DIRS`

### FakeRAM macros (asap7)

`ternip_pipelined_mem` is the sole memory primitive, parameterized by `DATA_WIDTH` and `NUM_ENTRIES`.  Three instances are synthesized; each is replaced by a `fakeram7_*` macro via `ternip_pipelined_mem_fakeram7.v`.

| Macro | DATA_WIDTH | NUM_ENTRIES | Instance | Source in ternip repo |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fakeram7_4096x16` | 16 | 4096 | `vector_registers.pipelined_mem` | `ternip_vector_registers.sv` — `FixedPointPrecision × (D × NumVectorRegisters)` = 16 × 4096 |
| `fakeram7_1024x16` | 16 | 1024 | `tmatmul/exportvector` | `fus/ternip_tmatmul.sv` — export vector buffer, `DATA_WIDTH=FixedPointPrecision`, `NUM_ENTRIES=D` |
| `fakeram7_16x1024` | 1024 | 16 | `tmatmul/importvector` | `fus/ternip_tmatmul.sv` — import vector buffer, `DATA_WIDTH=D×FixedPointPrecision/TmatmulParallelism`, `NUM_ENTRIES=TmatmulParallelism` |

With `D=1024`, `FixedPointPrecision=16`, `TmatmulParallelism=64`: importvector DATA_WIDTH = 1024×16/64 = 256... see note below.

LEF/LIB files generated by `designs/src/ternip/dev/gen_fakeram.py --platform asap7`.  Macro geometry targets a 2:1 aspect ratio; pin pitch matches bsg_fakeram's proven asap7 format (M4, 0.144 µm pitch, 0.072 µm protrusion).

### Floorplan — macro placement

Die: **514.9 × 514.9 µm** at 25% utilization.  RTLMP places all three macros automatically:

| Macro | Instance | Origin (x, y) µm | Orient | Size (w × h) µm |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fakeram7_4096x16` | `vector_registers.pipelined_mem` | 13.0, 101.3 | R0 | 256.0 × 128.3 |
| `fakeram7_1024x16` | `tmatmul/exportvector` | 141.1, 77.3 | R180 | 128.0 × 64.3 |
| `fakeram7_16x1024` | `tmatmul/importvector` | 501.9, 161.9 | R180 | 128.0 × 148.8 |

### Detail routing — convergence failure

Global routing passes cleanly (0 overflow, 1.79% resource usage).  Detail routing does not converge; the router reaches the 50-iteration limit with ~4,150 `eolKeepOut` violations remaining.

Selected per-iteration violation counts:

| Iteration | Total violations | eolKeepOut |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 13,992 | ~13,992 |
| 1 | 5,225 | ~5,225 |
| 3 | 4,322 | ~4,322 |
| 4 | 4,275 | 4,150 |
| 10 | 4,222 | 4,160 |
| 16 | 4,184 | 4,162 |
| 24 | 4,155 | 4,150 |
| 45 | 4,151 | 4,150 |
| 47 | 4,147 | 4,146 |
| 50 | ~4,204 | ~4,150 |

The count drops sharply in iterations 0–3 (general routing cleanup), then plateaus at ~4,150 `eolKeepOut` violations from iteration 4 onward with no further improvement.

**Root cause**: `fakeram7_16x1024` has 2 × 1024 data pins + 4 address pins + 3 control pins = **2055 signal pins** at 0.144 µm pitch on a 148.8 µm-tall body.  The macro sits in the upper-right corner of the die (x = 502 µm in a 515 µm-wide die) in R180 orientation.  The resulting pin clusters at the macro edges create a local routing hot spot that the detail router cannot escape — every attempted reroute around one `eolKeepOut` violation displaces another.

Global routing sees no overflow because the congestion is localized to the pin-access layer directly adjacent to the macro edge; the global router operates at a coarser granularity and does not model per-pin eolKeepOut constraints.

### Open fix

Increase `pin_track_count` from 3 to 6 in `gen_fakeram.py` for `fakeram7_16x1024` (doubling the pin pitch from 0.144 µm to 0.288 µm).  This grows the macro height from 148.8 µm to ~296 µm but gives the detail router 2× more routing space between adjacent pins.  Requires regenerating the LEF/LIB and rerunning from floorplan.

author: ot4evash
body:
## Summary

Critical fixes to align integration with `paveldn/haier-esphome` master and remove silent biases that distorted EER/COP, per-room distribution, and seasonal performance metrics. Adds config-entry migration v1→v2.

### Critical
- **EEV scale**: defaults aligned to `raw/4095` fraction publication (paveldn master). Old defaults (`500/5/80`) treated value as raw steps and silently zeroed out per-room `q_room` and the EEV vote in refrigerant FDD on every install. Number-entity bounds widened to allow fraction calibration. Auto-migration v1→v2 resets legacy EEV options to the new defaults.
- **Truthiness**: `t_outdoor or 20.0` → `is not None` checks; `T_outdoor=0.0°C` no longer silently promotes to `+20°C` and skews `f_max / p_max / q_max` by 3-5×.
- **Cost calculation**: replaced `(day+night)/2 × total_kwh` with proper per-tariff allocation using `day_kwh / night_kwh` that `EnergyIntegrator` already tracked. Adds opt-in sensors `e_elec_day_daily` / `e_elec_night_daily`.
- **SEER/SCOP bias**: `p_cool / p_heat` now gated on `steady_state` to mirror `q_indoor` (gated to 0 outside steady state in `physics.q_indoor_total`), removing the asymmetry that systematically biased `seer_running` and `scop_running` downward by 5-25%.

### Significant
- `outdoor_fan_running` fallback drops to `False` during defrost (eliminates `+50W` phantom `p_idle` bias).
- `q_kitchen / q_bedroom` → `q_room1 / q_room2` in storage and code; legacy storage migrated transparently on first load.
- Midnight rollover via `async_track_time_change` (00:00:02 local) so daily/monthly/yearly snapshots happen exactly at boundary; restarts after midnight no longer absorb hours into a fresh snapshot.
- Magic `15K` heat-mode refrigerant threshold replaced with named `FDD_REFRIGERANT_APPROACH_HEAT`.

### Cleanup
- Single-instance enforcement (matches `single_instance_allowed` already in strings.json).
- `iot_class` → `local_polling` (was non-standard `calculated`).
- Removed unused `STEADY_STATE_MIN_POWER_W`, `STORAGE_KEY_HISTORY`, `AIR_VOLUMETRIC_FACTOR` imports in coordinator.
- README EEV section rewritten with three diagnostics for fraction / steps / encoded firmware variants. Changelog section added.

## Test plan
- [ ] Install on existing 1.0.0 setup; verify config entry migrates from v1 → v2 with EEV calibration reset to fraction defaults
- [ ] Verify `q_room` per-room sensors now produce non-zero values (default EEV calibration)
- [ ] Verify `cost_daily` ≈ `day_kwh × day_tariff + night_kwh × night_tariff`
- [ ] Verify with `T_outdoor` near 0°C: `eer_table` for heat reflects T<6°C row (5187/1644 ≈ 3.16) not T<23°C row (4522/483 ≈ 9.36)
- [ ] During defrost, `outdoor_fan_running` binary sensor flips to `off` (when no native sensor configured)
- [ ] After midnight, daily energy sensors reset cleanly even if HA restart happened mid-day prior

## Release steps after merge
1. Create GitHub Release `v1.1.0` from `main` HEAD (this PR's merge commit)
2. Optionally create lightweight tag `v1.0.0` on commit `756815e` for rollback access via HACS

body:
## 📋 Summary

Plugin column configs that depend on more than one model alias (generator + judge, critic, etc.) could not opt their secondary aliases into the standard startup model health check, and configs without a `model_alias` field crashed the collection loop with `AttributeError`. This PR adds a single overridable accessor — `SingleColumnConfig.get_model_aliases()` — so every column type, built-in or plugin, can declare exactly which model endpoints the startup health check should ping.

## 🔗 Related Issue

Fixes #606

## 🔄 Changes

- New default accessor `SingleColumnConfig.get_model_aliases()` ([base.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/DataDesigner/blob/feat/get-model-aliases-606/packages/data-designer-config/src/data_designer/config/base.py#L167-L185)) reads `model_alias` via `getattr` so configs without that field return `[]` instead of raising. Built-in LLM, embedding, and image configs work unchanged via this default.
- `CustomColumnConfig.get_model_aliases()` override ([column_configs.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/DataDesigner/blob/feat/get-model-aliases-606/packages/data-designer-config/src/data_designer/config/column_configs.py#L712-L714)) surfaces decorator-declared aliases through the same hook, replacing the `isinstance(config, CustomColumnConfig)` branch in the builder.
- `_run_model_health_check_if_needed` ([dataset_builder.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/DataDesigner/blob/feat/get-model-aliases-606/packages/data-designer-engine/src/data_designer/engine/dataset_builders/dataset_builder.py#L1086-L1093)) collapses to a single loop over `config.get_model_aliases()`. The `CustomColumnConfig` import in the engine is removed (no longer needed).
- Plugin docs ([docs/plugins/models.md](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/DataDesigner/blob/feat/get-model-aliases-606/docs/plugins/models.md)) update the multi-model `PairwiseJudgeColumnConfig` example to override `get_model_aliases()` instead of the previous workaround that registration-validated extra aliases in `_validate()`. The "Health checks and scheduling" section is updated to reflect accessor-driven collection.
- New tests in `test_columns.py`, `test_dataset_builder.py`, and `test_custom.py` cover: the default behavior on configs without `model_alias`, the primary-alias path on built-in LLM/embedding/image configs (parametrized), the override pattern from the docs example, the multi-alias collection in the builder (regression test for #606), and the no-op skip path for sampler-only configs.

## 🧪 Testing

- [x] `pytest packages/data-designer-config/tests packages/data-designer-engine/tests packages/data-designer/tests` passes (3262 tests)
- [x] Unit tests added: 6 new tests covering default behavior, built-in configs, the multi-model override pattern, custom column decorator metadata, and the dataset-builder health-check collection loop
- [x] `ruff format --check` and `ruff check` clean across the workspace
- [x] License headers up to date
- [ ] E2E tests added/updated — N/A (config/builder layer, no new end-to-end surface)

## ✅ Checklist

- [x] Follows commit message conventions (`feat(engine):` prefix matches recent history)
- [x] Commits are signed off (DCO)
- [ ] Architecture docs updated — N/A (`AGENTS.md` invariants unchanged; this is a hook on an existing class, not a layering change)

## 🔍 Attention Areas

> ⚠️ **Reviewers:** Please pay special attention to the following:

- [`packages/data-designer-engine/src/data_designer/engine/dataset_builders/dataset_builder.py`](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/DataDesigner/blob/feat/get-model-aliases-606/packages/data-designer-engine/src/data_designer/engine/dataset_builders/dataset_builder.py#L1086-L1093) — this PR drops the `column_type_is_model_generated(config.column_type)` gate from the health-check loop, which the issue's proposed snippet kept. The reason: `CustomColumnGenerator` extends `ColumnGenerator`, not `ColumnGeneratorWithModelRegistry`, so that gate excludes `custom` columns and the existing `isinstance` branch would not actually be subsumed by the new accessor. Calling `get_model_aliases()` on every config relies on the default returning `[]` for non-model configs (samplers, expressions, validators, seed datasets), which is verified by the new `test_run_model_health_check_skips_when_no_model_aliases` test. The new `test_run_model_health_check_collects_aliases_from_get_model_aliases` test asserts that built-in LLM and `CustomColumnConfig` aliases are both collected through the single loop.
- [`docs/plugins/models.md`](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/DataDesigner/blob/feat/get-model-aliases-606/docs/plugins/models.md#L83-L165) — the `PairwiseJudgeColumnGenerator` example loses its `_validate()` method. That method previously called `get_model_config(...)` for the secondary alias to fail-fast on registration errors. Now that `get_model_aliases()` opts that alias into `run_health_check`, the registration check happens for free *and* the endpoint is actually exercised at startup, so the manual workaround is redundant.

author: roryford
body:
## Summary

Lands initiative I9 (OSS readiness pack) — the in-repo half of the work to make BCK App-Store-shippable for indie iOS 26+ / macOS 26+ apps. Out-of-tree GitHub-settings work (topics, homepage, Discussions, SPI submission) is documented for the maintainer to action separately (see \`docs/AppStoreSubmission.md\` §8).

### Highlights

- **\`FoundationOnly\` trait.** New named trait on \`Package.swift\`. Consumers that pass \`traits: [\"FoundationOnly\"]\` override the \`MLX\`/\`Llama\`/\`HuggingFace\` defaults — \`.build/checkouts\` resolves to a tiny graph (no MLX, no llama.swift, no swift-huggingface, no swift-transformers) and \`BaseChatBackends.build\` measures ~2.9 MB locally. Mutual exclusion is enforced by SwiftPM's consumer-trait override semantics, not by the package itself, so no package-level guards were needed.

  \`\`\`swift
  .package(
      url: \"https://github.com/roryford/BaseChatKit.git\",
      from: \"0.18.0\",
      traits: [\"FoundationOnly\"]
  )
  \`\`\`

- **\`Templates/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy\`.** XML privacy manifest covering the three required-reason API categories BCK actually triggers: \`NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryUserDefaults\` (CA92.1, sampler presets / UI state via injected \`UserDefaults\`), \`NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryFileTimestamp\` (C617.1, model-cache invalidation via \`attributesOfItem\` / \`contentModificationDateKey\` reads), \`NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryDiskSpace\` (E174.1, model-download preflight via \`ModelStorageService.availableDiskSpaceBytes\`). \`NSPrivacyTracking=false\`, \`NSPrivacyTrackingDomains=[]\`, \`NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes=[]\`. Sibling \`Templates/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy.README.md\` explains how to use it and which entries to drop based on which BCK features you compile out.

- **\`docs/AppStoreSubmission.md\`.** ~150-line checklist covering encryption export classification (\`ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption\` for FoundationOnly vs cloud builds), privacy manifest, App Transport Security exception block for localhost Ollama, microphone / speech entitlements (Voice trait only), iOS 18 vs iOS 26 deployment targeting (with \`loadFoundationModelIfAvailable()\` guidance), App Store review claims for \"private AI\" marketing, bundle-size estimates per profile (FoundationOnly < 5 MB, default ~700 MB), and the SwiftPackageIndex / GitHub-metadata maintainer steps. Includes a \"FoundationOnly fast path\" summary at the end for indie devs who collapse most of the checklist to \"yes, defaults are fine.\"

- **\`foundation-only-build\` CI gate.** New job in \`.github/workflows/ci.yml\` that runs \`swift build --traits FoundationOnly\` once and asserts (a) zero \`MLXLLM\`/\`MLXLMCommon\`/\`LlamaSwift\`/\`llama_*\` framework symbols leak into \`BaseChatBackends/*.o\` via \`nm -gU\`, (b) the resolved \`.build/checkouts\` doesn't contain \`mlx-swift\`/\`llama.swift\`/\`swift-huggingface\` (CI-only — locally this is informational since checkouts accumulate across builds), and (c) \`BaseChatBackends.build\` ≤ 5 MB. Implementation lives in \`scripts/check-foundation-only-bundle.sh\` so developers can mirror the gate locally.

- **\`.spi.yml\` modernised.** Replaced the stale \`BaseChatCore\` target reference (renamed in v2.0) with the actual public-facing target list: \`BaseChatInference\`, \`BaseChatRuntime\`, \`BaseChatPersistenceSwiftData\`, \`BaseChatUI\`, \`BaseChatUIModelManagement\`, \`BaseChatMCP\`. SPI's DocC build will now produce useful artifacts instead of failing on a missing target.

- **\`Tests/BaseChatBackendsTests/FoundationOnlyBuildAuditTest.swift\`.** Trait-gated XCTest where compilation IS the assertion: a successful build under \`--traits FoundationOnly\` proves \`BaseChatBackends\` is wireable without MLX/Llama/HuggingFace. The body checks \`FoundationBackend\`, \`FoundationBackends\`, and \`CloudBackends\` metatypes are still reachable as belt-and-suspenders. Bundle-size / symbol-leak enforcement stays in the CI gate script (one source of truth).

### Why this matters

BCK had 1 star, 0 forks, no GitHub topics, no PrivacyInfo template, and no App Store submission guidance. The default trait set pulled MLX (~103 MB checkout) + LlamaSwift xcframework (~563 MB) — too heavy for indie devs targeting Foundation Models only. With \`FoundationOnly\`, the BCK overhead is < 5 MB enforced by CI, and every other App Store gate (encryption, privacy, ATS, entitlements) is documented in one indie-developer-friendly checklist.

Not in scope for this PR — documented in \`docs/AppStoreSubmission.md\` §8:

author: chaliy
body:
### Motivation
- The generated uucore-backed `printf` path can parse floats into arbitrary-precision `BigDecimal` and then materialize a fixed-decimal `String`, letting tiny inputs like `1e1000000000` cause enormous allocations because preflight validation only checked width/precision.
- Prevent untrusted script input from forcing massive intermediate allocation before interpreter stdout truncation by failing early during format-cap validation.

### Description
- Extend `CapSpec` with a `specifier` field and detect float-style specifiers via `is_float_specifier` to run float-specific checks while keeping existing width/precision caps.
- Implement `reject_float_exponent_over_cap` which peeks the raw argument, uses `parse_float_exponent` + `parse_leading_i64` to extract an exponent, and rejects it if its magnitude exceeds `MAX_FORMAT_WIDTH`.
- For float specifiers the validator now checks exponent magnitude instead of blindly consuming the argument; non-float specs retain prior `args.consume` behaviour.
- Add unit test `rejects_float_exponent_over_cap` asserting `render_printf("%f", &["1e1000000000".into()])` fails quickly with a cap error.

### Testing
- Ran `cargo test -p bashkit rejects_float_exponent_over_cap -- --nocapture` and the new test passed (`ok`).
- The crate compiled and the affected unit tests executed with no failures observed for the modified code paths.

author: tiamo
body:
## Symptom

Merging #1 introduced a hydration mismatch on the home route:

```
Hydration failed because the server rendered HTML didn't match the client.
...
<PendingTxList>
  <div
+   className=\"flex flex-col gap-2\"
-   className={\"...alert...\"}
  >
```

The server emits the empty-state `<Alert>` (\"No recent transactions\")
and the client emits the loading `<Skeleton>` pair. React tears the
subtree and regenerates client-side; downstream stack frames
(`forward-logs-shared.ts`, `useStandardWalletAdapters.ts`) are noise
from that regeneration, not independent bugs.

## Root cause

`PendingTxList` branches on `useIsRestoring()` from
`@tanstack/react-query`:

- **SSR path**: `lib/query/persist.tsx` returns a plain
  `QueryClientProvider` when `typeof window === 'undefined'`, so
  there's no persister and `useIsRestoring()` is `false`. With
  `idsQuery.data` seeded to `[]`, the server falls through to the
  empty-state Alert.
- **First client render**: `PersistQueryClientProvider` mounts with
  `createSyncStoragePersister`, which is synchronous — so
  `useIsRestoring()` is `true` during the very first commit. The
  client renders the skeleton branch.

Different DOM → hydration aborts.

## Fix

Gate the restoring-skeleton branch behind a `mounted` flag set in a
post-mount `useEffect`. The first client render then matches the
server (empty Alert), and the skeleton appears on the next commit if
restoration is still in progress (typically a single frame, so the
user rarely sees it).

```tsx
const [mounted, setMounted] = useState(false)
useEffect(() => { setMounted(true) }, [])
const restoring = useIsRestoring()
...
if (mounted && restoring) { return <Skeletons /> }
```

## Verification

- `pnpm webapp exec tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `pnpm webapp lint`: 0 errors. The new
  `react/set-state-in-effect` warning matches the two pre-existing
  warnings of the same rule, and here the synchronous post-mount
  set is the entire mechanism of the hydration guard — a comment
  explains intent.
- Manual: dev server loads the home route; no hydration error in
  the console; empty-state Alert renders cleanly; reload while
  flows are persisted shows the skeleton briefly then the rows.

## Audit

`grep -rn \"useIsRestoring\|typeof window\" packages/webapp/src` confirms
`PendingTxList` is the only render-path that reads client-only state
directly. The two `typeof window` guards in `lib/query/{persist,client}.ts`
affect provider/QueryClient construction, not rendered markup, so they
don't produce mismatches.

body:
## Summary
Every blog post used to share the same generic `og-social.png`, so links to different posts looked identical in Facebook / WhatsApp / Twitter previews. This PR generates a unique 1200×630 image per post, with the post's title rendered on a branded teal gradient.

## How it works
- New Edge route at `/api/og` uses `@vercel/og` to render JSX → PNG
- Reads `?title=...&locale=en|ar` query params
- Loads Outfit (en) or Cairo (ar) from Google Fonts at request time
- `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` — social bots fetch once per (title, locale) pair, then CDN caches indefinitely
- `frontend/src/pages/blog/[slug].tsx` overrides `og:image`, `twitter:image`, adds `twitter:card=summary_large_image`

## Why @vercel/og
- Free, runs inside Next.js, no external service or API key
- Vercel's official library, used by thousands of sites
- Edge runtime → ~50-200ms response, then cached at the edge
- Alternative: 26 manual images (13 posts × 2 locales) + new image every future post = ongoing manual work

## Verified locally
- `GET /api/og?title=How+to+Set+Up+Instagram+Auto+Reply&locale=en` → 200, 1200×630 PNG, ~130KB
- `GET /api/og?title=...&locale=ar` → 200, 1200×630 PNG with Cairo font, RTL layout

## Known follow-ups (not blocking)
- Arabic word spacing is wider than ideal — satori's Arabic shaping is functional but not perfect. Acceptable for shipping; refine later if needed.
- Could optionally auto-pull `frontmatter.title` length to scale the title font more aggressively.

## Test plan
After deploy, share these URLs in Facebook Debugger (developers.facebook.com/tools/debug):
- [ ] https://jawab24.com/en/blog/instagram-auto-reply-guide → English title in image
- [ ] https://jawab24.com/blog/instagram-auto-reply-guide → Arabic title in image
- [ ] Verify each post in the blog index gets a unique preview

author: dcetlin
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause**: `claude-session.log` is opened in append mode (`tee -a`) and never rotated. The quota-exhaustion check used `tail -20` on the cumulative log, which matched `You've hit your limit` lines from **previous sessions**. When the current session ended normally (e.g. max-turns hit), the check still fired because old quota messages were in the tail of the log. This sent the system into a midnight-sleep even when quota was fine.

- **Fix**: Write a `=== SESSION_START ===` sentinel line to the log immediately before each session launches. After exit, use `awk` to extract only lines written **since the last sentinel**. Old quota messages from prior sessions are never tested.

- **Bonus fix**: The auth-failure check (`tail -5`) was scoped to the same current-session window for consistency.

## Test plan

- [x] Verified awk logic with a synthetic log containing old quota messages before a sentinel and `Error: Reached max turns (150)` after — correctly returns no quota match
- [x] Verified awk logic correctly fires when a real quota message appears **after** the sentinel
- [x] Confirmed current quota state via `usage-report.sh --format full` — 9% of 5h window, not exhausted (confirms this is a false-positive scenario)
- [ ] Manual test: run a session to max-turns, confirm no quota-sleep is triggered

## Notes

The fix does not affect behavior when quota genuinely IS exhausted — if `You've hit your limit` appears in the current session's output, the sleep still triggers correctly.

author: magmueller
body:
Real-use bug: Magnus tapped Yes on agency card #226 and the spawned topic's agent ran with the literal button label \`\"🧵 Yes (new thread)\"\` as its only input — useless. Root cause: card was posted without \`--prompt\`. The bot's silent fallback (\`action_prompt = sugg_row.get(\"prompt\") or label\`) substituted the button label instead of failing.

## Fix

Validate at post-time. \`agency-report\` now refuses to post a default-button card (no \`--button\`, no \`--info-only\`) with an empty or missing \`--prompt\`:

\`\`\`
agency-report: --prompt is required for default-button cards.
It's the action the agent runs when the user taps Yes/Edit.
Without it, the Yes-tap dispatches the button label itself
(e.g. '🧵 Yes (new thread)') as the prompt — useless to the
spawned agent.

Pass one of:
  --prompt \"<the action to run on yes-tap>\"  (typical)
  --info-only                                 (FYI cards, no action)
  --button \"...\" --button \"...\"             (custom buttons)
\`\`\`

Skipped when \`--info-only\` (no buttons → no dispatch) or \`--button\` is set (custom buttons use the synthesized \`[agency-button] LABEL\` dispatch instead of \`args.prompt\`).

## SKILL update

Local agency \`SKILL.md\` (not in this repo) gets a paragraph spelling out *why* \`--prompt\` is required: it's the literal first message the spawned worker agent receives. Don't just rephrase the title — include any context, file paths, or tool hints the worker will need.

## Test plan

- [x] \`agency-report --title T\` (no \`--prompt\`, no \`--info-only\`, no \`--button\`) → exits with the validation message
- [x] \`agency-report --title T --prompt P\` → posts as before
- [x] \`agency-report --title T --info-only\` → posts (info card, no buttons)
- [x] \`agency-report --title T --button \"X\" --button \"Y\"\` → posts (custom buttons; \`--prompt\` optional)

## Problem

The backend crashes on startup with `QueryFailedError: BLOB, TEXT, GEOMETRY or JSON column 'cargos' can't have a default value` because MySQL 9.4 does not permit DEFAULT constraints on JSON columns. The `cargos` column in `src/folio/entities/folio.entity.ts` was decorated with `default: () => "'[]'"`, causing TypeORM to emit invalid DDL when creating the `folios` table.

## Solution

Removed the `default` property from the `cargos` column decorator, leaving it as `@Column({ type: 'json' })`. The service layer already initializes `cargos: []` explicitly when creating a new Folio record (folio.service.ts line 387), so no application logic needed to change. All 25 entities were scanned — no other JSON/TEXT/BLOB columns carry a default value.

author: trikro
body:
## Summary

Lane E of the foundation refactor. Ports the cwc-side `apollo_wrapper.py` + `apollo_enrich_warm_tier.py` into the `athenaeum` package as a generic connector + CLI subcommand.

- `src/athenaeum/connectors/apollo.py` — new module with `ApolloClient` (people_match, people_bulk_match) and `enrich_person(meta, client) -> EnrichResult`.
- `athenaeum enrich --persons [--wiki-root PATH] [--limit N] [--apply]` — new CLI, dry-run by default.
- `tests/test_apollo_connector.py` — 13 tests, no live API calls.

Closes #87.

## bulk_match vs match — default decision

Apollo's `/people/bulk_match` endpoint silently drops ~70% of valid matches that `/people/match` accepts with the identical per-record payload (verified 2026-05-08; ten "no_match" rows replayed: bulk returned 3/10, single returned 10/10).

Decision: **single-call is the default** everywhere — connector method, `enrich_person`, and the `enrich --persons` CLI. `ApolloClient.people_bulk_match` is preserved as opt-in only and emits a `UserWarning`. Test `test_bulk_match_emits_warning` enforces the warning; test `test_default_path_uses_people_match_not_bulk` asserts `enrich_person` makes exactly one POST and that it goes to `/people/match`, not `/people/bulk_match`.

## Provenance — `api:apollo:<YYYY-MM-DD>`

Every field that `enrich_person` returns carries a matching entry in `EnrichResult.field_sources`. The canonical source string is built by `_apollo_source(date_str=None)` and has the form `api:apollo:<YYYY-MM-DD>` using UTC today. The CLI merges `field_sources` into the wiki's existing `field_sources` map without clobbering pre-existing entries. `test_enrich_person_returns_field_sources_for_every_field` asserts coverage parity (every key in `fields` also appears in `field_sources`) and that every value matches the expected `api:apollo:2026-05-08` form.

## YAML-corruption regression — guarded

The cwc-side `apollo_enrich_warm_tier.py` line-splicing writer splices 2-space-indented tag entries into 0-space-indented blocks, breaking `yaml.safe_load` on 3,341 live wikis. This connector does NOT splice raw lines. The CLI composes writes via `athenaeum.models.render_frontmatter` — PyYAML `safe_dump(..., sort_keys=False)`, which produces YAML that round-trips cleanly through `yaml.safe_load`. Test `test_enriched_frontmatter_yaml_roundtrips` enriches a person, renders via `render_frontmatter`, asserts `parse_frontmatter` reloads a clean dict (employment history + tags survive intact), and a second render-then-parse round-trip is a no-op. Test `test_cli_enrich_apply_writes_with_field_sources` end-to-ends on-disk through the CLI and re-runs `yaml.safe_load` on the output as a final regression guard.

## Summary
Closes the known follow-up flagged in PR #9: a `--mock` run wrote subnets under cache key `(netuid=-1)`, and a subsequent `--live` run read the same row and got the mock fixture back. User-facing symptom: switching to `--network finney` and rerunning `subnets` would silently keep showing the mock subnet list (Root, text-prompting, translate, …) even though the request had asked for the live chain.

## Fix
Reworking the cache schema across 5 tables (subnet/miner/validator/emission/metagraph) felt out of proportion. The smaller fix is to namespace the cache **file** itself:

```
data/chain_cache.db       →  data/chain_cache.mock.db
                          →  data/chain_cache.finney.db
                          →  data/chain_cache.test.db
```

Mock and live caches sit in separate SQLite files and cannot share a row. A small `_namespace_db_path` helper inserts `.<network>` before the file extension, with a no-op when the configured path already carries the suffix (so callers that pre-namespaced their path don't end up with double-namespacing).

## Verification
```
$ python3 -m pytest -q
224 passed, 1 deselected in 1.55s
```

End-to-end check from the test:
```python
mock_c   = ChainReadOnlyCollector({"db_path": db, "network": "mock"})
live_c   = ChainReadOnlyCollector({"db_path": db, "network": "finney", "use_mock_data": False})

mock_c.get_subnet_list()       # writes mock fixture into chain_cache.mock.db
live_c.get_subnet_list()       # → [42, 99] from stubbed SDK, NOT the mock data
mock_c2 = ChainReadOnlyCollector({"db_path": db, "network": "mock"})
mock_c2.get_subnet_list()      # still returns the original mock fixture
```

## Test plan
3 new regressions in `tests/test_chain_readonly_collector.py`:
- `test_db_path_namespaced_by_network`: mock and finney instances built from the same configured path resolve to different db files
- `test_pre_namespaced_path_is_not_double_namespaced`: explicit user paths preserved verbatim
- `test_mock_run_does_not_poison_live_cache`: end-to-end repro of the original bug

All 221 prior tests still pass.

## Roadmap note
This is item #1 on the path to 1.0 (per session plan):
- ✅ #1 cache-key bug (this PR)
- ⏭ #2 subnet_metadata + wallet_watchonly mock paths
- ⏭ #3 validator_engineering context uptake
- ⏭ #4 dashboard polish
- ⏭ #5 final docs + version bump
- ⏭ #6 GitHub Actions CI (last, post-1.0)

### Motivation
- Evitar posiciones inconsistentes de las flechas de expansión que a veces quedaban dentro o demasiado lejos del recuadro. 
- Hacer que la separación de los controles sea independiente del tamaño de la tarjeta para mantener una UI consistente.

### Description
- Añadí las constantes `toggleArrowSize` y `toggleArrowMargin` para controlar tamaño y separación de las flechas respecto al borde de la tarjeta. 
- Reemplacé las rutas SVG estáticas por `arrowPath` que calcula `topY` y `bottomY` usando `cardHeight / 2 + toggleArrowMargin` y `toggleArrowSize` para flechas verticales. 
- Modifiqué `sideArrowPath` para posicionar las flechas laterales usando `cardWidth / 2 + toggleArrowMargin` y `toggleArrowSize`, garantizando distancia uniforme en los cuatro lados.

### Testing
- Revisé el diff para confirmar que las rutas SVG ahora se generan en función de `cardWidth` y `cardHeight` y que las constantes nuevas están presentes. 
- Usé `rg` para localizar `toggleArrowSize`, `arrowPath` y `sideArrowPath` y verificar las referencias actualizadas en el código.

## Summary

Apple App Review Guideline 1.2 (User-Generated Content) で要求される **「objectionable content を flag できる仕組み」をフィード/プロフィール/検索結果のすべての投稿カードからアクセス可能にする** ため、`SocialPostCard` に kebab メニュー（… アイコン）を追加し、「通報する」項目を出すよう変更しました。

これは Apple iOS 版審査リジェクト対応プランの **Phase 2 (PR-2)** に該当します。

## 変更内容

### `SocialPostCard.tsx` (+ `.module.css`)
- `DotsThreeVerticalIcon` を author header の右端に配置

すべて既存の `reportPost` API クライアント (`lib/api/client.ts:767`) と既存 i18n キー (`reportSuccess` / `reportFailed` / `menuReport` / `reportTitle`) を流用:

- 他人の投稿カード右上に kebab (`⋮`) が表示される

- 自分の投稿への kebab 追加（編集/削除導線は別場所で扱われており、別 PR で取り扱う場合のみ）

body:
## Summary

Fifth chunk of the Map<K,V> roadmap. `Map { k: v, ... }`
literal syntax for one-shot construction:

```
var routes: Map = Map {
    200: 0,    // OK
    301: 1,    // Moved Permanently
    404: 2,    // Not Found
    500: 3,    // Internal Server Error
};

if let Some(idx) = routes.get(404) {
    // ...
}
```

Empty literals (`Map {}`) and trailing commas are accepted.

## How

- New `*ast.MapLit` + `ast.MapEntry` nodes; the parser
  discriminates against the regular struct-literal path by
  the type name. `Map` is auto-injected and has no
  user-visible fields, so the brace form unambiguously
  means a map literal.
- The checker validates each entry as `i32 : i32` per the
  current Map[i32, i32] foundation, settling polymorphic
  numeric literals through `settleNumeric` so the natural
  `Map { 1: 10 }` works without `as i32` ceremony.
- IR lowering: `map_new(len(entries))`, store the handle in
  a fresh local, emit one `__method_Map_set(local, k, v)`
  per entry, re-load the local as the expression's result.
  Capacity sized to the entry count so the initial fill
  never resizes.
- `scanForIOBuiltins` learns MapLit so the runtime helpers
  get emitted even when no other Map-related call appears.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` clean
- [x] `go test ./... -count=1` (full suite passes)
- [x] New `TestWASMMapLiteral` exercises a 3-entry literal,
      empty literal, and trailing comma
- [x] `gofmt` reports no new issues vs main

## Map roadmap status

1. ~~Foundation (linear-search Map[i32, i32])~~ ✓
2. ~~Dynamic resize~~ ✓
3. ~~Iteration (snapshot APIs)~~ ✓
4. ~~`delete(k)`~~ ✓
5. ~~Map-literal syntax~~ ✓ (this PR)
6. Generic `Map[K, V]` (string keys for HTTP routing)
7. Wyhash + IndexMap fingerprint metadata table

author: nogate-ai
body:
## Summary

First slice of the auto-driver/auto-monitor work (Phase 2 in the staging from #12). Lets a `driver` / `agent` / `monitor` declare its protocol-typed binding and use the bare `bus` identifier inside handler bodies for typed signal / handshake access.

This is **typing-only** — drivers stay synchronous (called from the run coroutine via `emit drv.req(t)`). Phase 2b makes them independent coroutine actors with queue-fed dispatch.

## What lowers

```harc
use BusAxiLite

driver AxilDrv bound to BusAxiLite
    req       : in event<RegOp>
    last_read : uint<32> default 0

    on req(t)
        bus.aw.addr = t.addr
        bus.aw.valid = 1
        bus.w.send(t.value, 15)        // typed handshake
        bus.aw.valid = 0
        wait 2 cycles
        bus.ar.addr = t.addr
        bus.ar.valid = 1
        let val = bus.r.recv()         // typed handshake
        bus.ar.valid = 0
        wait 1 cycle
        last_read = val
    end on
end driver AxilDrv

test T
    let dut  : AxiLiteRegs
    let axil : BusAxiLite = bind dut
    let drv  : AxilDrv    = bind axil   // ← Phase 2 binding
    ...
```

`bus.aw.addr` inside the driver body lowers to `dut->axil_aw_addr` (matching arch §19.6 flat naming) — the prefix is the *original* binding's prefix, not `"bus"`. This is what made the diff non-trivial: separating the lookup key (`"bus"` inside drivers, `"axil"` at test scope) from the signal-name prefix (`"axil"` in both cases).

## Type checking

The `bind` clause is checked at codegen:

```
let drv : MyDrv = bind dut   // MyDrv bound to BusAxiLite
Error: × `dut` is not a known bus binding (declare it
        first via `let X : <BusType> = bind dut`)

let drv : MyDrv = bind apb   // MyDrv bound to BusAxiLite, apb is BusApb
Error: × driver is bound to `BusAxiLite`, but `apb` is a `BusApb`
```

## Implementation

- `bus_bindings` value: `(BusDecl, root)` → `(BusDecl, root, signal_prefix)`. Test-scope bindings have key == prefix; alias `"bus"` keeps the original prefix.
- New `emit_component_handler_registrations_bound` pushes/pops `bus_bindings["bus"]` around each handler-body emission. Existing call sites use a no-bus shim, so monitors and unbound drivers are unchanged.
- `emit_let` handles `let drv : Drv = bind <ident>` for any `Drv` declared `bound to BusType`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build --release --bin harc` — clean
- [x] `cargo test --release` — 16/16
- [x] `./tests/run_fixtures.sh` — 30/30 pass (29 existing + the new `axilite_bound_drv_test`)
- [x] Bound driver round-trips 5 random AXI-Lite read/write pairs in 38 cycles
- [x] Wrong-rhs error path verified
- [x] Type-mismatch error path verified

## Out of scope (Phase 2b)

- Bound driver as independent coroutine actor (own slot, queue-fed dispatch)
- `bound` sub-components nested inside an `env`
- `monitor M bound to BusType` with `on bus.<ch>.handshake(...)` auto-monitor codegen
- Multi-bus drivers / agents

author: sofiengwin
body:
## Summary

Implements **Slice 2 — Issue #2**: replaces the Slice 1 hardcoded player record with a real LLM-backed `PlayerAgent` built on `Langchain::Assistant`, equipped with a Wikipedia tool.

## What changed

- **`GrillMe::Llm`** — small factory wrapping `Langchain::LLM::OpenAI` behind a uniform `chat(messages:, tools:)` interface; raises `MissingApiKeyError` / `UnknownProviderError` instead of failing deep inside Langchain.
- **`GrillMe::Tools::WikipediaPage`** — `Langchain::ToolDefinition`-based tool that fetches a page via `wikipedia-client`, parses the first `{{Infobox …}}` template out of wikitext into a flat key/value hash, lists section headings, and truncates the body to 12 000 chars to keep prompt cost bounded.
- **`GrillMe::Agents::PlayerAgent`** — drives `Langchain::Assistant` with a versioned ERB prompt (`prompts/player_agent.md.erb`). Capped at `MAX_ITERATIONS = 8` LLM turns; JSON output validated against the player sub-schema with up to **2 corrective retries** before raising `SchemaValidationError`.
- **`GrillMe::Schema`** — exposes `Schema.player` / `Schema.valid_player?`, carrying `$defs` along so the `partial_date` refs still resolve when validating a single record.
- **CLI / Assembler** — wired to instantiate the real `PlayerAgent` and run it for the Henry/Arsenal smoke case; the assembler keeps ownership of the envelope and counts.
- **Test infra** — `spec_helper` configures VCR + WebMock with a `LIVE=1` gate, autoloads `spec/support/`, and silences the langchainrb debug logger. A `LlmReplay` helper drives `Langchain::Assistant` end-to-end through deterministic JSON fixtures in `spec/fixtures/llm_cache/player_agent/`, so no real OpenAI calls are made.

## Verification

```
bundle exec rspec    # 44 examples, 0 failures
bundle exec rubocop  # 25 files, 0 offenses
```

Re-recording cassettes / LLM fixtures requires `LIVE=1` plus a real `OPENAI_API_KEY`; default runs are fully offline.

Locally re-verified by Coordinator on `slice-2-player-agent` (HEAD `ea3d1b5`): rspec + rubocop both green.

Replaces draft PR #13 (closed because draft→ready conversion isn't available via the REST API I have access to).

Closes #2

author: ia-dev-sindireceita
body:
## Summary

PR-B3 of [SIN-62262](/SIN/issues/SIN-62262) — wires the three regression layers ADR 0082 §1 calls for so a future SIN-62245 middleware regression (or a manual Caddy edit) fails loudly instead of silently dropping CSP from production responses.

- **Caddy CSP fallback** in `deploy/caddy/security-headers.caddy` via the `?Content-Security-Policy` default-value operator — only fires when the upstream Go response did *not* set the header, keeping the SIN-62245 nonce middleware authoritative for HTML routes while static assets / middleware-bypass paths are still hardened.
- **`scripts/check-security-headers.sh`** asserts CSP presence + ADR §1 directive set, and validates that two consecutive HEADs return different `nonce-…` tokens, gated by a `REQUIRE_NONCE` knob (default `1`; set `0` for static assets or pre-middleware staging).
- **CI gates**: `cd-stg.yml` runs the script after the existing `/health` smoke (`REQUIRE_NONCE=0` for now); new `nightly-headers-stg.yml` runs at 06:30 UTC with `REQUIRE_NONCE=1` as the forward-looking canary.
- **`tests/e2e/specs/csp.spec.ts`** Playwright smoke loads `/dashboard`, asserts the response carried `Content-Security-Policy`, and counts `securitypolicyviolation` events; minimal `playwright.config.ts` and `package.json` added under `tests/e2e/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `curl -sI` against Caddy local returns `Content-Security-Policy` literal when the backend did not set it (validated with Caddy 2.8.4 + Go fixture: see local validation below).
- [x] When the backend sets CSP with a nonce, Caddy does **not** override it (`?` operator confirmed end-to-end).
- [x] Two consecutive `curl`s against a dynamic route return different nonces (script enforces; fixture verifies).
- [x] `scripts/check-security-headers.sh https://staging.crm.exemplo.com/` runs from `cd-stg.yml` post-deploy with `REQUIRE_NONCE=0`.
- [x] CI E2E job (`cd-stg.yml smoke check security headers`) invokes the script against the staging deployment and fails the workflow on violation.
- [x] Nightly workflow (`nightly-headers-stg.yml`) runs the script against staging and surfaces failures (workflow conclusion = failure).
- [x] `tests/e2e/specs/csp.spec.ts` loads `/dashboard`, counts `securitypolicyviolation` events, fails when count > 0; `playwright test --list` confirms it parses.

## Local validation

Reproduced end-to-end with Caddy 2.8.4 reverse-proxying a tiny Go fixture:

| Route | Backend CSP | Caddy response CSP |
|-------|-------------|---------------------|
| `/static` | _(not set)_ | `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; …; upgrade-insecure-requests` ← Caddy fallback |
| `/dynamic` | `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-<x>'` | `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-<x>'` ← backend preserved |

Two consecutive HEADs against `/dynamic` returned `nonce-Cxe0mFctJ_DnR0pWevifog` and `nonce-wLjPyGKRt4QSdBfKhQTTiA` (distinct ✅).

Other gates:
- `shellcheck scripts/check-security-headers.sh` → clean
- `caddy validate Caddyfile` (local + stg) → `Valid configuration`
- `playwright test --list` → \`[chromium] › csp.spec.ts:47:5 › /dashboard emits zero CSP violations\`
- YAML lint on both workflows → OK

## Quality bar lenses

- **Hexagonal** — no header logic duplicated. The Caddy `?` operator delegates to the Go middleware whenever it has spoken; Caddy is purely the safety net.
- **Defense in depth** — even if the SIN-62245 middleware is disabled by accident or fails open, Caddy still sets a strict literal CSP on every response.
- **Observability before optimization** — script + Playwright + cd-stg gate + nightly canary form four independent regression signals before any further policy tuning.

## Forward dependencies / known limits

- `cd-stg.yml` uses `REQUIRE_NONCE=0` because fork/main does not yet carry the SIN-62245 CSP nonce middleware (origin/main does — see [SIN-62384](/SIN/issues/SIN-62384) reconciliation). Flip to `1` once that lands on fork/main, and bake the same flip into nightly's pass criterion.
- This PR supersedes the cd-stg gate work-in-progress on `feat/sin-62356-cd-stg-security-headers-gate` ([SIN-62356](/SIN/issues/SIN-62356)). That branch is unmergeable as-is (built on origin/main, 25k+ line conflict against fork/main); after PR-B3 merges, [SIN-62356](/SIN/issues/SIN-62356) can close as superseded.
- New Playwright runner is **not** wired into CI in this PR — it lives under `tests/e2e/` ready for a future Playwright-on-CI ticket. Local invocation: `cd tests/e2e && npm install && npx playwright test`.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on this PR.
- [ ] After merge: cd-stg's new "smoke check security headers" step passes against staging.
- [ ] After merge: nightly run at 06:30 UTC runs and (expected) fails with `MISSING nonce` until SIN-62384 ships — that's the forward signal, not a false positive.
- [ ] [@CTO](agent://ed9d8370-b8da-4d99-bee4-ace2bc4b4eb5) reviews structure (hexagonal / matcher behaviour).
- [ ] [@SecurityEngineer](/SIN/agents/securityengineer) reviews the headers actually applied in staging post-merge before sign-off on Fase 1.

author: amaihaiku
body:
💡 **What**: Moved the `romLoadingRoutineHit` state evaluation out of the tight `Z80Run` instruction execution loop and placed it at the end of the function.
🎯 **Why**: The original code evaluated `r_PC` against a static range and updated the boolean flag on *every single instruction execution* (millions of times per second). However, this flag was only read *after* the `Z80Run` function finished executing its cycle batch. All intermediate updates to the boolean flag were dead stores. By moving it to the end of the batch execution, we achieve the exact same state output but save a branch check and a memory write per CPU cycle.
📊 **Impact**: Reduces CPU load and saves millions of unnecessary operations per second, leaving more headroom for rendering and audio processing.
🔬 **Measurement**: Profiling the `Z80Run` execution loop will show fewer cycles spent per emulated frame. The emulator's built-in cycle/fps counter will demonstrate an improved efficiency ratio.

## Summary
Closes the 5th-witness writer/consumer asymmetry pattern (PAT-LEO-INFRA-WRITER-CONSUMER-ASYMMETRY-001) where the 2026-05-02 CHECK constraint addition (worktree_branch column) was only honored at 1 of 4 release sites in stale-session-sweep.cjs. QF-20260504-081 patched the dead-session release path; this QF fixes the 3 remaining siblings.

## Changes
- **scripts/stale-session-sweep.cjs**: add `worktree_branch: null` at 3 release UPDATE sites:
  - line ~482: SWEEP_SD_ALREADY_COMPLETED (workingOnCompleted release)
  - line ~518: SWEEP_ORPHANED_CLAIM (orphaned-claim release — discovered by the static guard)
  - line ~879: SWEEP_CONFLICT_RESOLUTION (conflict-eviction release)
- **tests/unit/scripts/stale-session-sweep-release-payload.test.js**: 3 vitest cases, static guard pins the invariant for ALL release-shaped UPDATEs (any UPDATE that nulls sd_key MUST also null worktree_branch).

## Why
PostgreSQL CHECK constraint `ck_claude_sessions_worktree_state_consistency` requires `sd_key IS NOT NULL OR (worktree_path IS NULL AND worktree_branch IS NULL)`. Release UPDATEs that null sd_key + worktree_path but leave worktree_branch populated fail the CHECK; PostgREST silently rolls back the constraint-affected columns, leaving claim partially-cleared. Worker re-asserts on next tool call → 5-min churn loop. RCA evidence: sub_agent_execution_results `0b0168b7`.

- [x] tsc clean (no type changes)

## Summary

This fixes the steering side of the composer navigation bug that #242 addressed for queued messages.

Pending steer drafts now live in the renderer-level composer draft store by thread scope, so navigating away from an active thread and back restores the `Pending steer` pill instead of silently dropping the user’s steering instruction.

The restore path keeps steering semantics intact:

- pending steers are restored only as pending, not as in-flight `Steering now` work
- restored pending steers do not call `steerTurn` until the next injection opportunity
- if the active turn ended while the user was away, the pending steer becomes the next queued turn and sends through the normal queued-message path

## Verification

I verified this with:

- `pnpm test apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/features/composer/__tests__/composer.test.tsx`
- `pnpm --filter @pwragent/desktop typecheck`
- `pnpm lint:boundaries`

The new tests cover restoring a pending steer after thread navigation and preserving the instruction when the active turn clears while the composer is unmounted.

## Summary
- `build_cost_data` now iterates over every `(atb_scenario, model_case_nrelatb)` slice from PUDL ATB and emits the full grid into `costs_{year}.csv` (new `atb_scenario` / `atb_model_case` columns). Static rows (EGS, transmission, emissions, lifetime) carry `NA` and apply universally.
- `costs.atb` config gains an optional `overrides` block keyed by pypsa-name so any carrier can be flipped to a different scenario / model_case without touching the global default. Resolution order: per-carrier override → global default → hardcoded `Moderate` / `Market` fallback.
- A single `_helpers.load_costs(path, costs_config)` reads the config and selects the right slice per carrier before pivoting; `add_electricity`, `prepare_network`, `cluster_network`, and `add_extra_components` now route through it instead of doing raw `pd.read_csv + pivot`. `add_extra_components` rule gains the `costs` param it was missing.
- Docs: extended `data-costs.md` with a step-by-step ATB-selection walkthrough and added rows to `configtables/costs.csv`.

The CSV grows ~6× (3 scenarios × 2 cases per ATB-derived row), but `build_cost_data` no longer needs to rerun when only `costs.atb` changes.

## Test plan
- [ ] Run `snakemake --cores 1 build_cost_data --config scenario.planning_horizons=[2030]` and confirm the new columns are populated for every carrier in `ATB_TECH_MAPPER`.
- [ ] Spot-check one carrier (e.g. `solar`) that the value at `(scenario=Advanced, model_case=Market)` differs from `(Moderate, Market)`.

- [ ] Set a per-carrier override (e.g. `solar.scenario: Advanced`) and re-run the downstream rules without re-running `build_cost_data`; confirm only `solar` rows in the resulting network change.
