body:
This pull request updates several GitHub Actions workflow files and Terraform variable handling to improve environment configuration management and CI/CD flexibility. The most significant changes are the addition of support for a new feature branch, improved handling of sensitive EmailJS credentials, and enhanced placeholder replacement logic in deployment scripts.

**CI/CD Workflow Enhancements:**

* Added support for the `feature/sprint3` branch in all relevant CI/CD workflow files, ensuring that automated checks and deployments run for this new development branch. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ada1b6583776c7aeff592f5301de592eb325189c01ace9af2c5c56128e39a90eR23) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7ea07750bedbd73864e28f588787159ef672a34da68bf27a7a0b3edb4f48162bR23) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-f518e88febf21edf9518ba569c5d4deaee95674a9ccc4beb0fc1df7d6bfb5641R23) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-7ac1b25e831b1975f5e4aab34dc7ad2e1aa812dcfe0530f8b38f75e26c678939R23) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-7fa79ebf09244f74f4d5dbd4fc476df31867abea997e69171b3642cb019e00f7R23) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-1c0c637c6c3a903b1215bbc6cfdcbd8551a7f7a41def66112e1c15e62f77b9f7R23) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-0e6ca417a83e639d90cc16c20343434f5ff9f9f2d2a343c6c7af29db7a2085ddR23)

**Environment Variable and Secret Management:**

* Updated `.github/workflows/cd-aws-main.yml` to source EmailJS credentials (`EMAILJS_SERVICE_ID`, `EMAILJS_PUBLIC_KEY`, `EMAILJS_PRIVATE_KEY`, `EMAILJS_VERIFICATION_TEMPLATE_ID`) from GitHub Actions secrets and variables, improving security and centralizing configuration. These are now passed both as Terraform variables and as environment variables for deployment steps.
* Removed hardcoded EmailJS credentials from `infra/aws/terraform/local-plan.tfvars` and added guidance to use GitHub secrets/variables instead, preventing accidental exposure of sensitive information.

**Deployment Script Improvements:**

* Enhanced the deployment script in `.github/workflows/cd-aws-main.yml` to:
  - Extract and replace new placeholders (`__CORS_ORIGINS__`, `__WEBCLIENT_URL__`, and EmailJS-related placeholders) with environment variable values.
  - Add a check for unresolved placeholders, causing the deployment to fail if any remain, which helps catch misconfigurations early. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e1f749ca0a5841ae3613a759e2ac01e53422b4679779a0d3b1f33964a5bf8e59R197-R198) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e1f749ca0a5841ae3613a759e2ac01e53422b4679779a0d3b1f33964a5bf8e59R275-R286)

author: ywatanabe1989
body:
## Summary

Sac becomes SDK-only: every accepted ``spec.runtime`` (docker / podman / apptainer) wraps the long-running Claude Agent SDK runner; HTTP A2A is the sole introspection surface; lifecycle is just start/stop.

- **Validator** (\`config/_validation.py\`): drops the F-CS6 yaml-alias machinery (\`_RUNTIME_RENAMES\`, \`normalize_runtime\`) and the F-CS17 redirect dictionary. Drops \`screen\` and \`multiplexer\` from accepted spec keys. \`health.method\` accepts \`sdk-alive\` (was \`multiplexer-alive\`) plus \`a2a-card\`.
- **Lifecycle dispatch** (\`_lifecycle/lifecycle.py\`): collapsed to a single SDK path. \`runtimes/__init__.py\` no longer ships \`ClaudeCodeRuntime\` / \`ApptainerRuntime\` legacy.
- **CLI surface dropped**: \`sac auto-accept {send,start,stop}\` group, the legacy flat aliases, and \`sac agent attach\` (multiplexer-only).
- **CLI surface simplified**: \`sac agent inspect\` is now a runtime \`is_running()\` probe (rich state lives behind the agent's HTTP A2A surface). \`sac agent check\` drops the SSH preflight branch and the screen-binary check.
- **Source files removed**: \`runtimes/{claude_code, apptainer (legacy SIF), multiplexer, tmux, screen, pane_capture}.py\`, the \`auto/\` package, \`cli_pkg/auto_accept_group.py\`. ~2 700 LOC gone.
- **Tests**: 58 obsolete cases deleted (CLI/TUI runtime, multiplexer, auto-accept TUI handler, SSH-dispatch). 710 unit tests pass.

The persistent SDK runner inside the container (\`_runners/claude_session.py\`) and the SDK dispatch shim (\`runtimes/claude_session.py\`) are intentionally preserved — both are reachable from \`runtime: docker|podman|apptainer\`.

## Test plan
- [x] \`pytest tests/\` — 710 passed (down from 768 baseline; 58 deleted)
- [ ] CI workflow on chore/sdk-only branch lights green
- [ ] sac \`agent start\` smoke-launch with the new SDK shape

author: copilot
body:
## Summary

Addresses all visual and UX issues raised in the problem statement.

---

## Changes

### 🐾 Breed differentiation — dogs now look different from each other

Added `BREED_TRAITS` map in `dog.js` with per-breed visual overrides:

| Breed | What's different |
|---|---|
| **Corgi** | Short legs (0.60×), widened body, large perky ears with pink inner ear |
| **Dachshund** | Elongated body (+28px rx), very short legs (0.50×) |
| **Husky** | Dark eye-mask band across eyes, inner ear highlights |
| **Poodle** | Fluffy puff shapes around body + pompom head and leg puffs |
| **Golden Retriever** | Flowing ear fringe, chest fluff |
| **Shiba Inu** | Cream muzzle + forehead markings, inner ear highlights |

Added `renderBreedExtras()` function that layers breed-specific SVG elements on top of the shared base render.

### 👂 Ear visibility

Ear contrast increased from `darken(color, 0.1)` → `darken(color, 0.32)`. Inner-ear highlights now appear on all ear types (floppy ears get a soft inner ellipse, perky/semi-erect get a pink inner triangle).

### 👗 Clothes details

- **Sweater**: 3 horizontal contrasting stripes
- **Raincoat**: Front seam line, 3 buttons, collar ruffle
- **Tutu**: 3 layered ruffles (each slightly lighter)
- **Bowtie**: Improved proportions and edge lines

### 🚶 Walking animation

Dog now walks left-right across the room (`dog-walk` animation with `alternate infinite`) when mood is `happy` or `okay` and no specific activity is in progress. Stride distance scales proportionally with the dog's size. Activity animations (fetch, eat, pet, outside, wake) override walking while active.

### 🏠 Richer room scene

Curtains on window, a framed picture on the back wall, a floor rug, a toy ball, and detail on the food/water bowls.

### ⚡ Energy level — fixed UX and bug

- **Hint threshold changed** from `< 40` to `< 70` — the hint now appears exactly when the Sleep button becomes available, so users immediately know what to do
- **Sleeping state indicator**: green "💤 Sleeping — energy is recharging…" hint (with `role="status"`) shown while dog is asleep
- **Auto-wake**: dog automatically wakes and the action panel updates when energy hits 100
- Both hints use distinct CSS classes (`stat-hint-warn` / `stat-hint-info`) for clear visual contrast

### ✅ Tests

All 58 existing Python unit tests pass unchanged. No Python-level logic was modified.

### Motivation
- Remove fallback/synthetic pricing math so the system does not invent prices when live market data is missing.
- Ensure UI and engines fail honestly by showing explicit unavailable states instead of placeholder numbers.

### Description
- Added a strict live-price guard in `generateTradeDeployment` to return an `unavailableBattlefieldPricing` payload when `selectedTicker.price` is missing or <= 0, preventing further pricing calculations (`lib/intelligence/tradeDeployment.ts`).
- Introduced `unavailableBattlefieldPricing` with null/unavailable semantics and explicit offline warnings for entry/stop/targets/allocation/profit fields (`lib/intelligence/tradeDeployment.ts`).
- Removed client-side synthetic math in the Capital Allocation Engine by gating share/option calculations on live price availability and returning `N/A`/`Unavailable` UI values when offline; option strike/premium/contract cost values are now `null` when pricing is unavailable (`components/intelligence/IntelligenceDashboardShell.tsx`).
- Updated the offline alert copy to explicitly state market pricing is offline and awaiting live market data (`components/intelligence/IntelligenceDashboardShell.tsx`).

author: jeremyandrews
body:
Fixes #42

## What

The Search API "Manage fields" form showed no guidance when Scolta was the backend. Field configuration has no effect on Scolta — Scolta indexes the full rendered entity view, not individual Search API fields — but admins had no way to know this and were spending time configuring fields that were silently ignored.

## Why

Scolta's indexer never reads Search API field configuration. It calls `entity_view()` and exports the rendered HTML. Fields added in the Search API UI exist in the index schema but are never populated or queried.

## How

Implements `scolta_form_search_api_index_fields_alter()` in `scolta.module`. When `$index->getServer()->getBackendId() === 'scolta_pagefind'`, an info notice is injected at weight −100 (above the fields table) explaining that field selection is not required. The hook guards against unconfigured indexes via try/catch around `getServer()`.

## Tests

Added `SearchApiFieldsHelpTextTest` with 9 file-inspection tests:
- Hook function exists with the correct name
- Hook checks for `scolta_pagefind` backend ID
- Hook calls `getServer()` to retrieve the backend
- Hook returns early for non-Scolta indexes
- Hook wraps server lookup in try-catch
- Hook adds `scolta_fields_notice` form element
- Notice text explains field selection is not required
- Notice text mentions rendered content
- Notice has negative `#weight` so it renders above the fields table

author: abl030
body:
## Summary

Fixes #233 (cratedigger-web silently wedged for 9 hours on 2026-05-08) with the smallest possible Python patch on the existing stdlib \`http.server\` stack — no framework migration, no Rust, no architectural change. Three commits map 1:1 to the plan's three implementation units.

Architectural framing for why we are NOT rewriting the web layer right now lives at \`docs/solutions/web-rewrite-deferred-pending-runtime-redesign.md\`. TL;DR: \`web/routes/*.py\` POST handlers orchestrate ~4,000 LOC of pipeline lib code, so no clean web-only carve-out exists today. Defer to a future cratedigger runtime redesign (cycle-driven → static / event-driven).

## What changes

### U1 — \`fix(cratedigger)\` — delete the end-of-cycle cache-invalidate POST

\`cratedigger.py:1605-1617\` posted to \`/api/cache/invalidate\` every cycle via \`urlopen(req, timeout=2)\` and never read the response body. urlopen closed the socket when scope exited, while the server was still mid-write — every invocation produced a server-side BrokenPipeError. The endpoint has been a documented no-op since #101 (no \`web:\` cache keys exist to invalidate). Pure dead-code removal.

### U2 — \`fix(web)\` — narrow do_GET/do_POST catch-all to skip reconnect on disconnect

The bare \`except Exception\` catch-all called \`_try_reconnect_db()\` on every caught exception, including BrokenPipeError. The reconnect storm wedged the single thread in poll(). This PR adds a typed \`except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError, ConnectionAbortedError)\` clause before the existing catch-all in both \`do_GET\` and \`do_POST\`. Disconnect errors now produce a single WARNING log line, no DB reconnect, no second body-write attempt.

The function-level \`except\` in \`do_POST\` covers both the legacy \`/api/cache/invalidate\` short-circuit and the dispatch path (they share the outer try block). The cache-invalidate handler stays in place to absorb the deploy-window asymmetry — cleanup tracked in #234.

### U3 — \`ThreadingHTTPServer\` swap — DEFERRED per audit

A focused read-only sub-agent audit confirmed the expected blocker: ThreadingHTTPServer is **NOT SAFE** to land alongside this fix. Concrete blockers:

1. \`web/server.py:67\` — \`db: PipelineDB | None = None\` is a single shared psycopg2 connection. psycopg2 documents that connection objects (and cursors created from them) are not thread-safe — protocol bytes will interleave on the wire even for read-only queries.
2. \`lib/beets_db.py:127\` — \`sqlite3.connect(...)\` opens the beets handle without \`check_same_thread=False\`. Threaded use raises \`ProgrammingError: SQLite objects created in a thread can only be used in that same thread.\`
3. \`lib/pipeline_db.py:837-839\` — \`advisory_lock\` docstring explicitly relies on the assumption that "the web server (single-threaded HTTPServer) already serialises within its own session." Threading silently breaks the mutual-exclusion guarantee.
4. \`web/server.py:50-65\` — \`_try_reconnect_db()\` rebinds the module-global \`db\` from request threads with no lock; concurrent requests would observe a closed conn.
5. \`scripts/web_dev_server.py:20,80\` — already declares \`class DevHTTPServer(ThreadingHTTPServer)\` and monkey-patches \`web_server._try_reconnect_db\`. **This is a latent bug today, masked only by single-developer use.**

What would have to change before ThreadingHTTPServer is safe: per-thread psycopg2 connection (e.g. \`threading.local()\` or \`psycopg2.pool.ThreadedConnectionPool\`); reopen \`BeetsDB\` with \`check_same_thread=False\`; update \`advisory_lock\` to acknowledge that single-session serialisation no longer holds; replace \`_try_reconnect_db\` 's module-global mutation with pool-managed reconnect. All four landings together.

This is exactly the design surface the deferred Rust rewrite would address structurally. Tracked in #234 and in \`docs/solutions/web-rewrite-deferred-pending-runtime-redesign.md\`.

## Tests

New \`TestClientDisconnectHandling\` class in \`tests/test_web_server.py\` (6 tests, RED-then-GREEN):

- 3 disconnect-class tests (\`BrokenPipeError\`, \`ConnectionResetError\`, \`ConnectionAbortedError\`) assert no \`_try_reconnect_db\`, single WARNING line, no \`log.exception\` traceback.
- 2 regression-guard tests (\`psycopg2.OperationalError\`, \`ValueError\`) confirm the existing catch-all behaviour is unchanged for real handler errors. Narrowing the catch-all further (so non-DB exceptions skip reconnect) is deliberately deferred to #234.
- 1 happy-path guard confirms a normal POST emits no disconnect WARNING and no ERROR.

The exception is injected via \`mock_db.update_request_fields.side_effect\` rather than raw-socket mid-body close — same code path inside \`do_POST\`'s try block, deterministic where raw-socket timing is flaky on localhost.

Full suite: **3,156 tests, 55 skipped, 0 failures.**

## Test plan

- [x] Full unittest suite passes (\`nix-shell --run \"bash scripts/run_tests.sh\"\`)
- [x] New \`TestClientDisconnectHandling\` class passes
- [x] No new pyright errors on touched files (existing \`# type: ignore[operator]\` warnings on the dispatch code are pre-existing)
- [ ] After deploy: \`ssh doc2 'sudo journalctl -u cratedigger-web --since \"24 hours ago\" | grep -B1 BrokenPipeError | grep -c \"^Traceback\"'\` returns < 5. **Note: grep for the traceback signature, not bare \`BrokenPipeError\`** — the new typed except clause emits a single WARNING line containing \`type(e).__name__\` (i.e., the literal string "BrokenPipeError"), so a naive \`grep -c BrokenPipeError\` would count those WARNING lines too. The 30-line traceback flood (the journald-flood signature from #233) is what we need to confirm is gone.
- [ ] After deploy: \`ssh doc2 'sudo journalctl -u cratedigger --since \"10 min ago\" | grep cache/invalidate'\` returns nothing (confirms U1 took effect).
- [ ] No wedge incident for 30 days under normal traffic.

## What this does NOT fix

Per the plan and the doc-review, several items remain open and are tracked in **#234**:

- Per-request socket/read timeouts on Beets sqlite + Redis (a virtiofs hitch or Redis hang still holds the single thread).
- Per-request watchdog that crashes the process via \`os._exit\` after N seconds.
- Narrowing the bare \`except Exception\` further (a real handler bug like ValueError still triggers an unnecessary DB reconnect).

The Q1 dashboard cache wrapper from #227 also remains separately open (perf optimization, unrelated to the wedge).

The fundamental "head-of-line blocking from a single slow request" risk persists until the cratedigger runtime redesign captured in \`docs/solutions/web-rewrite-deferred-pending-runtime-redesign.md\` happens. This patch fixes the SPECIFIC wedge from #233, not the wedge CLASS.

## Deploy

Standard nix flake flow per \`.claude/rules/deploy.md\`:

\`\`\`bash
# After merge:
ssh doc1 'cd ~/nixosconfig && nix flake update cratedigger-src && git add flake.lock && git commit -m \"cratedigger: web wedge fix\" && git push'
ssh doc2 'sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake github:abl030/nixosconfig#doc2 --refresh'
\`\`\`

\`cratedigger-web.service\` restarts on switch; \`cratedigger.service\` does not (per \`restartIfChanged = false\`) but the next 5-min timer tick picks up the new code.

## References

- Closes #233
- Related #227 (sibling perf issue; this PR addresses the BrokenPipe-storm angle only)
- Followup #234 (sqlite/Redis timeouts + watchdog + catch-all narrowing + ThreadingHTTPServer prerequisites)
- Plan: \`docs/plans/2026-05-09-001-fix-cratedigger-web-wedge-minimal-patch-plan.md\`
- Architectural framing: \`docs/solutions/web-rewrite-deferred-pending-runtime-redesign.md\`
- Superseded brainstorms (kept as journey records): the Bottle+waitress and Rust attempts in \`docs/brainstorms/\`

author: trek-e
body:
## Fix PR

---

## Linked Issue

Fixes #3263

---

## What was broken

Three related contract-drift defects in the code-review pipeline traveled together as facets of one defect:

1. **SUMMARY parser leaks prose into file scope** — `compute_file_scope` boundary regex `^\s*\w+:` excluded hyphens, so `key-decisions:`, `patterns-established:`, and `requirements-completed:` did not reset `inSection`. Prose bullets from those sections were captured as file paths. Bullet capture also took the full line including em-dash descriptions and parentheticals, producing invalid paths downstream.

2. **Severity-label drift in `present_results`** — frontmatter was only grepped for `critical:`; when reviewer emitted `blocker:`, `CRITICAL` was empty and the critical-findings count was lost. The top-issues preview also missed `### BL-NN` headings.

3. **Fixer agent silently dropped BL-* findings** — `gsd-code-fixer` ID alphabet only documented `CR-\d+`/`WR-\d+`/`IN-\d+`. `BL-*` findings were silently excluded from `critical_warning` scope, the severity description, and sort order.

## What this fix does

- **Bug 1** (`get-shit-done/workflows/code-review.md` compute_file_scope): Replaces `\w+:` boundary with `[\w-]+:` (hyphen-aware) and adds em-dash/parenthetical stripping with a path-validity guard (`/\//` + `/\.[A-Za-z0-9]+$/`) in the Node script.
- **Bug 2** (`get-shit-done/workflows/code-review.md` present_results): Updates `CRITICAL=` grep to `-E "^\s*(critical|blocker):"` and adds `### BL-` to the top-issues preview grep pattern alongside `### CR-` and `### WR-`.
- **Bug 3** (`agents/gsd-code-fixer.md`): Updates ID alphabet, severity description, filter sets (`critical_warning` and `all`), and sort order to treat `BL-*` as Critical-tier-equivalent to `CR-*`.
- **Reviewer contract** (`agents/gsd-code-reviewer.md`): Adds a label-equivalence note in the `write_review` step acknowledging `blocker:`/`BL-` as accepted alternatives while noting `critical:`/`CR-` as canonical.

## Root cause

The reviewer agent uses `BLOCKER`/`BL-` severity labels (documented in its `<adversarial_stance>`) but the downstream workflow and fixer agent only knew about `critical:`/`CR-`. The SUMMARY parser separately had a regex that was not hyphen-aware, causing false section boundary matches that bled prose bullets into the file scope.

## Testing

### How I verified the fix

18-test regression suite in `tests/code-review-pipeline-regression.test.cjs`:
- **Bug 1**: Pure-function `parseKeyFiles()` that mirrors the workflow script logic exactly, tested against fixture YAML strings. 5 behavioral tests + 2 docs-parity assertions on the workflow `.md` text.
- **Bug 2**: Pure-function `parseFrontmatterCritical()` helper tested with `blocker:`, `critical:`, and absent-key fixtures. 3 behavioral tests + 2 docs-parity assertions.
- **Bugs 3 + reviewer contract**: 4 + 2 docs-parity assertions scoped to the relevant XML sections in each agent `.md`.

All 18 tests pass. `npm run lint:tests` reports 0 violations.

Workflows:

- deploy-image.yml: build and push image to DO Container Registry, deploy to Droplet
- deploy-preview.yml: spin up ephemeral pr-{N} Droplet per PR, run full setup, comment live URL
- delete-preview.yml: destroy pr-{N} Droplet when PR is closed

- Skip wp core update in --yes mode to reduce CI runtime
- Poll port 22 before SSH connect to handle Droplet boot lag
- docker compose down before re-deploy to clear stale container name conflicts

File permissions:
- local: setfacl grants container uid 82 rw ACL; developer retains ownership
- preview: chmod 777 (ephemeral host, no concern)
- production: chown 82:82 + chmod 755 (tight, no world-write)

- Add --yes / --non-interactive flag forwarded to wp_setup.sh

### Motivation
- Reduce recurring `NAVER_INVESTOR_TREND: NOT_WIRED` noise by exposing a wired NAVER collector as a SHADOW_ONLY semantic investor-flow candidate without changing live execution semantics. 
- Provide a normalized, diagnostic-only semantic sample (foreign/institution/program net-buy, confidence, coverage, freshness, signal) so ADR-0477/ADR-0473/ADR-0475/ADR-0476/ADR-0480 can observe NAVER coverage and lower-priority data-availability actions instead of P1 NOT_WIRED evidence.

### Description
- Add a new SHADOW_ONLY collector SSOT `server/trading/signalScanner/naverInvestorTrendCollectorAdr0481.ts` implementing `buildNaverInvestorTrendCollectorResultAdr0481(input)` plus `safe` builder, compact/detail formatters, and a detail-registry entry; it normalizes raw rows, derives `semanticNetBuyCandidate`, and enforces policy invariants (`executionImpact='NONE'`, `liveExecutionAllowed=false`, `policyPromotionMode='SHADOW_ONLY'`, `operatorApprovalRequired=true`).
- Wire ADR-0481 into the router & warmup paths by updating `investorFlowProviderRouterAdr0477.ts` and `server/supply/investorFlowProviderHealth.ts` so NAVER is reported as wired (or as DATA_UNAVAILABLE/EMPTY/PARTIAL/STALE/PARSE_ERROR/PROVIDER_ERROR/ NON_TRADING_DAY) rather than `NOT_WIRED`, and allow ADR-0477 to consume the collector result as a semantic candidate in SHADOW_ONLY diagnostics (mapping ADR-0481 statuses to router statuses without live promotion).
- Expose NAVER candidate to dry-run positive-source and observation ledger by updating `gate1PositiveSourceWiringAdr0475.ts` and `gate1DryRunObservationLedgerAdr0476.ts` so ADR-0475 may list NAVER as a SHADOW_ONLY positive-source candidate and ADR-0476 saves sanitized observation rows (no raw payload persisted). 
- Adjust operator action routing `operatorActionRouterAdr0480.ts` to add a lower-priority `NAVER_INVESTOR_TREND_EMPTY_OR_UNAVAILABLE` action and to avoid keeping `INVESTOR_FLOW_PROVIDER_UNWIRED` solely because NAVER was previously not wired. 
- Add unit tests `server/trading/signalScanner/naverInvestorTrendCollectorAdr0481.test.ts`, and update existing tests to exercise wiring and integration points; add ADR doc `docs/adr/0481-naver-investor-trend-collector-wiring.md` and update `docs/adr/INDEX.md`.

### Testing
- Ran unit tests for the new collector and impacted components: `server/trading/signalScanner/naverInvestorTrendCollectorAdr0481.test.ts` (passed) and the related ADR signalScanner tests for ADR-0477/ADR-0473/ADR-0475/ADR-0476/ADR-0480 were executed and validated during the rollout; initial fixture/index expectations surfaced two minor failures which were fixed (test fixture for positive-source input and ADR index entry), after which the targeted tests for the wiring passed.
- Verified the new unit tests by running `npx vitest` for the new collector test and the related router/warmup/positive-source/ledger/operator-action tests (all targeted tests passed after fixes).
- Confirmed the implementation preserves invariants: no live execution modules or KIS order APIs were imported, `requiredScore` and Gate/Kelly thresholds were not changed, and raw NAVER payload is not persisted (checked by test assertions and source inspection).

author: trek-e
body:
## Fix PR

---

## Linked Issue

Fixes #3265

---

## What was broken

`state-snapshot` (and the CJS `cmdStateSnapshot` twin) passed the entire STATE.md blob — frontmatter + body — to `stateExtractField`. That function's bold pattern (`\*\*Field:\*\*`) has no line anchor, so a body Markdown table cell such as `**Status:** to ✅ COMPLETE` shadowed the authoritative YAML frontmatter `status:` value.

## What this fix does

Both `stateSnapshot` (TypeScript, `sdk/src/query/state.ts`) and `cmdStateSnapshot` (CJS, `get-shit-done/bin/lib/state.cjs`) now:
1. Parse `extractFrontmatter(content)` before any body extraction.
2. Strip frontmatter with `stripFrontmatter(content)` to produce a clean `body` string passed to `stateExtractField`.
3. For each canonical scalar field (`status`, `current_phase`, `current_plan`, `last_activity`, `paused_at`, etc.) use the non-empty frontmatter value when present, falling back to body extraction when the field is absent or no frontmatter block exists.

Body-only fields (decisions table, blockers list, session block) continue to use body extraction only.

## Root cause

`stateExtractField`'s bold-anywhere regex (`**Field:**` with `i` flag, no `^` anchor, no `m` flag) can match anywhere in the file, including inside table cells. The same precedent for frontmatter-first lookup was already established by `buildStateFrontmatter` (Bug #2613 fix), but `stateSnapshot` was not updated alongside it.

## Testing

### How I verified the fix

Regression tests added in both test suites confirm the fix.

### Regression test added?

- [x] Yes — added a test that would have caught this bug

Tests added:
- `sdk/src/query/state.test.ts` — 4 vitest cases (frontmatter status beats table cell **Status:** match; frontmatter current_plan beats body bold; no-frontmatter body fallback; per-field frontmatter absence fallback)
- `tests/state.test.cjs` — 3 node:test cases (same core scenarios, CJS parity)

### Platforms tested

- [x] macOS
- [ ] Windows (including backslash path handling)
- [ ] Linux
- [x] N/A (not platform-specific)

### Runtimes tested

- [x] Claude Code
- [ ] Gemini CLI
- [ ] OpenCode
- [ ] Other: ___
- [x] N/A (not runtime-specific)

---

- [x] Issue linked above with `Fixes #NNN` — **PR will be auto-closed if missing**
- [x] Linked issue has the `confirmed-bug` label
- [x] Fix is scoped to the reported bug — no unrelated changes included
- [x] Regression test added (or explained why not)
- [x] All existing tests pass (`npm test`)
- [x] `.changeset/` fragment added if this is a user-facing fix (`npm run changeset -- --type Fixed --pr <NNN> --body "..."`) — or `no-changelog` label applied
- [x] No unnecessary dependencies added

None

body:
## What

User wanted zero-click crash recovery + a Chrome-like recent-sessions menu + a launcher with preset AI flag combos. v3.4.2 ships all three as a wezterm Lua plugin (\`wezterm/wezbridge.lua\`).

## Three features

1. **Auto-restore on \`mux-startup\`** — silent re-spawn of AI panes after any wezterm crash if snapshot < 30 min old AND has ≥ 2 entries.
2. **\`LEADER+R\` fuzzy picker** — wezterm's \`InputSelector\` over all historical snapshots.
3. **\`LEADER+L\` launcher menu** — preset launches (claude --continue, claude --channels, codex resume --last, etc.).

## User install (one-time)

Drop into \`~/.wezterm.lua\`:
```lua
local wezterm = require 'wezterm'
local config = wezterm.config_builder()
local wezbridge_dir = '/abs/path/to/wezbridge'
package.path = package.path .. ';' .. wezbridge_dir .. '/wezterm/?.lua'
config.leader = { key = 'a', mods = 'CTRL', timeout_milliseconds = 2000 }
require('wezbridge').apply(config, {
  wezbridge_dir = wezbridge_dir,
  auto_restore = true,
  restore_keybind = { mods = 'LEADER', key = 'r' },
  launcher_keybind = { mods = 'LEADER', key = 'l' },
})
return config
```

## Tests
- 232/232 existing unit tests pass (no test changes — Lua isn't tested in this repo).

## Test plan (manual)
- [ ] Drop the snippet into \`~/.wezterm.lua\`, restart wezterm
- [ ] Confirm a fresh wezterm launch with no snapshot does nothing weird (logs: \`wezbridge: no snapshot to auto-restore\`)
- [ ] Crash wezterm, reopen → AI panes auto-restore from latest snapshot
- [ ] LEADER+R → fuzzy picker shows snapshots; pick one → panes spawn
- [ ] LEADER+L → launcher menu shows presets; pick "Claude — continue" → spawns claude --continue

body:
### Motivation

- Provide a configurable global root cache path and create deterministic per-task/per-UV cache directories to avoid collisions and simplify cleanup. 
- Surface cache path information to the browser run result for diagnostics. 
- Improve OffScreen capture reliability by increasing frame rate, screenshot timeouts and initial screenshot delay, and enable persisting user preferences where appropriate.

### Description

- Introduced `CefCachePaths` helper (in both GUI and OffScreen projects) to centralize cache path construction and safe filename segment generation via `SafeSegment` and SHA256 hashing. 
- Added support for a `--root-cache-path` CLI argument and set `CefCachePaths.RootCachePath` in `Program.cs` for both `CefClient` and `CefClient.OffScreen`, and ensure `DefaultCachePath` is created. 
- Propagated the root cache path from `MainClient` into `CefClientSession` and have the session pass `--root-cache-path` when starting the child process. 
- Reworked browser slot/cache handling: `MainForm.CreateBrowserAsync` now accepts `taskId`, creates per-task cache dirs using `CefCachePaths.GetTaskSlotCachePath`, stores `CachePath` on `BrowserSlot`, and includes `cachePath` in the `RunAsync` result JSON. 
- In OffScreen mode, added `GetUvCachePath` usage to build per-UV cache directories; set `RequestContextSettings.PersistUserPreferences = true` and `PersistSessionCookies` where applicable. 
- Tuned OffScreen defaults: increased `WindowlessFrameRate` to 15, `DefaultFirstScreenshotDelayMs` from 500 to 1000, `DefaultScreenshotTimeoutMs` from 1500 to 3000, and updated payload defaults to match. 
- Improved error logging for screenshot capture failures and adjusted various callsites to create required directories. 

### Testing

- Ran a full solution build with `dotnet build`, which completed successfully. 
- No automated unit tests were present or executed as part of this change.

author: devin-marks
body:
## Summary

Brings pi-forge's prompts surface to **feature parity with skills** — list, invoke from chat, Settings → Prompts management tab, per-project enable/disable overrides, cascade view across projects.

Pi prompts are markdown templates under `<dir>/prompts/` (mirrors the skills layout). The pi SDK loads them via the resource loader and `session.prompt()` already expands `/<promptname> args` to the template body before sending to the model (`expandPromptTemplates: true` is the SDK default — pi-forge does NOT need to expand server-side; the integration is purely **discovery + management**).

## What lands

### Server
- **`prompt-overrides.ts`** (new) — pi-forge-private per-project tri-state store at `${FORGE_DATA_DIR}/prompts-overrides.json`. Mirrors `skill-overrides.ts` byte-for-byte (atomic writes, tri-state semantics, cascade-clear on project delete).
- **`config-manager.ts`** — `listPrompts` + `setPromptEnabled` + `effectivePromptsForProject` + `getAllPromptOverrides` + `PromptNotFoundError` + `PromptSummary` + `PromptsListResult`. Uses `DefaultResourceLoader.getPrompts()` for discovery (the standalone `loadPromptTemplates` isn't exported from the SDK package index).
- **`session-registry.ts buildSessionSettingsManager`** — extended to inject BOTH skill AND prompt patterns into the SettingsManager monkey-patch.
- **`agent-resource-loader.ts buildForgeResourceLoader`** — adds the `promptsOverride` callback (parallel to existing `skillsOverride`).
- **`routes/config.ts`** — four new routes: `GET /config/prompts`, `GET /config/prompts/overrides`, `PUT /config/prompts/:name/enabled`, `DELETE /config/prompts/:name/enabled`. Same shape as the corresponding skills routes.

### Client
- **`api-client/`** — `PromptSummary`, `PromptOverridesResponse`, `PromptsListResponse`, `PromptOverrideState` types + matching validators + `listPrompts` / `listPromptOverrides` / `setPromptEnabled` / `clearPromptProjectOverride` api methods.
- **`SettingsPanel.tsx`** — new "Prompts" tab + `PromptsTab` component (mirrors `SkillsTab` with the extension/`disableModelInvocation` columns dropped, `argumentHint` chip added when present).
- **`ChatInput.tsx`** — fetches the active project's enabled prompts and appends them to the slash-command catalog as `/<promptname>` entries with description + argument hint. Selecting one inserts `/<name> ` into the input so the user can append args before pressing Enter; the SDK expands the template at send time.

## Differences from skills

| | Skills | Prompts |
|---|---|---|
| Source kinds | `global` / `project` / `extension` | `global` / `project` (no package source today) |
| `disableModelInvocation` field | Yes | No (not a prompts concept) |
| Argument hint | No | Yes (`argument-hint` frontmatter) |
| Diagnostics | SDK surfaces collisions | SDK doesn't surface today (always `[]`) |
| File location | `<dir>/skills/` | `<dir>/prompts/` |

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run check` clean (typecheck + lint + format)
- [x] `npm run build` clean
- [x] `npx tsx tests/test-prompts.ts` — 22/22 PASS (new file, mirrors skills coverage in test-config.ts)
- [x] `npm run test:ci` — 25/25 PASS (was 24)
- [ ] Live: drop a `summarize.md` with `name:` + `description:` + `argument-hint:` frontmatter into `<project>/.pi/prompts/`, confirm it appears in:
  - Settings → Prompts (with the argument-hint chip)
  - the chat-input slash-command palette as `/summarize`
- [ ] Live: type `/summarize foo.ts` in the chat, hit send, confirm the agent receives the EXPANDED template body (with `$1` substituted) — that's pi SDK behaviour we're trusting; the chat input shouldn't echo the literal `/summarize foo.ts`.
- [ ] Live: toggle the prompt off in Settings → Prompts, confirm it disappears from the slash palette on next session.
- [ ] Live: per-project override (Settings → Prompts → Overrides) — toggle on for one project, off for another; verify each session sees its own state.

author: fxacc
body:
### Motivation
- Provide an easy-to-build, ultra‑minimal ImmortalWrt/OpenWrt firmware for Newifi D2 (MT7621) that only includes LuCI and a PassWall2-based proxy stack to keep Flash usage and CPU overhead low.
- Ensure PassWall2's maintained packages (`xray-core`, `sing-box`, geodata) are sourced from the correct feeds so newer/core implementations override older base-feed copies.
- Set device defaults and build metadata for Breed / sysupgrade-friendly images and long‑uptime operation (DNS cache tuning, compile date in version string).
- Prevent inclusion of heavy/unwanted packages (OpenClash, SSR‑plus, AdGuardHome, ZeroTier, etc.) to reduce image size and runtime load.

### Description
- Add `feeds.conf.default` that places PassWall related feeds (`passwall_packages`, `passwall2`) at the top followed by ImmortalWrt 23.05 feeds to prefer PassWall-maintained proxy cores.
- Replace `newifi3.config` with a minimal device seed that targets `DEVICE_d-team_newifi-d2` and explicitly selects `luci`, `luci-app-passwall2`, `xray-core`, and `sing-box` while leaving other heavy plugins disabled.
- Update `DIY/diy-part2-d2.sh` to set default LAN IP to `192.168.2.1`, set hostname to `Newifi-D2`, inject compile-date/version metadata into `openwrt_release`, apply DNS cache tuning for long uptime, and remove unwanted package directories to keep the tree minimal; script is made strict (`set -euo pipefail`).
- Add `Scripts/build-newifi-d2-passwall2.sh` as a standalone local build helper that clones ImmortalWrt, copies the `feeds.conf.default` and `newifi3.config`, runs feeds update/install, applies the DIY script, downloads sources and builds the firmware.
- Update `.github/workflows/newifi3.yml` to watch the new files, use the new product name, fix Actions output usage (`$GITHUB_OUTPUT`), add `FILE_NAME`/release tag changes, and improve the Release body describing the minimal PassWall2 build.

### Testing
- Ran `git diff --check` to validate no whitespace/errors and it passed. 
- Performed shell syntax checks with `bash -n DIY/diy-part2-d2.sh` and `bash -n Scripts/build-newifi-d2-passwall2.sh` and both returned without syntax errors.
- Validated workflow YAML parsing with `ruby -e 'require "yaml"; YAML.load_file(".github/workflows/newifi3.yml")'` which succeeded.
- Verified presence of PassWall2-related entries and configuration lines with quick `rg`/file inspections (feeds, config and DIY script) which confirmed the expected additions and exclusions.

body:
### Motivation
- Prevent playback from stopping after a few tracks by fixing edge cases when the player reaches the end of the native queue or when the playlist is extended near its end.

### Description
- Desktop: guard against invalid `currentIndex` and, when lazy-loading more tracks near the end, re-read `get().playlist` and compute `nextIndex` from the updated playlist to avoid using stale length information (`apps/desktop/src/store/player.ts`).
- Desktop: compute `shouldLoadMore` from `currentIndex` and only call `loadMoreSourceTracks()` if needed, then use the refreshed playlist for next-track selection.
- Mobile: avoid calling `TrackPlayer.skipToNext()` when the native active index is already on the last queued item by checking `activeIndex < queue.length - 1`, allowing the business-layer fallback to continue playback (`apps/mobile/src/context/PlayerContext.tsx`).
- Changes are limited to next-track / queue boundary logic to ensure reliable continuation across both platforms.

### Testing
- Ran `git diff --check` on the modified files which reported no whitespace errors and showed the intended changes (success).
- Attempted `pnpm --filter sound-x run build` which failed due to existing workspace TypeScript/module resolution issues unrelated to these logic changes (known workspace type errors, failure not caused by this PR).
- Attempted `pnpm --filter mobile exec tsc --noEmit` which also failed due to existing TypeScript type/module resolution problems in the workspace unrelated to these changes (failure not caused by this PR).

author: src893
body:
# xCloud store integration

## Summary
 
Lands the Microsoft xCloud store implementation, its OAuth + XBL/XSTS
token chains, and the Layer-5 subscription service that gates xCloud
sync on an active Game Pass entitlement.
 
This is the fifth and final per-store implementation to ship on
`new-architecture`. It depends on the `stores/shared/` infrastructure
(StoreBase, StoreRegistry, `inject_store_dependencies`) which must be
merged first.
 
## What's added
 
### `stores/microsoft/` (7 files, 1156 L)
 
| OP-code | File | Lines | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OP-53`  | `__init__.py` | 2 | Package re-exports |
| `OP-53a` | `microsoft_store.py` | 343 | `MicrosoftStore` — `StoreBase` impl, no install / no Wine, streaming-only |
| `OP-53b` | `microsoft_catalog.py` | 208 | xCloud catalog reader — fetch product IDs, batch resolve titles |
| `OP-53c` | `microsoft_browser_auth.py` | 85 | OAuth flow orchestration via `EdgeBrowser` + `OAuthBrowserMonitor` |
| `OP-53d` | `microsoft_config.py` | 125 | Frozen `MicrosoftConfig` — endpoints, scopes, allowed redirect URIs |
| `OP-53e` | `microsoft_auth.py` | 231 | XBL / XSTS HTTP plumbing — standard chain + GSSV chain |
| `OP-53f` | `microsoft_subscription.py` | 162 | Per-store subscription gate, calls into Layer-5 service |
 
### `stores/microsoft/tokens/` (5 files, 458 L)
 
| OP-code | File | Lines | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OP-54`  | `__init__.py` | 7 | Subpackage re-exports |
| `OP-54a` | `manager.py` | 43 | `MicrosoftTokenManager` — façade over the four mixins |
| `OP-54b` | `persistence.py` | 182 | Encrypted on-disk tokens, legacy plaintext migration |
| `OP-54c` | `oauth.py` | 88 | Code exchange + refresh, staleness threshold |
| `OP-54d` | `xbl_chain.py` | 138 | `build_chain` + `build_gssv_chain` — both XBL/XSTS chains |
 
### `services/microsoft_subscription/` (8 files, 335 L)
 
| OP-code | File | Lines | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OP-22`  | `__init__.py` | 3 | Package re-exports |
| `OP-22a` | `service.py` | 110 | `MicrosoftSubscriptionService` — Layer-5 façade |
| `OP-22b` | `cache_mixin.py` | 65 | Read / write / TTL plumbing, end-of-month UTC expiry |
| `OP-22c` | `probe_emission.py` | 80 | Probe runner + `SUBSCRIPTION_*` event emission |
| `OP-22d` | `event_handlers.py` | 24 | Bus subscriptions for cache invalidation |
| `OP-22e` | `cache.py` | 34 | `CacheManager` backend |
| `OP-22f` | `time_utils.py` | 13 | UTC end-of-month TTL helper |
| `OP-22g` | `constants.py` | 6 | Magic numbers (relying parties, refresh threshold) |
 
**Total : 20 files, 1949 lines.**
 
## Architectural compliance
 
- **Layer separation respected.** `MicrosoftStore` (Layer 4) imports
  from `core/`, `event_bus/`, `auth/`, `cdp/`. It depends on
  `MicrosoftSubscriptionService` (Layer 5) only via the
  `inject_store_dependencies()` post-discovery wiring — no direct
  Layer-5 import in the store itself.
- **`StoreBase` contract honoured.** All seven abstract methods
  implemented (`is_available`, `start_auth`, `complete_auth`,
  `logout`, `get_library`, `install_game`, `launch_game`).
  `supports_install=False` and `uses_wine=False` reflect the
  streaming-only nature of xCloud.
- **Subscription gate is fail-safe.** When the probe fails and no
  cached tier exists, `get_library` skips the sync with
  `SYNC_SKIPPED(reason="subscription_check_error")` rather than
  fetching a catalog the user can't launch. Stale-cache fallback
  serves the last known tier with a warning log.
- **GSSV chain isolation.** `xCloud streaming endpoints reject the
  standard XSTS token (relying party `xboxlive.com`). A dedicated
  GSSV chain (`gssv.xboxlive.com`) is built on demand by
  `build_gssv_chain` and used exclusively for streaming-related
  calls.
- **Volumetry gates green.** Largest file is `microsoft_store.py`
  at 343 L (cap 550 L). Largest function is `MicrosoftStore.get_library`
  at ~50 L with 6 locals, nesting 3, fan-out 9 — all within budget.
- **Security gates green.** Every token write goes through
  `SecureTokenStore` ; legacy plaintext files are migrated on next
  save and emit `LEGACY_PLAINTEXT_DETECTED`. Strict SSL context
  on every Microsoft HTTPS call. Allowed redirect URIs whitelisted
  in `MicrosoftConfig`.
## Subscription gate behaviour (Sprint 18e)
 
`MicrosoftSubscriptionService.get_tier(tokens)` is the single source
of truth for "is this user a Game Pass subscriber". Called once per
sync from `MicrosoftStore.get_library`, with cache-first semantics :
 
| Probe result | Cached entry | Returned tier | Bus event |
|---|---|---|---|
| Success, parsed | — | `STANDARD` / `ULTIMATE` / `NONE` | `SUBSCRIPTION_DETECTED` or `SUBSCRIPTION_EXPIRED` |
| Success but unparseable | — | `ACTIVE_UNKNOWN` | `SUBSCRIPTION_DETECTED` |
| Failed | Fresh cache | cached tier | (silent re-emit) |
| Failed | Stale cache | stale cached tier | (warning log) |
| Failed | None | `NONE` | `SUBSCRIPTION_CHECK_FAILED` |
 
Cache invalidation on three bus events :
`STORE_AUTH_COMPLETE` (microsoft) · `STORE_LOGOUT` (microsoft) ·
`ACCOUNT_SWITCHED` (any account).
 
TTL is end-of-month UTC. In normal use, an active subscriber
triggers exactly one probe per calendar month — every other sync
serves the cached tier instantly.
 
Tier discrimination between Essential / Premium / Ultimate is
**best-effort** in this PR. Sprint 18f will sharpen the boundaries
once we have real-account capture data ; for now, anything that
parses as "active" is mapped to `STANDARD` or `ULTIMATE` based on
the response shape.
 
## `inject_store_dependencies()` wiring
 
`MicrosoftStore` exposes a writable `subscription_service` attribute
that `service_bootstrap` populates via the `_STORE_INJECTIONS` table
after Layer-5 services are constructed. Without this wiring the
attribute would be `None` and the subscription gate would silently
no-op — the bug Sprint 18e was created to fix.
 
The injection table entry :
```python
("microsoft_subscription_service", "subscription_service")
```
 
Reads as : "after constructing `microsoft_subscription_service` at
Layer 5, assign it to `store.subscription_service` on every store
that declares the attribute (only `MicrosoftStore` here)".
 
## Out of scope
 
- **Owned-games filtering** (showing only purchased + streamable
  games, hiding the public Game Pass catalog). Spec'd separately in
  `microsoft_owned_games_spec.md` and deferred — Microsoft's policy
  on owned-game streaming changed twice in 2024-2025 and is
  expected to keep evolving. We ship the catalog-based behaviour
  for now and revisit when the dust settles.
- **Sprint 18f tier discrimination.** Capture real Essential /
  Premium / Ultimate response payloads from live accounts, then
  sharpen `_parse_tier_from_response` accordingly.
- **Multi-account support.** Token store is keyed on a single
  `ms_user.json` file. Multi-account (one user, several Microsoft
  accounts) is a frontend / settings problem, tracked separately.
- **Frontend "Game Pass required" badge.** When tier expires, the
  current behaviour is to skip sync entirely. The UX of showing an
  expired-subscription state with a re-subscribe CTA is part of
  v7.1.0 Section 4.
## Migration notes
 
For reviewers comparing with the legacy `staging` branch :
 
- `MicrosoftStore.__init__` signature changed — now requires
  `subscription_service: MicrosoftSubscriptionService | None = None`
  to allow the bootstrap-time injection. Legacy callers that
  instantiate the store directly must pass `None` explicitly or
  rely on the default.
- The `microsoft_tokens.json` file format is unchanged — existing
  authentications survive the upgrade. Plaintext legacy files
  detected on first read trigger a warning event and are
  re-encrypted on next save.
- `MicrosoftCatalogReader.fetch_catalog_ids` no longer accepts a
  `language` kwarg ; the reader now consults
  `get_unifideck_locale()` interna

## Summary
- Ships 7 new minds (Abraham Lincoln, Andrew Carnegie, Florence Nightingale, Frederick Douglass, Julius Caesar, Napoleon Bonaparte, Seneca) end-to-end so per-mind landing pages render for the full 26-mind corpus. Live `ALLOWED_SLUGS` goes from 19 → 25; Albert Einstein remains held out pending Hebrew University legal review.
- Adds vitest gate (`website/src/lib/frameworks.test.ts`, 23 tests) that locks `ALLOWED_SLUGS` ↔ `DISPLAY_ORDER` ↔ `SLUG_COLOR_VAR` ↔ shipped `framework.json` ↔ `globals.css` color-vars in lockstep.
- Wires complementary CSS custom properties for each new mind (`--color-lincoln/carnegie/nightingale/douglass/caesar/napoleon/seneca`) in all three palette blocks: `:root` (dark Late Study), `html.light` (Reading Room parchment), and the `@media print` override.

Per task `8987b12a` / capsule `ff13fd3d`. Marketing brief `eb1de1a5` + `docs/roster-expansion.md` called out these 7 specifically; `packs.ts` already references them in `pack.members[]`, they were just dark for lack of an `ALLOWED_SLUGS` entry.

## Implementation notes
- `frameworks/<slug>/framework.json` → `website/data/frameworks/<slug>/framework.json` for all 7. Florence Nightingale + Frederick Douglass have a `critical_incident_database_ref` pointer in the source instead of an inline array, so I inlined their `incidents/incidents.json` array into `framework.json` to keep the shipped data dir flat (matches `marcus-aurelius/`'s shape; the helper still supports the separate `incidents/` subfolder for backward compat).
- Normalized `meta.born` / `meta.died` to year-only strings (e.g. `"1809-02-12"` → `"1809"`) so the era display in `getFramework()` reads `"1809–1865"` rather than the ugly ISO form. ERA_FALLBACK kicks in for Napoleon + Seneca whose source has empty born/died.
- `DISPLAY_ORDER` is grouped by domain rather than alphabetical: Stoics together (`marcus-aurelius → seneca → epictetus → cicero`), 19th-c statesmen (`benjamin-franklin → abraham-lincoln → frederick-douglass`), industrialists (`john-d-rockefeller → andrew-carnegie`), reformers (`harriet-tubman → florence-nightingale`), conquerors (`alexander-the-great → julius-caesar → napoleon-bonaparte`).

## Acceptance verification

**`npm run build` (Next.js SSG):**
```
● /frameworks/[slug]
  ├ /frameworks/isaac-newton
  ├ /frameworks/marie-curie
  └ [+22 more paths]   ← 25 total, all 7 new minds in .next/server/app/frameworks/
```
All 7 new mind HTML files were generated:
```
✓ abraham-lincoln    ✓ andrew-carnegie    ✓ florence-nightingale
✓ frederick-douglass ✓ julius-caesar      ✓ napoleon-bonaparte
✓ seneca
```

**Roster index page (`/frameworks`):** lists 25 distinct `/frameworks/<slug>` href links including all 7 new minds.

**`/api/agon` council validation:** route imports `ALLOWED_SLUGS` from `@/lib/frameworks`, so adding the 7 slugs there is sufficient — no API changes required.

## Test Coverage

**`npm test` → 91 / 91 pass** (5 test files).

`frameworks.test.ts` alone runs 23 assertions covering:
- 4 roster-gate assertions (`length === 25`, no Einstein, all 7 new minds, no dups)
- 2 `DISPLAY_ORDER` parity checks (set equality + dup-free)
- 2 `SLUG_COLOR_VAR` parity checks (every slug → CSS var; no extras)
- 4 framework.json parity checks (file exists, parses, `getFramework()` populated, expansion slugs all have ≥1 incident)
- 4 era-resolution branch tests (born+died wins / `meta.era` fallback / `ERA_FALLBACK` fallback / null on unknown slug)
- 2 `getAllFrameworks()` tests (length matches `DISPLAY_ORDER`; ordering preserved)
- 2 `getValidation()` tests (returns object when shipped / null when missing)
- 3 globals.css color-var coverage tests (file readable, every var declared, expansion slugs declared in BOTH dark + light palettes)

**Coverage on `frameworks.ts`** (vitest v8 reporter):
```
File           | % Stmts | % Branch | % Funcs | % Lines
frameworks.ts  |   88.57 |       70 |     100 |   87.87
```
The 12 uncovered lines are the `incidents/incidents.json` separate-file fallback (lines 248–251) which no shipped mind currently exercises (all 26 use inline `critical_incident_database`). That branch is pre-existing dead code; not introduced by this PR. The added lines (slug data tables) hit 100% via the `for-each-slug` loops in the tests.

## Capsule scope
Touched files match `wanman capsule mine` allowed paths:
- `website/src/lib/frameworks.ts`, `website/src/lib/frameworks.test.ts`
- `website/src/app/globals.css`

## Summary

First Case-B (lift-z) extension beyond the four Section-15 primes `{13, 19, 31, 37}`. Mirrors the Section 22/23/24/25 Case-A extension pattern along the parallel `selmer_padic_solubility_lift_z` parametric theorem.

- 3 new per-prime axiom-free `ℚ_[p]`-solubility theorems via `selmer_padic_solubility_lift_z`:
  - `selmer_padic_solubility_p43_hensel` — witness `(x₀, y₀, z₀) = (1, 0, 2)`; `43 ∣ 3 + 0 + 40 = 43 = 43·1`, `gcd(60, 43) = 1`
  - `selmer_padic_solubility_p67_hensel` — witness `(1, 0, 12)`; `67 ∣ 3 + 0 + 8640 = 8643 = 67·129`, `gcd(2160, 67) = 1`
  - `selmer_padic_solubility_p79_hensel` — witness `(0, 1, 17)`; `79 ∣ 0 + 4 + 24565 = 24569 = 79·311`, `gcd(4335, 79) = 1`
- 1 new bundled theorem `selmer_padic_solubility_extended_caseB_primes` (3-fold conjunction across `{43, 67, 79}`)
- Brings the discharged sub-collection of `selmer_padic_solubility` from **22 primes** (Section-8 + extended Case-A v4) to **25 primes total**: 12 Section-8 + 10 extended Case-A + 3 extended Case-B.

## Witness verification

All three witnesses are decidable from `Int.isCoprime_iff_gcd_eq_one.mpr (by decide)` + numeric divisibility `(by decide)`. Verified by Python:

| p  | (x₀, y₀, z₀) | 3·x₀³ + 4·y₀³ + 5·z₀³ | matches `(mod p)` | gcd(15·z₀², p) |
|----|--------------|------------------------|-------------------|-----------------|
| 43 | (1, 0, 2)    | 43                     | 43·1              | 1               |
| 67 | (1, 0, 12)   | 8643                   | 67·129            | 1               |
| 79 | (0, 1, 17)   | 24569                  | 79·311            | 1               |

## Counts

- File: 1674 → **1764** lines (+90)
- theoremCount: 69 → **73** (+4: three per-prime + one bundle)
- definitionCount: unchanged at 8
- axiomCount: unchanged at 2
- sorries: unchanged at 0
- meta.json + research/problems/.../json + state.md synced

## Build status

Build pending. New theorems are structurally identical to existing
`selmer_padic_solubility_p13_hensel`/`p19_hensel`/`p31_hensel`/`p37_hensel`
with only the prime literal and witness `(x₀, y₀, z₀)` differing — no
new Mathlib API surface required.

## Coordination

PR #17610 (Iter 15 universal Case-A theorem) is parallel to this work.
Universal Case-A subsumes the per-prime Case-A corollaries (Sections 22-25)
but does NOT subsume the Case-B chain that Section 26 begins extending.
Both PRs touch the same file but in disjoint regions; merge order
should not affect correctness.

Diese PR setzt die Verbesserung #4 (Retry-Logik bei fehlgeschlagenen ffmpeg-Calls) um.

Dadurch wird der Exportprozess robuster gegen kurzzeitige Fehler oder Flakes während des FFMPEG-Renderings.

author: mekenthompson
body:
## Summary

v0.7.0 had two compose-mount bugs that crash-looped the fleet on first
boot. I hit both during a real cutover today — host got rolled back to
v0.6 to recover. This is the smallest-viable patch to make v0.7
installable without rebuilding the docker images.

- **vault file mounted as a directory.** Compose mounted
  `${HOME}/.switchroom/vault:/state/vault` but the actual vault file is
  `~/.switchroom/vault.enc` (top-level file, not a `vault/` subdir).
  Docker auto-created the missing source as an empty root-owned
  directory; broker found no vault and restart-looped. Fixed by
  mounting the file directly at `/state/vault.enc:ro` plus an explicit
  `SWITCHROOM_VAULT_PATH` env so the broker doesn't fall back to its
  `~/.switchroom/vault.enc` default that resolves to `/root/...`
  inside the container.
- **agent containers crash-looped on `cd` to a host path.**
  Scaffolded `start.sh` bakes the absolute host path of `agentDir` at
  scaffold time (`cd "/home/<user>/.switchroom/agents/<name>"`), but
  the bind-mount destination was `/state/agent`, so the host path
  didn't exist inside the container. Fixed by **dual-mounting**: the
  same host directory is bound BOTH at the canonical `/state/agent`
  (Dockerfile.agent's `CMD` is `/state/agent/start.sh`, has to stay)
  AND at the original host path (so start.sh's host-pathed `cd`
  Just Works). Same dual treatment for `/state/.claude` and
  `/var/log/switchroom`. **No image rebuild required** — operators
  just `switchroom apply && docker compose up -d`.
- **defensive `mkdir` on every host bind-mount source.** Apply now
  creates the host directories docker is about to bind-mount BEFORE
  invoking compose. Closes the bug class that produced both the
  root-owned `~/.switchroom/vault` stub AND the root-owned

author: davidlandreman
body:
## Summary

The kernel desktop and TTYs now render text from a real TrueType font with 8bpp anti-aliased glyphs, replacing the embedded 8x8 bitmap. JetBrains Mono Regular ships as `assets/system.ttf` (OFL 1.1) and is parsed once at boot into a per-glyph coverage cache; the embedded 8x8 stays as a parse-failure fallback. Cleanup along the way removed a non-functional hand-rolled TTF backend, a VFNT bitmap path, and a pile of residual font scaffolding that no longer had callers.

## Design decisions

- **One monospaced TTF for the whole kernel.** Cell-grid TTYs and proportional widgets sharing a face means the face has to be monospaced; `cell_width()` is the advance of `'M'` after scaling, which holds for any monospaced family.
- **Boot-only selection.** `init_fonts()` runs once after heap init and before the first window is built. The `Mutex<Option<FontRef>>` runtime-swap path and the `font arial` / `font embedded` / `font status` shell commands are removed.
- **8bpp anti-aliasing from day one.** `ab_glyph_rasterizer` produces 8bpp natively; the `GraphicsDevice::draw_text` default impl alpha-blends each glyph pixel against `read_pixel`, so adapters inherit it for free.
- **Vendor over hand-roll.** `ttf-parser` 0.25 (`no-std-float`) and `ab_glyph_rasterizer` 0.1 (`libm`) are both `no_std`-clean for the `x86_64-unknown-none` target. Vendoring beat the previous hand-rolled parser, which mishandled per-glyph `bytes_per_row`, capped glyphs at 256 bytes, and rendered every advance at a single average value.
- **Glyph-centric `Font` trait.** Every glyph carries its own `width`, `height`, baseline-relative `x_offset` / `y_offset`, `advance`, and `coverage` slice. `char_width()` / `char_height()` / `bytes_per_row()` / `get_char_bitmap()` are gone; consumers use `cell_width()` / `line_height()` / `ascent()` / `glyph(ch)`.

## What got cleaned up

| Removed | Why |
|---|---|
| `src/graphics/fonts/truetype_font.rs` (~750 LOC), `vfnt.rs` (~130 LOC) | Replaced by `ttf.rs` against a real parser |
| `assets/{arial.ttf,tiny.ttf,ibmplex.fnt,ibmplex-large.fnt}` | Old experiments; one bundled face now |
| `ARIAL_*`, `IBM_PLEX_*` lazy statics; `try_load_arial_font`, `set_default_font`, `reset_to_embedded_font` | Boot-only selection eliminates the runtime-swap surface |
| `font arial` / `font embedded` / `font status` shell subcommands | Diagnostic scaffolding for the broken TTF path |
| `CHAR_WIDTH: 12` / `CHAR_HEIGHT: 16` constants in `text_buffer.rs` (and their `.max()` floors) | Dead carryover from a prior TTF attempt |
| Hard-coded `char_width = 8` literals in `button.rs`, `label.rs`, `text_input.rs`, `menu.rs` | Replaced with `font.cell_width()` |

## Tests

5 new font tests (`src/tests/fonts.rs`): parse the bundled face, monospace invariant (advances of `A` / `M` / `i` all equal `cell_width`), layout sums (5-char string equals `5 * cell_width`), AA invariant (rasterized `'A'` has both fully-opaque and partial-coverage pixels), and embedded-fallback completeness (printable ASCII fully covered). The existing filesystem tests now read `/system.ttf` instead of `/arial.ttf`. `./test.sh` exits 33 with 42/42 passing; headless boot reaches `init_fonts: parsed system.ttf at 14px (cell 8x18, ascent 14)` and completes the initial render with no panics.

---

author: keithduncan
body:
## Summary

Re-lands stack13 from the maintenance-reduction series (the original
PR #39 was merged then reverted via the master force-push). Combines
what was previously two commits ([PR12] + [PR13]) into one stack PR
per the index plan.

### PR12 — opt-in Moo backend

Adds `Paws::Materializer::Moo`: a parallel materialiser that builds
Moo classes with Type::Tiny type constraints from the IR. The Moo
classes populate the Paws::SerDes side-table (from stack12) directly
via the new `Paws::SerDes->register` API, so the wire layer never has
to inflate Moo to Moose for introspection.

Files added:
- `lib/Paws/Materializer/Moo.pm` — Moo backend
- `t/model/03_materializer_moo.t` — smoke (6 subtests)
- `docs/oo-backends.md` — type mapping + backend tradeoffs

Files changed:
- `lib/Paws/SerDes.pm` — new `->register` entry point that backends
  call instead of relying on `_build_from_meta` introspection
- `cpanfile` — declare `Moo`, `Type::Tiny`, `Types::Standard`,
  `MooX::ClassAttribute`
- `docs/architecture.md` — PR12 section

### PR13 — flip the default

`Paws::Materializer::Auto` now defaults to the Moo backend instead of
Moose. `PAWS_OO_BACKEND=Moose` remains the documented escape hatch
for one release.

Files changed:
- `lib/Paws/Materializer/Auto.pm` — default flipped from Moose → Moo
- `t/model/05_auto_hook.t` — assertions updated: default subtest now
  exercises Moo; Moose subtest exercises the `PAWS_OO_BACKEND=Moose`
  escape hatch in a child process
- `docs/oo-backends.md`, `docs/architecture.md` — default-vs-escape-
  hatch swap

### Scope of the flip

This affects classes loaded **through** the materialiser hook
(`-MPaws::Materializer::Auto`). On-disk AOT classes in `auto-lib/`
remain Moose; nothing under `auto-lib/` changes here. The dist-layout
change (drop `auto-lib/`, ship JSON in `share/`) is the
maintainer-driven major-version-bump moment in stack19.

## Cherry-pick conflict resolution

Cherry-picking [PR13] on top of stack11 (already on master)
conflicted in `t/model/05_auto_hook.t` because stack11's
re-land had wrapped the Moo subtest in a `plan skip_all` (Moo
backend wasn't available yet) and PR13 reorganised the same
subtest. Resolved by keeping PR13's intent (Moose-as-escape-hatch
+ Moo-as-default subtests) and dropping the skip_all guard since
`Paws::Materializer::Moo` is now present in this PR.

## Stack context

This is stack13 of the 21-PR maintenance-reduction series tracked
in #6. Stacks 02–12 plus the auto-lib regen (#55) are merged.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI `test` workflow passes — wire-layer parity preserved (the
      stack12 SerDes migration unblocks this).
- [ ] CI `regen-byte-identical` workflow stays green.

author: sachiniyer
body:
## Summary
- `pixel_style_at` ran a `source_region != region` check that mixed a 1D `source_x` (computed from a shuffled array index) with the current pixel's 2D `local_y`. That comparison has no geometric meaning and was hiding ~27.7% of triangle pixels during the Idle and Sorting phases of the satisfying-sort animation. The holes only "disappeared" during Completion because `visual_source_index_for_nominal` happened to return `nominal_index` once the scan finished, accidentally making `source_x ≈ local_x`.
- The shuffled-source path was never used to color pixels — styling reads `nominal_index` via `style_for_index_with_min_window` — so the gate was effectively dead code that only removed pixels. Dropped the gate and the helpers that exclusively supported it (`shuffled_index_for_nominal`, `source_local_x_for_index`, `visual_source_index_for_nominal`, plus the `SortState` accessors used only by them).
- Added a regression test (`idle_phase_populates_every_triangle_pixel`) that walks the full viewport during Idle and asserts every `TopTriangle`/`BottomTriangle` pixel renders as `Base`.

Fixes #268. Detail bug: `bug_85d5ca30-433d-43d9-9ffd-5e80c7d4e8aa`.

Companion to [#322](https://github.com/xpaysh/awesome-x402/pull/322) which added Askew's direct x402 endpoints. This entry covers the OpenClaw plugin published yesterday at <https://www.npmjs.com/package/@askew-network/openclaw-plugin> (MIT, source at <https://github.com/rubix1138/askew-openclaw-plugin>).

**What it is**

A thin Node bridge that exposes Askew's 5 paid + 3 free MCP tools as native OpenClaw skills. Payments settle directly to Askew's wallet on Base mainnet via x402 — no aggregator on the data path, no credit balance, no API key. The plugin holds no wallet keys and reads no environment variables; x402 challenge envelopes are passed verbatim to whatever x402-aware runtime invoked the plugin (typically OpenClaw's gateway or `@blockrun/clawrouter`).

```
openclaw plugins install @askew-network/openclaw-plugin
```

Tools (mirroring `x402.askew.network/offers`): `askew_yields` ($0.002), `askew_staking_router` ($0.003), `askew_research_query` ($0.003), `askew_intel_threats` ($0.002), `askew_intel_feed` ($0.005), plus 3 free tools (`askew_yields_preview`, `askew_offers`, `askew_health`).

author: zitonwei
body:
Fixes #1258

## Summary
This PR fixes missing `action_details` in `Node.Action.Failed` callbacks when an action exits through an early failure path.

Previously, some failed actions returned an empty `ActionResult`, which left `action_id` as `MaaInvalidId`. As a result, the failed action detail written to runtime cache and emitted through callbacks could lose useful metadata.

Now `Actuator::run()` fills a failed `ActionResult` with the current action id, node name, action type, hit box, and `success=false` before storing it.

## Validation

- `cmake --build build-make --target MaaFramework -j 8`
- `cmake --build build-make --target PipelineTesting -j 8`
- `./build-make/bin/PipelineTesting ./test/TestingDataSet`
- `git diff --check`

## Summary by Sourcery

确保失败的操作始终记录并发出详细的失败元数据，而不是返回空结果。

错误修复：
- 当某个操作返回空结果时，在 `Actuator::run()` 中填充一个默认的失败 `ActionResult`，以便在运行时缓存和回调中保留失败操作的详细信息。

测试：
- 扩展 `RunWithoutFile` pipeline 测试，发布一个失败的操作，捕获 `Node.Action.Failed` 上下文消息，并断言 `action_id`、`name`、`action` 和 `success` 字段被正确填充。

## Summary by Sourcery

Ensure failed actions always record and emit detailed failure metadata instead of returning an empty result.

Bug Fixes:
- Populate a default failure ActionResult in Actuator::run() when an action returns an empty result so failed action details are preserved in the runtime cache and callbacks.

author: sakura565-afk
body: ## Summary This updates `scripts/error_learning.py` so the error-learning log is useful for spotting repeats and judging fix quality. ## Changes - **Taxonomy**: `category_kind` is inferred from category + error text (tool, network, parse, auth, resource limits, config, workflow, etc.) with optional `--kind` override on `add`. - **Pattern detection**: `pattern_key` groups similar failures using normalized error signatures (paths, UUIDs, line numbers, and bare numerics collapsed). - **Repeated errors**: Exact duplicate adds merge into the same row and increment `occurrence_count`; `--failed-fix` / unresolved merges increment `failed_fix_attempts`. - **Fix quality**: Heuristic 0–10 score (action verbs, lesson length, overlap with error, resolution, recurrence, penalty for failed fix attempts); shown in `list` and folded into `search` ranking. - **Trends**: New `trends` command (day/week buckets) with top kinds per bucket and a simple trajectory label (improving / stable / worsening). - **Patterns**: New `patterns` command rolls up occurrences by `pattern_key`. - **Stats**: Enriched with inferred-kind breakdown (weighted by occurrences), hot patterns, and weekly trajectory. - **Persistence**: `save_store` retries on transient OS errors; schema bumped to v2 with automatic migration when loading older logs. ## Testing `python3 -m unittest tests.test_error_learning -v`

author: fabnak
body:
## Summary

Implements Phase 2 for the Sourcing Analyzer Center backend/MCP connector contract surface.

- Adds conceptual MCP tool contracts for `create_sourcing_job`, `get_sourcing_job_status`, and `get_sourcing_job_results`.
- Adds Zod domain schemas/types for supplier item input, job creation, job status, job results, and job status enum.
- Adds internal `POST /jobs`, `GET /jobs/:jobId`, and `GET /jobs/:jobId/results` routes backed by an isolated deterministic in-memory Phase 2 store.
- Adds standardized JSON error responses for validation and not-found cases.
- Fixes log payload sanitization so `Error` fields preserve `name`, redacted `message`, redacted `stack`, and sanitized `cause` while retaining circular-reference protection and secret redaction.
- Addresses Codex Review P1 by redacting sensitive string patterns before serializing `Error.message`, `Error.stack`, string `Error.cause`, and regular string payload values.

Closes #5.

## Phase Boundaries

This PR intentionally does not implement MCP runtime registration, Amazon SP-API calls, Keepa calls, D1 persistence, Queue, Durable Objects, CSV/XLSX parsing, ROI/profit calculations, exports, frontend, dashboard, landing page, upload UI, or admin UI.

The in-memory job store is temporary and isolated so it can be replaced by D1 in a future phase without changing the route contract.

author: boosterchile
body:
## Problema

`https://app.boosterchile.com` queda en blanco con "Cargando...". Consola del navegador:

```
[env] Invalid environment configuration
Error: Invalid env — check VITE_* vars in .env or .env.local
```

## Causa raíz

1. `apps/web/src/lib/env.ts` valida con Zod y lanza si falta `VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY`, `VITE_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN`, `VITE_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID`, `VITE_FIREBASE_APP_ID`.
2. `apps/web/Dockerfile` recibe los `VITE_*` vía `ARG` y los inyecta a Vite en build-time (correcto).
3. `cloudbuild.production.yaml` declaraba `_VITE_FIREBASE_*` con default `''`.
4. `.github/workflows/release.yml` invoca `gcloud builds submit` pasando solo `_COMMIT_SHA` — los `_VITE_FIREBASE_*` quedaban vacíos.
5. Vite construye el bundle con `import.meta.env.VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY === ''` → Zod `min(1)` falla → la app no monta.

`VITE_API_URL` sí tenía default (`https://api.boosterchile.com`) y por eso ese no rompía.

## Fix

Hardcodear los valores reales en `cloudbuild.production.yaml`. Las claves Firebase web son **públicas por diseño** (viajan en el bundle al cliente; las protege Firebase Security Rules + dominio autorizado en Firebase Auth Settings) — el rationale ya está documentado en `apps/web/Dockerfile`. No requiere Secret Manager.

`VITE_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` queda vacío: el schema lo marca opcional y los mapas en `/vehiculos/:id` y `/cargas/:id` caen al fallback "no configurado". Setear cuando se aprovisione la API key de Maps.

## Evidencia

- Repro pre-fix en https://app.boosterchile.com → console.error `[env] Invalid environment configuration` (Chrome DevTools).
- Cambio: solo `cloudbuild.production.yaml` (+14 -9), un único hunk en la sección `substitutions`.
- Lint/typecheck/test no aplican — el cambio es config YAML de CI, no de código.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI verde
- [ ] Tras merge, "Release + Deploy" workflow dispara `gcloud builds submit`
- [ ] Cloud Build re-construye `web` con Firebase config válido
- [ ] Cloud Run recibe nueva imagen
- [ ] Verificar https://app.boosterchile.com monta la SPA (no más "Cargando...")

## Notas

MR equivalente en GitLab (cerrado por cuota CI agotada): https://gitlab.com/boosterchile-group/booster-ai/-/merge_requests/46

author: blove
body:
## Summary

PR #124 ran a high-repeat (n=20) re-measurement of `S2/hypothesis/scroll` for pretable + mui and found the B2 H1 `failing` verdict was a low-sample artifact. Memo at `docs/research/2026-05-09-pretable-vs-mui-scroll-perf.md` recommended raising the repeat protocol but didn't action the downstream cleanup. This PR closes that loop.

## What changed

- **`status/milestones/2026-05-09-b2-h1-high-repeat-correction.json`** (new) — overlays the original B2 evidence with the n=20 result and `correctedH1.status = "satisfied"`. The original B2 milestone is left intact for historical reference.
- **`apps/website/app/bench/page.tsx`** — loads both the n=3 milestone and the n=20 correction. `verdictFor` now respects a `parityAdapters` set so adapters with parity verdicts get `parity at n=20 (full quality pass)` instead of being crowned. Prose rewritten: parity is the headline; the original snapshot is described as a low-sample artifact.
- **`scripts/bench-matrix.mjs` `evaluateH1`** — adds a minimum-repeat gate. When the pretable / best-full-grid frame-p95 ratio is in the tight zone (0.9 ≤ r ≤ 1.2) **and** either adapter has < 10 repeats, returns `insufficient` with guidance to re-run at `--repeats=10+`. Outside the tight zone the existing path still fires.
- **`scripts/__tests__/bench-matrix.test.mjs`** — new test for the gated `insufficient` case (using the actual B2 ratio of 1.115); existing failing test rewritten to use a clearly out-of-zone ratio (1.6) so the failing path stays exercised.
- **`docs/research/repo-memory.md`** — appends a 2026-05-09 entry overturning the H1 flip narrative.

## What's NOT changed

- AG Grid (16.7 ms p95, 1 blank gap, 2 px row-height drift) and TanStack (16.7 ms p95, 1 blank gap) status from the B2 n=3 runset is **not** corrected. Both are >50% above pretable, well outside the noise zone. They remain ~1.7× pretable's `scroll_frame_p95_ms` with quality gaps pretable does not have.
- No public-package source changes. Affects only `apps/website`, `scripts/bench-matrix.mjs`, status milestones, and docs.

author: mattreya
body:
This PR enhances the eBPF CPU Guardian by adding the ability to monitor file deletions (unlink/unlinkat). 

Key changes:
1. **Shared Data**: `guardian-common` now includes `UnlinkEvent` and relevant event type constants.
2. **eBPF Program**: `guardian-ebpf` implements new tracepoints for `unlink` and `unlinkat`.
3. **Analysis Logic**: The `Analyzer` in `guardian` now tracks deletions. Processes are penalized for deleting files, with higher scores for deleting documents like PDFs or text files.
4. **Cgroup Infrastructure**: `CgroupManager` now explicitly enables the `cpu` controller in `cgroup.subtree_control`, ensuring that resource limits can be applied to child cgroups.
5. **Testing**: A new `simulator` tool is provided in `guardian/src/bin/simulator.rs` to help verify detection and throttling logic.
6. **Robustness**: Unit tests were added to `analysis.rs` to verify the new scoring rules.

Agent text rows in the run-records dialog (`查看记录` / `AgentTranscriptDialog`) now show a chevron and expand for any non-empty message — not just multi-line ones. Bash/Read/etc. already behaved this way; text was the odd one out because `hasDetail` required `split("\n").length > 1`.
- Lead the collapsed summary with the first non-empty line instead of the last, so multi-paragraph Agent replies preview the lede and the row stays stable while content streams in.
- RFC posted on [MUL-1912](https://multica.ai) and approved before implementing.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @multica/views typecheck` clean
- [x] `pnpm --filter @multica/views test` — 330 tests, all pass

author: copilot
body:
## Summary

Adds `crates/use-catalan` as a new direct crate under the `use-math` workspace, providing exact Catalan number primitives in `u128` with no external dependencies.

## Changes

### New crate: `crates/use-catalan/`

**Public API:**

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| `catalan(n: u32) -> Option<u128>` | Recurrence-based checked computation of C(n) |
| `catalan_by_binomial(n: u32) -> Option<u128>` | Closed-form binomial formula C(2n,n)/(n+1) |
| `catalan_recursive(n: u32) -> Option<u128>` | Direct recurrence entry point (same recurrence as `catalan`) |
| `catalan_sequence(count: usize) -> Option<Vec<u128>>` | First `count` Catalan numbers as a `Vec` |
| `is_catalan_number(value: u128) -> bool` | Membership test against the Catalan sequence |
| `CatalanSequence` | Iterator yielding Catalan numbers, stopping cleanly before `u128` overflow |

**Implementation details:**
- All arithmetic is exact integer arithmetic (`u128`)
- GCD-based factor cancellation keeps intermediate values small
- `None` returned on overflow — no panics, no floating-point
- 70 Catalan numbers fit in `u128` (C(0)=1 through C(69)); C(70) overflows
- No external dependencies

**Tests (26 total — all pass):**
- Unit: known values C(0)–C(10), overflow boundary, sequence, membership, binomial/recursive agreement, iterator count
- Integration: `catalan_basics.rs` covers the public API surface
- Doc-tests: all 10 inline examples verified

### Updated files
- `Cargo.toml` — added `crates/use-catalan` to workspace members
- `README.md` — updated crate count badge, crate table, and project structure

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all --check` ✅
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` ✅
- `cargo test --workspace` ✅ (26 new tests, all passing)
- CodeQL scan: 0 alerts ✅

## Deferred follow-ups

- `use-fuss-catalan` — Fuss-Catalan number generalization
- `use-hyper-catalan` — hyper-Catalan extensions
- `use-geode` — Geode logic (may use `use-catalan` primitives)
- Exact rational coefficient support
- Generating function helpers

body:
## Summary
- 試合結果削除時の 404 をクライアント側で成功扱いに変更し、404 連打ループを解消
- `isAxios404` / `invalidateGameResultRelated` ヘルパーを新規追加し、削除/作成系の invalidate 漏れを解消

## Background
モバイル Sentry [BUZZBASE-MOBILE-8](https://0dd1e9c639d9.sentry.io/issues/BUZZBASE-MOBILE-8) で 9 users / 22 events の AxiosError 404 が観測されていた。Breadcrumb を読むと、ユーザーが「削除に失敗しました」アラートを見て**短時間に連打**しており（user 1447 は 1 分内に 5 回）、クライアント側のキャッシュやナビゲーション params に削除済みの `game_result_id` が残ったまま再操作する経路で 404 を踏み続けていた。

サーバ側冪等化（buzzbase_back PR #196）と合わせて、クライアント側でも 404 を成功扱いにすることでループを断つ。

## Changes
### 新規ヘルパー
- `utils/axiosError.ts`: `isAxios404(error)` で AxiosError + status 404 を判定
- `utils/queryInvalidation.ts`: `invalidateGameResultRelated(queryClient)` で `gameResults` / `userGameResults` / `filteredGameResults` / `filteredUserGameResults` / `dashboard` / `profile` を一括 invalidate

### 削除画面修正
- `app/game-result-detail.tsx` / `app/(tabs)/(game-results)/[id].tsx`:
  - 404 は成功扱い（router.back + invalidate）
  - それ以外のみ Sentry.captureException + Alert
- `app/(game-record)/summary.tsx`: 試合記録完了時の invalidate もヘルパーに統一（個別の queryKey 列挙を削除）

## Test plan
- [x] `yarn typecheck`
- [x] `yarn lint`（既存の警告のみ、新規 issue なし）
- [ ] iOS Simulator で実機検証（試合詳細 → 削除 → 一覧から消える / 既に削除済みの id を強制的に渡しても 404 アラートが出ず一覧に戻る）
- [ ] バックエンド PR とセットでステージングデプロイ後に Sentry 監視

##### What's Changed

In addition to fixes and general enhancements this release adds support for exciting nats-server 2.14 JetStream features.

\[JETSTREAM]

- FEAT: message schedules — messages fire on cron — **requires nats-server 2.14+** ([#​381](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.js/issues/381)) by [@​aricart](https://redirect.github.com/aricart)
- FEAT: `resetConsumer()`/`reset()` on `JetStreamManager` — reset durable consumer ack sequence; enables order consumers backed by durables — **requires nats-server 2.14+** ([#​391](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.js/issues/391)) by [@​aricart](https://redirect.github.com/aricart)
- FIX: push consumers stuck on heartbeat ([#​375](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.js/issues/375)) by [@​aricart](https://redirect.github.com/aricart)
- FEAT: `JetStreamAccountStats`/`JetStreamApiStats` — add `reserved_memory`, `reserved_storage`, `inflight`; `max_bytes_required` is boolean; tiers use dynamic record ([#​376](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.js/issues/376)) by [@​aricart](https://redirect.github.com/aricart)
- FEAT: fast ingest — exposed via [orbit fastingest](https://redirect.github.com/synadia-io/orbit.js/tree/main/fastingest) — **requires nats-server 2.14+** ([#​379](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.js/issues/379)) by [@​aricart](https://redirect.github.com/aricart)
- FEAT: configure stream mirror/source consumers — `StreamSource.consumer`, `StreamConsumerSource`, `AckPolicy.FlowControl` — **requires [nats-server 2.14+](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/releases/tag/v2.14.0)** ([#​399](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.js/issues/399)) by [@​aricart](https://redirect.github.com/aricart)

\[KV]

- FIX: KV `create` passes `markerTTL` via `_put` ([#​367](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.js/issues/367)) by [@​Bre77](https://redirect.github.com/Bre77)

\[OBJ]

- FEAT: faster entry add via fast ingest (**requires nats-server 2.14+**); native SHA-256 when available.
