author: dawg2004
body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a complete automated posting system for the LUXEWAVE X account, featuring Claude AI-powered content generation, scheduled posting, and a comprehensive brand style guide.

## Key Changes

- **Style Guide (`style_prompt.md`)**: Comprehensive brand guidelines defining the LUXEWAVE voice as 70% science / 30% wellness-intuition, with specific rules for tone, structure, and prohibited content. Establishes the 3-tweet thread format (Hook → Explanation → CTA).

- **Content Generator (`generator.py`)**: Claude API integration that generates 3-tweet threads based on randomly selected topics from weighted categories. Validates output against character limits and enforces JSON schema compliance.

- **Posting System (`poster.py`)**: Tweepy-based Twitter API client that posts generated threads as reply chains. Includes dry-run mode for testing without publishing.

- **Scheduler (`scheduler.py`)**: Daily job scheduler using the `schedule` library to post at a configurable time (default 08:00).

- **Main Entry Point (`main.py`)**: CLI application supporting multiple modes:
  - `--now`: Execute immediately without scheduling
  - `--dry-run`: Log output without posting
  - `--time HH:MM`: Custom post time
  - Default: Run as daemon with daily scheduling

- **Topic Database (`topics.json`)**: 30 pre-curated topics across 3 weighted categories (Threat 40%, Lifestyle Hack 35%, Wellness 25%) covering electromagnetic wave science and practical mitigation strategies.

- **Configuration Files**: `.env.example` for API credentials and `requirements.txt` with dependencies (anthropic, tweepy, python-dotenv, schedule).

## Implementation Details

- All tweets are validated to stay within 140 characters
- Claude is instructed to return only JSON output with no markdown formatting
- Thread posts maintain reply relationships via `in_reply_to_tweet_id`
- 2-second delay between tweet posts to avoid rate limiting
- Comprehensive logging to both stdout and `autopost.log`
- Error handling with graceful scheduler continuation on failures

### Fix TimescaleDB JDBC URL validation for MainUI and backend handling

This PR fixes #20676 by removing the overly strict URL UI context and by making backend URL handling more robust.

#### What changed
- Removed the URL context from the TimescaleDB URL config parameter so MainUI no longer enforces http/https URL validation for this JDBC field.
- Added backend normalization so both variants are accepted:
  - jdbc:postgresql://host:port/db
  - postgresql://host:port/db
- If the JDBC prefix is missing for PostgreSQL URLs, it is added automatically before datasource initialization.
- Reworked the bundle config regression test to use structural XML parsing instead of brittle string matching.
- Updated TimescaleDB documentation to clarify accepted URL formats.

body:
Adds SSZ support for the Engine API types needed by the EIP-8178 binary transport.

This implements SSZ for the existing forkchoice and payload response types, adds `PayloadId` SSZ support, and implements `PayloadAttributes` SSZ directly on the existing superset type. The payload attributes codec emits the V1/V2/V3/V4 SSZ layout from the existing optional fork fields and decodes by the fixed-section/withdrawals offset defined by the consensus-layer container layout.

This lets downstream Engine API SSZ transports use alloy types directly instead of carrying local proxy structs for these consensus-layer wire shapes.

author: hannahmarks
body:
**Stacked on top of [#20](https://github.com/HannahMarks/freetime/pull/20)** so the diff here only shows the new edit + FAB-color work. After #20 merges, I'll re-target this PR to \`main\` (the diff stays the same).

Two of the four items from Hannah's editing wishlist (the rest are in queued PRs F/G/H — multi-day events, recurrence, friend invites).

## Edit existing items

- Tap any of your own busy_blocks or unavailable_days on the day timeline → action sheet titled by the item label, with **Cancel / Edit / Delete** (was: just Cancel / Delete).
- **Edit** reuses \`AddItemSheet\` pre-filled with the item's current title and times. Heading flips from "Add to your day" to "Edit"; the kind toggle hides (you can't switch a busy_block to an unavailable_day — delete + re-add).
- Save calls \`updateBusyBlock\` / \`updateUnavailableDay\` (new actions) and refetches the month so changes appear immediately.

## FAB in your color

- The bottom-right "+" button now uses the current user's profile color as its background (was: dark gray). Falls back to dark gray while the profile is loading or absent.
- Required extending \`lib/auth.tsx\` to also fetch the calling user's \`profiles\` row. \`AuthContext\` now exposes \`profile\` alongside \`session\`, plus a \`refreshProfile()\` callback for future "edit my display name" flows.

## Files

| Path | Notes |
|---|---|
| \`lib/auth.tsx\` | AuthContext extended with \`profile\` (\`{ id, display_name, color }\`) and \`refreshProfile()\`. Profile is fetched whenever the session user id changes. |
| \`lib/availability-actions.ts\` | New \`updateBusyBlock\` + \`updateUnavailableDay\` actions, mirroring the create variants but going through \`.update().eq(...)\`. Same \`{ error }\` return shape. |
| \`components/AddItemSheet.tsx\` | Accepts optional \`editing\` prop. When set: prefills title + times, hides the kind toggle, and routes save through the update path. Reset effect handles both "open with editing" and "open with editing: null". |
| \`app/(app)/calendar.tsx\` | Action sheet now offers Edit before Delete; Edit sets \`editing\` and opens the sheet. FAB applies \`profile.color\` inline. New \`closeAddSheet()\` clears editing. |

## Tests (10 new — suite total **155 passing across 16 files**)

| File | New | What |
|---|---|---|
| \`__tests__/availability-actions.test.ts\` | 3 | \`updateBusyBlock\` builds the right \`update\` payload + \`eq('id')\` filter; error path; \`updateUnavailableDay\` uses the composite (user_id, date) filter. |
| \`__tests__/AddItemSheet.test.tsx\` | 5 (under \`edit mode\`) | Heading reads "Edit"; kind toggle hidden in edit mode; prefill from busy_block; save routes through \`updateBusyBlock\` (not create); prefill + save for unavailable_day. |
| \`__tests__/calendar.test.tsx\` | 2 (under \`add + delete flows\`) | FAB uses \`profile.color\` background; tapping "Edit" on the action sheet opens \`AddItemSheet\` with the prefilled item. |
| \`__tests__/index.test.tsx\` | mock fix | useAuth mocks updated for the new AuthContextValue shape. |

## Architectural choices worth flagging

- **Kind toggle hidden in edit mode** rather than disabled. A busy_block and an unavailable_day are different rows in different tables — switching kinds would mean delete-and-recreate, which is more confusing than just telling the user to delete and re-add.
- **Profile fetch in AuthProvider** rather than as an ad-hoc hook in CalendarScreen. Single source of truth, available to any future screen that wants to know "who am I" beyond the auth user id (sign-out button styling, profile editing screen, etc.).
- **No optimistic updates on edit** — same as for delete. Refetch after save is cheap and keeps state simple.

## Out of scope (queued)

- **PR F**: multi-day events (date pickers + render across days).
- **PR G**: recurring events (schema migration + recurrence rule + query expansion).
- **PR H**: invite friends (full event/invite schema, kicks off Phase 2).

## Test plan

- [ ] CI Tests workflow goes green (155 tests).
- [ ] Manual: tap an existing block → action sheet → Edit → modify → Save → block updates on the timeline.
- [ ] Manual: FAB displays in your profile color.

author: rehanmollick
body:
## What this fixes

**Line non-uniformity**: \`MetroTrack.tsx\` had a hardcoded \`STATION_LAYOUT\` array with per-station shifts (\`-60, +40, -30\`) tuned for the old 7-project order. With 10 projects in a different order now, those shifts were applied to the wrong projects, causing aggressive line jogs and inconsistent card placement.

Replaced with \`layoutFor(i)\`: every station alternates sides cleanly with shift=0. The line stays a straight vertical track; the visual rhythm comes from the alternating L/R card placement, not from jogs that can collide with station-sign plaques. Works for any project count.

## What this adds

\`<BottomGlow />\` — fixed-position radial-gradient at the bottom 32vh of the viewport, only on home (\`/\`). Subtle burnt-orange wash so the page always carries a slight warm bottom edge. Below the modal layer (\`z-index 5\` vs modal \`200\`), so bulletin / lightbox overlays cover it cleanly when open.

author: shydenmcm
body:
## Summary
`SITE_BASE` and `API_BASE` used unconditional `|| 'https://shytalk...'` and `|| 'https://api.shytalk...'` fallbacks. If either env var was unset on dev / local (env-loading glitch, missing `.env`, fresh shell), every roadmap-suggestion email would emit **PROD URLs** in:
- `List-Unsubscribe` header (one-click unsubscribe per RFC 8058)
- "View suggestion" CTAs (5+ template variants)

A developer clicking unsubscribe in a dev test email would unsubscribe their **PROD account** from suggestion notifications — silent cross-environment data flow violating the strict env-isolation rule.

## Fix
Replaced unconditional prod fallbacks with env-aware single-line ternaries:
- `NODE_ENV=production` → prod URLs
- `NODE_ENV=local` → localhost URLs (matches Mailpit-captured emails the dev actually clicks)
- otherwise → dev URLs

Explicit `SITE_BASE_URL` / `API_BASE_URL` overrides still win. Kept on one line each (`prettier-ignore`) so the pre-commit URL-isolation guard sees the localhost fallback alongside the prod URL.

Mirrors the env-aware ladder already in `routes/data-export.js`.

## Test plan
- [x] 4 new regression tests in `tests/utils/suggestion-email-templates.test.js` — `jest.isolateModules` reloads the module under each NODE_ENV scenario, asserts: (1) prod fallback when `NODE_ENV=production`, (2) **localhost** fallback when `NODE_ENV=local` (NOT prod), (3) dev fallback when `NODE_ENV` undefined (NOT prod), (4) explicit overrides beat NODE_ENV.
- [x] All 194 tests pass (190 prior + 4 new).
- [x] Prettier formatting clean.
- [x] SonarCloud pre-push quality gate passed.

## Summary
This PR fully automates the visa site login flow by integrating OpenAI's GPT-4o-mini for CAPTCHA solving, eliminating the need for manual login. All configuration is now environment-based, removing the need to edit `main.py`.

## Key Changes

- **Automated Login & CAPTCHA**: Script now uses provided credentials and GPT-4o-mini to automatically handle login and CAPTCHA solving instead of requiring manual intervention
- **Environment-based Configuration**: Moved all hardcoded settings from `main.py` to `.env` file:
  - `LOCATION_NAME` (consulate selection)
  - `BOOKING_ENABLED`, `EARLIEST_DATE_STR`, `LATEST_DATE_STR`, `DRY_RUN`, `KEEP_BROWSER_OPEN_ON_EXIT` (booking settings)
  - New: `VISA_USERNAME`, `VISA_PASSWORD`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and optional `SECURITY_A1/A2/A3` for security questions
- **Documentation Updates**: 
  - Updated README to reflect automated login flow and new configuration approach
  - Clarified that visible browser is still required to avoid headless detection
  - Updated "How It Works" section to describe automatic login and API-based date retrieval
  - Updated disclaimer to reflect new capabilities
  - Synchronized Chinese README with English version

## Implementation Details

- Configuration now reads from environment variables with sensible defaults

body:
## Why

Codex's plugin spec ([codex-rs/skills/.../plugin-json-spec.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/skills/src/assets/samples/plugin-creator/references/plugin-json-spec.md)) requires repo-rooted plugins to live at \`<repo-root>/plugins/<plugin-name>/\` with the marketplace source path referencing that subfolder:

\`\`\`json
{
  "source": { "source": "local", "path": "./plugins/<plugin-name>" }
}
\`\`\`

PR #4 set our path to \`"."\` thinking the marketplace root could double as the plugin root. It can't — Codex's discovery scans for plugins inside subfolders, so \`"."\` produced **0 plugins** in the Marketplace tab and nothing in the Plugins tab.

## What

Restructure to match the spec exactly. All plugin assets move from repo root into \`plugins/armorcodex/\`:

\`\`\`
armorCodex/
├── README.md, install_armorcodex.sh        ← unchanged
├── .agents/plugins/marketplace.json        ← marketplace metadata, stays at root
├── .codex-plugin/marketplace.json          ← mirror, stays at root
└── plugins/armorcodex/                      ← NEW: the plugin
    ├── .codex-plugin/plugin.json
    ├── .codex/hooks.json
    ├── .mcp.json
    ├── scripts/, assets/, tests/, hooks/
    └── package.json, package-lock.json
\`\`\`

author: spectual
body:
## Motivation

`TemplateManager` opens user-supplied chat/completion template files without specifying an encoding:

- `_load_jinja_template` — `python/sglang/srt/managers/template_manager.py:267`
- `_load_json_chat_template` — `python/sglang/srt/managers/template_manager.py:285`
- `_load_json_completion_template` — `python/sglang/srt/managers/template_manager.py:314`

On platforms whose default text encoding is not UTF-8 (notably Windows, where `locale.getpreferredencoding()` is typically `cp1252` or `gbk`), templates that contain non-ASCII characters fail to load with a `UnicodeDecodeError`. This is a common situation in practice — templates with Chinese/CJK system prompts, multilingual instructions, or special tokens with non-ASCII bytes are widely used.

## Modifications

Add `encoding="utf-8"` to the three `open()` calls in `template_manager.py`. This matches the convention already used elsewhere in the codebase, e.g.:

- `python/sglang/auto_benchmark_lib.py` — many `open(..., encoding="utf-8")` calls
- `python/sglang/srt/compilation/backend.py:85` — config cache
- `python/sglang/check_env.py:359` — version file
- `python/sglang/srt/speculative/cpp_ngram/external_corpus.py:26` — corpus reader

## Accuracy Tests

No behavior change for ASCII-only template files. For non-ASCII templates that previously failed on Windows, loading now succeeds.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

N/A — read-time encoding fix; no runtime hot-path impact.

body:
## Summary
- The Gram-Schmidt step computed the exact `u_k` from the projection formula but immediately rescaled it to a clean integer vector, so the displayed vector was proportional to — not equal to — what the formula said.
- Now each orthogonalization step shows: the formula, the exact `u_k` (with fractions) written as `factor × integer-vector`, then a "Dropping the scalar factor" line giving the final integer `u_k` that subsequent steps use.
- Projection is invariant under scaling, so the orthogonal/orthonormal results are unchanged numerically; only the display now tells the truth.
- Also dropped the silent gcd-simplification inside `vectorToLatex` so user input vectors and the new `u_true` line render exactly as given instead of being quietly divided by their numerator gcd.

## Test plan
- [ ] Load Example (3×3 `[[1,1,0],[1,0,1],[0,1,1]]`) and verify the formula `u_2 = v_2 − (1/2) u_1` is followed by `u_2 = [1/2, −1/2, 1]ᵀ = (1/2) · [1, −1, 2]ᵀ` and then `u_2 = [1, −1, 2]ᵀ`.
- [ ] Same for `u_3`: `[−2/3, 2/3, 2/3]ᵀ = (2/3) · [−1, 1, 1]ᵀ` → `u_3 = [−1, 1, 1]ᵀ`.
- [ ] Confirm the orthonormal basis at the top is unchanged (1/√2, 1/√6, 1/√3 scalars with the clean integer vectors).
- [ ] If user enters a vector like `(2, 4, 6)` directly, it should display as `(2, 4, 6)`, not silently be reduced to `(1, 2, 3)`.

## Prompt Given

Fix preview workflow (8e349468-9ea1-4cb7-8d04-41c90055b8c3)

**Root cause:** Two new dependencies (`@circleci/circleci-config-sdk@^0.12.5` and `chunk@^0.0.3`) were added to `package.json` but the `pnpm-lock.yaml` lockfile was not updated to reflect these additions. CI runs with `frozen-lockfile` by default, causing `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE` in both `lint-and-test` and `build-functions` jobs.

**Fix approach:** Ran `pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile` locally to regenerate the lockfile with the correct package resolutions for the two new dependencies. Also reverted an invalid entry (`'@firebase/util': set this to true or false`) that was accidentally introduced into `pnpm-workspace.yaml` during the install process.

**Changes made:**
- Updated `pnpm-lock.yaml` to include resolved entries for `@circleci/circleci-config-sdk@0.12.5` and `chunk@0.0.3`
- Restored `pnpm-workspace.yaml` to its original valid state (removed invalid `@firebase/util` placeholder text)

author: richardcao06
body:
## 问题

工作目录里出现 `.claude/scheduled_tasks.lock` 时 `git status` 把它标为未追踪。这是 scheduled-tasks 运行时产生的进程锁文件，内容形如：

```json
{"sessionId":"cb3386b4-...","pid":56537,"procStart":"Sat May  9 ...","acquiredAt":1778289462891}
```

每次启动都会重新生成、每台机器的内容不同——典型的 per-process / per-machine 状态，不应进入版本库。

## 改动

`.gitignore` 加一行：

```
.claude/*.lock
```

用 glob 而不是具体文件名，覆盖任何未来同模式的运行时锁文件。继续保留 `.claude/commands/` 等需要追踪的内容。

## 验证

应用规则后 `git status` 不再把 `.claude/scheduled_tasks.lock` 标为未追踪，工作目录干净。

author: knowltod
body:
Adds a background staleness checker that fires NODE_OFFLINE alerts when a node hasn't reported in over 30 minutes, and auto-acknowledges those alerts when the node comes back online.

### Changes:

- New `alerts/staleness.py` — daemon thread that polls every 60s, fires `NODE_OFFLINE` for any node with enabled alert preferences that hasn't reported within the threshold. Uses the same alert/queue/cooldown pipeline as the rest of the alert system.
- `alerts/engine.py` — on every incoming telemetry row, auto-acknowledges any open `NODE_OFFLINE` alerts for that device. 
- `alerts/worker.py` — starts the staleness checker alongside the email workers under the existing `ALERTS_ENABLE_WORKERS` guard.

### Tunable env vars:

- `NODE_OFFLINE_THRESHOLD_SECONDS` (default: 1800 / 30 min)
- `NODE_STALENESS_POLL_SECONDS` (default: 60)
- `STALENESS_ALERT_PREF_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` (default: 86400 / 24 hr)

### Test Changes:

- `alert_type` argument now required and no longer has a default, added to tests
- `FIRE_RISK` is no longer an alert type, changed to `SMOKE_DETECTED`
- added `start_staleness_checker` to `TestStartWorkers`

author: danicajiao
body:
## Summary
- Add `ignoreDifferences` to the `external-secrets` Argo CD Application so ESO's admission-webhook-mutated defaults (`conversionStrategy`, `decodingStrategy`, `metadataPolicy`, `nullBytePolicy`) don't register as drift.
- Add `RespectIgnoreDifferences=true` to `syncOptions` so auto-sync honors the same rules — otherwise `selfHeal` would keep "fixing" the diff and the webhook would keep re-adding it.

## Why
After merging #3, the smoke-test `ExternalSecret` showed perpetual `OutOfSync` in the Argo CD UI. The diff was the four webhook-defaulted fields under `spec.data[]` — the cluster had them, git didn't. Not real drift; the webhook fills them on every apply. Without `RespectIgnoreDifferences`, `ignoreDifferences` would only suppress the badge while auto-sync continued the tug-of-war on every reconcile.

`jqPathExpressions` (vs `jsonPointers`) covers `spec.data[]` regardless of how many entries are in the list, so this stays correct for future `ExternalSecret` resources too.

## Test plan
- [x] Merge, force a refresh of the root Application
- [x] `external-secrets` Application card shows `Synced / Healthy` (smoke test will still be `Degraded` until the GCP-side `eso-smoke-test` secret exists — that's separate)
- [x] No more diff lines in the Argo CD diff view for the `eso-smoke-test` ExternalSecret

## Notes
This is a follow-up to #3. The original PR shipped the operator end-to-end; this fix removes the false-drift noise that surfaced once the smoke test was reconciling.

author: luminairprime
body:
### 💡 What
Extracted uncompiled, inline regex patterns in loops (`pass_2_link_all` and `pass_1_normalize_all`) into pre-compiled, module-level constants (e.g. `RE_FRONTMATTER`, `RE_FENCED_CODE`, `RE_MD_LIST_LINK`).

### 🎯 Why
Repeatedly compiling literal strings inside `re.finditer` and `re.match` during loops over many documentation markdown files is inefficient. Pulling them out to pre-compiled module-level constants reduces execution overhead across multiple items.

### 📊 Measured Improvement
A specialized synthetic benchmark script that repeatedly processes dummy l2 files utilizing `pass_2_link_all` was constructed.
- Baseline (current code): `~2.72s` for 100 loops
- Optimized (compiled regex): `~2.69s` for 100 loops
- The performance improvement is modest (~1-2%) because Python’s `re` module caches recent string patterns (up to 512 internal slots), minimizing compilation costs. However, pre-compiling regexes used inside heavily nested loops is a foundational best practice explicitly mentioned in the project's memory directives, preventing overhead and avoiding implicit reliance on the internal `re` module cache eviction behavior.

author: clattribe
body:
## Summary
Phase 3c expands the deterministic specialists from GET-querystring-only to **GET + POST + PUT + PATCH** with **JSON body / form body / path params**. Without this, scan_xss/scan_sqli can't probe ANY of Juice Shop's 9 must-find vulnerabilities (POST/JSON login, path-param basket, etc.) — explaining the 0/9 recall observed post-#173.

## What's new
- `_request_builders.build_request(...)` — shared request-construction helper.
- `scan_sqli` / `scan_xss` accept:
  - `method=` (default `GET` → Phase 3b shape preserved)
  - `body_template=` (dict for JSON/form, str for raw with `{param}` placeholder)
  - `body_format=` (`json` | `form` | `auto`)
- Param inference: omit `params` → infer from URL query keys → body_template dict keys → `{name}` placeholders in URL path.

## Detection logic unchanged
DB error fingerprints, reflection escape patterns, boolean-blind comparison — all response-side, protocol-agnostic. No regressions on the 28 Phase 3b tests.

## Examples
```python
# Phase 3b (still works)
scan_sqli(url=\"http://x/search?q=test\", params=[\"q\"])

# Phase 3c — Juice Shop login shape
scan_sqli(
    url=\"http://x/rest/user/login\",
    method=\"POST\",
    params=[\"email\"],
    body_template={\"email\": \"x@example.com\", \"password\": \"x\"},
)

# Phase 3c — path param
scan_sqli(url=\"http://x/api/Baskets/{id}\", params=[\"id\"])

# Phase 3c — old-school PHP form
scan_sqli(
    url=\"http://x/login.php\", method=\"POST\",
    body_template={\"username\":\"admin\", \"password\":\"x\"},
    body_format=\"form\",
)
```

## Backward compatible
Every existing call works unchanged. New args default to `GET` / `None` / `auto`.

## Coverage prediction (juiceshop)
- sqli-login → now reachable (POST + JSON)
- idor-basket → now reachable for SQLi probing (path param)
- nosqli-products, deprecated-interface → reachable
- xss-search → still partial (DOM XSS needs browser specialist; Phase 3d)

## Test plan
- [x] `tests/tools/specialist/test_request_builders.py` — 18 cases (path / JSON / form / headers / mutation safety)
- [x] `tests/tools/specialist/test_scan_sqli.py` — 6 new cases (POST/JSON, POST/form, path param, inference paths)
- [x] `tests/tools/specialist/test_scan_xss.py` — 3 new cases (POST/JSON, path param, inference)
- [x] All 157 specialist tests pass

## Summary

Wave 3 Phase A — **W3-9**: adds the `user_role_log` audit table that records every Admin change of `users.role` / `users.is_active` from the Users screen (**OQ-3 Option A**, 별 테이블).

## Spec refs

- `docs/specs/requires/requirements.md §4` — `user_role_log` schema (authoritative)
- `docs/specs/plans/wave-3-admin.md §6.2 W3-9` + §OQ-3 (Option A)
- `claude-progress.txt` — Wave 3 Phase A "4 PR full parallel" entry, OQ-3 = Option A

## Schema (line-by-line per spec §4)

```
id          uuid        PK
user_id     uuid        NOT NULL  REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
changed_by  uuid        NOT NULL  REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
old_role    text
new_role    text
old_active  boolean
new_active  boolean
reason      text
created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL  DEFAULT now()

INDEX idx_user_role_log_user_created (user_id, created_at DESC)
```

`ON DELETE RESTRICT` on **both** FKs makes audit-protect intent explicit at the schema layer (codex review confirmed: stricter than `voc_history`'s default `NO ACTION`, not a regression). Down migration drops the index then the table (idempotent `IF EXISTS`).

## TDD evidence

Failing-first → green. `backend/src/__tests__/migration-017-user-role-log.test.ts` — 7 schema-contract tests:

- file exists at `backend/migrations/017_user_role_log.sql`
- after `up.sql`: column set matches spec
- after `up.sql`: NOT NULL on `id`/`user_id`/`changed_by`/`created_at`; `reason` nullable (DDL contract)
- after `up.sql`: FK `ON DELETE RESTRICT` on `user_id` + `changed_by` (DDL contract; no `CASCADE`/`SET NULL` allowed)
- after `up.sql`: composite index on `(user_id, created_at DESC)` (DDL contract)
- after `up.sql`: behavioural — deleting a referenced user throws (pg-mem)
- after `down.sql`: table is dropped cleanly (round-trip)

Result: `Tests: 7 todo, 165 passed, 172 total` (full backend suite green).

## Codex adversarial review summary

Focus: FK ON DELETE behavior for `changed_by`, nullable rules, index correctness, down ordering, `voc_history` reuse. Verdict: **no blocking issues, ship**. Key points:

- `changed_by ON DELETE RESTRICT` justified — explicit > implicit `NO ACTION`.
- Nullable `old_*`/`new_*` matches spec (validation belongs in service layer).
- Index direction matches dominant "user-specific recent role/activity history" query.
- Down ordering harmless (DROP INDEX before DROP TABLE redundant but valid).

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck -w backend` — clean
- [x] `npm run test -w backend` — 16 suites passed, 165 tests passed (no regressions)
- [x] migration 017 contract tests — 7/7 passed
- [ ] reviewer: confirm FK ON DELETE RESTRICT vs NO ACTION choice
- [ ] reviewer: spot-check `(user_id, created_at DESC)` index direction matches dominant query

### Motivation
- Unit tests were slow because polling used real `sleep()`/`usleep()` which causes multi-second waits inside `OzonAdClient` tests.
- Make polling testable and fast by allowing a `ClockInterface` to be injected so tests can pass a `MockClock` while production continues to use a real clock that actually sleeps.

### Description
- Added imports for `ClockInterface` and `NativeClock` and a readonly `ClockInterface $clock` field in `site/src/MarketplaceAds/Infrastructure/Api/Ozon/OzonAdClient.php`.
- Appended an optional constructor argument `?ClockInterface $clock = null` (last parameter) and fall back to `new NativeClock()` when no clock is provided to preserve existing `new OzonAdClient(...)` calls.
- Replaced direct `sleep(self::POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS)` with `$this->clock->sleep(self::POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS)` in the polling loop.
- Replaced ad-hoc time reads in polling (`new DateTimeImmutable()` / `microtime(true)`) with `$this->clock->now()` and a `format('U.u')`-based timestamp for waited-seconds/timeouts and `firstNonPendingAt` updates, without changing HTTP/state-machine/retry semantics.

author: 5qtb5t9v5k-rgb
body:
## Summary

Adds the **alternative valuation** feature — an opt-in extension where the
LEAD synthesis surfaces a Greenwald-Gordon hybrid fair value alongside
Inderes' analyst target price. Sidebar toggle is OFF by default; default
research flow is unchanged.

## What's shipping

**Engine layer** (`src/inderes_agent/valuation/`)
- `engine.py` — deterministic Python valuation. Reproduces Excel
  `Arvonmääritys2023.xlsx` Data-sheet outputs (FV, EPV, GV, P/B, GM,
  Rock Bottom, yli/ali %), within 0.02€ tolerance for 10 hand-picked
  Finnish companies (laatu / keskinkertainen / tuhoutuva mix)
- `roe_selection.py` — single source of truth for the sustainable-ROE
  rule (5y median for vakaa/nouseva, min(3y_median, trend_weighted) for
  laskeva, lfy + warning for short history). Used both by the agent
  prompt (documentation) and by the parser (validation)
- `parser.py` — strict JSON validator with Levenshtein-≤2 fuzzy match
  on `*_rationale` fields (Flash Lite occasionally typos `g_ratonale`)

**Agent + prompt layer**
- `aino-valuation` subagent fetches BVPS / ROE history / current price
  from Inderes MCP and emits structured JSON
- Prompt mandates a separate `get-fundamentals` call without year range
  to fetch fresh sharePrice (yearly value is fiscal-year-end, can be
  10–20% stale)

**Orchestration layer** (`synthesis.py`, `router.py`)
- Tool-call guard rejects valuation outputs with zero `get-fundamentals`
  calls — closes the Q2 hallucination path where Flash Lite skipped MCP
  and invented company_id, price, and ROE history
- LEAD prompt has 3 distinct synthesis modes: A (toggle off), B (parse
  error — explicit DON'Ts on hand-computed Gordon math), C (success —
  4-section structure with separate Inderes / own model / comparison)
- Edge-case warnings for absurd safety margins (>100%) and
  manual-override-tuhoutuva combinations
- `query_has_valuation_intent()` heuristic gates the toggle — purely
  qualitative questions (\"selitä mistä kannattavuus tulee\") no longer
  trigger an unwanted Greenwald table

**UI layer** (`ui/app.py`)
- Sidebar toggle \"Käytä vaihtoehtoista arvonmääritystä\"
- Forces QUANT inclusion when valuation runs, so LEAD has Inderes
  target for comparison

## Key design decisions

1. **Engine is pure Python**, no LLM dependency. Deterministic: same
   inputs always produce the same Valuation. Validated against Excel
   parity tests (20 cases, 10 companies).

2. **ROE rule is the only source of truth**. Parser recomputes statistics
   from agent's `roe_history.raw` and validates the chosen ROE — agents
   can't silently mis-compute medians.

3. **Implied values are DUAL**. Gordon has 2 unknowns (ROE, g) but 1
   constraint (price). Surfaces both `implied_g` (hold ROE) and
   `implied_roe` (hold g) so users see that the gap can be explained
   by either dimension.

4. **Tool-call guard at orchestration boundary**. Prompt-level
   instructions don't suffice — Flash Lite occasionally skips MCP. The
   structural enforcement is in `synthesis._process_valuation_subagents`.

## Test coverage

- 26 engine unit tests (math correctness, edge cases, dual implied)
- 20 Excel parity tests (10 companies × {numerical match, quality label})
- 21 ROE selection rule tests (medians, trend classification, validation)
- 35 parser tests (happy path, malformations, typo tolerance, sibling
  protection)
- 10 tool-guard + edge-case warning tests
- 33 router intent-gate tests
- **146 tests total, all green**

Smoke-tested end-to-end on Sampo, Nordea, Bittium, Witted Megacorp
(loss-making → valid:false path), and various manual_override /
sensitivity scenarios.

## Known limitations (deferred to follow-up)

- 🔴 Multi-company fan-out broken: agents emit JSON arrays instead of
  single objects when the query implies comparison. Single-company
  valuations work correctly. Tracked for next iteration.
- 🟡 Toggle leakage on borderline phrasings — heuristic is conservative,
  may miss queries that are valuation-flavored without the keywords.
  False negatives are intentionally preferred over false positives.

## Deployment notes

This branch was developed locally over multiple sessions and was
validated against the live Inderes MCP. Cloud deployment expected to
just rebuild — no schema changes, no new secrets required, no
breaking changes to existing flow (toggle is opt-in).

## Summary

Mirrors the Python mutation pilot's design (#329-#333, 67/70 caught at 31 functions) for **Go-side pure functions** in \`components/threshold-exporter/app/pkg/config\`. Closes the "Go mutation testing absent" gap from my post-campaign reassessment.

## Pilot results — 12/14 caught (~86%), 2 real Go test gaps surfaced

Verified end-to-end via:

\`\`\`bash
make dc-run CMD="python tests/shared/_go_mutation_pilot.py"
\`\`\`

**Survivors are real test gaps in the existing Go suite**:

1. \`parseHHMM\`: no test passes \`h < 0\` (e.g., \`"-5:00"\`)
2. \`parseHHMM\`: no test passes leading whitespace (e.g., \`" 12:30"\`)

Both are filed in the docstring's "Latest run" section. Adding the kill-tests is intentionally out of scope for this PR — the value here is the methodology + catalog, and writing tests to fix the gaps would muddy what the pilot demonstrated.

## What's added

### \`tests/shared/_go_mutation_pilot.py\` — runner with hand-crafted catalog

**14 mutations across 5 functions**:

| Function | Mutations | Mutation classes |
|---|---|---|
| \`parseHHMM\` | 5 | Drop hour upper/lower bounds, drop minute upper bound, drop format check, drop TrimSpace |
| \`matchTimeWindow\` | 3 | Invert end-bound \`<→<=\`, invert cross-midnight \`or→and\`, swap branch condition |
| \`parsePromDuration\` | 2 | 'd' returns hours not days, drop length-check guard |
| \`deepMerge\` | 3 | Drop \`_metadata\` skip, drop nil-delete, **skip recursive merge (semantic, not compile error)** |
| \`extractDefaultsBlock\` | 1 | Return nil instead of root fallback |

**Test target is `./...` from app/** — broad enough to exercise the parent \`package main\` tests that actually cover these primitives via the lowercase wrappers in \`config_inheritance.go\`. (First run with \`./pkg/config/...\` got 1/14 caught because pkg/config in-package tests only cover scope/benchmarks. Sharper test target was the fix.)

### \`tests/shared/test_go_mutation_pilot.py\` — 34 catalog smoke tests

Cross-platform (no Go toolchain required) catalog hygiene checks. Each parametrised over all 14 mutations:

- Each \`old=\` appears EXACTLY ONCE in target file (catches refactor drift)
- Each \`fn_name\` findable via \`func <name>(\`
- \`apply()+revert()\` round-trips byte-identically
- Each \`test_target\` uses Go-package selector form

## Why a catalog smoke test (not the runner itself in CI)

The actual mutation runner needs the Go toolchain (Cowork VM doesn't have it); it runs in Dev Container via \`make dc-run\`. But the **catalog can drift** — old strings becoming stale on refactor, fn_names being renamed — and that's what the smoke tests catch at commit time, cross-platform.

Same split as the Python pilot: \`_mutation_pilot.py\` is invocation-only (no pytest collection due to underscore prefix), companion test file enforces hygiene.

## Memory roadmap status

This is **PR 3 of 3** in the revised top-3:

- ✅ PR 1 (#346): Windows test infra
- ✅ PR 2 (#347): Process enforcement (property-coverage drift lint)
- ✅ **PR 3 (this)**: Go mutation pilot — 14 mutations / 5 functions / 12 caught / 2 real gaps surfaced

After this lands, follow-on tier (still in honest-assessment list):

- **Close the 2 Go gaps** (add parseHHMM tests for negative hours + whitespace)

## Summary

Slice Z bundles three small flags surfaced during EPIC-1..6 implementation into one PR; each is <50 LOC, none blocks shipping individually.

### Z1 — K-Cont-2: status.lastLuaRecord after PDM commit
Continuum reconciler's `runSwitchover` now wraps `PDMCommit` so each successful `/v1/lua/commit` patches `Continuum.status.lastLuaRecord` (records[].body shape U-DR-1's `LuaRecordView` already parses) + `status.lastLuaRecordAt` (server-stamped RFC3339). Rollbacks re-track to rolled-back records — status reflects what PDM actually has. CRD extended with explicit `status.lastLuaRecord` + `status.lastLuaRecordAt` fields (server-side dry-run apply confirmed).

Unblocks U-DR-1's `LuaRecordView` from the empty state.

### Z2 — EPIC-1 score aggregator → U-Fleet alerts count
Added `ComplianceHandler.SovereignAlertCount(clusterID) int` — wraps existing `violationsFor(clusterID, "")` with nil-tolerant receiver. `summarizeSovereign()` reads this instead of returning `alerts: 0`. When compliance is unwired the dashboard stays green at 0.

### Z3 — Gitea PR write seam for YamlEditor flux-managed branch
- `gitea.Client.CreatePullRequest` + `findOpenPR` (typed `PullRequest` shape; 409 race re-fetches existing PR; 404 → `ErrRepoNotFound`).

Branch name deterministic per `(path, content-hash)` so re-posting the same edit re-targets the same PR via 409 fallback.

Major optimization:
- Batch1: a new special kernel `moe_gemm_batch1` can directly use `topk_ids` and `topk_weight` and there is no dependency on moe_sorting

## Summary

- Add server-side PR title check (`amannn/action-semantic-pull-request@v6` SHA-pinned) blocking non-conformant prefixes at PR check time, before squash-merge can land them in main.
- Mirrors canonical pattern in `n24q02m/skret/.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

## Root cause

Local `scripts/enforce-commit.sh` runs only at `git commit` time. GitHub squash-merge uses the PR title as the commit message and skips `commit-msg` stage hooks. Three historical violations slipped through:

| Commit | Title | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| `2bc6657` | `[SECURITY] TOCTOU SSRF in DNS Resolution for URL Validation (#96)` | bracket prefix |
| `eb398a7` | `Sentinel: [CRITICAL/HIGH] Fix SSRF evasion via CGNAT bypassing is_private check (#76)` | bot emoji prefix |
| `038dc37` | `perf: cache default_provider_for lookups to avoid O(N log N) list traversal (#77)` | perf: not allowed |

## Decision on history

Historical commits accepted as-is. Force-push amend on released `v1.4.0` tag would shift SHAs and break any downstream pinned consumer. Per memory `feedback_pr_title_check_required.md` (2026-05-09 decision).

author: ialameh
body:
## Summary

Wave 4. Operational data movement, per-capture lifetimes, ergonomic CLI search, plus a correctness fix for a UDS frame-fragmentation bug surfaced by the new larger import payloads.

### Per-event TTL

- New `expires_at` column on events (NULL = retained indefinitely).
- `capture` API takes optional `ttlMs`; `recordEvent` persists `ts + ttlMs`.
- `Storage.sweepExpired(now?)` deletes expired events; cascades to summaries / embeddings via existing FK.
- Daemon runs the sweep every 5 min by default (`SIFTCODER_SWEEP_MS=0` to disable). New `mem_sweep_expired` MCP tool + `sweep_expired` RPC.

### Export / import (ndjson snapshots)

- `Storage.exportRows` is an async iterable yielding `{ table, row }` per record across sessions, events, summaries, embeddings, supersedes, provenance, cache. Embeddings are base64-encoded for portability.
- `Storage.importRow` uses `INSERT OR IGNORE` everywhere with a count-delta `inserted`/`skipped` check — `better-sqlite3` leaks `lastInsertRowid` from prior calls so it is an unreliable signal.
- CLI: `siftcoder export <file>` / `siftcoder import <file>`.
- RPCs `export` / `import`, surfaced as `mem_export` / `mem_import` MCP tools.
- Live: 991-record round-trip; second import reports 0 inserted, 991 skipped (idempotent).

### `siftcoder search`

`siftcoder search <query> [--k N] [--json]` wraps the daemon's hybrid search and renders `#id score [tool] snippet` per hit.

### `doctor --heal`

`siftcoder doctor --heal` runs `backfillVec` to repair vec0 cardinality drift in place. Returns `healed.vecBackfilled`.

### UDS multi-frame fix (correctness)

The server's data handler called `socket.end()` unconditionally after every chunk, even when `FrameDecoder` hadn't yet seen a complete frame. Large requests (10 KB+ import payloads) that the OS split across multiple `data` events would have the connection closed after the first chunk, leaving the client with `Error: short response` and the daemon never seeing the request.

Fix: track in-flight frame count + EOF flag; only close after every handled frame has responded *and* the client has signaled EOF.

Live: import of `/tmp/mem-snapshot.ndjson` (10 KB → 991 records) now succeeds cleanly through the daemon RPC path.

### UNIQUE(session_id, input_hash) on events

Migration adds a partial dedup pass + `UNIQUE INDEX`. `recordEvent` uses `INSERT OR IGNORE`; on conflict, returns the existing event id. Eliminates the SELECT-then-INSERT TOCTOU race in concurrent backfill.

## Numbers

- Tests: **686 → 694 (+8)** — UNIQUE dedup, `ttlMs` persisted, `sweepExpired`, export-import round-trip idempotency.
- Coverage: **90.48 %** lines / 92.77 % branches / 97.13 % functions.
- Lint clean. Build clean.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` clean.
- [x] `npx vitest run` — 694 passed.
- [x] `npm run lint` clean.
- [x] Live: doctor --heal, export to file, import full snapshot (idempotent), search CLI returns ranked hits.

body:
## Summary

Adds counter-style sugar for state mutations in `onClick` lambdas:

```ddd
Button("+", onClick: e => { count += 1 })
Button("-", onClick: e => { count -= 1 })
```

→

```tsx
<Button onClick={() => { setCount(count + 1); }}>+</Button>
<Button onClick={() => { setCount(count - 1); }}>-</Button>
```

Slice 11.7 already shipped the long form `count := count + 1`; this slice closes the gap so click handlers read naturally. Mixed `:=` / `+=` / `-=` in one block all emit in source order.

## What landed

- **`emitStmt` handles `kind: "add"` and `kind: "remove"`** — same setter-call shape `assign` uses, but the rhs is wrapped as `(name op value)`.
- **Same scope rules as `:=`** — only valid for single-segment paths that resolve to a state field; nested paths fall through to a placeholder comment.

## Out of scope (deliberate)

- **Collection `+=` / `-=`** (e.g. `tags += "new"` against an array state field) — IR uses the same `add`/`remove` kinds; walker would need to distinguish array vs scalar state types and emit `setTags([...tags, "new"])`.
- **`*=` / `/=`** — not in the grammar today.

## Test plan

- [x] `count += 1` → `setCount(count + 1)`
- [x] `count -= 1` → `setCount(count - 1)`
- [x] Compound rhs: `count += step * 2` → `setCount(count + (step * 2))`
- [x] Mixed `:=`, `+=`, `-=` in one block all emit in source order

body:
## Problem
Users often need to merge multiple annotation masks into a single mask. This is especially common when using ML-assisted auto-annotations or interactive tools such as the magic wand, which frequently produce overlapping or fragmented masks. Label Studio currently lacks a native front-end capability to merge multiple masks.


## Added feature
- Feature branch: https://github.com/hua-cv-team/label-studio-merge-tool/tree/merge-tool-implementation

The tool allows users to select multiple mask annotations in the labeling interface and merge them into a single mask entirely from the front end. This functionality is currently used in our organization’s annotation workflow and has proven useful when refining ML-generated or magic wand–created masks and combining partially drawn masks. The merge functionality works for all drawn masks and any mask annotations that contain RLE information.

## User Stories
- As an annotator, I want to merge multiple mask annotations into one so that I
  can quickly refine ML-generated or magic wand–created masks.

- As a project manager, I want annotators to merge masks directly in the UI so
  that segmentation workflows are faster and more consistent.

- As an ML engineer, I want merged, cleaner masks so that the quality of training
  data is improved.

## Usage

To merge two or more masks:

1. In the annotations side panel, select (highlight) two or more mask annotations you want to combine.
2. Click the **Merge** button located above the annotations panel, next to the **Hide/Unhide** button.
3. The selected masks will be merged into a single mask annotation.

author: hitalin
body:
## Summary

#460 Phase B-4: 起動時の sinceId gap reconcile を、B-6 prefetch ジョブと統合実装する。

旧 B-6 (PR #474) は「DB に 2 件以上ある thread は skip」していたが、これだと WS 切断中に届いた新着差分が永続的に取り損ねる中途半端な動作だった。「ユーザーがその thread を開けば取り戻せる」のは true だが、開かない thread の history view 最新 1 件は古いまま。

本 PR で `useChatThreadPrefetch` のディスパッチ判定を変更:

| DB の状態 | 動作 |
|---|---|
| 0-1 件 (履歴未取得) | `untilId` pagination で **全件**取得 (B-6) |
| 2 件以上 (履歴取得済) | `sinceId` で **新着差分**取得 (B-4) |

これで各 thread が常に「過去全件 + WS 切断中の差分」がローカルに揃い、ログアウト/オフライン時でも完全な履歴が読めるようになる。

## Why

Misskey は sync token を持たないため、起動時/再接続時に client 側で gap を埋めるのが定石 (Signal/Telegram/iMessage/Element も同パターン)。旧 B-6 の skip 判定は「過去に prefetch 済」を前提にしていたが、prefetch 後に経過した時間 = WS 切断時間 中の差分は取り戻されない問題があった。

## Changes

### [`src/composables/useChatThreadPrefetch.ts`](src/composables/useChatThreadPrefetch.ts)

- `syncOne` で DB の状態を見てディスパッチ:
  - **`fullPrefetch`** (新規 helper): `untilId` pagination で全件取得 (旧 prefetchOne 本体)
  - **`sinceReconcile`** (新規 helper): `apiGetCachedChatLatestMessageId` で DB latest を取得 → `sinceId` 差分 fetch (limit=100)
- 長期切断で 100 件超の差分があっても、次回起動の reconcile で順次埋まる
- 公開 API (`prefetch(targets)`) シグネチャは変更なし、`DeckChatColumn` の呼び出しはそのまま

### `ARCHITECTURE.md`

B-4 行を「実装済」に、Status を「Phase 全完了」に更新。

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm lint`
- [x] `pnpm test` (566 passed)
- [ ] 手動: アプリ起動 → history view を開く → 既存 thread に対して `sinceId` 差分 reconcile が走る (Network タブで `chat/messages/*-timeline?sinceId=...` を確認)
- [ ] 手動: WS 切断中に外部端末から DM 送信 → 起動 → 切断中の message が cache に入る
- [ ] 手動: 完全に新規の thread → `untilId` pagination で全件取得される (= B-6 経路)
- [ ] 手動: `chat.cacheEnabled=false` 設定で起動 → reconcile も走らない

## Related

- Issue: #460
- 前提 PR: #474 (merged)
- Phase 進捗: A ✅ / B-1 ✅ / B-2 ✅ / B-3 ✅ / B-5 ✅ / B-6 ✅ / **B-4 ✅** → **#460 Phase 全完了**

author: jah-yee
body:
## Summary

Values like `61e9540` (e.g., a git SHA) are parsed as floats and become `Infinity`, breaking round-trip as required by YAML 1.2 spec.

**Before:**
```js
yaml.load('gitsha: 61e9540') // { gitsha: Infinity }
```

**After:**
```js
yaml.load('gitsha: 61e9540') // { gitsha: '61e9540' }
```

## Fix

In `resolveYamlFloat()`, pre-check if `parseFloat(data)` would produce a finite number. Explicit `.inf`/`.nan` are still allowed. All other behavior is unchanged.

## Changes

- **lib/type/float.js**: Added finite-number check in `resolveYamlFloat`

## Testing

```
61e9540 -> '61e9540' (string, not Infinity)
1e308 -> 1e308 (still finite float)
1e309 -> '1e309' (string, would otherwise be Infinity)
.inf -> Infinity (still allowed)
.nan -> NaN (still allowed)
3.14 -> 3.14 (normal floats unchanged)
```

All 64 existing unit tests pass.

## Fixes

Fixes #737

The plugin needed a premium-feeling UI while addressing functional bugs and security gaps in OTP verification, checkout blocking, and gateway handling. This PR upgrades the admin/frontend experience and tightens critical verification/blocking flows.

- **UI refresh (admin + checkout OTP modal)**
  - Upgraded visual system (gradients, shadows, contrast, hover states, table polish) for a more premium, consistent look.
  - Improved modal and dashboard styling without changing plugin workflows.

- **Feature-toggle consistency fixes**
  - Introduced shared option-state handling so `yes/on/1` toggles behave consistently across OTP, gateway, logs, notifications, and blocker activation.
  - Updated settings rendering and runtime checks to remove mismatch between saved checkbox values and behavioral checks.

- **OTP verification hardening**
  - Fixed cooldown transient keying and normalized phone handling.
  - Added max-attempt enforcement and strict OTP format/length validation.
  - Kept guest verification tied to WooCommerce session only (removed insecure IP-based fallback).
  - Strengthened user verification key derivation using HMAC with a scoped WordPress salt.

- **Order blocker correctness + security**
  - Fixed checkout phone extraction/parsing and normalization.
  - Added explicit checkout nonce validation guard in blocker validation paths.
  - Clarified combined-block setting semantics and variable naming.
  - Tightened IP source handling to avoid trusting spoofable forwarded chains by default.

- **Gateway transport security**
  - Replaced hardcoded `sslverify=false` with secure default TLS verification and a filter override hook for edge environments.

```php
// unified toggle semantics across the plugin
if (!hkdev_option_is_enabled('hkdev_enable_otp', 'yes')) {
    return false;
}

// secure default for outbound gateway requests
$response = wp_remote_post($this->gateway_url, [
    'sslverify' => apply_filters('hkdev_sms_sslverify', true),
    // ...
]);
```

🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: The MDX adapter (`packages/adapter-mdx/src/index.ts`) was using `new Function` to parse and evaluate MDX meta block objects (`export const meta = { ... };`).
🎯 Impact: This allowed arbitrary code execution if an attacker could control the MDX file content, giving full access to the Node.js environment.
🔧 Fix: Replaced `new Function` with `runInNewContext` from `node:vm` with an empty context (`Object.create(null)`) and an execution timeout to safely sandbox the evaluation. Updated `tsconfig.json` to include `@types/node` and created the required `.jules/sentinel.md` journal entry.

author: kamruj-akash
body:
## Summary

Three independent improvements that landed today:

1. **Per-profile mode** (`salary` / `expense_only`) — users who only want to track spending (no income) can flip a profile into Expense Tracking mode and the dashboard, add-transaction screen, and history filters all simplify accordingly.
2. **Unified profile switcher** — the Home chip and the Settings → Profile row now open the *same* sheet, which handles switching, editing, and creating profiles in one place. Removed ~200 lines of duplicate UI.
3. **APK size optimisation** — Expo config plugin that injects ABI splits into the generated `build.gradle` (arm64-v8a + armeabi-v7a, no x86), plus dropping two unused libraries (`expo-blur`, `expo-media-library`). Expected drop: **~95 MB universal APK → ~35 MB arm64-v8a APK**.

## What changed

### Profile modes
- New SQL: [`supabase/profile_modes.sql`](supabase/profile_modes.sql) — adds `mode` column to `profiles` with check constraint, defaults `'salary'`. Idempotent / safe to re-run. Existing profiles auto-default so nothing changes for current users until they opt in.
- `DEFAULT_PROFILE` in DataContext now seeds `mode: 'salary'`.
- `ProfileEditor` exposes a two-card mode picker (Salary / Expense Tracking) with descriptive subtitles.
- `HeroBalanceCard` accepts `mode` + `count` props. In expense-only mode it shows "Spent this month" + transaction count instead of net balance + income/expense breakdown.
- `add-transaction.js` hides the income/expense segmented control and locks `type` to `'expense'` when the active profile is expense-only.
- `history.js` drops the Income/Expense filter chips in expense-only mode (they'd be empty/redundant anyway).

### Unified profile switcher
- New: [`components/profiles/ProfileSwitcherSheet.js`](components/profiles/ProfileSwitcherSheet.js) — single source of truth, owned by neither screen. Tap any profile to switch, tap "⋯" or long-press to edit, tap "Add new profile" to create. Shows mode badge ("Salary mode" / "Expense tracking") + budget per row.
- Home (`app/(tabs)/index.js`): removed the inline `Sheet` (~60 lines), unused styles, `onPickProfile` helper, and the dead `Sheet`/`SheetHeader`/`useToast`/`hSuccess` imports. Replaced with a single `<ProfileSwitcherSheet />`.
- Settings (`app/(tabs)/settings.js`): merged the two rows ("Active profile" + "Manage profiles") into one. Removed the inline switcher Sheet (~100 lines), the `<ProfileEditor>` mount, `editingProfile` state, `onSaveProfile` / `onDeleteProfile` helpers, and unused destructured `useData` props.

### APK size optimisation
- New: [`plugins/with-abi-splits.js`](plugins/with-abi-splits.js) — Expo config plugin. Idempotently injects an `splits.abi { include 'arm64-v8a','armeabi-v7a'; universalApk true }` block into the generated `android/app/build.gradle`. Required because `android/` is gitignored and regenerated by `expo prebuild`, so manual gradle edits don't persist.
- `app.json`: registered the plugin in the `plugins` array.
- `package.json`: removed `expo-blur` and `expo-media-library` (audited — neither is imported anywhere in the codebase).

## Why

- **Profile modes** unlock a different user persona: people who don't budget by salary, just want to know how much they spent each month. Currently they were misusing the app by leaving income at 0 and ignoring the net-balance display.
- **Unified switcher** because two slightly-different switcher modals diverged in feel and behaviour (Home one didn't have edit/create, Settings one had two redundant rows). Single component = one place to maintain.
- **APK size** because v1.3.0's APK ships at ~95 MB which is ~3× larger than comparable Bangladeshi finance apps (e.g. bKash ~65 MB) and feels heavy on slow mobile data. The bundled-but-unused x86 libs alone account for ~25 MB.

## Reviewer notes

- ⚠️ **Supabase migration**: [`supabase/profile_modes.sql`](supabase/profile_modes.sql) needs to be applied in the SQL editor before users start exercising the new mode picker. Existing profiles default to `'salary'` so the app keeps working unchanged before the migration too.
- 🧪 **APK split testing**: After merging, the next prebuild + `./gradlew assembleRelease` will produce `app-arm64-v8a-release.apk`, `app-armeabi-v7a-release.apk`, and `app-universal-release.apk`. Upload the arm64 one to GitHub releases (rename to `app-release.apk` for URL stability), keep universal as a fallback.
- 🚫 **No version bump in this PR** — left for the next release commit so we can decide whether to roll into 1.3.0 or call this 1.4.0.
- The `ProfileEditor` file diff is +75 lines because the mode picker UI (a new `ModeOption` sub-component) was added inline. Considered extracting but it's only used in one place.

## Test plan

- [ ] Apply `supabase/profile_modes.sql` on a dev project, confirm column exists with default `'salary'`.
- [ ] Open ProfileEditor → toggle to "Expense tracking" → save → dashboard hero changes to "Spent this month" + count.
- [ ] In expense-only mode, open add-transaction → no income/expense segment shown, type locked to expense.
- [ ] In expense-only mode, open history → no Income/Expense chips, only All / This month / Last month.
- [ ] Toggle back to Salary mode → all original UI returns.
- [ ] Tap profile chip on Home → switcher opens. Tap "⋯" on a row → editor opens. Save edits → list refreshes.
- [ ] Tap "Add new profile" → editor opens blank → save → auto-switches to new profile, sheet closes.
- [ ] Settings → Profile row shows active profile name + count, opens the same switcher.
- [ ] After next `expo prebuild --clean`, inspect `android/app/build.gradle` — should contain the `splits.abi` block.
- [ ] After `./gradlew assembleRelease`, three APKs in `outputs/apk/release/`. Install `app-arm64-v8a-release.apk` on a real device, confirm app launches and behaves identically.

author: homenshum
body:
## Summary

Second of three P0s in the user's editorial-home sprint loop directive
("go with all of them loop again and again until all done").

Today, every guest visiting `/redesign` sees §1 "What moved today" as
literally `"No pulse generated yet today."`. HONEST_STATUS-correct, but
the editorial-as-default landing reads as mostly empty for a fresh
visitor. This PR adds a public-trending fallback sourced from
`industryUpdates` (cron-fed every morning, already public), labelled
explicitly so the affordance is honest about provenance.

## Diagnostic

- **Symptom**: guests see "No pulse generated yet today." with no
  recovery affordance.
- **Why**: `getTodayPulse` returns `[]` for guests by design, then the
  surface's literal empty state kicks in.
- **Why is the substrate not surfaced**: the daily content pipeline
  (`convex/workflows/dailyLinkedInPost.ts`, populating
  `dailyBriefSnapshots` + `industryUpdates`) was the very thing the
  redesign spec §0 called the "ai-2027-shaped substrate." The pulse
  query just wasn't wired to it.

## Fix

| Layer | Change |
|---|---|
| Backend | `getTodayPulse` returns `provenance: "user" \| "public-trending" \| "empty"` and falls back to up to **5** rows from `industryUpdates.by_scanned_at` desc when the user has no pulse. When `industryUpdates` is also empty, returns `provenance: "empty"` honestly. |
| Hook | `useTodayPulse` re-exports the provenance type. |
| Surface | `WhatMovedSection` renders a `Public · trending` terracotta badge + lead-in ("You haven't run a pulse today. Here's what's trending publicly.") when provenance is `public-trending`. Entity-line meta says `· trending` instead of fabricating a change count. |
| Section | `EditorialSection` accepts arbitrary `data-*` attrs so §1 can carry `data-provenance`. |
| Tests | Scenario I (guest §1 shows trending fallback or honest empty). |

The fallback's `summaryMarkdown` is the provider's actual title +
summary verbatim — no fabricated narrative. `changeCount = 1`,
`materialChangeCount = 0` for trending rows because we cannot honestly
claim a public update is "material" to any owner.

## 8-point reliability checklist

| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| BOUND | `PULSE_FALLBACK_MAX = 5` with `.take(5)` |
| HONEST_STATUS | 3-state provenance enum, `empty` literal when both sources empty |
| HONEST_SCORES | counts are real (1 update = 1 change, 0 material), summary comes from provider field |
| TIMEOUT | n/a (Convex-managed) |
| SSRF | n/a (no fetch added) |
| BOUND_READ | n/a (no external HTTP) |
| ERROR_BOUNDARY | preserved (`EditionErrorBoundary` wraps §1) |
| DETERMINISTIC | `by_scanned_at` desc is stable |

## Scenario I anatomy

- **User**: Anonymous guest (cookies + localStorage cleared)
- **Goal**: Find something useful in §1 instead of a blank "no pulse"
- **Prior state**: `pulseReports` empty for this guest; `industryUpdates`
  may or may not have rows depending on cron freshness
- **Actions**: navigate `/redesign` → wait for `data-provenance` to
  appear → branch on its value
- **Scale**: 1 user
- **Duration**: single page load
- **Expected**: §1 affordance honest about provenance; signal counts
  not fabricated
- **Edge cases**: Convex unavailable → §1 stays in skeleton (test
  waits up to 10s, won't falsely pass)

## Verification

- [x] `npx convex codegen` — clean
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit --pretty false` — 0 errors
- [x] `npx vite build` — clean (built in 9.89s)
- [ ] Live verification on prod after merge (Tier A bundle hash + Tier B Scenario I against prod)

## Test plan
- [x] Local Vitest unaffected
- [x] Scenario I locally (both `public-trending` and `empty` branches covered)
- [ ] After merge: `vercel build --prod && vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod`
- [ ] After merge: `BASE_URL=https://www.nodebenchai.com npx playwright test tests/e2e/edition-home.spec.ts`

author: jp-ellis
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to the SCSS foundation PR (#75). The derived color tokens used `calc(l + N)` which assumes a dark base color — correct in light mode but broken in dark mode where ink/semantic tokens are bright and the additions clamp at white.

- **Ink soft/mute/dim**: replaced `calc(l + 0.19–0.54)` with `color-mix(in oklch, ink 75/50/30%, bg)` — interpolates toward background regardless of theme direction
- **Border tokens**: replaced `calc(l + 0.62–0.68)` from ink with `color-mix(in oklch, ink 10/18%, bg)`
- **Semantic soft tokens**: replaced `calc(l + 0.38–0.42)` with `color-mix(in oklch, semantic 12%, bg)` — gives light tint in light mode, dark tint in dark mode
- **Surface-alt/hi in dark mode**: added explicit dark-mode overrides (`calc(l + 0.07/0.11)`) since elevation = lighter in dark mode, but the default `calc(l - N)` made them darker
- **Status pill gap**: corrected from `var(--bc-space-3)` (8px) back to `var(--bc-space-2)` (6px)

## Test Plan

- [ ] Light mode: ink-soft/mute/dim are visibly graduated grays between ink and background
- [ ] Dark mode: ink-soft/mute/dim are visibly graduated grays between ink and background (not white)
- [ ] Dark mode: StatusPill good/warn/bad backgrounds are dark tints (not near-white)
- [ ] Dark mode: borders are subtle, not near-white
- [ ] Dark mode: surface-alt/hi are lighter than the base background (elevated appearance)
- [ ] `trunk build` succeeds

body:
- 🎯 **Architecture Shift:** Separated the monolithic `processLeadBackground` execution block into discrete, domain-specific modules for I/O operations (Apollo API, Gemini AI, Email SMTP, and DB Queries). The original file now serves purely as a high-level orchestration layer.
- 💡 **Maintainability Impact:** Vastly reduces the cognitive load of `processLeadBackground`. Business logic is abstracted away into cleanly-typed helpers with minimal crossover. Future updates to the Apollo strategy or Email layouts will no longer bloat the core pipeline logic.
- 🛡️ **Risk Mitigation:** Serverless boundaries are strictly enforced. The new `fetchApolloEnrichment` helper utilizes a native 2-retry loop with exponential backoff (respecting 429 headers) bounded by a hard 10-second `AbortController`. This guarantees that long-hanging network connections will never exhaust Vercel lambda execution limits. author: dherick07
body:
## Why this change is needed

When the Phase 1b SSO code was written, Supabase's legacy HS256 signing key was assumed to be active. The implementation in `app/services/auth/jwt.py` hardcoded `_ALGORITHMS = ["HS256"]` and required a `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` env var (the HS256 shared secret from Settings → API).

**Supabase has since rotated to ECC P-256 (ES256) as the current signing key.** Any JWT issued by Supabase today is signed with the ECC key — our HS256 verification would silently reject every login attempt in production, resulting in an infinite redirect loop to `/auth/login`.

The root cause: JWT signing algorithms are asymmetric once you leave HS256. ECC tokens can't be verified with the old shared secret — you need Supabase's **public key**, which Supabase publishes via its standard JWKS endpoint.

## What changed

### `app/services/auth/jwt.py`
- Replaced `_secret() → str` + `_ALGORITHMS = ["HS256"]` with `_jwks_client() → PyJWKClient`
- Production path: `PyJWKClient` fetches Supabase's public key set from `{SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/.well-known/jwks.json`, caches it in-process, and uses it to verify ES256 (or RS256) tokens. Key rotation is handled automatically — no code change needed if Supabase rotates again.
- Test path: unchanged — `DEXFLOW_TEST_MODE=true` still uses the fixed HS256 `test-secret-do-not-use-in-prod`. All 143 tests continue to pass.

### `app/main.py`
- Removed `config.required("SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET")` from the `verify_auth_config()` startup hook — no longer a required env var since the public key is fetched from Supabase at runtime.

### `.env.example`
- Removed the `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` entry and replaced it with an explanatory comment clarifying that JWKS verification requires no secret.
- Added the four auth env vars that were missing from the previous commit (`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `DEXFLOW_PUBLIC_URL`, `DEXFLOW_ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAIN`, and the JWKS note).

### `CLAUDE.md`
- Updated the auth architecture description to reflect ES256/JWKS instead of HS256.
- Updated the required env vars list: `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` removed, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` + `DEXFLOW_PUBLIC_URL` + `DEXFLOW_ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAIN` retained.
- Updated Task 22 manual checklist to remove the "capture JWT secret" step.

## Required env vars after this change

| Var | Source |
|-----|--------|
| `SUPABASE_URL` | Supabase → Settings → API → Project URL |
| `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` | Supabase → Settings → API → anon public key |
| `DEXFLOW_PUBLIC_URL` | Your deployed domain (e.g. `https://dexflow.dexterousgroup.com.au`) |
| `DEXFLOW_ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAIN` | `dexterousgroup.com.au` |

`SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` is **no longer needed** — do not set it.

## Test plan
- [x] All 143 pytest tests pass (`PYTHONPATH=. pytest`)
- [ ] After Tasks 21–22 (Azure + Supabase config): sign in with a real Dexterous Microsoft account, verify token is accepted, verify `/analytics` blocks non-admin users

body:
## Summary

Method-level visibility reduction in the \`tenant\` module — net **1 of 8** candidates flipped.

The \`tenant\` module is a near-pure-interface module (domain entity + cross-cutting scope utility) so most of its public surface is by-design cross-package API. Bringing this in for completeness even though the net is small.

| File | Flipped | Kept public |
|---|---|---|
| \`Tenant\` | 0 | \`withDisplayName\`, \`withStatus\`, \`isSystem\` |
| \`TenantScope\` | 1 (\`SCOPE\` constant) | \`slug\`, \`tenantId\`, \`run\`, \`call\` |
| **Total** | **1** | **7** |

## Why seven stayed public

All proven by \`mvn clean verify\`:

- **\`Tenant.withDisplayName\`** — \`system.TenantDetailsController\`
- **\`Tenant.withStatus\`** — \`provisioning.TenantProvisioningService\`
- **\`Tenant.isSystem\`** — used in \`system\`, \`user\`, \`provisioning\`, \`management.web\`
- **\`TenantScope.slug/tenantId/run/call\`** — used across \`auth/ott\`, \`oauth2\`, \`observability\` (15+ call sites). The whole point of \`TenantScope\` is cross-package per-request context propagation via Loom \`ScopedValue\`.

## The one flip

\`TenantScope.SCOPE\` — the underlying \`ScopedValue<Data>\` — is internal to the class. The public surface is the 4 static accessor methods (\`slug\`/\`tenantId\`/\`run\`/\`call\`), not the \`ScopedValue\` itself.

## Verification

\`mvn clean verify\` green: compile + test + Error Prone + NullAway + JaCoCo + PMD all pass.

- [x] CI green on push

author: lucascaro
body:
## Summary

- **Slice A:** Wire existing `def.ResumeCmd` into `Registry.Revive` so daemon restarts recover Claude/Codex/Gemini/Copilot conversations the same way Restart Session does.
- **Slice B:** Capture a per-session conversation ID (Claude `~/.claude/projects/<cwd>/<UUID>.jsonl`, Codex `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-...-<UUID>.jsonl`), persist on `MetaFile`, and revive via `claude --resume <id>` / `codex resume <id>` — eliminates the duplicate-cwd collision that ⌘P duplicate (#149) introduced.

Resume-by-ID failure is fail-loud: entry stays dead with `LastError`; user clicks Restart Session to recover.

## Architecture

```
DAEMON STARTUP (after this PR)
hived → Registry.Revive(id, BootstrapSession)
          ├── load Entry (now includes ConversationID)
          ├── opts.Cmd = resumeArgsFor(agentID, ConversationID)
          │     1. ResumeArgsWithID(id, convID)  if both set
          │     2. def.ResumeCmd                 if convID empty
          │     3. def.Cmd                       no resume
          └── session.Start
```

Conversation-ID capture pipeline:

```
session.Start → goroutine polls every 500ms for 5s scanning agent's
                on-disk store; persists ID on first hit and broadcasts
                SessionEventUpdated. If no JSONL appears in that window
                (idle session), a 30s janitor on the Registry keeps
                retrying for the lifetime of the session.
```

## Test plan

- [x] `internal/agent/locator_test.go` — Claude + Codex locators, layout-missing graceful-degrade, UUID parser
- [x] `internal/registry/resume_args_test.go` — `resumeArgsFor` selection logic + Restart regression for empty convID
- [x] `internal/registry/conversation_id_test.go` — MetaFile round-trip, set-once semantics, disk persistence, full janitor integration test that plants a JSONL and waits for the registry to pick it up
- [x] `go test ./internal/... ./cmd/hived/... -count=1` clean
- [x] `go vet ./internal/... ./cmd/hived/...` clean
- [ ] Manual: kill `hived`, restart, confirm Claude session resumes its conversation
- [ ] Manual: ⌘P-duplicate a Claude session, type into both, kill `hived`, restart, confirm both revive into their own conversations

## Known limitations

- Locator wrong-UUID race: two duplicated sessions starting within milliseconds before either has written may attribute the same JSONL. Documented v1 limitation.
- Filesystem coupling to `~/.claude/projects/` and `~/.codex/sessions/` layouts. Locators return "" on layout mismatch, revive falls through to `ResumeCmd`. v2 follow-up: layout-version detection if upstream adds markers.
- Gemini / Copilot still use `--continue` / `--resume`, so duplicate-cwd collisions remain for those agents (no stable on-disk ID). Documented.
- Aider has no resume command; stays on plain `Cmd`.

## Summary

- Adds `worker_terminal` as a single canonical log event emitted exactly once on every spawn exit path (PRO-330)
- Closed cause taxonomy: `spawn_error` | `timeout` | `exit_clean` | `exit_nonzero`
- Exports `computeTerminalCause` and `TERMINAL_CAUSES` for unit testing
- 7 new pure-function tests covering all four cause branches and the constant invariants

## Context

PRO-329's worker exited without emitting `worker_exit` or `worker_timeout_kill` — the listener had no debuggable signal. This PR adds `worker_terminal` as the foundation for worker continuation logic, guaranteeing a uniform terminal event regardless of which exit path fires.

**Exit path audit:**
| Path | Previous | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `error` event (spawn failed) | `worker_spawn_error` only | + `worker_terminal { cause: spawn_error }` |
| `exit` code 0 | `worker_exit` only | + `worker_terminal { cause: exit_clean }` |
| `exit` non-zero | `worker_exit` only | + `worker_terminal { cause: exit_nonzero }` |
| `exit` after timeout kill | `worker_exit` + `worker_timeout_kill` | + `worker_terminal { cause: timeout }` |

The `finalized` guard already prevents double-emission, so `worker_terminal` is safe to add to both handlers.

## Test plan

- [x] 25/25 dispatch_listener tests pass (`npm test`)
- [x] pre-commit (prettier, eslint, secret scan) all green
- [x] `computeTerminalCause` tested for all four branches including timed-out override
- [x] `TERMINAL_CAUSES` constant tested for completeness, no-duplicates, and membership

Closes PRO-330

## Summary - stop returning legacy MiniMagick-style gallery variant URLs that crash under the vips processor - requeue ready gallery images that are missing the current vips-safe thumbnail/large variants so existing prod photos repair in the background - avoid falling back to full original images in public/admin gallery grids and lightbox; show controlled processing placeholders instead - reduce public page size to 24 photos and make the admin gallery denser at 3-4 columns on large screens with 72 images per page ## Root Cause Render logs show ActiveStorage representation requests failing with VipsOperation class quality not found. That came from legacy variant URLs whose transformation hash used top-level quality; vips expects encoder options under saver. Serving those legacy URLs caused 500s, broken admin thumbnails, broken public lightbox images, and slow page loads from synchronous variant attempts and S3 downloads. ## Testing - npx tsc -b from web - ruby syntax check for api/app/models/event_gallery_image.rb using Ruby 3.3.4 - ruby syntax check for api/app/jobs/requeue_stale_event_gallery_images_job.rb using Ruby 3.3.4 - npx eslint src/pages/EventGalleryPage.tsx src/pages/admin/EventsAdmin.tsx passes with one pre-existing warning in EventsAdmin.tsx:137 outside this change ## Notes - Full npm run lint -- --max-warnings=0 is still blocked by existing unrelated lint errors across the app.

Greptile Summary

This PR eliminates the vips `quality` 500 crashes by removing legacy MiniMagick transformation constants from `EventGalleryImage` and adding a background repair loop that requeues existing \"ready\" images whose ActiveStorage variant records were created under the old transformation hash. The frontend is updated in parallel to show processing placeholders instead of falling back to full originals. - **Backend**: `LEGACY_THUMBNAIL_TRANSFORMATIONS` / `LEGACY_LARGE_TRANSFORMATIONS` deleted; `variant_url` now returns `nil` if no current-format variant record exists, preventing any ActiveStorage representation request for a legacy digest. `ProcessEventGalleryImageJob` stamps `vips_variants_repaired_at` and resets `vips_variant_repair_attempts` on success. - **Repair loop**: `repair_ready_images_missing_vips_variants` batches up to 200 unrepaired \"ready\" images per job run, checks for the current-format variant records under a `SELECT FOR UPDATE`, and requeues at most `MAX_READY_VARIANT_REPAIR_ATTEMPTS` times before marking the image failed. - **Frontend**: Public gallery tiles and lightbox, and admin gallery grid, no longer fall back to `image_url`; unprocessed images render an icon placeholder; admin grid widens to 3-4 columns and reduces page size to 72.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the vips crash fix is surgical (removing two legacy constant sets and one fallback method), the repair loop is well-guarded with locks, status re-checks, and attempt caps, and the frontend changes only hide broken image URLs rather than introducing new data paths. The model change is a strict removal of the broken legacy paths; no existing correctly-processed images are affected. The repair loop correctly handles the race conditions discussed in prior review threads (status re-check after lock, attempt cap, batch limit). The only findings are a non-deterministic batch order and an N+1 query pattern introduced by `reload` inside the lock — both are background-job efficiency concerns with no correctness impact. api/app/jobs/requeue_stale_event_gallery_images_job.rb — the new repair loop has minor query efficiency concerns worth watching under large gallery volume.

The Inventory management layer (warehouses, suppliers, stock levels, transfers, purchase orders) had zero unit test coverage across both command handlers and query handlers.

## Added

### `InventoryManagementHandlerTests.cs` — 52 tests
Command handler coverage for the full inventory CRUD and lifecycle surface:

- **Warehouse** — `CreateWarehouseHandler` (validation, default-clearing, whitespace trim), `UpdateWarehouseHandler` (not-found, row-version mismatch, update)
- **Supplier** — `CreateSupplierHandler` (email validation, null-address normalization), `UpdateSupplierHandler` (not-found, concurrency, update)
- **StockLevel** — `CreateStockLevelHandler` (duplicate prevention per warehouse+variant pair), `UpdateStockLevelHandler` (not-found, concurrency, update)
- **StockTransfer** — `CreateStockTransferHandler` (same-warehouse guard, lines persisted), `UpdateStockTransferHandler` (not-found, concurrency); `UpdateStockTransferLifecycleHandler` covering all guards (empty ID, empty row-version, not-found, stale version), MarkInTransit (success + insufficient stock + wrong-status), Cancel on Draft
- **PurchaseOrder** — `CreatePurchaseOrderHandler` (empty order-number validation, lines persisted), `UpdatePurchaseOrderHandler` (not-found, concurrency); `UpdatePurchaseOrderLifecycleHandler` covering all guards, Issue (success + non-Draft rejection), Cancel (Issued success + Received rejection), Receive (warehouse resolution, stock-level creation, ledger entry)

### `InventoryManagementQueryHandlerTests.cs` — 26 tests
Query handler coverage:

- **Warehouse** — lookup (default-first ordering, soft-delete exclusion), page (business scoping, Default filter, page-param normalization), ops-summary (correct counts + empty state), for-edit (found / not-found / soft-deleted)
- **Supplier** — page (MissingAddress filter), ops-summary, for-edit
- **StockLevel** — page (LowStock / Reserved filters, cross-warehouse isolation), for-edit
- **Variant stock** — aggregate across warehouses, warehouse-scoped subset
- **Inventory ledger** — Inbound / Outbound / Reservations filters, variant filter, ops-summary

### Key pattern note
`GetWarehousesPageHandler` and `GetSuppliersPageHandler` use navigation subqueries (`StockLevels.Count(x => !x.IsDeleted)`, `PurchaseOrders.Any(...)`). The embedded test `DbContext` must configure those relationships explicitly with `HasMany/WithOne` rather than `Ignore()`, otherwise EF In-Memory cannot translate the subqueries.

Updated to record the new test inventory.

author: wu-sheng
body:
### Fix two related issues in the live debugger surface for unreleased SWIP-13 code

**Bug 1 — terminal MAL `output` sample shows the wrong shape in the UI.**
Operators inspecting a `histogram_percentile([...])` rule see bucket-keyed
samples (`(service_name=…, le=10)`, `…, le=20`, …) in the value column instead
of the percentile result they expect to see in storage (`{p=50}`, `{p=90}`, `{p=99}`).
Two reasons: (1) the captured `output` sample never carried the metric's actual
reading on `payload.value` — the wire only had `metric` / `entity` / `valueType`
/ `timeBucket`, so the UI fell back to rendering the upstream
`histogram_percentile` function-stage `SampleFamily`, which legitimately has
`le=` keyed samples but isn't what the rule emits. (2) Even if we add `payload.value`,
two-phase functions (`AvgHistogramPercentileFunction`, `SumHistogramPercentileFunction`)
populate their user-visible field (`percentileValues`) lazily in `calculate()`,
which the L1 streaming pipeline calls *after* the `captureMeterEmit` probe site,
so a naive `getValue()` read returns the empty pre-calculate map.

This PR fixes both:
- New `appendValue(JsonObject, AcceptableValue<?>)` in `MALDebugRecorderImpl`
  renders `payload.value` per holder type — JSON number for `LongValueHolder`
  / `IntValueHolder` / `DoubleValueHolder` (with `\"NaN\"` / `\"Infinity\"`
  string fall-back for non-finite doubles so the wire stays valid JSON), and
  `JsonObject {key: long}` for `LabeledValueHolder` (label combos for
  `*Labeled` functions, `p=<rank>` entries for percentile functions).
- Forces `Metrics.calculate()` once before the `getValue()` read. Safe because
  the function's `isCalculated` guard makes the streaming pipeline's later
  call a no-op, and cross-node `combine()` resets `isCalculated=false` so
  post-merge state still recomputes on read.

Both edits are inside `MALDebugRecorderImpl`, which is only reached from the
gated `captureMeterEmit` probe — when no operator has installed a session the
probe gate is JIT-elided on hot paths, so steady-state runtime cost is **zero**.

**Bug 2 — `recordCap` ceiling is too generous for an operator-driven debugger.**
Hard cap was `10000` records / session, default `1000`. Both burn UI page
real estate and heap (per-record JSON ≈ 10 KiB → ~100 MiB worst case per
session). Operators inspect a handful of executions, not a paginated firehose.

This PR drops both to `100` (default = hard cap = `MAX_RECORD_CAP`),
yielding ~1 MiB worst-case heap per session. Out-of-range requests still get
`400 invalid_limits` from the constructor.

- [x] Add a unit test to verify that the fix works.
  - All 16 existing `dsl-debugging` unit tests pass against the new code; no
    fixture broke. The cap-aware test (`DebugSessionRegistryTest.reapExpired_…`)
    was switched to `SessionLimits.MAX_RECORD_CAP` so it tracks the cap going
    forward instead of pinning a stale literal.
  - The MAL e2e flow now asserts `payload.value` is present and numeric on
    every terminal `output` sample.
  - Live-verified against a local stack feeding a `histogram_percentile`
    rule: terminal sample now reports
    `value: {\"{p=50}\": 250000, \"{p=90}\": 5000000, \"{p=99}\": 10000000}`.
- [x] Explain briefly why the bug exists and how to fix it.
  - See above. Both bugs are debug-only paths; fix is debug-only and gated.

- [ ] If this pull request closes/resolves/fixes an existing issue, replace the issue number. Closes #<issue number>.
- [x] Update the [`CHANGES` log](https://github.com/apache/skywalking/blob/master/docs/en/changes/changes.md).
  - Not required: this patches unreleased SWIP-13 code that's already in the
    10.5.0 changelog entry. The wire/cap changes won't be visible to any
    released version.
