body:
## Summary
- add a `codex` LLM provider backed by the local Codex CLI
- register the provider in CLI and server default LLM gateways
- document the auth boundary and add `examples/codex-workflow.yaml`

## Security boundary
RustFlow invokes `codex exec` as a subprocess and captures stdout. It does not read, copy, expose, or persist Codex auth tokens; authentication remains inside the locally logged-in Codex CLI.

The provider runs Codex with conservative defaults:
- `--sandbox read-only`
- `--ask-for-approval never`
- `--ephemeral`

author: onmax
body:
Adds the new `@vitehub/agent` package and wires `@vitehub/chat` to call discovered agents with a first-class `agent` binding. The happy path is now `defineChat({ agent: 'triager' })`, with typed hooks for input preparation, run lifecycle, custom response sending, and error handling.

The chat binding owns the chat-specific boundary: it gathers recent thread history, converts it through Chat SDK `toAiMessages()`, resolves the named agent from the generated registry, streams the agent result, and posts it back through `thread.post()`. Agent remains independent from Chat and exposes registry/runtime helpers that other integrations can reuse.

Also updates the Nitro playground and docs with a concrete chat-to-agent example so the intended DX is visible from the first screen.

author: kelvinkoko
body:
Three fixes:

## 1. Uniform touch arrows
The d-pad arrow emojis (⬆ ⬅ ➡ ⬇) and the jump emoji (⤴) render at noticeably different sizes between systems. Replaced all five with inline SVG: a 40×40 triangle for the d-pad (rotated four ways) and a chunky 52×52 up-arrow for jump. All buttons now look perfectly uniform.

## 2. Platformer jump fix
The Jump & run template was unwinnable. With `gravity=900` and `jumpV=460`, max jump height was 117px, but the first floating platform sits 120px above the ground. Bumped the jump table to `380 / 560 / 720` (≈ `80 / 174 / 288 px` max heights) and switched the template's player to `jump: 3`. The frog can now clear every platform comfortably.

## 3. Time-limit rule
Wired up the previously defined `timeLimit` rule:
- New ⏱️ Time toolbar button: Off / 30s / 1m / 2m / 5m.
- Runtime ticks down each frame, reports whole seconds via a new `onTime` callback.
- When time hits zero: if a score goal exists and isn't met → **lose**; otherwise → **win** (player survived).
- HUD shows `⏱️ N` next to score, switches to red when ≤ 5s.

body:
## Summary

Второй PR Спринта 3.4 «Заточка предметов» — поднимает persistence-слой инвентаря для будущей use-case `EnchantItem` (3.4-C) и bot-UI (3.4-D).

**Корректировка скоупа на старте 3.4-B (см. `docs/history.md` запись 3.4-B).** План §3.4.2 говорил «миграция `add_enchant_level_to_items`» — подразумевалось, что таблица `items` уже существует. Реальность (на `main = 5c21d4e`): таблицы `items` нет, последняя миграция `0020_boss_fights.py`. После согласования с владельцем выбран **Вариант 2** (только `items`, `scrolls` откладываются в 3.4-C ровно перед use-case-ом).

**Что добавлено:**

- **Доменный слой** (`src/pipirik_wars/domain/inventory/`):
  - `ports.py` (новый, ~50 строк) — `IItemRepository(Protocol)` с `async get` / `add` / `update_enchant_level`. Контракт чистый: репозиторий не видит ORM, не видит SQL.
  - `errors.py` — `ItemNotFoundError(InventoryDomainError)`, kw-only `(player_id, item_id)`.
  - `entities.py` — `ItemCategory.from_slot(Slot) -> ItemCategory` (8 слотов → 3 категории по ГДД §2.6/§2.8.1: `right_hand|left_hand → WEAPON`, `hat|body|legs|boots → ARMOR`, `ring|chain → JEWELRY`).

- **Persistence** (`src/pipirik_wars/infrastructure/db/`):
  - `models/items.py` (новый) — `ItemORM(Base)`, `__tablename__ = "items"`. Колонки: `player_id BIGINT FK→users.id ondelete=CASCADE` (PK#1), `item_id VARCHAR(64)` (PK#2), `enchant_level INT NOT NULL server_default text("0")`, `acquired_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL`. CheckConstraint `enchant_level 0..30`. Composite PK `(player_id, item_id)` — каждый каталожный предмет существует у игрока в единственном экземпляре (ГДД §2.6 «не копится»).
  - `migrations/versions/20260509_0021_items.py` — `revision="0021_items"`, `down_revision="0020_boss_fights"`. `op.create_table` зеркалит ORM. `downgrade` дропает таблицу.
  - `repositories/items.py` (новый, ~135 строк) — `SqlAlchemyItemRepository`. Зависимости: `uow`, `balance`. Категория **не хранится** в БД — выводится через `_category_for_item_id(item_id, balance)` lookup-ом в `items_catalog` + `ItemCategory.from_slot(...)` (один источник правды). `get(...)` → `ItemNotFoundError` на 0 строк; `add(...)` валидирует `item_id` в каталоге заранее (иначе `DomainIntegrityError`); `update_enchant_level(...)` → `ItemNotFoundError` на `rowcount == 0`, иначе re-`get`.

- **Тесты** (24 новых):
  - `tests/integration/db/test_migrations.py` (+5) — revision exists, chain `0021 → 0020`, файл в whitelist, `items` в expected-наборе после `upgrade head`, `test_0021_creates_items_table` инспектит схему (4 колонки, composite PK, FK с CASCADE).
  - `tests/integration/db/test_item_repository.py` (новый, 17 тестов в 5 классах) — round-trip × 8 слотов с проверкой `slot → category`; default `enchant_level=0`; `update_enchant_level` персистится / идемпотентен / `ItemNotFoundError` на промахе; `get` промах + изоляция между игроками; `add(unknown_item_id)` / повторный `add` → `DomainIntegrityError`; legacy-record `INSERT` без `enchant_level` → `get` отдаёт `enchant_level=0` (server_default backfill).
  - `tests/unit/domain/inventory/test_ports.py` (новый, 4 теста) — `_InMemoryItemRepository` стаб для проверки conformance к Protocol.
  - `tests/unit/domain/inventory/test_errors.py` / `test_item.py` (расширены) — kw-only init `ItemNotFoundError` + наследование + 7 тестов на `from_slot`.

**Локальный `make ci`:** **4664 passed / 2 skipped, coverage 95.47%** (от baseline 95.46% Спринта 3.4-A); mypy `--strict` 0 issues на 854 source files; 4 import-linter contracts kept.

**Что НЕ в этом PR (defer):**
- Скроллы (`ScrollORM`, миграция `0022_scrolls`, `IScrollRepository`) — переехали в 3.4-C.
- Use-case `EnchantItem` — 3.4-C.
- Bot-handler `/enchant`, локали, display `+N` — 3.4-D.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

Risk: **зелёный** (изолированный новый слой; никакого продового кода не трогает; ровно 0 модификаций существующих миграций; все 4 import-linter contracts kept).

Если в будущем кто-то решит грузить тестовые данные прямым `INSERT INTO items (player_id, item_id, acquired_at) VALUES (...)`, `enchant_level` без `server_default` упрётся в NOT NULL без значения.

body:
## Summary

Cycle-4 audit (`/sdcard/Download/APPROVAL_AUDIT_2026-05-09.md` §C1-c4) headline: `agentStudio.publish.decideApproval` was the highest-severity finding — it decides on publish-workflow approval steps, mutates `agsApprovalSteps` + `agsPublishRequests` + agent lifecycle state, but was `protectedProcedure` (not governedProcedure), unmapped in `action-key-map.ts`, and emitted **zero audit rows**. Any authenticated user could decide an approval with no audit trail.

The original Phase-19 downgrade comment justified the change by citing "the per-agent lifecycle state machine as the actual enforcement surface." That framing is wrong on the same axis cycle-2 R2-c2 found broken: the state machine enforces transition order, not who is allowed to decide.

## Changes

- **`server/governance/action-key-map.ts`** — register identity mapping `agentStudio.publish.decideApproval`.
- **`config/governance/platform_action_registry.yaml`** — add YAML def matching `agentStudio.toolApprovals.decide`'s shape (R2 / agent.manage / approval:none / no evidence).
- **`server/agent-studio/api/router.ts`** — convert `decideApproval` from `protectedProcedure` to `governedProcedure`. Add `getAuditLogger().log({...})` with `LIFECYCLE_TRANSITION` action type after each successful state change branch (rejected / all-approved / partial-rollup), capturing actor, target step ID, and the lifecycle effect.
- **`tests/agent-studio/governed-procedure-coverage.test.ts`** — add to EXPECTED_REGISTERED + bump router.ts per-file count 5 → 6 + update baseline 656/12 → 657/13.

## Why `governance_audit_logs` and not `agsRuntimePolicyEvents`?

`agsRuntimePolicyEvents.runId` is `notNull` and publish-workflow approvals are not bound to a runtime run. `governance_audit_logs` (via `getAuditLogger`) is the correct platform-wide audit surface for lifecycle transitions.

## Behavior change

Callers without sufficient role under `agent.manage` now receive 403 from `decideApproval`. Subject-id-0 freeze applies (per the R4-c3-known limitation: input uses `stepId` not `subjectId`/`id`/`entryId`, so middleware resolves subjectId=0 and only the system-wide freeze branch fires — per-step freezes remain L4-c4 carryover work).

## Tests

- `governed-procedure-coverage`: **29/29** (was 27, gained 2 from EXPECTED_REGISTERED expansion)
- `require-governed-action`: **13/13** (no regressions)
- `retrofit-acceptance`: **52/52** (no regressions)
- `npm run check`: **clean** (tsc + CAG boundary)

body:
## Summary

Two paper-cuts that block the canonical conformance workflow described in
`scripts/session/conformance-agent-prompt.md` on a fresh checkout:

1. **Workspace clippy was red on `main`.** PR #4714 added two
   `unsafe { std::env::set_var(...) }` blocks to a `tsz-core` test.
   The workspace lints set `unsafe_code = "warn"` and `verify-all.sh`
   runs `cargo clippy ... -- -D warnings`, so every fresh checkout fails
   the lint gate before any conformance work even begins. The blocks
   already have a SAFETY comment (nextest's per-test process isolation
   makes the env mutations safe). I added `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` to
   the test rather than relaxing the workspace policy. Reproduced
   on `origin/main` before the fix to confirm it is not introduced by
   this branch.

2. **`scripts/session/quick-pick.sh` printed unopenable paths.** The
   detail snapshot stores absolute paths captured on the machine that
   produced it — currently `/Users/<author>/code/tsz/.worktrees/<wt>/TypeScript/...`.
   The picker echoed those verbatim, leaving the `path:` line useless
   on every other machine. Now we strip everything before the
   `TypeScript/` segment when a repo root is available; the existing
   `resolve_test_source` lookup that the runner uses is unchanged, so
   `--filter` / `--run` behaviour is identical.

   Per CLAUDE.md §20.25 (do **not** create new picker scripts), this
   change extends the canonical `pick.py` instead of adding a new
   wrapper. Per the §25 anti-hardcoding directive, the rewrite is keyed
   on the structural `TypeScript/` segment — there is no contributor
   name or worktree name baked into the rule, and one of the new tests
   exercises that with a few different fake usernames.

## Before / after

```
$ scripts/session/quick-pick.sh --seed 42
- path:     /Users/mohsen/code/tsz/.worktrees/fix-export-equals-require-surface-20260509/TypeScript/tests/cases/compiler/instantiationExpressionErrorNoCrash.ts
+ path:     TypeScript/tests/cases/compiler/instantiationExpressionErrorNoCrash.ts
```

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check` — clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — clean (was failing on `origin/main` with the two unsafe blocks above)
- `cargo nextest run -p tsz-core --lib` — 3146 passed, 9 skipped
- `cargo nextest run -p tsz-checker --lib` — 3778 passed, 7 skipped
- `cargo nextest run -p tsz-solver --lib` — 5713 passed, 7 skipped
- `python3 -m unittest test_pick` (in `scripts/session/`) — 11 passed (4 new for `display_path`)
- `./scripts/conformance/conformance.sh run --max 200` — 200/200, no regressions
- `scripts/session/quick-pick.sh` — manually exercised with and without `--seed`; `path:` line is now local-relative on this machine

The full `verify-all.sh` (full-workspace nextest + full conformance + emit + fourslash) was not run end-to-end in this session because building every workspace test target with `cargo test --workspace` exhausted disk on this sandbox; the touched/adjacent crates were tested individually instead. CI will run the full suite.

## Conformance

No checker/solver/emitter behaviour change. Conformance pass count is
unchanged.

```
Conformance:
- passed: 12528 -> 12528 (+0)
- fixed: 0 (none)
- new failures: 0 (none)
- changed failures: 0 (none)
- category delta: false_positive 0, all_missing 0, wrong_code 0, fingerprint_only 0, close_to_passing 0
```

## Notes on the picked random failure

For the record, `scripts/session/quick-pick.sh` initially picked
`mixinAccessModifiers.ts` (XFAIL — known compiler debt: missing TS2509
on intersection-typed `extends`, missing TS2445 on protected static
inheritance through `Mix(A, B): T & U`, and three extra TS2339s for
static `s` access on classes whose static side does not currently
inherit from the intersection). The root cause spans the binder's
treatment of `extends Mix(...)` calls, the solver's intersection-base
resolution, and the static-side propagation of access modifiers — a
multi-day campaign rather than a single-session fix, and the test is
explicitly tagged `XFAIL` for that reason. I did not file a half-done
suppression; that would be the symptom-patching the prompt forbids.
This PR clears the operational blockers so the next agent picking the
same target lands on a workflow that actually works.

## Summary

Fixes Codex plan-mode approval parity with Claude Code. Codex plans now expose the same approval actions in the frontend, route the selected decision through the backend, and keep Codex collaboration-mode instructions synchronized when entering or leaving plan mode.

The branch also hardens stale-plan handling so only the latest undecided Codex plan can be acted on, and declined/cancelled plans stop rendering as actionable cards until Codex emits a newer plan.

## Changes

### Backend
- Added `decision` handling to Codex plan approval requests for `accept`, `acceptForSession`, `decline`, and `cancel`.
- Kept `accept` / `acceptForSession` on the existing approve-and-exit path, restoring the saved pre-plan permission mode.
- Added decline/cancel handling that keeps the session in plan mode and sends Codex a rejection prompt with any user note.
- Added normalized Codex plan metadata and backend validation so stale or already-decided plan ids are rejected.
- Render Codex collaboration-mode developer instructions per turn, with non-empty fallback instructions when vendored templates are unavailable.

### Frontend
- Added a shared plan view model that normalizes Codex plan events and Claude ExitPlanMode approval data.
- Updated Codex plan approval cards to render Approve, Approve for session, Decline, and Cancel.
- Suppressed decided Codex plan cards so the same declined/cancelled plan cannot be repeatedly acted on.

## Summary

The reusable release workflow declared `RELEASE_CLIENT_ID` as a required secret. Consumer repos that hadn't set it (tradedesk, tradedesk-dukascopy) failed at `Generate Token` with:

```
The 'client-id' (or deprecated 'app-id') input must be set to a non-empty string.

author: dannyyycodes
body:
Three Stripe-layer findings from the 2026-05-09 readiness audit.

## 1. Stop swallowing handler errors with 200

\`api/stripe/webhook.ts\` caught any uncaught handler error and returned 200 to Stripe with \`{error: <msg>}\`. The reasoning was \"don't endlessly retry on programmer error\" — but that meant a transient DB blip during a subscription credit grant lost the credit forever (customer paid £8.99, no credits, no log to replay).

Now returns 500 on uncaught error so Stripe retries (exponential backoff, ~72h). Programmer errors will surface as repeated 500s in the Stripe dashboard event log instead of silent data loss. Also deletes the dedup row from \`portraits_stripe_events\` on retry-eligible failure so the next attempt actually re-runs the handler.

## 2. Add four missing event handlers

Previously only 5 event types were handled. The webhook silently no-op'd on:

| Event | Behavior |
|---|---|
| \`invoice.payment_failed\` | Subscription card declines — flips \`portraits_subscriptions.status='past_due'\` |
| \`payment_intent.payment_failed\` | One-off pack pre-checkout failure — \`console.warn\` |
| \`charge.refunded\` | Manual refund — \`console.warn\` (no auto-clawback because tokens may already be spent) |
| \`charge.dispute.created\` | Chargeback raised — \`console.error\` with evidence_due_by date so Vercel log alerts page ops within the 7-day response window |

**Net before:** customer's card declines → we keep granting credits / printing canvas / shipping. Chargeback lands → we miss the evidence window → automatic loss.

## 3. Add USD price IDs (US sub buyers were silently broken)

\`api/_lib/stripe.ts\` only had GBP price IDs. \`priceIdToTier\` returned null for any USD price → US sub buyer charged → no subscription upsert → no credits granted. **Customer paid \$17.99/mo Elite, got nothing.**

- \`PRICES\` gains \`*Gbp\` and \`*Usd\` variants for pass / elite / pack
- New \`priceIdForSku(sku, currency)\` helper picks the right one
- Legacy \`*Monthly\` / \`pack20\` aliases kept (point at GBP) for backwards-compat
- \`api/stripe.ts\` (handleCheckout) now accepts an optional \`currency\` field; defaults to GBP
- \`priceIdToTier\` in the webhook recognises both currencies so subscription upserts work for US customers

## ⚠️ Post-merge steps

1. Set Vercel env vars \`STRIPE_PRICE_PASS_USD\`, \`STRIPE_PRICE_ELITE_USD\`, \`STRIPE_PRICE_PACK_USD\` once the matching prices are created in the Stripe dashboard.
2. Confirm \`STRIPE_AUTOMATIC_TAX=1\` is set if you want Stripe Tax for US states (currently gated, no change in this PR).

## Out of scope

Frontend currency hardcoding (\`Portraits.tsx:756 const currency='GBP'\`) intentionally NOT changed — that's a UX decision (geo-IP detection vs explicit picker) you should weigh in on. Backend now ready to accept whichever flow you pick.

## Test plan

- [ ] POST \`/api/stripe?action=checkout\` with \`{sku:'pass'}\` → GBP price as before
- [ ] POST same with \`{sku:'pass', currency:'USD'}\` → USD price (after env set)
- [ ] Trigger an \`invoice.payment_failed\` webhook (Stripe CLI: \`stripe trigger invoice.payment_failed\`) → \`portraits_subscriptions.status='past_due'\` for that sub
- [ ] Trigger a \`charge.dispute.created\` → check Vercel logs for the \"CHARGE.DISPUTE.CREATED\" error line with evidence_due_by

## Related

PR #60 (OTP), PR #61 (DB schema), PR #62 (Gelato cron worker). Remaining: generation pipeline (#18/#19/#20), brand/UX (#21/#22/#23/#24).

author: aristocles
body:
# What changed

`replayFromArchive` now processes each archived push one at a time (aggregate within a push, then `mergeByDate` the running state against it) instead of flattening all entries into a single list and aggregating once at the end. Matches the live dispatcher's semantics. New `scripts/reingest-hae.js` re-applies the fixed logic to already-populated manifests. Chat prompt gains display-template guidance.

# Why

Fixes #168. Refs #150, #160.

Caught during live QA on klebbtest with a real iPhone HAE export. With 10+ scheduled pushes, each re-sending the current day's running-total samples, replay was reporting 41,372 steps for today. Actual plausible value: ~8,700. The flattened aggregation path summed every push's contribution to today as if they were independent samples. Also subtly wrong for `mean-per-date` (mean over union ≠ mean over latest push) and `last-per-date` (last-in-union depends on iteration order, not the user-meaningful "most recent reading").

# How

### replay.js

```js
// Before (broken):
for each push: flatten entries into one list
aggregate(list) once
write

// After (fixed):
merged = []
for each push:
  push_aggregated = aggregate(push.entries)
  merged = mergeByDate(merged, push_aggregated)   // later wins
write merged
```

This is exactly what the live dispatcher does per push. End state matches "what would be on disk if this manifest had existed at the time of each push".

Added a `{ force: true }` option that bypasses the "skip if `data[]` non-empty" guard, needed for operators re-running against already-populated manifests.

### scripts/reingest-hae.js

New CLI: walks every HAE-backed manifest, backs each file up to `<file>.pre-reingest-<ts>.json`, wipes `data[]`, force-replays. Flags: `--dry-run` for inspection, `--id=<id>` to target one manifest. Idempotent.

### describe.js

Chat system prompt gains two sentences of display-template guidance: use `{field:round(N)}` for numeric values, set `view.dateContext: "latest"` on HAE cards. Both failure modes surfaced repeatedly in QA ("7.283333..." headline; "No data yet" on today because HAE hasn't pushed today yet).

# Testing

- [x] `npm test` passes locally (762/763; the one pre-existing `no-personal-refs` failure is unchanged on this branch and fails identically on main).
- [x] Existing "multiple pushes merge by date" test updated — its assertion (4200 + 500 = 4700 for same date) was asserting the pre-fix buggy behaviour. Now asserts per-push replacement.
- [x] New: "overlapping pushes do not double-count sum-per-date metrics (#168)" — three pushes each claiming today=1000/2000/2000, expects 2000 not 5000.
- [x] New: "overlapping pushes honour last-per-date correctly for sleep_analysis" — later push's totalSleep wins.
- [x] New: "force: true overrides the non-empty guard and rewrites data[]" — essential for the reingest script.
- [x] New: describe helper surfaces the round/dateContext guidance.
- [ ] Manual QA on klebbtest: pull latest main, run `node scripts/reingest-hae.js`, reload, confirm today's step count is plausible (~8k not ~41k) and sleep card shows a headline instead of "No data yet".

# Checklist

- [x] Commit messages follow CONTRIBUTING.md conventions
- [x] CHANGELOG.md updated under ## Unreleased
- [x] Docs — the reingest script self-documents via `--help`-style top-of-file comments; no user-facing doc change needed beyond the changelog entry
- [x] No personal identifiers or hardcoded paths
- [x] No secrets or high-entropy tokens
- [x] New source files carry SPDX AGPL-3.0-only header

# Breaking changes

None for clients. Replay's output shape is unchanged; the values it produces are now correct. One existing test updated because its assertion was encoding the pre-fix bug.

author: wesleysimplicio
body:
## Problem

`_get_cloud_provider()` in `tools/browser_tool.py` caches a transient `None` for the entire process lifetime. If credentials are briefly unavailable on the first browser call (managed Nous Portal access token mid-refresh, config read raises, explicit provider's `__init__` momentarily fails), the resolver pins the gateway to local mode forever, even after credentials self-heal seconds later.

This regresses #10883: that issue's PR added runtime fallback in `_get_session_info()`, but the resolver itself still poisons its own cache up front.

## Root cause

`_cloud_provider_resolved = True` was set **before** resolution. Every fall-through path returned `_cached_cloud_provider` (still `None`) and the flag was already sticky.

## Fix

Invert the bookkeeping. The cache flag is now set only when:

- The user explicitly chose `cloud_provider: local` (a positive opt-in), or
- A provider was successfully resolved (registry hit or auto-detect found credentials).

All transient `None` paths return without setting the flag, so the next call retries. Explicit-provider instantiation failures are now logged at `warning` level with `exc_info=True` so operators can see why their config didn't take effect.

## Tests

5 new cases in `tests/tools/test_browser_cloud_provider_cache.py`:

- `test_explicit_local_caches_permanently` — regression guard for the explicit case
- `test_successful_cloud_resolution_caches_permanently` — happy path
- `test_no_credentials_yet_does_not_cache_none` — primary regression guard for #22324
- `test_config_read_failure_does_not_cache_none`
- `test_explicit_provider_instantiation_failure_does_not_cache`

Stash-verify confirmed the 3 transient-`None` tests fail on `main` and pass with the fix. All 320 existing browser tests in `tests/tools/` still green.

Closes #22324

author: mvirtai
body:
## Summary

This branch brings repository documentation and the published OpenAPI description in line with the current web stack—reading plans and PostgreSQL migrations, UI language, gated AI routes, and optional docs-site URL configuration—while fixing an invalid YAML merge in `openapi.yml`. It also replaces broken in-app `/docs` footer targets with absolute links to the VitePress site and splits heavy client vendors in `vite.config.ts` so production builds stay under Vite’s default chunk size warning.

## Purpose

- Readers following `PROJECT_OVERVIEW`, roadmap copies, and architecture pages should see the same reality as `server.ts` and the Postgres schema (reading plans, `ui_language`, `ai_access`).
- API consumers and Redoc need a parseable spec and coverage for reading-plan routes and `UserSettings.uiLanguage`, without duplicate YAML keys breaking tooling.
- Users clicking “Documentation” or “API” in the web footer should land on the actual docs site, not an empty same-origin path.
- CI and local builds should not emit misleading Rollup/Vite chunk warnings when the bundle is legitimately split across libraries.

## Changes in This PR

### 1. Overview and roadmap (`docs/PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md`, `docs-site/architecture/project-overview.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `docs-site/roadmap.md`)

The project overview tables and file map now record web Postgres migrations through `004_reading_plans`, seeded templates under `src/clible-web/data/reading_plans/`, and related React/context/routes modules. The roadmap status table calls out EN/FI UI, reading-plan progress on the web, and AI gated by `ai_access`; medium-priority rows distinguish what is already shipped (saved searches/history surfaces, baseline reading plans) from follow-on work (richer query syntax, per-verse notes). Dates and backlog blurbs were refreshed so “what’s next” matches the current narrative.

### 2. Architecture narratives (`docs/architecture/overview.md`, `docs-site/architecture/overview.md`, `docs/architecture/web-architecture.md`, `docs-site/architecture/web.md`)

Overview prose now mentions reading-plan persistence next to sessions and settings. The web-architecture pages describe PostgreSQL tables for plans and progress, the authenticated `/api/user/reading/*` surface, stricter wording on what `requireAuth` covers, and a structured AI section: prerequisites (`ai_access`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`), a route table for all five `POST /api/ai/*` handlers, and response fields `text` / `nextFocus` with pointers to `extractNextFocus` and `server.ts`.

### 3. OpenAPI (`docs/api/openapi.yml`)

The spec documents reading-plan paths and schemas (`ReadingPlanSummary`, `ActiveReadingPlanState`, etc.), adds `uiLanguage` to user settings, extends the API info block with AI/admin notes, and separates `TranslationCatalogEntry` from `ReadingDayCompleteResponse` so YAML maps have unique keys (fixes “Map keys must be unique” from invalid nesting). `AiResponse` documents optional `nextFocus`; AI operation descriptions note 403 when `ai_access` is false.

### 4. Root and web README (`README.md`, `src/clible-web/README.md`)

README highlights reading plans in Postgres, UI language, documentation footer behavior at a high level, and optional `VITE_DOCS_SITE_URL`. The clible-web README lists reading plans and UI language in the feature list for operators scanning that folder.

### 5. Footer docs URLs and env typing (`src/clible-web/utils/docsSiteUrls.ts`, `App.tsx`, `vite-env.d.ts`, `.env.example`)

`docsSiteUrls` centralizes the default published docs base (`https://mvirtai.github.io/clible-v2`) with trimming and optional override via `VITE_DOCS_SITE_URL`. The footer uses `docsSiteHomeUrl` and `docsSiteApiReferenceUrl` with `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. `vite-env.d.ts` augments `ImportMetaEnv`; `.env.example` documents the variable.

### 6. Vite production chunks (`src/clible-web/vite.config.ts`)

`rollupOptions.output.manualChunks` assigns `react`/`react-dom`, `lucide-react`, `motion`, `recharts`, `d3`, and markdown/remark-related packages to named vendor chunks. A generic `vendor` fallback was avoided because it introduced circular chunk warnings between Rollup outputs.

## Files added

- `src/clible-web/utils/docsSiteUrls.ts` — Default and configurable VitePress root; exports home and API reference URLs for the footer.

## Files modified

- `README.md` — Features and architecture diagram mention reading plans, docs URL env, and AI access gating.
- `ROADMAP.md` — Status rows and M1/M3 wording aligned with shipped vs planned work.
- `docs-site/architecture/overview.md` — PostgreSQL bullet includes reading-plan progress.
- `docs-site/architecture/project-overview.md` — Done/planned tables, file map, dates, backlog reference.
- `docs-site/architecture/web.md` — PostgreSQL, reading API table, expanded AI section.
- `docs-site/roadmap.md` — Mirrors root roadmap updates for the docs site build.
- `docs/PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md` — Same substantive updates as docs-site project overview (plus existing VitePress note).
- `docs/api/openapi.yml` — Reading routes, settings field, AI/docs preamble, schema fixes.
- `docs/architecture/overview.md` — Same PostgreSQL clarification as docs-site copy.
- `docs/architecture/web-architecture.md` — Matches docs-site web architecture content where applicable.
- `src/clible-web/.env.example` — Documents `VITE_DOCS_SITE_URL`.
- `src/clible-web/App.tsx` — Footer links use external docs URLs.
- `src/clible-web/README.md` — Reading plans and UI language in the capability list.
- `src/clible-web/vite-env.d.ts` — Types `VITE_DOCS_SITE_URL`.
- `src/clible-web/vite.config.ts` — `manualChunks` vendor split without circular fallback.

## Tests

```bash
uv run pytest -v
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .
cd src/clible-web && npm run lint
```

345 tests passed; coverage total **94.36%** (gate 80%). Ruff and Ruff format checks passed; `npm run lint` (`tsc --noEmit`) passed.

## Usage

```bash
# Optional: point footer “Documentation” / “API” at your fork’s GitHub Pages base (no trailing slash); rebuild the web bundle.
export VITE_DOCS_SITE_URL=https://youruser.github.io/your-repo
cd src/clible-web && npm run build

# Confirm production chunks stay split and no default 500 kB warning fires.
npm run build
```

## Notes

OpenAPI still does not enumerate every Express route (saved searches, search history, admin, extra AI payloads); the spec and architecture pages defer to `server.ts` for the exhaustive list. Docs-site `public/api/openapi.yml` remains generated by `npm run sync-openapi` during docs builds—it must not be edited by hand.

## Related documentation

- `docs/PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md` — File map and implementation status.
- `docs/architecture/web-architecture.md` — Bridge, Postgres, reading plans, AI.
- `ROADMAP.md` — Priorities and shipped vs planned features.
- `docs/api/openapi.yml` — REST contract source for Redoc.

body:
The `SendImage` node in `nodes/telegram.py` was repeatedly calling `utils.guess_mimetype` for every image in a media group or sequential send, even though the file extension (and thus the mimetype) is constant across all images in the set.

By hoisting this resolution logic outside the loop, we eliminate redundant calls to `mimetypes.guess_type`. 

### Benchmark Results:
- **Before:** ~0.085s for 10,000 iterations.
- **After:** ~0.003s for 10,000 iterations.
- **Improvement:** ~96.6% reduction in CPU time spent on mimetype resolution.

While the absolute time saved per typical batch (e.g., 2-10 images) is small, this change follows performance best practices and removes unnecessary overhead from the image processing pipeline.

author: lucasbaziliocomercial-crypto
body:
## Symptom
StatusBar and UpdateButton each subscribed to the auto-updater IPC events independently and held their own copy of the state — they drifted apart. Typical case on macOS without code-signing where the download fails right after `update-downloaded` fires: StatusBar still shows the green '**reinicie para atualizar**' banner while UpdateButton already flipped to the yellow error icon.

## Refactor
- **`src/store/updater.ts`** — single source of truth. State machine: `idle | checking | up-to-date | downloading | downloaded | error | dev-disabled`. Tracks `lastAnnouncedVersion` so an error state can name the version it was trying to deliver.
- **`src/lib/use-updater-events.ts`** — registers IPC listeners exactly once at the `<App/>` root and dispatches into the store. Components just read from `useUpdater`.
- `electron-updater` has `autoDownload=true`, so `update-available` is the same moment as 'started downloading'. We skip the intermediate `available` state and go straight to `downloading(version, percent=0)`.

## Manual fallback (the user-facing fix)
- New IPC `app:open-external-url` (preload: `openExternalUrl`) gated to `http(s)` URLs.
- StatusBar error state now renders a **'Baixar v{X} manualmente'** button pointing to the GitHub `releases/latest` page, so when auto-update trips users still have a one-click escape hatch instead of seeing 'falha ao atualizar' with no next step.

## Test plan
- [ ] Install v1.0.12, push something to trigger v1.0.13 → both StatusBar and UpdateButton transition through `downloading → downloaded` together (no drift).
- [ ] Force a download error mid-update → StatusBar shows the rose error chip + green 'Baixar v1.0.13 manualmente' button; clicking it opens the GitHub release page in the default browser.
- [ ] 'Up-to-date' chip disappears from UpdateButton after 3s (existing behavior preserved).
- [ ] No more conflicting banners between StatusBar and UpdateButton in any state.

author: pinguuss
body:
Tightens the Linux Computer Use backend after the windowing refactor landed in #136, now focused on fallback and readiness robustness.

What changed:

- The window backend registry keeps trying later backends when an earlier backend returns an empty window list, instead of treating that empty result as final
- The i3 backend from #134 stays in the registry order, diagnostics, activation path, and tests after the rebase on current `main`
- Runtime ydotool setup now only exports `YDOTOOL_SOCKET` when the socket can actually be connected to, so stale socket files are skipped
- `doctor` reports ydotool socket connection failures with useful detail, including permission problems
- `can_send_development_input` now requires `ydotool`, a running `ydotoold`, and a connectable ydotoold socket, matching the current runtime path that still calls the `ydotool` CLI
- `/dev/uinput` stays in diagnostics as useful detail, but it no longer makes input readiness pass by itself
- `press_key` stays on raw `ydotool key` events such as `29:1 25:1 25:0 29:0`
- `type_text` sends literal text through stdin via `ydotool type --file -`, avoiding shell quoting issues without changing the `ydotool key` protocol
- Large KWin-generated `window_id` values tolerate JSON/JavaScript number rounding on the client side, while still preferring exact id matches first
- The flaky update-manager lock test was made less timing-sensitive, and CLI lookup tests no longer depend on a system-installed `codex`

What stayed out after review feedback:

- Symbolic `ydotool key` names are not part of this PR anymore
- The PageUp/PageDown keyboard-scroll fallback was removed from this PR; scroll remains on the existing portal path and ydotool wheel fallback for now

How this fits the #136 refactor:

- Backend ordering, fallback labels, and capability metadata stay in `computer-use-linux/src/windowing/registry.rs`
- Backend-specific i3 behavior remains in `computer-use-linux/src/windowing/backends/i3.rs`
- Target resolution, including the rounded large-window-id fallback, stays in `computer-use-linux/src/windowing/target.rs`
- Shared MCP input handling stays in `computer-use-linux/src/server.rs`, with diagnostics matching the runtime ydotool socket requirement

Validation run locally:

```bash
rtk git diff --check
rtk cargo fmt --check
rtk cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
rtk cargo test -p codex-computer-use-linux
rtk cargo test -p codex-update-manager
rtk cargo test --workspace --all-targets
```

All passed locally after the scope reduction.

body:
Styling was compiling through an incomplete Tailwind pipeline, so project-specific utilities and semantic tokens were not making it into the built CSS. This switches the app to the Tailwind v4 Vite plugin path and aligns the config/CSS entrypoint with the project’s hybrid Laravel + Tailwind setup.

- **Build pipeline**
  - Added `@tailwindcss/vite` and registered it in `vite.config.ts`
  - Removed the old Tailwind PostCSS plugin path from `postcss.config.js`
  - Kept `autoprefixer` in place for the remaining CSS pipeline

- **Tailwind configuration**
  - Refactored `tailwind.config.js` to ESM imports for plugins
  - Preserved the existing CSS-variable-backed theme extensions
  - Added missing semantic tokens used in Blade templates, including:
    - `bg-section-alt`
    - `text-on-dark`
    - `text-on-dark-secondary`

- **CSS entrypoint**
  - Reordered `resources/css/app.css` so all stylesheet imports load before Tailwind generation
  - Wired Tailwind v4 to the existing JS config via `@config`
  - Kept the layered hybrid architecture intact: custom CSS owns tokens/components/sections, Tailwind owns structural utilities

- **Generated assets**
  - Rebuilt the tracked Vite output so the manifest and compiled CSS reflect the new pipeline
  - Restores generation of project-specific utilities such as `max-w-container`, `px-md`, `bg-bg-section-alt`, and `text-text-on-dark`

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
import tailwindcss from '@tailwindcss/vite';
import laravel from 'laravel-vite-plugin';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    tailwindcss(),
    laravel({
      input: ['resources/css/app.css', 'resources/js/app.ts'],
      refresh: true,
    }),
  ],
});
```

author: aureliolo
body:
Closes #1836.

## Why

GitHub CodeQL on default-setup repeatedly flags the same idioms in every PR because its built-in data-flow models can't see through SynthOrg's custom sanitiser helpers. Roughly 70 manual dismissals to date across `py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data`, `py/path-injection`, `py/partial-ssrf`, `go/path-injection`, `js/log-injection`, and `go/log-injection`. Default-setup forbids custom queries, sanitiser models, and query-suite filters, so closing the gap requires advanced setup plus a Models-as-Data extension pack pinned in the repo.

## What changed

**Workflows**
- `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` — advanced-setup scan (push + PR + Mon 07:23 UTC cron). 6-language matrix (`actions, go, javascript, javascript-typescript, python, typescript`); `security-extended` query suite explicit on both the action and the config; pinned action SHAs; `permissions: {}` at workflow root with per-job grants; concurrency-grouped.
- `.github/workflows/codeql-pack-validate.yml` — runs only when pack files / fixtures / driver scripts change. Installs CodeQL CLI via the action, then drives `scripts/run_codeql_pack_validation.sh`. Uploads SARIF artifacts on failure.

**Extension pack** (`.github/codeql/extensions/synthorg-sanitisers/`)
- `qlpack.yml` — extension targets `codeql/{python,go,javascript}-all`.
- `python-sanitisers.model.yml` — `safe_error_description`, `scrub_secret_tokens`, `_resolve_root` across 7 scripts (the 12 sites listed in the issue collapse to 7 distinct modules in the diff), `_validate_repo_prefix`, `_validate_image_tag`. `kind: "value"` summary rows so taint is dropped without affecting unrelated rules.
- `go-sanitisers.model.yml` — `config.SecurePath`, `cmd.safeStateDir`.
- `js-sanitisers.model.yml` — `sanitizeForLog`, `sanitizeWsString`, `sanitizeWsEnum`.

**Fixtures** (negative + positive pair per language)
- Python: `.github/codeql/fixtures/python/{negative,positive}.py`
- JS/TS: `.github/codeql/fixtures/javascript/{negative,positive}.ts`
- Go: `cli/internal/codeqlfixtures/fixture.go` (lives inside the `cli/` module so `internal/config` imports resolve). Covers both `go/path-injection` and `go/log-injection` shapes (the latter mirroring `Logger.Info(msg, kvs ...any)` with int+bool args from `docker/sidecar/internal/health/health.go`).
- `expected.json` manifest of `must_fire` / `must_not_fire` assertions per fixture.
- `scripts/check_codeql_fixtures.py` — SARIF assertion script (stdlib only; per-rule + per-function granularity).
- `scripts/run_codeql_pack_validation.sh` — driver that calls `codeql database create / analyze` per language and pipes the result through the assertion script.

**Docs + conventions**
- `docs/reference/sec-prompt-safety.md` — new "CodeQL barrier inventory" table (10 sanitisers → rules), a "Rules covered without a barrier model" subsection (paths-ignore strategy for `py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization`; typed-args fixture for `go/log-injection`), and a cross-link from the Key reference call sites.
- `CLAUDE.md` — new `CodeQL Sanitisers (MANDATORY)` one-liner; bumped the gate-inventory count from 35 to 38.
- `docs/reference/convention-gates.md` — added `check_codeql_fixtures.py`; bumped the RS counter from 37 to 38.
- `data/runtime_stats.yaml` — same counter bump.
- `scripts/convention_gate_map.yaml` — registered `claude-md::codeql-sanitisers` against `scripts/check_codeql_fixtures.py` so the meta-gate accepts the new MANDATORY paragraph.
- `pyproject.toml` — per-file ruff ignores for `.github/codeql/fixtures/python/*.py` (deliberate anti-pattern demonstrations).

## Issue FP-table coverage

| Rule | Coverage |
|---|---|
| `py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data` | Barrier rows for `safe_error_description` + `scrub_secret_tokens`; fixtures assert |
| `py/path-injection` | Barrier rows for `_resolve_root` (7 modules); fixtures assert |
| `go/path-injection` | Barrier rows for `config.SecurePath` + `safeStateDir`; fixtures assert |
| `js/log-injection` | Barrier rows for `sanitizeForLog` + `sanitizeWsString` + `sanitizeWsEnum`; fixtures assert |
| `py/partial-ssrf` | Barrier rows for `_validate_repo_prefix` + `_validate_image_tag`; fixtures assert |
| `py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization` | Suppressed by `paths-ignore: ['tests/**']` (every historical dismissal was on test code); documented in inventory |
| `go/log-injection` | Typed-args fixture (`NegativeLogInjection` int+bool) asserts CodeQL's built-in `Logger.Info(msg, kvs ...any)` handling is sufficient; positive fixture proves the rule still fires on raw user-string args |

## Test plan

- `go -C cli vet ./internal/codeqlfixtures/` ✅
- `go -C cli build ./internal/codeqlfixtures/` ✅
- `uv run pre-commit run --all-files` ✅ (incl. zizmor + actionlint on both new workflows)
- `uv run pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push convention-gate-inventory` ✅ (meta-gate accepts the new MANDATORY)
- The new `codeql-pack-validate` workflow itself runs on this PR's diff and is the end-to-end regression test for the pack's precision.

## Deploy checklist (BLOCKING — manual repo-settings step)

- [ ] **Disable default-setup CodeQL** in repo Settings → Code security → Code scanning → Default → Disable. The advanced-setup workflow cannot start while default-setup is still active; both compete for the same `code-scanning` SARIF channel and only one may be enabled at a time.
- [ ] Wait for the first advanced-setup run on the merged `main` commit to complete (~15 min wall-clock for 6 languages).
- [ ] Verify all six language entries appear under Security → Code scanning alerts.
- [ ] Existing dismissals carry over: CodeQL dedupes by `(ruleId, file, startLine, fingerprint)`. Already-dismissed alerts stay dismissed; new alerts that the pack does not suppress will (correctly) re-fire.

## Review coverage

- 7 local-agent reviewers (docs-consistency, comment-quality-rot, infra-reviewer, go-reviewer, go-security-reviewer, go-conventions-enforcer, issue-resolution-verifier) plus a triage round that surfaced 9 valid findings; all 9 implemented in commit 2 of this branch.
- After merge: run `/aurelio-review-pr` for external-reviewer feedback (CodeRabbit, etc.).

## Out of scope

- Dismissing the 12 currently-open alerts (handled in #1825).
- Any change to sanitiser implementations themselves (the pack only models existing helpers).

author: ggalloni
body:
## Summary

Two ADR 0009 follow-up fixes:

1. **`core._build_fixed_spectra`** — the `S_fixed` low-band loop iterated `range(min(lmin_signal), lmin)` uniformly across spectra, leaking unphysical fiducial entries below a component's spin floor (e.g. `cl_EE[1] != 0`) into S_fixed via cross-pair entries. Replaced with per-pair `max(lmin_signal[i], lmin_signal[j])` filtering. Byte-identical at uniform `lmin_signal=2`.

2. **`harmonic.cl_to_vec` / `vec_to_cl`** — computed `lmax = cl.shape[0] + 1` and iterated `range(2, lmax)`, dropping the last row of every `(n_bins, n_spec)` matrix. The two production callers in `qube/spectra.py` wrote output files (`errors.dat`, spectra files, convolved.dat) with the last bin of every spectrum silently zeroed. Tests passed because the in-memory `get_error_bars` / `get_power_spectra` accessors bypassed the reshape. Fixed by iterating all rows; docstrings cleaned of stale ℓ-language. Closes the first PR1 review comment.

Two PR1 review nits also resolved:
- `test_harmonic_operations.py:389` — stale `(3, lmax-1)` comment corrected to match the `lmax+1` assert.
- `pixel.py:194` `remove_dipole` — moot, PR2 deleted `remove_dipole` entirely.

ADR 0010 (Proposed/deferred) captures the full per-spectrum multipole-window design discussed during PR3 scoping; the actual per-spectrum lmin/lmax implementation is deferred to a follow-up after cosmoforge v0.1 / Paper I.

## Stacking

Based on `lmin-feature` (PR #22). Re-target to `master` once #22 merges.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest src/cosmoforge.cosmocore/tests/ -s` — 403 passed.
- [x] `uv run pytest src/cosmoforge.qube/tests/ -s` — 105 passed + 1 dipole-MC + 1 deselected. `test_pipeline_regression` and `test_dipole_mc` green.
- [x] `uv run pytest src/cosmoforge.picslike/tests/ -s` — 86 passed.
- [x] New regression `test_cl_to_vec_preserves_last_row` uses a bait value (99.0) in the last row to lock in the fix.

## Files

- `src/cosmoforge.cosmocore/cosmocore/core.py` — `_build_fixed_spectra` helper, rewire S_fixed assembly.
- `src/cosmoforge.cosmocore/cosmocore/harmonic.py` — fix `cl_to_vec` / `vec_to_cl`.
- `src/cosmoforge.cosmocore/tests/test_signal.py` — three tests for the per-pair floor.
- `src/cosmoforge.cosmocore/tests/test_harmonic_operations.py` — corrected legacy tests + new last-row regression test + fixed stale beam-shape comment.
- `docs/adr/0010-per-spectrum-multipole-windows.md` — Proposed (deferred) per-spectrum design.

author: sam-phinizy
body:
## Summary - Adds persistent bus subscriptions: an alias subscribes to a topic glob (`repo-a.*`, `**.completed`) and matched bus events land in the subscriber's mailbox. `roux mailbox read` returns them, the unread badge bumps via `mailbox-event`, and the subscriber can mark-read / ack like any other mail. Subscriptions persist to `subscriptions.json`. - MQTT-style globbing: `*` matches one segment, `**` matches many. Pattern segments use the same alphabet as topics (lowercase, digits, hyphens). Partial-segment globs (`foo*`) are rejected at validation. - Closes the **persistent bus subscriptions** and **glob topic patterns** items from #161. ## Stack This PR is **stacked on top of #162** (\`feature/improve-mailbox\` → \`main\`). The base of this PR is \`feature/improve-mailbox\` so the diff shows only the subscription work; once #162 lands, this auto-rebases onto \`main\`. **#164** (mailbox-watch) is stacked on top of this one. Review order: **#162 → #163 → #164**. ## Surface - Core: \`topic_glob\` matcher (22 tests); \`BusSubscription\` model; \`MailboxEvent::TopicDelivered\` variant. - Backend: \`subscriptions/\` module mirroring \`aliases/\` (store / persistence / manager). Mailbox store gains pattern-aware \`list_for_recipient\` / \`recipient_owns\` / \`unread_count\` so subscribers see and ack topic events without losing the existing addressed-mail gatekeeping. - CLI: \`roux bus subscribe '' [--alias ] [--project ]\`, \`roux bus unsubscribe \`, \`roux bus subscriptions [--alias ]\`. \`--alias\` defaults to the calling pane's auto-claimed alias. - MCP: \`roux_bus_subscribe\` / \`roux_bus_unsubscribe\` / \`roux_bus_subscriptions\` tools. - Tauri commands: \`subscriptions_list\` / \`subscriptions_create\` / \`subscriptions_delete\`. - UI: Subs tab in the Mailbox panel — list, create, delete, with live updates via the new \`subscription-event\` Tauri channel. - Persistence: versioned \`subscriptions.json\` envelope (mirrors \`aliases.json\`). ## Test plan - [x] \`cargo test --bin roux\` — 478 pass - [x] \`cargo test --lib --workspace\` — 385 pass across crates - [x] \`npm run test\` — 1003 pass (4 new for the subscription store) - [x] \`npm run check\` — 0 errors - [x] \`cargo clippy --bin roux --tests\` — clean - [ ] Manual end-to-end (per the design doc): - Subscribe \`auditor\` to \`**.completed\`; publish from another pane; confirm unread badge ticks and \`roux mailbox read --ack\` from auditor's pane returns the event. - Subscribe with a project scope; publish without that scope; confirm no match. - Delete via the Subs tab; confirm next publish is silent. ## Out of scope (explicit) - \`mailbox-watch\` push CLI — addressed in **#164**, stacked on top of this PR. - Group aliases. - Subscription rate-limiting / pause-resume. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

- Adds persistent bus subscriptions with MQTT-style glob matching (`*` = one segment, `**` = zero-or-more). The memoized `O(P×T)` matcher, duplicate-triple guard, versioned persistence, and cross-project authorization fix (`patterns_for_event` scoped to the event's own project for `mark_read`/`ack`) are all correct and well-tested. - The previous listener-leak issue is resolved: `startSubscriptionEventListenerWithCleanup` returns `stopSubscriptionEventListener` and is properly pushed to `tauriUnlisteners` in `App.svelte`. - One P2 in `SubscriptionManager::unsubscribe`: when `persist()` fails and a concurrent `subscribe` has raced to re-add the same triple, the rollback `store.add(removed)` silently fails, leaving memory and disk transiently out of sync until the next restart.

Confidence Score: 4/5

 Safe to merge; the single P2 is an edge-case race on a rare error path with no data loss beyond the current session. Only P2 findings present — the silent rollback failure in `unsubscribe` requires a concurrent subscribe racing a persist failure, which is extremely unlikely in a desktop app. All core paths (glob matching, project-scoped authorization, persist-before-emit, listener cleanup) are correct and well-tested. src-tauri/src/subscriptions/manager.rs — the `unsubscribe` rollback at line 136–139.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | crates/roux-core/src/topic_glob.rs | Well-implemented MQTT-style glob matcher with memoized O(P×T) matching; 22 tests cover edge cases including adversarial multi-`**` patterns. | | src-tauri/src/subscriptions/store.rs | Clean in-memory store with correct duplicate-triple prevention and project-scope matching; `patterns_for_alias` correctly includes only scope-compatible patterns. | | src-tauri/src/subscriptions/manager.rs | Correct persist-before-emit pattern mirrors alias manager; minor silent rollback issue in `unsubscribe` if concurrent subscribe races with failed persist. | | src-tauri/src/subscriptions/persistence.rs | Versioned JSON envelope with backcompat bare-array fallback; mirrors aliases persistence pattern faithfully. | | src-tauri/src/mailbox/store.rs | Subscription-aware visibility and ownership correctly layered on top of existing addressed-mail semantics; `recipient_owns` None-arm (any recipient can track state on topic-only events) is intentional and documented. | | src-tauri/src/mailbox/manager.rs | `patterns_for_event` (not `patterns_for(Any)`) is used for `mark_read`/`ack` ownership so cross-project authorization is correctly blocked; the `TopicDelivered` fan-out on `post` is clean. | | src-tauri/src/commands/subscriptions.rs | Thin Tauri command adapter; delegates all logic to `SubscriptionManager`; consistent with repo convention. | | src-tauri/src/socket.rs | `resolve_subscriber_alias` correctly disambiguates explicit vs pane-context aliases and errors on multi-alias panes; new bus-subscribe/unsubscribe/subscriptions handlers are consistent with existing socket command style. | | src/lib/stores/subscriptions.ts | Previous listener-leak issue resolved: `startSubscriptionEventListenerWithCleanup` returns `stopSubscriptionEventListener` and is pushed to `tauriUnlisteners` in App.svelte. | | src/lib/components/MailboxPanel.svelte | Subs tab wired correctly; global subscription list is intentional; alias pre-fill on tab switch is a nice UX touch. | | crates/roux-core/src/models/subscription.rs | New `BusSubscription` and `BusSubscriptionEvent` models are well-structured and match the TypeScript types exposed via `tauri.ts`. | | src-tauri/src/mcp.rs | Three new MCP tools (`roux_bus_subscribe`, `roux_bus_unsubscribe`, `roux_bus_subscriptions`) route through the socket, consistent with all other MCP tools in the file. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant CLI as CLI / MCP participant Socket as Socket Handler participant SubMgr as SubscriptionManager participant SubStore as SubscriptionStore participant Disk as subscriptions.json participant Tauri as Tauri Events CLI->>Socket: "bus-subscribe {pattern, alias}" Socket->>Socket: resolve_subscriber_alias() Socket->>SubMgr: subscribe(alias, pattern, project_id) SubMgr->>SubMgr: validate_alias_name + validate_topic_pattern SubMgr->>SubStore: add(subscription) — duplicate-triple check SubStore-->>SubMgr: Ok(inserted) SubMgr->>Disk: save_to_path (persist before emit) Disk-->>SubMgr: Ok SubMgr->>Tauri: emit(subscription-event, Created) Tauri-->>CLI: Ok(subscription) note over CLI,Tauri: Later: bus publish triggers delivery CLI->>Socket: "bus-publish {topic, body}" Socket->>SubMgr: matching_topic(topic, project_id) SubMgr-->>Socket: [BusSubscription, ...] Socket->>SubStore: post event to mailbox loop for each matching subscription Socket->>Tauri: emit(mailbox-event, TopicDelivered) end ```

body:
Login, logout, and password reset for the admin guard. This is the v2 equivalent of v1's Admin\Auth\AuthenticatedSessionController and the missing-then-restored Breeze auth controllers.

## Files
- `Admin\Auth\AuthenticatedSessionController` - login form, login submit, logout. Filters by user_type IN ['a', 'sa'] (super admin + company admin only). Updates login_time, last_login_at, login_ip_address on success. Redirects to /admin/change-password when must_change_password='y' (column added in v1 PR #31).
- `Admin\Auth\PasswordResetController` - forgot-password + reset flow against the 'admins' password broker (defined in v2 config/auth.php). Clears must_change_password on successful reset.
- `Http\Requests\Admin\Auth\LoginRequest` - email + password validation
- `resources/views/admin/auth/{layout,login,forgot-password,reset-password}.blade.php` - minimal placeholder views (real Tailwind/styling theme will land in phase 4)

## Routes (all under /admin prefix, namespaced 'admin.')
- GET /admin/login -> admin.login
- POST /admin/login -> admin.login.store (throttle:5,1)
- POST /admin/logout -> admin.logout (auth:admin)
- GET/POST /admin/forgot-password -> admin.password.request / .email (throttle:3,1 on POST)
- GET/POST /admin/reset-password/{token} -> admin.password.reset / .update (throttle:5,1 on POST)

## Verified
- All 7 routes show in route:list with correct middleware
- /admin/login renders 200
- /admin/forgot-password renders 200
- /admin/reset-password/abc123 renders 200
- POST /admin/login with bogus creds returns 302 with error (no row in v2 DB yet, expected)

## What's NOT in this PR
- Sub-admin / employee login (the public /login flow with company picker) - separate controller in next PR
- Email verification flow - low priority, deferred
- Confirm-password gate for sensitive actions - deferred until any sensitive action needs it

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary When a user enables a theme or selects a profile that lists `dependencies` not currently installed locally, the Desktop UI now auto-downloads them from the deckthemes Theme Store before handing off to the backend's `setThemeState` / `changePreset`. This is what makes a tiny preset whose `theme.json` is just a list of dependencies actually work on a fresh install — previously the user had to manually search for and install each dependency in the store first. ### How it works - New `logic/resolveAndDownloadDeps.ts`: - Compares the preset/theme's `dependencies: string[]` against the locally installed `themes` (by name). - For anything missing, queries the store's batch endpoint `GET https://api.deckthemes.com/themes/ids?ids=`. The endpoint matches against both `id` and `name`. - For each item the store returned, calls the existing `downloadThemeFromUrl(remote.id)`. - Returns three buckets: `downloaded`, `notFound`, `failed`. - Wired into: - `components/SingleTheme/ThemeToggle.tsx` (toggling a theme/preset on directly). - `components/Presets/PresetSelectionDropdown.tsx` (changing the active profile via the dropdown). - UI feedback (per user request: toast in the corner, non-blocking): - One progress toast per download — `Downloading X of Y - `. - At the end, if any names couldn't be resolved on the store, a final toast: `Some dependencies could not be found - foo, bar, baz`. - Same shape for transient download failures. - The apply proceeds with whatever made it through; nothing here is fatal. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] **Happy path — preset with only deps**: import the user-supplied profile (the `theme.json` with ~30 dependencies). Toggle it on / select it as a profile. Confirm a sequence of `Downloading X of N` toasts appears and the dependencies show up in `manage-themes` afterwards. - [ ] **All deps already present**: enable a theme whose deps are already installed. Confirm there are no spurious download toasts. - [ ] **Some deps missing, some present**: have a few deps already installed, others not. Confirm only the missing ones download. - [ ] **Unknown dep**: temporarily edit a `theme.json` to add a fake dep name (e.g. `"definitely-not-real-theme-zzz"`). Confirm a final toast `Some dependencies could not be found - definitely-not-real-theme-zzz` appears, and the rest still install. ### Notes - The store's `/themes/ids` endpoint is the same one already used by `bulkThemeUpdateCheck`. We rely on its name-or-id matching behaviour because preset `dependencies` are theme names, not ids. - Each download is sequential (not `Promise.all`'d). This keeps the toast progress numbers honest and avoids hammering the API for big presets. - After successful downloads we call `refreshThemes()` so the freshly-installed themes are visible to the subsequent `changePreset` / `setThemeState`. Without this the backend would still find them on disk after its own scan, but the UI would briefly look stale. - Pairs cleanly with #3 (Run at Startup); they're independent and either can land first. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/d7712eb9a55f48dd9609c8679d60da0b Requested by: @biscock ---

body:
⚡ Bolt: [performance improvement]

**What:** 
* Moved all JS->WASM WSM evaluations into a single batch vector function to avoid FFI ping-pong lag.
* Altered the IQR Anomaly Engine from a full O(N log N) `sort_by` arrays algorithm to a linear time O(N) `select_nth_unstable_by` memory-optimised variant.
* Adjusted tie-breakers in the generic sorting arrays using `sort_unstable_by`.
* Refactored JS logic array grouping. Swapped O(N*M) loop-filtering with a clean O(N) hash-dictionary.
* Implemented proper XSS unicode-escapes `\u003c` in raw string dumps directed at audit tables to maintain architectural integrity/security parameters.
* Configured `web/evaluation_engine/.gitignore` correctly.

**Why:** 
The evaluation engine handles heavy compute during scoring and needed architectural scaling at the compiler and memory bounds for maximum efficiency. 

**Impact:** 
Substantially lowers system execution time under large payloads while eliminating overhead caused by continuous linear searches and unoptimised native bridging.

**Measurement:** 
Algorithmic complexity reduction and large boundary batching translates to measurable constant-time wins across the evaluation endpoints.

author: cucumber-sp
body:
## Summary

Stage 3 of the ref-construction redesign rollout (after #25 spec, #26 foundation). Closes the construction invariant from `docs/design/ref-construction-redesign.md` §3:

> Every field of an `unsafe struct` literal must be initialized by name. Empty literals (`Shared<T>{}`) and partial literals are rejected at compile time.

## Why

The old design had `addr(s.field) = ptr` + `init s.field = value` as a multi-step protocol. The literal could be empty (`Shared<T>{}`); the slots got seated later inside an `unsafe` block. That worked but invited a real foot-gun: forget one of the seatings and the slot stays null. The first auto-deref through it is UB the type system didn't catch.

After this PR the struct literal IS the binding ceremony. Either every binding is supplied or it doesn't compile; there's no observable half-initialized state.

## What changes

`src/checker/literal-checker.ts` — both code paths (explicit and inferred type args) had an exception that let `ref T` fields on `unsafe struct`s be omitted. The exception is gone. Single uniform rule: every field of every struct literal must appear by name.

```diff
- if (structType.isUnsafe && fieldType.kind === "ptr" && fieldType.isRef) {
-   continue;
- }
- checker.error(`missing field '${fieldName}'...`);
+ checker.error(`missing field '${fieldName}'...`);
```

## Test plan

`tests/checker/required-init.test.ts` — five cases pin the new rule:

- empty literal of an unsafe struct with a `ref T` field → rejected
- partial literal omitting one of two `ref T` fields → rejected
- full literal initializing every `ref T` field → accepted
- generic unsafe struct with a `ref T` field, empty literal → rejected
- generic unsafe struct with a `ref T` field, full literal → accepted

Three pre-existing fixtures that relied on the exception are migrated:
- `§4.7 init inside unsafe` test (`Box{}` → `Box{ data: ... }`)
- `Shared<T>.wrap typechecks` test (body now seats both fields in the literal via `malloc` + offset arithmetic)
- `addr-lvalue assignment` test (literal seats payload first; the addr write is the second seating; both field_ptr + store pairs are asserted)

`bun test` clean: 2135 / 16 / 0.
`bunx tsc --noEmit` clean.
`biome ci src/ tests/` clean locally.

## Note

`addr` and `init` are still legal in `unsafe` blocks after this PR — they coexist with the new struct-literal-only construction. PR 3 drops both keywords entirely once the few remaining test fixtures using them are migrated.

## Related

- #24 — design doc.
- #25 — spec sweep.
- #26 — PR 1: `onCopy` / `onDestroy` / `placeAt` / `*T → ref T` literal coercion.

author: got3nks
body:
## Summary

Fixes #376 ("Error: unsupported Zip compression method"). On 2024-08-04 the eMule-security IPFilter feed published a malformed `ipfilter.zip` and every daemon that auto-fetched it spun in an infinite log loop, filling logs with gigabytes of `Error: unsupported Zip compression method` per minute until disk filled or the operator killed the process. The upstream feed has since been fixed, but nothing in our code prevents the next bad zip from doing the same.

## Root cause

`UnpackZipFile()` in `src/libs/common/FileFunctions.cpp` reads each interesting entry with:

```cpp
while (!zip.Eof()) {
    zip.Read(buffer, sizeof(buffer));
    target.Write(buffer, zip.LastRead());
}
```

When `wxZipInputStream` encounters an unsupported compression method (or any other entry-level decompression error), `Read()` emits one `wxLogError`, returns zero bytes, and parks the stream in an error state — but `Eof()` keeps returning false. The loop then spins forever, re-emitting the wx error on every iteration.

## Fix

Break the inner loop when `Read()` returns zero bytes. The wx error still surfaces exactly once so the operator sees what failed; `target.Length()` stays 0; `UnpackZipFile` returns false; `UnpackArchive` returns `EFT_Error`; the existing `IPFilter::Reload` caller logs `Failed to load ipfilter.dat file '...', unknown format encountered.` and abandons the file. Next IPFilter fetch picks up a clean copy as before.

## Verification

Standalone reproduction on Ubuntu 26.04 ARM64, libwx 3.2 — built a hand-crafted zip with one entry using compression method `0xff`:

```
original loop:  50+ iterations of "Error: unsupported Zip compression method"
                (capped at 50 by the test harness; production would run unbounded)
fixed loop:     1 iteration, single error message, clean exit
```

Then compile-tested `FileFunctions.cpp` clean against the project's exact flags.

Closes #376

## Symptome (zwei Probleme in einem PR)

### 1. Pairing scheitert trotz übereinstimmender Codes

iPhone und TV joinen den trystero-Room mit demselben Code, finden sich aber nicht — TV-Seite zeigt nach 30 s „Kein iPhone in 30 s". Loading geklappt (v9-Diagnostik bestätigt), aber `onPeerJoin` feuert nie.

**Ursache**: Die `/torrent`-Strategie nutzt die WebTorrent-Tracker-Wolke für Signaling. Die ist seit Jahren fragmentiert — einzelne Tracker sind tot, andere sehen nur Teilmengen der Peers, sodass iPhone und TV in unterschiedlichen Tracker-Pools landen.

**Fix**: Strategie auf `/nostr` umgestellt (beide Seiten). Nostr-Relays sind 2025 deutlich zuverlässiger, gleiche trystero-API, identischer WebRTC-Layer danach. Nur der Signaling-Kanal wechselt; der Datentransfer bleibt WebRTC/WebTorrent.

### 2. TV-Pair-Screen ist hochformat-gequetscht

Alle Pair-Elemente waren vertikal gestapelt (Brand → h1 → Lede → QR → „oder" → Eingabe). Auf einem Querformat-TV wirkt das wie ein schmaler Mittelstreifen, der QR-Code ist mit max. 340 px Pixel-Postage-Stamp.

**Fix**:
* `@media (min-aspect-ratio: 1/1) and (min-width: 800px)` → zweispaltiges Grid: links QR (jetzt **38vmin**, also gut sichtbar), rechts Code-Pille + manuelles Eingabefeld
* h1/Lede etwas kompakter, damit die actionable Elemente (QR, Code, Eingabe) den Bildschirm dominieren
* Im Portrait bleibt das alte gestapelte Layout

## Versions-Bump

v9 → **v10**.

body:
## Summary

cclaw 8.5.0 fixes the issues you surfaced from the test run on `/Users/zuevrs/Projects/test/`:

- ship duplicated the flow (active dir + shipped dir both kept the artifacts);
- sub-agents ran with inline ~30-line prompts instead of their 200+-line contracts under `.cclaw/lib/agents/`;
- triage.path was self-contradicting on large-risky;
- pre-mortem.md was orphaned in the active dir on ship-finalize;
- lastSpecialist stayed null after architect ran;
- no mechanism for grounded context gathering before plan authoring.

### What changed

1. **Hop 6 — Finalize.** New explicit hop. Orchestrator-only (never delegated). `git mv` (or `mv`) every artifact, asserts active dir empty, removes empty dir, resets flow-state. The word "copy" is forbidden anywhere in finalize or in dispatch envelopes leading to it. Re-entrant finalize on resume is idempotent.
2. **Mandatory contract reads in dispatch envelopes.** Every envelope begins with two non-negotiable reads: `.cclaw/lib/agents/<specialist>.md` (the contract) and the wrapper skill. Brainstormer / architect / planner prompts also do these as Phase 1, so even harnesses that don't render the envelope verbatim get the right behaviour.
3. **Brainstormer rewritten as 8-phase workflow.** Bootstrap → Posture pick → Repo signals → (deep) repo-research dispatch → Clarifying questions (one at a time, max 3) → Author → Self-review checklist (9 checks) → Slim summary. 194 → 280+ lines.
4. **Two new read-only research helpers — `repo-research` + `learnings-research`.** Dispatched by planner / architect / brainstormer (deep) BEFORE they author. Not specialists: never become `lastSpecialist`, never appear in `triage.path`. Each writes one short artifact (`research-repo.md` / `research-learnings.md`). Planner Phase 3 always dispatches `learnings-research`; Phase 4 dispatches `repo-research` on brownfield only.
5. **`discovery` is a sub-phase of plan, never a triage.path entry.** `triage.path ⊆ {plan, build, review, ship}` — full stop. On large-risky the plan stage expands into brainstormer → checkpoint → architect → checkpoint → planner. `currentStage` stays "plan"; `lastSpecialist` rotates.
6. **`pre-mortem.md` is a first-class `ArtifactStage`.** Added to `compound.ts` `allStages` and to the Hop 6 move list.
7. **`lastSpecialist` widened** from `DiscoverySpecialistId | null` to `SpecialistId | null`. Updated after every dispatch (not only at end of stage). Resume from a discovery checkpoint reads `lastSpecialist == "architect"` and skips straight to planner.

### Specialist prompts deepened

- Architect 256 → 320+ lines (Phase 1 bootstrap, Phase 2 assumptions, Phase 3 conditional `repo-research`, Phase 7 self-review with 8 checks).
- Planner 297 → 360+ lines (Phase 3 mandatory `learnings-research` dispatch replacing the in-prompt knowledge.jsonl scan, Phase 4 conditional brownfield `repo-research`, Phase 6 verbatim copy of surfaced lessons, Phase 7 self-review with 10 checks).

### Schema

- `flow-state.json` stays at `schemaVersion: 3`.
- `ArtifactStage` adds `"pre-mortem"`.
- `RESEARCH_AGENT_IDS = ["repo-research","learnings-research"]` is new.
- `CORE_AGENTS` now combines `SPECIALIST_AGENTS + RESEARCH_AGENTS`; renderer emits `kind: research-helper` only on research entries.

### Tests

429 passing — 383 baseline plus a new `tests/unit/v85-finalize-research-contracts.test.ts` (46 cases).

## Release Notes Draft

- **Hop 6 — Finalize.** Orchestrator-only `git mv` (or `mv`) of every artifact, post-condition asserts active dir empty, resets flow-state. "Copy" is forbidden in finalize or in dispatch envelopes leading to it.
- **Mandatory contract reads.** Every dispatch envelope mandates two non-negotiable reads (the agent contract + the wrapper skill) before the sub-agent acts.
- **Brainstormer rewritten** as an 8-phase workflow with one-question-at-a-time clarification and a 9-item self-review checklist.
- **Two new research helpers** (`repo-research`, `learnings-research`) dispatched by planner / architect / brainstormer before authoring. Not specialists.
- **`discovery`** is now a sub-phase of the `plan` stage on large-risky. `triage.path ⊆ {plan, build, review, ship}` — full stop.
- **`pre-mortem.md`** is a first-class artifact stage; archived on ship-finalize.
- **`lastSpecialist`** widened to every `SpecialistId`, updated after every dispatch.

## Summary
Fresh-host bootstrap now provisions lychee (link checker), keybase, Signal Desktop, and signal-cli — closing the gap between what `chezmoi apply` sets up and the daily-driver toolset.

## Gotchas
- Keybase's apt repo entry uses `[trusted=yes]`. Their published install guide does this because `prerelease.keybase.io`'s apt metadata isn't signed; the keybase service self-updates once installed, so pinning here would be theatre. Documented inline in script 01.
- signal-cli's release artifacts ship `.asc` GPG signatures but no sha256 — the existing `expected_from_checksums` pattern doesn't apply. Added a `verify_gpg` helper in `lib.sh` that imports the key into an ephemeral `GNUPGHOME` and asserts the imported fingerprint equals the pinned `FA10826A74907F9EC6BBB7FC2BA2CD21B5B09570` before verifying. The fingerprint was cross-checked against `keys.openpgp.org` (UID `AsamK <asamk@gmx.de>`).

## Summary

Follow-up to PR #207 (C1 bundle merged at \`63dfab3c\`) addressing the
post-merge fresh-context reviewer findings (89.45/100, 1 IMPORTANT + 2 NITs)
plus a 3-angle re-review (security + correctness + maintainability) that
converged on \`CHANGES_REQUESTED\` for the original prometheus.yml patch.

### What changed

**1. Prometheus config — refactor for actual prod ↔ local parity**

The previous attempt edited \`museum-backend/prometheus.yml\`, but CI scp
sources \`infra/grafana/*\` only — so the patched file was never shipped
to prod, and the local Grafana stack mounting the same file would have
broken silently (\`backend:3000\` does not resolve on the local \`obs\`-only network).

- \`git mv museum-backend/prometheus.yml → infra/grafana/prometheus.yml\` — CI rsync now ships it.
- New \`infra/grafana/prometheus.local.yml\` with \`host.docker.internal:3000\` for the standalone local stack.
- \`infra/grafana/docker-compose.yml\` mounts the local variant ; \`museum-backend/deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml\` continues mounting the prod variant (via \`./obs/prometheus.yml\` after CI rsync).
- Comment in \`prometheus.yml\` reworded — drops the misleading "override via env" claim (Prometheus \`static_configs.targets\` does NOT expand \`\${VAR}\`).

body:
## What

Fifth slice of Phase 3. Adds the settings surface required by Phase 3 DoD: **'Settings screen detects installed codex and claude binaries; user can select provider per workspace.'**

Cancels setState if unmounted before resolve. Falls back to the empty result when the bridge resolves to null. Accepts an injected api for unit tests. |

author: hridyansh24
body:
## What this PR changes ### Per-assignment verification config (professor decides, student doesn't) `ClassContext` gains `mode` (`quiz` | `summary` | `both`) and `num_questions` columns. The professor sets them when linking an assignment to a class (and can edit them later from the Assignments tab); the student never picks. `/submit/` now reads those settings from the persisted link instead of accepting them as form fields, so every student on a given assignment gets the same verification flow. Quiz pool multiplier dropped from 4x to 2x to keep cost manageable. [Professor assignment row showing Quiz · 5 q badge](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-5bf80516-ac7b-419b-a82e-2cef05abc7db/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fprofessor_assignment_row_with_quiz5q.webp) ### AI signals hidden from the student `/submit/` still runs detection / style / confidence and persists the full result on the `submissions` row, but the response returned to the student strips `ai_detection`, `style_analysis`, and `confidence_score` to `null`. Professor dashboards (`/classes/{id}/submissions`, `/submissions/{id}`) continue to read the persisted record unchanged. Frontend-student drops `DetectionCard`, `ConfidenceCard`, and `StyleCard` from the post-submission landing in favour of a generic "Submission received" card that routes directly into the professor-configured check. Student view (no AI signals): [Student submission received card with no AI signals](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-5bf80516-ac7b-419b-a82e-2cef05abc7db/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fstudent_submission_received_no_ai_signals.webp) Professor view (full signals on the submission row): [Professor submissions tab showing AI and confidence pills](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-5bf80516-ac7b-419b-a82e-2cef05abc7db/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fprofessor_submissions_with_ai_pills.webp) ### Demo professor auth New `Professor` model (full UUID id), `professor_store`, and `/professors/register|login|{id}` endpoints — same PBKDF2 hashing as the student flow. Frontend-professor wraps the existing classes UI in a `ProfessorAuthPage` with sign-up / log-in tabs, persists the session in `localStorage`, and surfaces a sign-out button on the nav. Demo-grade per the task brief: no per-route gating yet. ### Conceptual quiz prompt `QUIZ_GENERATION_PROMPT` rewritten to demand a ~40 / 40 / 20 mix of conceptual / applied / transfer questions, ban literal-string recall, and emit a `category` and `concept_tag` per question. Schema is backward-compatible (additive optional fields). ### Principled style / confidence math Three improvements bundled per the plan (A2 + B + C): - **A2** — replace the undocumented `dist * 20` cosine→z mapping with `dist / COSINE_STD` using a documented module-level constant (`0.05`). - **B** — replace the step-function quant/qual blend (50/50 → 60/40 → 70/30 at hard cutpoints) with a continuous schedule `quant_share = 0.7 - 0.4 * exp(-(n-3)/4)`. - **C** — `compute_deviation` reports coverage and scales the quantitative deviation when fewer than half of the weighted metrics had history. `compute_confidence_score` always includes the style component (with an `insufficient_history` flag) so the weighted denominator is stable instead of silently dropping the column. ### Submission flow ```mermaid flowchart LR Stu[Student uploads files via /submit/] --> Be[Backend reads
per-assignment settings] Be -->|mode + num_questions| Quiz[Quiz pool
generation + cache] Be -->|skip_detection?| Det[8-layer AI detection] Be --> Sty[Style fingerprint
+ deviation] Det --> Persist[(submissions row
full ai/style/confidence)] Sty --> Persist Quiz --> StuResp[Response to student
quiz + summary only] Persist --> ProfList[/classes/id/submissions/] ProfList --> ProfUI[Professor dashboard:
AI %, confidence, style dev,
quiz score, attempts] StuResp --> StuUI[Student dashboard:
quiz / summary,
no AI signals] ``` ## Migrations `database.init_db` runs lightweight `ALTER TABLE class_contexts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS mode ...` and `... num_questions ...` so existing class_contexts rows pick up the new columns on next backend start. The new `professors` table is created via `create_all`. No data migration required. ## Demo End-to-end recording (professor signup → create class → create assignment with Quiz/5 → student signup → join → submit → "Submission received" with no AI signals → professor sees AI/Conf pills on the submissions tab): [aiguard_demo_compact.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-5bf80516-ac7b-419b-a82e-2cef05abc7db/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Faiguard_demo_compact.mp4) Student inline notice that this assignment is configured for 5 comprehension questions (the professor's setting flowed through): [Student sees 5-question banner per professor config](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-5bf80516-ac7b-419b-a82e-2cef05abc7db/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fstudent_assignment_5q_banner.webp) ## Testing - Backend integration test (`/tmp/aiguard-test/verify_flow.py`, not committed) drives the full flow against a stubbed LLM and asserts: per-assignment settings persist on link / patch; the student response has `ai_detection / style_analysis / confidence_score = null`; correct number of quiz questions returned with `correct_index` and `explanations` stripped; the persisted submission row keeps full AI/confidence data for the professor view; `confidence_score.components.style_deviation.insufficient_history` is `true` when no profile exists; mode-switch (`quiz` → `summary`) returns a summary and no quiz; bumping `num_questions` to 12 serves the requested count. - Both Vite frontends build cleanly (`npm run build` in `frontend-professor` and `frontend-student`). - Manual UI walkthrough captured in the demo video above. To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.
