author: tclune
body:
## Summary

Remove `MAPL_PackDateTime` and `MAPL_IncYMD` from `base/Base/Base_Base.F90` and `base/Base/Base_Base_implementation.F90` as part of the MAPL3 migration.

Closes #4815

## Changes

- Remove `public MAPL_PackDateTime`, its `module subroutine` interface declaration, and its implementation (6 lines)
- Remove `public MAPL_IncYMD`, its `module function` interface declaration, and its implementation (29 lines)

## Rationale

Both symbols have **zero external callers** anywhere in the GEOSgcm ecosystem:

- `MAPL_PackDateTime`: no compiled callers found
- `MAPL_IncYMD`: the wider ecosystem carries ~12 independent private copies of the legacy GLA GCM `INCYMD` algorithm; none `USE MAPL_Base` for this

## Related

- Part of MAPL3 Base migration: #4805
- Companion to #4811 / #4814 (which removed `MAPL_PackTime`, `MAPL_UnpackTime`, `MAPL_UnpackDateTime`)

## Changes

Fixes and hardening from testing the pipeline with local MLX LLM + Kokoro/RVC TTS against real meetings.

### Audio playback queue (`agent_page.py`)
- Replaced single-play gating (`isSpeaking`) with a sequential queue (`audioPlayQueue` + `playFromQueue`)
- Multiple LLM responses no longer get silently dropped — they queue and play in order
- Explicit `AudioContext({ sampleRate: 24000 })` to match Kokoro WAV output

### Bot status polling (`server.py`)
- After `/api/bot/join`, background task polls Recall API every 3s (max ~90s) until bot is confirmed in-call

### Recall status derivation (`transports/recall.py`)

### WAV sample rate fix (`tts/local.py`)

### Webhook status codes (`webhook.py`)
- Accept `in_call_recording` / `in_call_not_recording` as in-meeting

author: rsterenchak
body:
## Task

> **[MEDIUM]** Add Ctrl+Pause global shortcut to toggle Pomodoro timer with status pill
> Wire a global `Ctrl + Pause/Break` keyboard shortcut that toggles the Pomodoro timer between running and paused, regardless of where focus is in the app. On every toggle, surface a brief auto-fading status pill near the top of the Pomodoro popover — amber `Paused` when pausing, primary-purple `Play` when resuming. If the popover was closed, open it just long enough for the pill to fade, then auto-close.

## Changes

- `pomodoro.js` — add a `toggle()` method to the controller. IDLE → start (returns `'playing'`), RUNNING → pause (returns `'paused'`), PAUSED → resume (returns `'playing'`), COMPLETE_UNACKED → no-op (returns `'noop'`, never auto-restarts from 00:00). Single entry point keeps `main.js` from second-guessing the state machine.
- `main.js` — register a global `keydown` listener for `Ctrl+Pause` (no Alt/Shift/Meta) that calls `ctl.toggle()` and renders a transient status pill via `showPomodoroStatusPill(kind)`. The pill is inserted between the popover header and the tab row, sits at full opacity for ~1.2s, fades over ~400ms via the `.fading` class, and is removed from the DOM at ~1.6s. When the shortcut itself opened the popover, the popover auto-closes ~200ms after pill removal; when the popover was already open, only the pill fades. Rapid repeated presses cancel and replace the in-flight pill so the latest toggle always wins.
- `style.css` — add `.pomodoroStatusPill` with `.paused` (amber) and `.playing` (primary purple) modifiers, plus the `.fading` opacity-transition class. Inline SVG icons keep the change icon-library-free per CLAUDE.md.
- `modals.js` — list `Ctrl + Pause` under the Global shortcut group so the help modal surfaces it.
- `changelog.js` — user-facing bullet describing the new shortcut.

## Files modified

- `toDoList_main/src/pomodoro.js`
- `toDoList_main/src/main.js`
- `toDoList_main/src/style.css`
- `toDoList_main/src/modals.js`
- `toDoList_main/src/changelog.js`
- `toDoList_main/tests/ctrlPausePomodoroToggle.test.js` (new)

## Testing

I have implemented "Snack Game 2.0", a polished version of the classic Snake game with several new features:

1.  **Shop System**: Players earn coins by eating snacks. These coins can be used in the "Snack Shop" to purchase and equip different colors for the snack and the game background.

    *   **Food Variety**: Snacks now spawn with random colors from a predefined palette.

author: copilot
body:
## Summary

Implements the complete V2 capture visit lifecycle described in the problem statement. Before this PR, a completed room scan had no durable commit path, no proper next-step UI, and no resume support after the app was killed.

## Changes

### New files
- **`AtlasScan/V2/Models/V2VisitLifecycleState.swift`** — `VisitCaptureLifecycleState` enum with 9 states: `noVisit → visitSetup → scanningRoom → reviewingRoom → roomSaved → choosingNextStep → visitReview → readyToExport → exported`
- **`AtlasScan/V2/Views/V2PostScanRoomReviewView.swift`** — Full-screen post-scan review shown immediately after a room scan completes. Replaces the old plain-text alert. Shows: floor plan polygon, area m², ceiling height, wall count, evidence counts (pins/photos/voice notes), editable room name, and action buttons (Save Room / Next Room / Finish Visit / Discard)
- **`AtlasScan/V2/Views/V2FinishVisitView.swift`** — Readiness checklist (7 flags derived from `VisitReadinessV1`) with Export / Open Atlas Mind and Finish as Draft actions

### Modified files
- **`ScanSessionCoordinator`** — Persists active `visitId` + lifecycle state to `UserDefaults` on every save; loads existing session from disk on init if the UserDefaults pointer exists; exposes `isResumingExistingSession`, `transition(to:)`, and `discardActiveSession()`
- **`V2RoomLoopView`** — Replaces the name-alert + minimal card with `showPostScanReview` full-screen cover → `V2PostScanRoomReviewView`; post-save card updated with "Finish Visit" button; VanModeView "Finish Visit" callback opens `V2FinishVisitView` instead of directly calling `handOffToMind`; `V2VisitReviewView` gains coordinator binding and a "Finish Visit / Export" section
- **`PropertyMapView`** — Shows a "Visit in progress" resume banner when `isResumingExistingSession` is true; banner includes visit reference, room count, "Resume Scanning" and "Discard Visit" actions; `onAppear` suppresses the visit-setup sheet when resuming
- **`project.pbxproj`** — Registers 5 new Swift files + fixes the pre-existing `V2IdentifiableDedupe.swift` missing project entry

## Acceptance test coverage addressed

- ✅ Scan → post-scan review screen with floor plan preview
- ✅ Save Room → durable commit → confirmation card
- ✅ Kill app → reopen → resume banner shows saved rooms
- ✅ Continue to Next Room preserves same visit context
- ✅ Finish Visit opens readiness checklist, not dead-end scan screen
- ✅ Export / Open Mind uses saved `SessionCaptureV2` data via `handOffToMind()`

body:
## Summary
1주차 Backend 스캐폴드 — `docs/specs/08-roles-and-handoffs.md` §5 "1주차 Backend = LangGraph 셋업 + super-graph 골격(stub sub-graph) + FastAPI 스캐폴드 + 전처리 노드" + Vision Agent 통합 어댑터까지 포함.

> 본 PR은 #3을 대체합니다. WinningBean 님이 #3에 남기신 디렉토리 구조 제안 ("agent 코드는 `agents/` 루트로 분리")을 backend 통합 레이어에 그대로 반영.

## 변경 범위 (CODEOWNERS 08 §3.3 기준 backend 영역 한정)

### FastAPI 스캐폴드 — `api/app/api/`, `api/main.py`
- `POST /v1/sessions`, `GET /v1/sessions/{id}`, `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/simulate`, `/healthz`
- 도메인 예외 (`BackendError` 계열) → JSON 매핑, multipart 업로드, CORS, structlog
- `main.py`에서 repo 루트를 `sys.path`에 삽입 — `agents.<name>` 패키지 import 가능하게

### LangGraph super-graph — `api/app/orchestration/`
- `SessionState` (Pydantic v2) — preprocess 결과 + 3개 agent 슬롯 + dict-merge reducer (08 §5.1)
- 토폴로지: `preprocess → vision/context (fan-out) → recommendation (fan-in) → pack_response → END`
- `preprocess_node`, `pack_response_node`만 backend 소유. Agent sub-graph는 외부 모듈로 위임.

### Vision Agent 통합 어댑터 — `api/app/agents_stub/vision_adapter.py` (NEW)
- `SessionState(image_bytes)` ↔ `agents.vision.VisionState(image)` 입력 키 변환
- `agents.vision.VisionResponse` (자체 스키마) → `app.schemas.VisionResponse` (공개 계약, 07 §2) 변환
- async — `analyze_outfit(session_id, image_bytes)` 단일 진입점 사용
- 셀렉터(`agents_stub/__init__.py`)가 `agents.<name>` 임포트 가능 시 어댑터/실 sub-graph 등록, 아니면 schema-valid stub 폴백

### Stub sub-graphs — `api/app/agents_stub/`
- vision / context / recommendation 각각 schema-valid fixture (08 §3.2 Mock-First)
- 실 agent 모듈 미머지 또는 deps 미설치 환경에서 폴백

### 전처리 서비스 — `api/app/services/`
- `preprocess_image`: EXIF 제거, MediaPipe person detect, 얼굴 블러, 리사이즈
- 인메모리 `session_cache`, IP `rate_limiter`

### 공개 데이터 계약 — `api/app/schemas/`
- `07-data-contracts.md` §1-§5의 enum + Vision/Context/Recommendation/Session Pydantic 모델

## Test plan
- [x] `cd api && .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_api.py tests/test_orchestration.py tests/test_preprocess.py -q` → **17 passed**
- [x] super-graph가 stub 3개로 e2e 통과 (`test_orchestration.py`) — 어댑터는 `agents.vision` 미존재 시 stub 폴백 검증
- [x] 동일 입력 5회 호출 결정성 검증 (08 §10 Done 기준 일부)
- [x] `git merge-tree` dry-run으로 main과 충돌 없음 확인

## 협업 메모
- **PR #3 대체**: 동일 작업물 + WinningBean 제안 반영. PR #3는 close 예정.

author: sifaoso
body: Hey all, Thanks a lot for all the work that has gone into nnU-Net over the years! I believe I found a bug in patch sampling when visualizing 3D CT batches (AMOS dataset), where some sampled patches contain slices outside the scan field-of-view (resulting in unexpected padding). The issue occurs in the `get_bbox()` method when `force_fg=True` (foreground oversampling). In this case, a foreground class is first selected, then a random voxel from that class is chosen as the patch center. However, when constructing the patch, the resulting bounding box is only constrained with respect to the lower bounds (`lbs`) and is not checked against the upper bounds (`ubs`), which define the valid sampling range to keep the patch fully inside the volume (here: https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnUNet/blob/e73bbc743f93877211ca434dd07eca07c1221d0b/nnunetv2/training/dataloading/data_loader.py#L145). As a consequence, some foreground patches may partially fall outside the valid image region and become padded. Note that this issue does not occur when `force_fg=False`, since `bbox_lbs` is sampled directly within the valid interval `[lbs, ubs]`. The proposed fix explicitly constrains the sampled bounding box to remain within both `lbs` and `ubs`, which fixes the issue in my tests. Below is a small GIF illustrating the problem (see the 3rd sample: some slices lie outside the scan field-of-view and are therefore padded unexpectedly).

author: jonyardley
body:
## Summary

Fixes [INTRADA-API-36](https://jon-yardley.sentry.io/issues/INTRADA-API-36) — 23 events, regressed:

> \`Internal error: Hrana: api error: status=404 Not Found, body={"error":"stream not found: f238e949:..."}\`
>
> GET \`http://intrada-api.fly.dev/api/sets\`

Same Hrana stream-drop class as the migration panic (INTRADA-API-2, fixed in [#602](https://github.com/jonyardley/intrada/pull/602)) but at runtime, not startup. The heartbeat in \`Db::spawn_heartbeat\` (#290) keeps the connection warm but a request can still land in the narrow window between a stream dropping and the heartbeat noticing — the request panics, the user sees a 500.

## Fix

1. **Extract** the transient-error classifier from \`migrations.rs\` into \`db::is_transient_db_error\` so it's shared between startup migrations ([#602](https://github.com/jonyardley/intrada/pull/602)) and runtime queries. Migration callers updated to use the shared function; the classifier coverage tests in \`migrations.rs\` still exercise both paths.

2. **Add** \`Db::with_transient_retry\` — takes a closure returning \`Result<T, ApiError>\`, retries up to 2 times with backoff (50ms, 500ms) on \`ApiError::Internal(msg)\` where \`msg\` matches a known transient signature. **Reconnects between attempts** so a half-broken HTTP session is replaced before the next try. Total max wall time ≈ 600ms. Terminal errors (NotFound, Validation, Unauthorized, Internal with non-transient message) surface immediately so real bugs aren't masked.

3. **Apply** to the \`list_sets\` route handler. The helper passes through \`AppState::with_transient_retry\` so handlers don't reach into \`state.db\` directly:

\`\`\`rust
let sets = state.with_transient_retry(|conn| {
    let user_id = user_id.clone();
    async move { services::sets::list_sets(&conn, &user_id).await }
}).await?;
\`\`\`

## Out of scope

[#611](https://github.com/jonyardley/intrada/issues/611) — wrap the other read endpoints (\`/api/items\`, \`/api/sessions\`, etc.) with the same pattern. Same bug-shape, hasn't been flagged by Sentry yet.

Write endpoints (POST/PUT/DELETE) are deliberately not retried — naive retry could double-create. Needs explicit per-handler thinking with idempotency keys.

## Test plan

- [x] \`cargo fmt --all -- --check\` clean
- [x] \`cargo clippy -p intrada-api -- -D warnings\` clean
- [x] \`cargo test -p intrada-api\` — **147 pass**, including the migration classifier tests that now cover the shared \`is_transient_db_error\`.
- [ ] Manual verify post-deploy: INTRADA-API-36 stops accumulating events; new \`Transient DB error; reconnecting and retrying\` warning appears in logs when a stream drop happens.

## Refs

- [INTRADA-API-36](https://jon-yardley.sentry.io/issues/INTRADA-API-36)
- [#602](https://github.com/jonyardley/intrada/pull/602) — migration retry (INTRADA-API-2)
- [#611](https://github.com/jonyardley/intrada/issues/611) — apply to other read endpoints

author: guitargeek
body:
Closes #21912, which reported that a Python session that constructs a TRootBrowser segfaults at exit inside `TROOT::EndOfProcessCleanups()`.

To fix this, register an atexit hook that calls
`gROOT->GetListOfBrowsers()->Delete()` while the Python interpreter is still alive. This is the same workaround suggested in the issue, just made automatic. Honors `PyConfig.ShutDown`, and short-circuits if `_finalSetup()` never ran (no ROOT C++ runtime means nothing to clean up, and we do not want to drag cppyy in).

Why we cannot just call `EndOfProcessCleanups()` from atexit? That was the previous behaviour, removed in commit e9d2803 ("[python] Avoid interfering with gc at exit time"). Doing this would re-introduce test failures that the removal commit as fixed:

```
  pyunittests-bindings-pyroot-pythonizations-pyroot-pyz-tdirectory-attrsyntax
  pyunittests-bindings-pyroot-pythonizations-pyroot-pyz-tdirectoryfile-attrsyntax-get
```

`EndOfProcessCleanups()` tears down C++ objects that the TestCase classes still hold via CPyCppyy proxies (TFile / TDirectory). When CPython's gc walks those classes, it deallocates the proxies and reads memory ROOT just freed. Limiting the exit-time work to `TROOT::fBrowsers` leaves such objects untouched, so those tests stay green.

body: ## 👀 관련 이슈 #361 ## ✨ 작업한 내용 ### 1. Testcontainers 의존성 오류 수정 기존 Testcontainers 의존성 설정에서 artifact 이름이 잘못 지정되어 있던 거 같습니다(?) #### 기존 설정 ```gradle org.testcontainers:junit-jupiter:2.0.3 ``` #### 수정 후 ```gradle org.testcontainers:testcontainers-junit-jupiter:2.0.3 ``` ### 2. Redis 테스트 환경 충돌 수정 워크플로우가 변경되며, Redis가 필요한 통합 테스트에서는 `RedisTestContainerSupport`를 통해 테스트 코드 내부에서 Redis 컨테이너를 직접 실행하는 구조가 추가된 것 같습니다. 하지만, 동시에 `RedisConfig`에 추가된 설정으로 인해 test 환경에서 Redis Bean이 생성되지 않아 문제가 발생했습니다. ```java @Profile("!test") ``` 이로 인해 `profileImageRedisTemplate`, `RedissonClient` 등 Redis 관련 Bean을 필요로 하는 테스트에서 `ApplicationContext` 로딩 실패가 발생한 듯하여, test 환경에서도 Redis Bean이 정상적으로 생성될 수 있도록 해당 설정을 삭제하였습니다. 또한 `ServerApplicationTests`는 전체 Spring Context를 로딩하는 `@SpringBootTest` 기반 테스트이므로, Redis Bean 로딩을 위해 `RedisTestContainerSupport`를 상속하도록 수정했습니다. ### 3. FriendLockService 동시성 테스트 코드 개선 기존 `FriendLockService` 동시성 테스트가 의도와 다르게 여러 스레드의 실제 동시 호출 상황을 보장하지 못한 거 같습니다. #### 기존 방식 - 기존에는 단일 `CountDownLatch`를 사용하여 작업 완료 여부만 대기하는 구조 - 10개의 작업이 모두 완료되었는지는 보장할 수 있지만, 10개의 스레드가 동시에 `followWithLock()`을 호출했는지는 보장 X #### 수정 후 - `readyLatch`, `startLatch`, `doneLatch` 3개의 latch로 역할 분리 ```text [메인 테스트 스레드] → ExecutorService를 통해 테스트 스레드 10개 생성 ↓ [테스트 스레드 1 ~ 10] → readyLatch.countDown() → "준비 완료" 상태로 변경 → startLatch.await() 에서 대기 [메인 테스트 스레드] → readyLatch.await() → 모든 테스트 스레드가 준비될 때까지 대기 → readyLatch == 0 확인 ↓ [테스트 스레드 1 ~ 10] → 아직 startLatch.await() 에서 대기 중 → followWithLock() 아직 호출하지 않음 [메인 테스트 스레드] → startLatch.countDown() → "동시 출발" 신호 전달 ↓ [테스트 스레드 1 ~ 10] → await() 해제 → 거의 동시에 followWithLock() 호출 → Redisson 분산 락 경쟁 시작 [메인 테스트 스레드] → doneLatch.await() → 모든 테스트 스레드 작업 종료까지 대기 ↓ [테스트 스레드 1 ~ 10] → 성공 또는 실패 처리 → doneLatch.countDown() → 작업 종료 [메인 테스트 스레드] → doneLatch == 0 확인 → 성공 횟수 / 실패 횟수 / DB 저장 개수 검증 ``` ## 🌀 PR Point X ## 🍰 참고사항 - 혹시나 `RedisConfig`의 `@Profile("!test")` 설정이 꼭 필요한 것이라면 알려주시면 감사하겠습니다. - `NotificationService`의 변경된 로직이 기존 테스트 코드에 반영되지 않아 테스트 실패가 발생하고 있었습니다. 해당 파트를 담당하지 않은 관계로, 우선 테스트 통과를 목적으로 GPT를 활용하여 임시 수정하였습니다. 확인 부탁드립니다! ## 📷 스크린샷 또는 GIF | 기능 | 스크린샷 | | :--: | :------: | | 테스트 | | ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Tests** * 통합 테스트 인프라 개선 — Redis 관련 설정이 테스트 환경에도 적용되어 통합 테스트 신뢰성 향상 * 동시성 테스트 로직 보강으로 멀티스레드 상황 검증 강화 * 알림 관련 테스트 및 단위 테스트들에서 인터페이스 변화에 맞춘 검증 업데이트 및 정리 * **Chores** * 테스트 빌드/설정 선언 형식 정리 (기능 변경 없음) [![Review Change Stack](https://storage.googleapis.com/coderabbit_public_assets/review-stack-in-coderabbit-ui.svg)](https://app.coderabbit.ai/change-stack/UMC8-TeumTeum/BE/pull/362)

body:
This switches repository source files from the full Apache license block to the shorthand source header format. It also updates `telepact_project_cli` so `make license-header` rewrites supported files consistently to the new form.

- **Header format**
  - Replace per-file long-form Apache text with:
    - copyright line
    - SPDX identifier
  - Apply the new header across tracked source files in the repo

- **`telepact_project_cli` license-header logic**
  - Derive source headers from `NOTICE` as shorthand output instead of copying the full license text
  - Default the emitted license line to `SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0`
  - Continue honoring `.license-header-ignore`

- **Supported file handling**
  - Extend rewriting support to additional source file types used in the repo:
    - `.go`
    - `.rb`
    - `.tsx`
    - `.mjs`
    - shebang-based scripts without extensions
  - Preserve shebangs correctly when rewriting executable scripts

- **HTML/template behavior**
  - Handle files with leading HTML comment preambles without leaving stale long-form header blocks behind
  - Keep non-license preamble comments intact while replacing the generated header

- **Coverage updates**
  - Update `telepact_project_cli` tests to assert shorthand header output
  - Add cases for shebang scripts and HTML files with preambles

Example of the new generated header:

```ts
//|  Copyright The Telepact Authors
//|  SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
```

body:
This pull request makes significant improvements to the `log-ingestion` n8n workflow. The main changes include restructuring the workflow to add context-aware log remediation using an LLM (Groq) with a static fallback, enhancing the handling of CRITICAL logs, and improving the retrieval and formatting of recent log history. Additionally, some nodes and connections have been reorganized or removed for clarity and better flow.

Key changes include:

**LLM Integration and Remediation Enhancements:**
* Added a new sequence for CRITICAL logs that retrieves the five most recent logs for the relevant `source_id`, formats them, and sends them to an LLM (Groq) for remediation recommendations, with a static fallback if the LLM is unavailable. body:
## Summary

PR-5 of the Symbol Graph rollout. Adds the Knowledge Browser Symbols tab per [FEAT--SYMBOLS-WEB-TAB](gks/feat/FEAT--SYMBOLS-WEB-TAB.md).

- Plan: `/root/.claude/plans/symbol-graph.md`
- Predecessor: PR-4 (#60) shipped the CLI + 5 MCP tools

### What's in it

- **6 HTTP endpoints** (`src/symbols/api.ts`, registered from `src/index.ts`):
  - `GET /api/symbols` (capped 5000, `?offset&limit`)
  - `GET /api/symbols/stats` (returns meta.json)
  - `GET /api/symbols/search?q=&limit=` (mirrors `msp_symbol_search` scoring)
  - `GET /api/symbols/community/:id` (community + members + internal edges)
  - `GET /api/symbols/:id/neighbors?depth=1` (capped depth 3)
  - `GET /api/symbols/:id` (symbol + 5-neighbor preview)
  - All return `{ ok: true, ... }` on success; `404 { ok: false, error: "graph not built — run 'npm run msp:graph build' first" }` when SQLite/meta.json missing.

- **4 new React components** (`web/src/components/`):
  - `SymbolsTab.tsx` — parent, three-pane layout, empty-state with copy-to-clipboard build hint
  - `SymbolList.tsx` — community→file→symbol tree with kind/exported/community filters + 200ms-debounced search
  - `SymbolGraphView.tsx` — Cytoscape cose layout; HSL community colors; kind→shape mapping; edge style per type
  - `SymbolDetail.tsx` — file:line, `vscode://` link, exported badge, parent link, neighbors grouped by edge type

- **Feature flag** in `web/src/App.tsx`: Symbols tab gated behind `VITE_MSP_SYMBOL_GRAPH=1` env var OR `?symbols=1` URL param. PR-6 will remove the flag.

- **Typed fetcher** in `web/src/api.ts`: `getSymbols`, `getSymbol`, `getSymbolNeighbors`, `getSymbolCommunity`, `searchSymbols`, `getSymbolStats` (returns `null` on 404). All ids `encodeURIComponent`-ed at the boundary.

### Tests

10 backend tests in `test/api/symbols.test.ts` exercising the live HTTP routes via Node's built-in `fetch` against `app.listen(0)` — no new deps. Covers empty-state (graph not built), happy path for all 6 endpoints, 404 for unknown id, and `400` for empty `q`.

Skipped web component tests because no `@testing-library/react` / jsdom infrastructure exists in MSP and `package.json` says no new deps. Followed the plan's fallback ("add 1–2 backend tests in `test/api/symbols.test.ts` instead").

### Out of scope

No atoms, no new MCP tools, no CLI subcommands, no edits to PR-4 territory.

- [x] `npm run build`

- [x] `npm test` — 625 passed (was 615)

- [x] `npm run msp:check-links` — OK
- [ ] Manual smoke (recommended for reviewer): build a graph with `npm run msp:graph build`, run `npm run dev`, hit `?symbols=1`, click through.

## Summary
Three site-role enhancements bundled together — all about giving site accountants the same read-level access HO has, scoped to their own projects, without granting destructive actions.

### 1. Month filter on My Invoices
Same UI as HO's All Invoices list — \`<input type="month">\` next to the category filter, plus a "Clear month" link. Filters by the invoice's \`month\` bucket (falls back to \`invoice_date\` when month isn't set).

### 2. Outstanding per project on the site dashboard
- Server: \`SITE_COLUMNS\` now includes computed \`balance\` (invoice_amount − Σ(payments)). Aging data (\`total_paid\`, \`days_past_due\`, \`overdue\`) stays HO+mgmt only.
- Client: site dashboard's per-project cards show outstanding alongside total invoiced (red if > 0, green when settled). Renders for single-site accountants too, not just multi-site.

### 3. Vendor Master → Vendor Detail for site role
- Server: \`GET /vendors/:id/detail\` opens to site role; the service accepts a \`siteFilter\` and the controller passes the user's assigned sites so the invoice list never leaks another project's rows. \`stats\` (totalAmount, paidAmount, outstanding, oldestUnpaid) recomputed off the scoped invoices.
- Client: vendor names in Vendor Master are clickable for site users; the detail page reuses the existing UI; the HO-only Delete column stays hidden.

CLAUDE.md updated to reflect the new boundary.

## Deploy
\`./infra/prod/deploy.sh\` on EC2 — no migrations.

## What this changes

### Buyer flow becomes friction-free
Click any "Reserve my seat" → land on Razorpay → pay → done. No sign-in prompt before, no auth modal after.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| Click "Reserve my seat" → scrolls to pricing section → click again to go to Razorpay | Click "Reserve my seat" → directly opens Razorpay |
| Sign in button shown at the top of the page (friction before paying) | No Sign in button on first impression. Tiny "Already paid? Sign in" link in footer |
| After paying → site asks user to sign in again with the same email they just typed in Razorpay | After paying → Supabase emails them a magic link automatically. They click it → they're signed in |

### Files
- `index.html` — 5 Reserve buttons (top nav desktop/mobile, hero, urgency band, mobile sticky) now use the Razorpay-rewritten URL. Footer gains a small "Already paid? Sign in" trigger.
- `js/auth.js` — Empty nav-auth slot when logged out (no Sign in button). Still shows email + Sign out when signed in.
- `js/checkout.js` — Replaces post-payment auth modal with a toast. Adds `/?welcome=1` handler for the magic-link redirect. Wires the footer sign-in trigger to open the existing auth modal.
- `api/razorpay-webhook.js` — After recording the paid registration, calls `supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ email, emailRedirectTo: SITE_URL/?welcome=1 })`. Best-effort: errors are logged but don't fail the webhook (registration is already saved).

## Required follow-ups (manual)

1. **Customise the Supabase email template** so the magic link email reads like a workshop welcome instead of "Confirm your email":
   - Supabase Dashboard → **Authentication** → **Email Templates** → **Confirm signup**
   - Subject: `You're in! Here's your Get AI Ready access link`
   - Body (key bits): "Welcome to Get AI Ready Dubai. Click the button below to access your seat. You'll get the Zoom link 24h before Sunday's workshop."
   - Make sure the magic link button uses `{{ .ConfirmationURL }}` (the default).
2. **Add `SITE_URL=https://dubaiaicourse.vercel.app`** as a Vercel env var (optional — falls back to that URL if unset).
3. **Confirm Supabase email rate limits** — free tier is 2/hour, Pro is 4/hour by default. If you expect a payment burst (e.g. ad campaign), bump SMTP via Resend/SendGrid in Supabase settings.
4. **Test end-to-end** with a 1 AED Razorpay page (per your earlier note): pay → check inbox for magic link → click → land on `/?welcome=1` → verify nav shows your email.

## Test plan
- [ ] Click every "Reserve my seat" button on production → all open Razorpay payment page directly (no intermediate scroll)
- [ ] Pay with a real email via the 1 AED test page → arrive at `/?paid=1` → see "Payment received, check your email" toast
- [ ] Receive a magic link email within ~30s → click → land on `/?welcome=1` → see "You're in" toast → nav shows email + Sign out
- [ ] Verify `registrations` row has `paid=true` and `user_id` populated (auto-link trigger)

author: freezylemon
body:
Supersedes #72 which has become a bit of a mess.

I went to the std documentation to collect the traits implemented on u8/u16:
- arithmetic: !, +, -, *, /, %
- bitwise: |, &, ^, <<, >>
- comparison: PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord
- formatting: {} {:?} {:o} {:x} {:X} {:e} {:E} {:b}
- conversions: various (from/into, tryfrom/tryinto, FromStr)
- common misc: Clone, Default, Copy, Hash, Sum, Step, Product
- marker (nightly): ZeroablePrimitive, SimdElement, RangePattern, AtomicPrimitive,
- nightly/wip misc: NumBufferTrait, FunnelShift, Distribution
- misc internals: DisjointBitOr, CarrylessMul, CarryingMulAdd

It's notable that a lot of operations on integers (`checked_*`, `wrapping_*`, `unsigned_abs`, `abs_diff`, `log`, `pow` etc. etc. etc.) don't live in a trait but are just type-inherent methods. Even `num_traits` doesn't expose most of these, maybe because `std` has steadily been growing over the years.

I see two main problems with keeping arithmetics/bitwise operations "in" Pixel:
- maintenance burden, i.e. keeping up with std/num_traits adding new stuff
- questionable usability of arithmetics given type size limitations (how often do you actually want to work in a `u8`? any sum will quickly overflow)

So I suggest **dropping arithmetic and bitwise operations** from the Pixel trait entirely. This requires users to convert to some concrete numeric type before "working" on pixels.

Because there is exactly one of each `TryFrom`, `TryInto`, `From` and `Into` required by `T: Pixel`, types can be fully inferred even without outside "help":

```rs
let a = pix.into();                // always u16
let b = pix.try_into().unwrap();   // always u8
let pix = T::from(x);              // always u8
let pix = T::try_from(y).unwrap(); // always u16
```

If you want to widen a Pixel into an integer, you can do `u64::from(pix.into())` (which is infallible so no panics ever). If you want to narrow an integer into `Pixel`, you have to do it twice though: `Pixel::try_from(my_u64.try_into().expect("fits into u16")).expect("Pixel is u16")`.

author: copilot
body:
This updates the Flask project to deploy reliably on Vercel serverless Python by fixing app bootstrapping and tightening production runtime behavior. It also aligns DB/config behavior with non-ephemeral production requirements and documents the expected deployment flow.

- **Vercel runtime entrypoint**
  - `api/index.py` now exports the Flask app directly for `@vercel/python` instead of returning `app.wsgi_app` from a custom handler.
  - App config selection now supports `APP_ENV` with `FLASK_ENV` fallback via `get_config_name(...)`.

- **Production configuration hardening**
  - `config.py` now reads env values at app init and normalizes `postgres://` to `postgresql://`.
  - Production config enforces:
    - `JWT_SECRET_KEY` must be set (no dev fallback in prod).
    - `DATABASE_URL` must be persistent (rejects SQLite in production).

- **Database lifecycle in serverless**
  - Removed unconditional `db.create_all()` during app startup.
  - Added guarded table creation for local/dev scenarios (`DEBUG`, `TESTING`, or `RUN_DB_CREATE_ALL=true`).
  - Added explicit schema bootstrap command:
    - `flask --app "app:create_app()" init-db`

- **Static HTML routing compatibility**
  - Page routes now resolve HTML from repo root first, then `templates/`.
  - Missing files return explicit JSON 404, avoiding brittle path assumptions in serverless artifacts.

- **Deployment/docs/deps alignment**
  - Updated `README.md` and `VERCEL_DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md` with minimal Vercel production setup and DB init flow.
  - Updated `.env.example` (`APP_ENV`, `RUN_DB_CREATE_ALL`) and `.gitignore` (`.vercel/`).
  - Updated dependencies for production compatibility/security and Postgres support:
    - `PyJWT==2.12.1`
    - `python-Levenshtein==0.27.1`
    - `psycopg2-binary==2.9.9`

```python
# api/index.py
from app import create_app, get_config_name
app = create_app(get_config_name(default='production'))
```

5) Update `VERCEL_DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md` / `README.md` with accurate, minimal, step-by-step deployment instructions for Vercel.

author: turnerluke
body:
## Summary

Introduces `libs/cms_api/`, a sync Python client library for CMS public
APIs, wired into the workspace as a uv member so the rest of the project
can `from cms_api import ...`.

### What's covered

- **Socrata** (`data.cms.gov`, `data.medicaid.gov`): generic
  `iter_dataset` plus a typed wrapper for Medicare Part D Spending by
  Drug (`mhdd-npjx`).
- **NPPES**: `get_provider_by_npi` and `search_providers`, paginating
  up to the API's 1200-row reachable cap.
- **Healthcare.gov**: `get_glossary` and `get_articles` against the
  public content API. The Marketplace plan-finder API is intentionally
  out of scope — it has separate auth and will land in its own module.
- Shared `_http` module: `httpx` client + tenacity retry on transport
  errors and HTTP 429/5xx, with timeouts and retry knobs configurable
  via `CMS_API_*` env vars. Client errors (non-429 4xx) surface
  immediately rather than burning retry budget.

### Design notes

- Pydantic models use `extra="allow"` so year-suffixed and
  schema-drift columns flow through without library releases.
- Pagination yields generators rather than lists so streaming-large-
  dataset callers don't materialise the full result set.
- No raw `httpx.Response` exposed from public APIs; ad-hoc HTTP needs
  can build a client with `cms_api._http.build_client`.

### Verification

- `uv run pytest` from `libs/cms_api/`: 28 passed, 95% coverage
  (threshold 80%).
- `uv run mypy` from `libs/cms_api/`: strict mode, no issues.
- `uv run pre-commit run --all-files`: all hooks pass.
- Root project structure tests pick up the new sub-project and pass.

### Out of scope

- Marketplace plan-finder API (gated, separate work).
- Hospital MRF scraping and bulk-file downloads (handled separately
  per the original brief).
- Adding more typed wrappers — the existing pattern is documented in
  the library README; new endpoints get added as pipelines need them.

author: odrobnik
body:
Closes the verification loop on the polyglot subprocess unification:

- [Cocoanetics/ShellKit#1](https://github.com/Cocoanetics/ShellKit/issues/1) — `Shell.processLauncher` primitive ✅ merged
- [Cocoanetics/SwiftBash#19](https://github.com/Cocoanetics/SwiftBash/pull/19) — `BashProcessLauncher` resolves against the bash command registry ✅ merged
- [Cocoanetics/SwiftScript#5](https://github.com/Cocoanetics/SwiftScript/pull/5) — `import Subprocess` bridge routes through `Shell.current.processLauncher` ✅ merged

A SwiftScript script under SwiftBash that does `Subprocess.run(Executable.name(\"echo\"), ...)` should **not** reach `posix_spawn`; it should hit `EchoCommand` (the pure-Swift bash builtin). Two tests confirm this end-to-end — they're the script-author-visible payoff for the layered work above.

## Tests

`subprocessRunRoutesThroughBashCommandRegistry` — script:
```swift
#!/usr/bin/env swift-script
import Subprocess
let r = try await Subprocess.run(
    Executable.name(\"echo\"),
    arguments: [\"hello-from-bash-builtin\"],
    output: Output.string(limit: 4096))
if let out = r.standardOutput, r.terminationStatus.isSuccess {
    print(\"got=\\(out)\", terminator: \"\")
}
```
Bridge calls `Shell.current.processLauncher.launch(...)`, `BashProcessLauncher` resolves `\"echo\"` to the registered `EchoCommand`, the captured `standardOutput` round-trips back to the script and prints `got=hello-from-bash-builtin\\n`. No `posix_spawn`, no host `/bin/echo` involvement.

`subprocessRunWithCanonicalPathHitsBashBuiltin` — same flow with `Executable.path(\"/bin/echo\")`. Verifies the canonical-bin-path resolution rule (PR #19's P2 fix): `/bin/echo` matches `BinCatalog.knownPaths[\"echo\"]`, so the launcher dispatches to the registered builtin instead of throwing `ProcessLaunchUnresolved`.

Both pass locally.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on macOS / iOS / tvOS / watchOS / Linux / Windows / Android
- [x] Local: 2/2 e2e tests pass

author: pat21889
body:
## Summary

Full code review of all Verilog source files and testbenches identified 8 bugs ranging from critical to low severity. All are fixed in this PR and documented in `FPGA_Video_Processing_Debug_Report.md`.

### ?? Critical

- **RGB format conflict** (`src/ov7670_init.v`): COM15 was `0xD0` which selects RGB565, while register `0x8C=0x02` enables xRGB444 - mutually exclusive. Changed COM15 to `0xC0` (full output range only) so xRGB444 is the sole active format, matching what the capture module's `d_latch[11:0]` extraction expects.
- **Hardware reset never fired** (`src/top.v`): `cam_rst` was hardwired `1'b1`, silently bypassing the `ov7670_init` reset FSM. The `cam_rst_from_init` wire was driven but never connected. Fixed: `assign cam_rst = cam_rst_from_init`.

### ?? Medium

- **VGA sync delay off by 1** (`src/top.v`): Pixel pipeline through `vga_display` has exactly 3 register stages (`bram_d1` ? `p_curr` ? `vga_r`), but sync was delayed 4 stages (`hsync_d4`). Reduced to `hsync_d3`/`vsync_d3` to eliminate 1-pixel horizontal boundary shift.
- **Wrong PCLK timing constraint** (`constraints/constraints.xdc`): Constraint said 41.667 ns (24 MHz) but XCLK=25 MHz with PLL bypass means PCLK=40.000 ns. Corrected for accurate Vivado timing analysis.
- **Testbench SCL edge count wrong** (`sim/tb_sccb_master.v`): STOP condition generates a 28th SCL rising edge; assertion checked for 27. The test was printing FAIL for a correctly operating module.

### ?? Low

Rewrote task, updated `send_line` and Test 5 reference values. Also fixed `pixel_count <=` to `=` (non-blocking assignment on integer variable).
- **LED[3] = cam_pclk** (`src/top.v`): 25 MHz signal appears permanently on - useless for debugging. Changed to `mmcm_locked` (visible PLL boot status).
- **cam_rst inconsistency**: Resolved as a direct consequence of the BUG-02 cam_rst fix above.

## Summary

Три дрібниці що випливли під час першого end-to-end тесту:

1. **`alwaysOutputData=true` на node 17 Get Last Dashboard Msg.** На першому ж запуску в чаті, де dashboard ще не відправлявся, SELECT повертає 0 рядків і n8n зупиняв ВЕСЬ workflow. Тепер вузол завжди емітить хоча б порожній item, downstream (18/19/20/21) добігає до Telegram.

2. **`parse_mode=HTML` на всіх 7 sendMessage Telegram-нодах.** Telegram Web рендерив `JOB_SEARCH` у dashboard як `JOB`+italic`SEARCH` (інтерпретував `_` як markdown). HTML-режим не чіпає підкреслення, рендериться чесно. Текст у нас без HTML-тегів, тому виглядає як plain.

3. **node 18 Format Dashboard — `escapeHtml(...)` на user-controlled рядках** (category name, code, activity). Belt-and-suspenders, щоб ніяка `<` в назві активності не зламала HTML-рендеринг.

4. **`/start` → та сама гілка що `/help`.** `/start` — це auto-launch-команда яку Telegram кидає при першому відкритті бота. Падати в TODO-стаб для нового користувача незручно.

## Verified

End-to-end на живому інстансі ПЕРЕД цим PR-ом вже працювали:
- explicit-формат (fast path, без AI)
- AI-класифікація для повідомлень без `[CODE]`
- clarification-question для multi-activity без точних длительностей
- `/goal_week` з progress bar
- `/delete_last` з auto-recompute dashboard

Цей PR — лише поліровка рендеру.

## Як підкотити

Після мерджу:
1. У GitHub Actions → Deploy to qoq-dev → Run workflow (деплой на сервер)
2. У n8n UI: Workflows → старий (поточний) workflow → видалити, тоді Import from File → `workflows/time-tracker-main.json` з нового checkout-у
3. Активувати, ще раз credentials якщо n8n не запам'ятав
4. Тест: `/start` має повернути help, dashboard має відправитись з першого ж запиту в чистому чаті

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/open-webui/open-webui/compare/v0.9.3...v0.9.3)

##### Added

- 🔇 **Voice Mode mute control.** Voice Mode now includes a dedicated mute toggle with an "M" shortcut and auto-unmute after assistant playback, so you can prevent accidental interruptions from background noise without leaving the call overlay. [Commit](https://redirect.github.com/open-webui/open-webui/commit/072d2000f35a9f7b96342fa9bb28f925a92e7b4c), [#​23832](https://redirect.github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/23832)
- 🚀 **Faster prompt list loading.** Prompt and prompt-tag pages now load much faster for non-admin users, even with large prompt libraries, because accessible prompts are filtered efficiently in a single database query. [#​24288](https://redirect.github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/24288), [#​24258](https://redirect.github.com/open-webui/open-webui/discussions/24258)
- ⚡ **Faster chat history loading.** Chat history maps now load from normalized message records when available, reducing overhead for large conversations while preserving fallback behavior for legacy chats. [Commit](https://redirect.github.com/open-webui/open-webui/commit/485d689cfd1ef8b9e7f77cd7b535b8b8747dff1f), [#​23159](https://redirect.github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/23159)
- 🗑️ **Delete from conversation menu.** You can now delete the current conversation directly from the chat menu with a confirmation step, so cleanup is faster without searching through the full chat list. [Commit](https://redirect.github.com/open-webui/open-webui/commit/ef6d4f2d6c4b79c7e12e864a4fcb6a57ee84e5d4), [#​24329](https://redirect.github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/24329)
- ⬆️ **Scroll to Top shortcut.** Long conversations now include a Scroll to Top action in the chat menu when you are away from the top, making it much faster to jump back to the beginning of a chat. [Commit](https://redirect.github.com/open-webui/open-webui/commit/cdfcbc4af6e9aec835b88dc1806a2a46711e6947), [#​24133](https://redirect.github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/24133)
- 📅 **Calendar creation flow.** Users can now create calendars from a dedicated modal and a quick-add action in the calendar sidebar, making calendar setup faster from the calendar workspace. [Commit](https://redirect.github.com/open-webui/open-webui/commit/34146ab60f5dc1a2f8bdda8e61ce02797233a25d), [Commit](https://redirect.github.com/open-webui/open-webui/commit/1baf73bdd56f4e5ded12a4bd3c168f4d2a70b840)
- 🧭 **Unified model unload controls.** Administrators can now unload running models from the model selector across supported providers, with loaded-state indicators shown for Ollama and llama.cpp models. [Commit](https://redirect.github.com/open-webui/open-webui/commit/4fe2de78643c2213652190d2820f4e8d9f4f89cc)
- ⚡ **Health check responsiveness.** Health and readiness probes now avoid blocking database calls and skip sync session commit handling on probe paths, improving responsiveness and reducing false unready transitions during database pressure. [#​24380](https://redirect.github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/24380), [#​24384](https://redirect.github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/24384)
- 🎛️ **Playground controls panel.** The Playground now includes a dedicated Controls toggle so you can adjust parameters like temperature and related settings per chat run without changing model-level defaults. [Commit](https://redirect.github.com/open-webui/open-webui/commit/c6763521c00f042a28829e33fb6f1b7355054046), [#​24103](https://redirect.github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/24103)
- 🎙️ **STT file extension controls.** Administrators can now configure which audio file extensions are accepted for speech-to-text uploads, helping enforce safer and more predictable upload policies. [Commit](https://redirect.github.com/open-webui/open-webui/commit/4754ece4a2de5bba85a1d53af2dc8d24fdfb58be)
- 📷 **Remembered call camera selection.** Voice call overlay now remembers your last selected camera and restores it automatically when available, so you do not need to reselect it every time you start voice mode. [Commit](https://redirect.github.com/open-webui/open-webui/commit/5c3edc2539ac4d92c4cc2d37079549995203238a), [#​24416](https://redirect.github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/24416)
- 👥 **User group prompt variable.** System and template prompts now support the "{{USER\_GROUPS}}" variable, which expands to the user’s group memberships so prompts can adapt to role- or access-based context automatically. [Commit](https://redirect.github.com/open-webui/open-webui/commit/c1202a23277abb8e7080271a929dcc9d29b67e66), [#​24462](https://redirect.github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/24462)

author: saiprasad-wissen
body:
**AI-generated patch by Sentinel**

**Root Cause:** The payment was successfully persisted but the corresponding order status update failed due to a lack of atomicity in the database operations.

**What changed:** Added `@Transactional` annotation (from `org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional`) to the `processPayment` method — which owns both the payment insert and the `orderService.markOrderPaid()` call. Without this annotation those two writes were independent: if `markOrderPaid` failed after the payment record was already stored, the system was left in a split-brain state (payment committed, order still un-paid), which is the exact `ORDER_UPDATE_FAILURE` reported in INC-20260509122412-044E31. Wrapping both writes in a single Spring-managed transaction ensures that any failure in either operation causes the entire unit of work to be rolled back atomically. The corresponding import `org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional` was also added; no other logic was altered.

**Patched file:** `src/main/java/com/hacksys/backend/service/PaymentService.java`

author: arkohut
body:
Fixes #96.

## Problem

Fresh `memos serve` on a clean database crashes during alembic migrations:

```
OperationalError: no such tokenizer: simple
[SQL: DELETE FROM entities_fts WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM _dedup_victims)]
```

Reported on Windows but reproduces on every OS — it is not platform-specific.

## Root cause

Two stacked bugs in the first-launch path of migration `fa40c9f33551`:

1. **`simple` tokenizer not loaded for alembic.** Runtime SQLite connections load both `simple` (the bundled FTS5 tokenizer) and `sqlite_vec` via `SQLiteInitializer._load_sqlite_extensions` (`memos/databases/initializers.py:218-231`). Alembic builds its own engine in `memos/migrations/alembic/env.py` and only loaded `sqlite_vec`. `fa40c9f33551` is the first migration to issue SQL against `entities_fts`, so the latent gap surfaced here.

2. **`op.create_unique_constraint` is unsupported on SQLite.** Once (1) is fixed, the same migration crashes with `NotImplementedError: No support for ALTER of constraints in SQLite dialect` because SQLite has no `ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT`.

## Fix

- `memos/migrations/alembic/env.py`: mirror `_load_sqlite_extensions` — load the platform-specific `libsimple` / `simple.dll`, register the jieba dict, then load `sqlite_vec`.
- `memos/migrations/alembic/versions/fa40c9f33551_*.py`: wrap unique-constraint add/drop in `op.batch_alter_table("entities")`. SQLite goes through alembic's copy-and-move strategy; Postgres path is unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] `rm -rf ~/.memos && memos serve` on a clean DB completes migrations
- [x] Verified resulting `entities` table carries `CONSTRAINT entities_library_filepath_unique UNIQUE (library_id, filepath)`
- [ ] Spot-check on Windows by the reporter (cc @heroje)

body:
## Summary

Implements Phase 1 of the continuity plugin per `.claude/plans/2026-05-07-implementation-plan.md`: the write surface that turns the 2026-05-07 / 2026-05-08 architectural decisions into running code.

- **`WriteProvider` interface** (`lib/write_provider.py`) — abstract write surface with `write(kind, id, frontmatter, body)` and `exists(kind, id)`. `kind` is a continuity-namespaced string (`cont.insight`, `cont.decision`, …) so memory plugin can later interpret it as schema.
- **`VaultWriteProvider`** (`lib/vault_write_provider.py`) — first concrete impl. Maps kinds to PARA paths under `<vault>/10-projects/<project>/{insights,decisions}/<id>.md`. Atomic write (`tempfile.mkstemp` + `os.replace`), YAML frontmatter via pyyaml, idempotent. Vault-path resolution mirrors `VaultProvider`.
- **`MemoryWriteProvider` stub** (`lib/memory_write_provider.py`) — raises `NotImplementedError` with a clear message; the seam Phase 2.5 will activate.
- **Config selector** (`lib/config.py`) — reads `~/.config/continuity/config.yaml` (overridable via `CONTINUITY_CONFIG_DIR` for tests). Default `write_provider: vault`.
- **`record-insight` CLI subcommand + `record_insight` MCP tool** — composes frontmatter (date, project, type=insight, title), generates id (`<date>-<slug>`), routes through the configured provider, returns the `kind:id` reference.

## Phase 1 exit met

From a Claude session, `continuity__record_insight` (or `continuity record-insight --project X --title T`) writes a frontmatter-tagged markdown file to the right vault PARA path. The same call against `write_provider: memory` raises a clear "memory plugin not yet available" error — the seam Phase 2.5 activates.

## Notes for reviewers

- Two commits: `1b20514` (1.1+1.2) and `b5327f7` (1.3–1.7). They split cleanly along interface vs. surrounding wiring + tests, in case you want to review them independently.
- Per the 2026-05-07 `vault-writer-stays-continuity-local` decision, `VaultWriteProvider` is owned by continuity for now; promotion to a shared layer is a Phase-2-entry decision.
- This is the first instance of the 2026-05-08 cross-plugin `(reader, writer)` contract — VaultWriteProvider + MemoryWriteProvider stub are already two impls of the same interface shape, validating the pattern in the small.

## Test plan

- [x] `python -m pytest -q` — 59 passed (was 24 in Phase 0)
- [x] Smoke test: `VaultWriteProvider.write` end-to-end with valid kinds, atomic semantics (no temp leftovers), idempotent overwrite
- [x] Error paths: unknown kind, missing project in frontmatter, no vault dir
- [x] CLI integration test exercising stdin → composer → VaultWriteProvider
- [ ] Live `continuity__record_insight` MCP tool call from a Claude session against the real vault (manual; not gated by CI yet)

author: henrycjchen
body:
## Summary

The static `CITY_ID` map in `clis/dianping/utils.js` only covers ~20 cities, so `opencli dianping search "X" --city 汕头` (or any other Chinese name / pinyin slug not on that list) fails with `ArgumentError`. Adding the missing cityIds by hand doesn't scale to dianping's full city list and silently goes stale when the site renumbers cities.

This PR adds an async resolver that falls back to `www.dianping.com` when the static map misses, so any city dianping itself supports is searchable without further patches.

Resolution strategy:

- Numeric input → pass through unchanged.
- Static map hit → fast path, no network. `utils.CITY_ID` is **untouched**.
- Pinyin slug (e.g. `shantou`) → `goto /<slug>`, parse `cityId` out of any `/search/keyword/{id}/` link rendered server-side on the per-city landing page.
- Chinese name (e.g. `汕头`) → `goto /citylist`, walk anchors to build a Chinese-name → pinyin map, then resolve the slug as above.

Resolved (input → cityId) pairs are memoized per-process so repeat searches skip both navigations.

Implemented as a new module (`clis/dianping/cityResolver.js`) so `utils.js` stays minimal and the existing synchronous `resolveCityId` / `CITY_ID` API keeps working for direct callers and the existing test suite.

## Files

- `clis/dianping/cityResolver.js` (new) — `resolveCityIdAsync(page, cityArg)` plus the pure DOM extractors `buildCitylistMap` and `extractCityIdFromPage`.
- `clis/dianping/search.js` — swap the synchronous `resolveCityId` call for `await resolveCityIdAsync(page, kwargs.city)` (wrapped in `wrapDianpingStep` for consistent error mapping); update the `--city` help text.
- `clis/dianping/dianping.test.js` — new suite covering the resolver paths.
- `cli-manifest.json` — regenerated by `npm run build` for the new help text.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run clis/dianping` — 27/27 passed.
- [x] `npm test` — 3196 passed, 1 skipped, no new failures.
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- [x] `opencli validate` — 0 errors.
- [x] Live spot-check: `opencli dianping search 烧鸟 --city 汕头` resolves cityId 207 via `/citylist` + `/shantou` and returns Shantou shops (verified against `https://www.dianping.com/shantou`).

New unit tests cover:

- null/empty/whitespace → `null`; numeric pass-through; static-map hits never touch the page.
- pinyin fallback navigates `/<slug>` once and caches the result.
- Chinese-name fallback navigates `/citylist` then `/<slug>`, and caches under both the Chinese name and the discovered pinyin.
- Garbage / non-pinyin-non-Chinese input rejected with `ArgumentError` before any navigation.
- Chinese name not present on `/citylist` rejected with `ArgumentError` after a single navigation.
- Per-city page lacking a `/search/keyword/{id}/` link surfaces a `CommandExecutionError`.
- JSDOM tests for `buildCitylistMap` (drops non-city slugs like `/citylist`, `/promo`, member pages, cross-domain links; keeps Chinese-labeled city anchors) and `extractCityIdFromPage` (picks up the first matching link; returns `null` on a blocked page).

author: aslmk
body:
# Description
This PR refactors logging across the system as the first step toward proper observability. The project already has a basic stack in place (Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Tempo, Alloy), but the logging it relied on was immature.
This PR lays the foundation before more advanced improvements (MDC context, trace ID propagation, custom Grafana dashboards, etc.) are added on top. 

Note: mechanisms like MDC and trace IDs are intentionally out of scope here and will be addressed in follow-up PRs.

# Changes Overview
- corrected log levels across the codebase (e.g. demoted verbose operational noise from `INFO` → `DEBUG`)
- added missing log statements for key business events that were previously invisible to Loki
- removed redundant or misleading log entries that polluted log streams

# Result
Business-critical events are now consistently captured at the right verbosity level. Loki receives a clean, meaningful log stream.

body:
## Summary

Sweep of `README.md` and in-code docstrings. Goal was to rewrite docstrings toward WHY over HOW where it adds context, and to fix examples and contradictions found along the way.

### Bugs surfaced via the doc review
- `target_context.__str__` referenced a nonexistent `self.query` (would `AttributeError`)
- `flux_stats.create` passed a single `Source` where `filter()` expects `List[Source]`
- README's `Target` example used degrees, but `Target.__post_init__` requires radians
- README's `tods()` example omitted the required `path` argument (would `TypeError`)
- README's TOML example omitted the required `amp` field (would `KeyError`)
- `locate_samples` docstring described "values"; the implementation returns sample indices
- `Scenario` docstring listed `target_profiles`; the actual field is `search_profiles`
- `search._run_search` return doc said "divergence"; should be "normal matrix" (matches the rest of the codebase)
- `mock_instrument` referenced the old `timedomain` package name

### Docstring rewrites (HOW → WHY)
`FilterOptions` & `filter()`, `FluxEstimator.estimate` / `.estimate_individual`, `RemovalProfile`, `FluxStat`/`FluxStatResult`, `Config`, `PeriodTimingModel`, `BarycentricTimingModel`, `jansky_sr` / `beam_sr`, `PmatTotTransient`, the `Instrument` / `TOD` / `PointingModel` protocols, and `Targeting`.

### Smaller cleanups
- Removed stale `# TODO: allow for multiple sources to be filtered out at once` in `filters.py` — the loop in `filter()` already handles it
- Noted via inheritance docstrings that `Source`-typed parameters accept `Target` instances (no rename)
- Called out the ACT-only constraint on `BarycentricTimingModel` because of the `enlib` dependency

author: ayuxsh009
body:
## Problem

`reportUser` in `UserSide.sol` had no authentication or duplicate-report protection. Any address — including unregistered users — could repeatedly call the function to blacklist any user after just 101 calls.

This allowed attackers to instantly and permanently blacklist doctors or patients, effectively causing a denial of service against legitimate users.

## Fix
Closes #71

Added validation checks before incrementing the report count:

1. Caller must be a registered user
2. Users cannot report themselves
3. Each user can report another user only once

Also introduced a `hasReported` mapping to track reporter-target relationships and prevent duplicate submissions.

## Changes

* Hardened `reportUser` with authorization and validation checks
* Added self-report prevention
* Added duplicate-report protection
* Added `hasReported` mapping:

  ```solidity
  mapping(uint256 => mapping(uint256 => bool)) public hasReported;
  ```

## Security Impact

This prevents malicious actors from mass-reporting and arbitrarily blacklisting legitimate users through repeated calls.

author: dirien
body:
## Summary

Both LoadBalancer-exposed UIs were unreachable externally because the existing NetworkPolicies only permit *in-cluster* sources:

- `adk` namespace: the `default-deny` from #219 + `allow-ingress-monitoring` (only allows from `gmp-system`) → external LB traffic dropped at pod boundary.
- `flux-system` namespace: the flux-operator chart's own `flux-operator-web` NetworkPolicy uses `from: namespaceSelector: {}`, which matches in-cluster pods only.

Add two NetworkPolicies with no `from:` clause (any source allowed) on the relevant pod ports so the public LB IPs actually work:

| Namespace | Policy | Pod | Port |
|---|---|---|---|
| `adk` | `allow-ingress-http` | `app.kubernetes.io/name=adk-agent` | 8000 |
| `flux-system` | `allow-ingress-flux-web-external` | `app.kubernetes.io/name=flux-operator` | 9080 |

K8s NetworkPolicy is additive — these layer on top of existing rules without weakening monitoring scrape, default-deny egress posture, or the CCNP metadata-server lockdown.

## Production note

These policies expose the Flux Operator UI (full GitOps state, source URLs, secrets references) and an unauthenticated ADK agent (prompt abuse, Vertex AI cost) on public anycast LBs. Acceptable for short-lived workshop clusters; for production drop both and use port-forward, IAP, or a VPN. The PR's YAML comments call this out.

## Test plan
- [ ] After merge + Flux reconcile, `curl http://<flux-web-lb-ip>/` reaches the operator web UI
- [ ] `curl http://<adk-lb-ip>/list-apps` returns `["capital_agent"]`
- [ ] `kubectl -n flux-system get networkpolicy` shows `allow-ingress-flux-web-external`
- [ ] `kubectl -n adk get networkpolicy` shows `allow-ingress-http`
- [ ] Managed Prometheus collectors still scrape /metrics (existing `allow-ingress-monitoring` policy intact)

## SPEC-V3R2-RT-004 — Typed Session State + Phase Checkpoint

> **Phase**: v3.0.0 — Phase 2 — Runtime Hardening
> **Module**: `internal/session/`
> **Priority**: P1 High
> **Breaking**: false (additive typed schema on top of existing `.moai/state/`)
> **Lifecycle**: spec-anchored

## Summary

Plan documents for SPEC-V3R2-RT-004 are ready for plan-auditor review. This SPEC formalizes moai's cross-phase and cross-iteration state as a typed Go schema with immutable updates checkpointed at every phase boundary, closes problem-catalog **P-C02** (no sub-agent context isolation primitive) and **P-C05** (no cache-prefix discipline), and adds **`moai state {dump,show-blocker}`** CLI subcommand for human-readable inspection.

## Goal (purpose)

- **Structural (P5 + P6)**: Every phase boundary (`plan` → `run` → `sync`) writes a typed checkpoint file that captures all inputs the next phase needs. The next phase reads the file, not the prior conversation. Closes **P-C02**.
- **Safety (P4 + P11)**: Sprint Contract state (SPEC-V3R2-HRN-002) and evaluator fresh-judgment memory boundaries require a durable substrate that survives agent-level memory resets. Checkpoint files are that substrate.

## Scope

### In-Scope

- `Phase` typed enum (9 values: plan, run, sync, design, review, fix, loop, db, mx)
- `PhaseState` Go struct (`Phase, SPECID, Checkpoint, BlockerRpt, UpdatedAt, Provenance`)
- `Checkpoint` typed interface + `PlanCheckpoint`, `RunCheckpoint`, `SyncCheckpoint` concrete variants
- `BlockerReport` struct for `interrupt()`-equivalent surfacing
- `SessionStore` interface with 6 methods (`Checkpoint`, `Hydrate`, `AppendTaskLedger`, `WriteRunArtifact`, `RecordBlocker`, `ResolveBlocker`)
- Canonical `.moai/state/` file layout per master §5.6
- Provenance tagging on every state mutation (`SrcUser`/`SrcProject`/`SrcLocal`/`SrcSession`/`SrcHook` subset)
- Validator/v10 schema tags on all typed checkpoints; `Checkpoint()` validates before writing
- Crash-resume semantics: STALE_SECONDS primitive (default 3600s, configurable via `ralph.yaml`); on hydration, stale checkpoint prompts user via AskUserQuestion
- `moai state dump` and `moai state show-blocker` CLI subcommands
- `--resume` flag bypassing the staleness AskUserQuestion prompt
- Cross-platform advisory file locking (Unix `flock` + Windows `LockFileEx`) with 3-retry / 10ms-backoff
- Team-mode per-agent checkpoint merge with bubble-mode blocker routing

### Out-of-Scope

- Settings file multi-layer merge (resolver) — SPEC-V3R2-RT-005
- Hook JSON protocol — SPEC-V3R2-RT-001
- Sprint Contract durable state schema — SPEC-V3R2-HRN-002
- Ralph `/moai loop` outer-loop flow — SPEC-V3R2-WF-003
- Memdir typed taxonomy — SPEC-V3R2-EXT-001
- Agent `memory:` field in frontmatter — SPEC-V3R2-ORC-001

## Plan Documents

| Document | Purpose | Size |
|----------|---------|------|
| `spec.md` | EARS requirements + ACs (existing, v0.1.0) | 24180 bytes |
| `plan.md` | Implementation plan (M1-M5 milestones, traceability matrix, mx_plan, plan-audit-ready checklist) | new |
| `research.md` | Deep research (12 sections, 30 file:line anchors, library evaluation, dependency analysis) | new |
| `acceptance.md` | 15 ACs in Given/When/Then format with edge cases + test mapping | new |
| `tasks.md` | 33 tasks (T-RT004-01..33) across M1-M5 with owner roles + dependencies | new |
| `progress.md` | Live progress tracker + paste-ready session-handoff resume message | new |

## EARS Requirements Summary

- **24 REQs across 6 categories**: Ubiquitous (8), Event-Driven (6), State-Driven (3), Optional (4), Unwanted (4), Complex (2)
- **15 ACs all map to REQs (100% coverage)**
- **Traceability matrix**: 27 REQ → 15 AC → 33 tasks (verified in `plan.md` §1.4)

## Implementation Methodology

`.moai/config/sections/quality.yaml`: `development_mode: tdd`. Run phase MUST follow RED → GREEN → REFACTOR per `.claude/rules/moai/workflow/spec-workflow.md`.

- **M1 (RED)**: ~11 failing tests covering AC-04, AC-05, AC-06, AC-08, AC-09, AC-10, AC-14, AC-15 + audit lint for AC-11
- **M2 (GREEN part 1)**: validator/v10 tags + atomic-write helper. AC-01, AC-09, AC-15 GREEN.
- **M3 (GREEN part 2)**: cross-platform advisory locking. AC-10 GREEN.
- **M4 (GREEN part 3)**: blocker-file scan + filename rename + HydrateWithOpts + STALE_SECONDS config + in-flight detection + team merge. AC-04, AC-05, AC-06, AC-07, AC-08, AC-14 GREEN.
- **M5 (GREEN part 4 + REFACTOR + Trackable)**: `moai state` CLI + cache-prefix invariant + retention_days + AskUserQuestion audit + CHANGELOG + 7 MX tags. AC-11, AC-12, AC-13 GREEN.

## Risks (Top 3)

1. **Validator/v10 dependency from SPEC-V3R2-SCH-001 not yet merged** (M, H) — Mitigation: check `go.mod` at run-phase plan-audit gate; add direct dependency if absent.
2. **Cache-prefix invariant comment ignored by future contributors** (L, H) — Mitigation: `@MX:ANCHOR` tag on `hydrate.go`; future CI grep can verify the comment string preservation.
3. **Concurrent test races flaky on slow Windows runners** (M, L) — Mitigation: `t.Skip("requires fast disk")` if timing margin insufficient.

Full 11-risk table in `plan.md` §5.

## Dependencies

### Blocked by

- SPEC-V3R2-SCH-001 (validator/v10 — at-risk, mitigation defined)
- SPEC-V3R2-RT-005 (Source enum subset — referenced not blocking)
- SPEC-V3R2-CON-001 (FROZEN zone declaration — completed per Wave 6)

### Blocks

- SPEC-V3R2-HRN-002 (Sprint Contract durable state)
- SPEC-V3R2-WF-003 (Multi-mode router `/moai loop` Ralph layout)
- SPEC-V3R2-WF-004 (Agentless fixed pipelines audit trail)

### Related (non-blocking)

- SPEC-V3R2-RT-001, RT-002, EXT-001, EXT-004, ORC-001, CON-003

## Plan-Audit-Ready Checklist

All 15 criteria PASS per `plan.md` §8:

- [x] Frontmatter v0.1.0 schema
- [x] HISTORY entry for v0.1.0
- [x] 24 EARS REQs across 6 categories

- [x] Acceptance.md G/W/T format with edge cases
- [x] tasks.md owner roles aligned with TDD methodology

## Worktree Discipline

[HARD] All run-phase work executes in `/Users/goos/.moai/worktrees/moai-adk/SPEC-V3R2-RT-004` on branch `plan/SPEC-V3R2-RT-004` (initial) or sibling `feature/SPEC-V3R2-RT-004-typed-state` (run phase).

[HARD] All filesystem operations use `filepath.Join` / `filepath.Abs`; tests use `t.TempDir()` per `CLAUDE.local.md` §6.

[HARD] Code comments in Korean; commit messages in Korean (per `.moai/config/sections/language.yaml`).

## Test Plan

- [ ] M1 RED gate: ~11 new tests fail with documented sentinels; existing tests still GREEN
- [ ] M2 GREEN part 1: AC-01, AC-09, AC-15 turn GREEN
- [ ] M3 GREEN part 2: AC-10 turns GREEN on Linux/macOS/Windows CI matrix

- [ ] `go vet ./...` and `golangci-lint run` pass with zero warnings
- [ ] All required CI checks green: Lint, Test (ubuntu/macos/windows), Build (5 platforms), CodeQL

## Next Action

After plan-auditor PASS on this PR:

author: inacionery
body:
## Summary

Adds a Paperclip-platform guardrail that blocks an agent-authored `PATCH /api/issues/:id` transition to `status: done` while the issue's execution workspace still has uncommitted changes that touch repo files. Mechanical complement to the doc-rule guidance — an agent currently has to read the convention to apply it; this enforces it at the API boundary.

### What changed

- **`server/src/services/execution-workspaces.ts`** (+150 lines)
  Exports `inspectExecutionWorkspaceDirtyForDoneTransition`. Resolves the workspace's `cwd` / `providerRef`, runs `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all`, ignores entries under `.paperclip/worktrees/`, and returns either a capped sample of dirty/untracked files (with a total count) or a structured skip reason: `no_local_path`, `path_missing`, `shared_workspace`, `provider_unsupported`, `git_error`. The skip reasons let the route make a clean decision.

- **`server/src/routes/issues.ts`** (+55/-1)
  Wires the inspector into `PATCH /api/issues/:id`. Scope of the gate:
  - actor is an `agent` (board users still pass through),
  - requested status is `done` and current status is not already `done`,
  - issue has an `executionWorkspaceId`,
  - issue does not carry a `no-code` label (case-insensitive).

  All skip reasons (no local path, shared workspace, etc.) pass through silently so the guardrail never blocks work it cannot reason about. On a real dirty workspace, the route returns `422` with `code: "execution_workspace_dirty"` and a structured `details` payload (workspace path, dirty/untracked sample, total entry count, bypass hints) so the heartbeat reminder can show the assignee what to commit and how to opt out.

- **`server/src/__tests__/execution-workspaces-dirty-done.test.ts`** (+170 lines)
  10 cases against real temp git worktrees — clean workspace, modified file, untracked file, mixed, ignored worktree carve-out, deleted file, missing path, shared workspace skip, unsupported provider skip, git error skip.

- **`server/src/__tests__/issue-dirty-workspace-done-routes.test.ts`** (+464 lines)
  9 cases at the route layer — happy path, dirty blocks, no-code label bypass, board-actor pass-through, no-execution-workspace pass-through, inspector-skipped pass-through, already-done no-op, missing label table tolerance, response shape verification.

### Test plan

- [ ] `pnpm -C server vitest run src/__tests__/execution-workspaces-dirty-done.test.ts src/__tests__/issue-dirty-workspace-done-routes.test.ts`
- [ ] `pnpm -r typecheck`
- [ ] Spot-check: in a local Paperclip instance, intentionally leave a file dirty inside an issue's worktree, attempt to mark the issue `done` via the API → expect 422 with `code: "execution_workspace_dirty"` and the details payload.
- [ ] Spot-check: same setup but add the `no-code` label → expect transition to succeed.

### Notes

- Workspace-wide `pnpm -r typecheck` already passes locally on this branch.
- Server vitest run on the branch was 1685 / 1692; the 6 failing cases are pre-existing `workspace-runtime.test.ts` `pnpm ENOENT`/timeout flakes on master, unrelated to this change.
- Out of scope (per the originating spec): symmetric "commit landed but issue still in_progress" detection, and worktree-vs-main divergence checks (handled by branch-merge gates).

author: bridgear
body:
## Summary
Replace Yarn 1.x across repository dev tooling with Bun 1.3.1 for installs and npm for run-scripts. Root and docs installs are lockfile-frozen. Per-plugin sandboxes retain isolated dependency trees and cached highest-in-range resolution. Yarn remains only where tests deliberately exercise it as a user package manager.

Fresh npm releases are held for three days by both root and sandbox installs. Temporary integration and package-manager sandboxes explicitly load the tracked Bun config. All Green installs its GitHub clients from a dedicated frozen lock before minting STS credentials. License attribution reads exact versions from Bun and npm locks, combines metadata across multiple installed versions, and fails closed on registry or license gaps.

## Why
Yarn Classic cannot enforce a minimum publication age on new resolutions. Bun gives us the age gate and faster installs. Frozen locks cover repeat installs, while the age gate covers dynamic sandbox resolution. Bun is pinned to 1.3.1 because later tested releases can stall during dependency resolution in this repository.

The local Bun-lock license reader is a stop gap until `watson/dd-license-attribution` supports `bun.lock`. Once released there, replace it with the upstream command and remove the local parser.

author: vellum-apollo-bot[bot]
body: Fixes the silent macOS CI skip on PRs where the `preview` label is added right after creation. ## Root cause `pr-macos.yaml` triggers on `[labeled, synchronize, opened, reopened]` with `cancel-in-progress: true` on `pr-macos-{number}`. Creating a PR and immediately adding `preview` fires two `pull_request` events within the same second. One cancels the other. If the `opened` event wins the slot — before `preview` is in the label set — all the `if: contains(...labels.*.name, 'preview')` jobs evaluate to false and are silently skipped. The `labeled` run that would have evaluated them correctly is already cancelled. ## Fix `synchronize` events share a group so rapid pushes still cancel each other. All other event types (`opened`, `labeled`, `reopened`) get a unique group via `run_id` — they never cancel each other, so the `labeled` run always completes. ```yaml group: pr-macos-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}-${{ github.event.action == 'synchronize' && 'sync' || github.run_id }} ``` ## Behaviour | Scenario | Before | After | |---|---|---| | PR open + label added same second | one run cancelled, macOS jobs may skip | both runs complete | | Push to open PR (single) | runs | runs | | Multiple rapid pushes | latest cancels earlier ✓ | latest cancels earlier ✓ | | Label re-added / reopened | may be cancelled | always completes | ---

body:
## What
Prepare CLEARn for safer hosting by adding Vercel static frontend deployment metadata, production storage safeguards, CI hardening, and PR/branch protection guardrails.

## Why
The app is moving toward hosted review and production deployment, so failed builds, unsafe production config, non-durable runtime files, and unstructured PRs need to be caught before deploy rather than after Vercel or the API runtime has already failed. The Vercel preview failure was caused by Vercel using an incompatible pnpm version for the existing lockfile, so the install command now activates the repository pnpm version through Corepack before running `--frozen-lockfile`.

## Changes
- Add root `package.json` and `vercel.json` so Vercel can build the Expo web client from the repository root and publish `platform/apps/client/dist`.
- Pin the Vercel install path to `pnpm@10.8.0` with Corepack before `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.
- Document the recommended split hosting model: Vercel for the static frontend and Render or another durable Node host for the Fastify API, local STT, uploads, admin auth, and backups.
- Add `APP_STORAGE_ROOT`, `MEDIA_UPLOADS_PATH`, and production fail-fast checks so content, uploads, and admin auth cannot silently use repo-local storage in production.
- Harden CI with production dependency audit, Windows full test/build, Linux build smoke, and API runtime smoke checks.
- Add PR-description enforcement with `## What`, `## Why`, and `## Changes`, plus a local PR description draft helper.
- Add branch protection policy documentation and JSON payload for required checks on `main`.
- Protect production debug routes, require strong admin session secret and configured CORS origins, and make the backup runner portable across Windows and Linux.

Validation:
- `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\web\tests\run-tests.ps1`
- `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\web\tests\Architecture.Tests.ps1`

## Summary

Phase 3 Task 8 cycle 1 — the first out-of-flow positioning helper.
Adds `FloatManager` (per-BFC float tracker + `clear` resolution),
extends `ComputedStyleLayoutExtensions` with typed keyword decoders
(`ReadFloatSide`, `ReadClearKind`), and integrates with
`BlockLayouter`'s main loop to emit float fragments + advance
non-floating blocks past relevant float bottoms when they have
`clear`.

**Solution-wide:** 3798 unit / 3928 solution-wide passing (+38 over
PR #29). AOT/JIT byte-parity green. 4 skipped (cycle 3 + cycle 2d
deferral pins + capture harness).

## What's in this PR

### New types — `src/NetPdf.Layout/Layouters/FloatManager.cs`

- `FloatManager` — per-BFC tracker. `PlaceFloat` (places a float on
  the named side, stacked along the block axis cycle-1 MVP),
  `GetClearedBlockY` (CSS 2.2 §9.5.2 clear resolution — none/left/
  right/both/inline-start/inline-end), `Snapshot`/`RestoreFrom` for
  `LayoutCheckpoint.FloatManagerStateSnapshot` plumbing.
- `FloatRecord` — readonly-record-struct.
- `FloatSide` enum (Left/Right after writing-mode resolution).
- `ClearKind` enum (None/Left/Right/Both/InlineStart/InlineEnd).

### New extensions — `ComputedStyleLayoutExtensions`

- `ReadKeywordOrDefault` — generic typed-keyword decode.
- `ReadFloatSide` — `PropertyId.Float` → `FloatSide?`.
- `ReadClearKind` — `PropertyId.Clear` → `ClearKind`.

Cycle 1 resolves `inline-start`/`inline-end` as `left`/`right`
(LTR-only assumption; cycle 3 will resolve against
`LayoutContext.WritingMode` + `IsRtl`).

### `BlockLayouter` integration

- New `_floatManager` field (one per layouter instance / per BFC
  root).
- `AttemptLayout`'s main loop dispatches floats via new `EmitFloat`
  helper BEFORE the in-flow box-model math. Floats are out-of-flow
  per CSS 2.2 §9.5: don't advance the cursor + don't affect the
  margin-collapse chain.
- Non-floating blocks consult `_floatManager.GetClearedBlockY` BEFORE
  the resolver consult; clearance advances `UsedBlockSize` AND resets
  the collapse chain (per §8.3.1 — clearance creates a new collapse
  boundary).

## Cycle 1 deferrals

- **Cycle 2.** Inline-axis flow-around — blocks + line boxes that
  pass a float should reduce inline-size to flow around it. Cycle 1
  keeps blocks at full containing-block inline-size; floats overlap
  in-flow content visually + the painter handles z-order.
- **Cycle 2.** Cross-fragmentainer floats per Fragmentation L3 §5.
- **Cycle 3.** Float interaction with negative margins,
  `shape-outside`, multi-column, abs-pos; inline-start/end
  resolution against writing-mode + direction.
- **Phase 3 Task 9-10.** Inline content flowing around floats —
  needs `LineBuilder` / `InlineLayouter`.

## Tests

### `FloatManagerTests` (new) — 28 unit tests

- `PlaceFloat` — left/right alignment, same-side stacking, opposite-
  side independence, arg validation (NaN/Infinity/negative).
- `GetClearedBlockY` — each `ClearKind` value, no-floats baseline,
  no-pull-below-input invariant, NaN guard.
- `Snapshot`/`RestoreFrom` — capture, null-restore, replay, no-
  aliasing, type guard.

### `BlockLayouterTests.Task8_*` — 10 integration tests

- Left/right float emission at containing-block edges.
- Float doesn't advance the in-flow cursor.
- `clear: left|right|both` correctness.
- Two stacked left floats.
- Floats don't break margin-collapse chain between in-flow blocks
  (out-of-flow per §9.5).
- `inline-start` resolves as `left` in LTR.
- Clearance resets collapse chain (per §8.3.1).

- [x] `dotnet test NetPdf.slnx -c Release` — 3928 passing / 4 skipped

body:
This pull request introduces a robust Azure CI/CD pipeline for the scoreboard project and adds support for Azure relay and QR overlay features in the application. The main changes include three new GitHub Actions workflows for CI, pre-production deployment, and production promotion, as well as significant updates to `CTS_Scoreboard.py` to support Azure relay integration, QR code overlays, and improved message broadcasting. The most important changes are summarized below.

---

**CI/CD Workflows:**

* Added `.github/workflows/azure-ci.yml` to run linting, type checks, unit/integration tests, and Docker builds for the Azure relay app on PRs and pushes to master.
* Added `.github/workflows/azure-deploy-preprod.yml` for on-demand pre-production deployments, including image build/push, Azure Container App update, smoke tests, and auto-rollback on failure.
* Added `.github/workflows/azure-promote-prod.yml` to promote a pre-prod image to production with manual approval, image import, app update, and health checks.

**Azure Relay & QR Overlay Support in Application:**

* Updated `CTS_Scoreboard.py` to add Azure relay and QR overlay settings, including new configuration options for Azure and QR code features in the `settings` dictionary.
* Implemented `is_dev_mode()` to distinguish between development and production environments using the `SCOREBOARD_MODE` environment variable.
* Integrated QR code overlay generation and substitution into message page rendering and template context, using `build_meet_url`, `render_overlay_svg`, and `substitute_qr_tokens`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e1f01ceadfaf16c980ae8aad72cb8c2fd6f9dc5043f85cd56739676241f602b9R788-R795) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e1f01ceadfaf16c980ae8aad72cb8c2fd6f9dc5043f85cd56739676241f602b9L1014-L1019) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-e1f01ceadfaf16c980ae8aad72cb8c2fd6f9dc5043f85cd56739676241f602b9R1041-R1042)

**Message Broadcasting and Refactoring:**

* Refactored all scoreboard update broadcasts to use a new `broadcast_scoreboard()` function instead of direct `socketio.emit` calls, centralizing message emission logic. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e1f01ceadfaf16c980ae8aad72cb8c2fd6f9dc5043f85cd56739676241f602b9L285-R309) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e1f01ceadfaf16c980ae8aad72cb8c2fd6f9dc5043f85cd56739676241f602b9L822-R854) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-e1f01ceadfaf16c980ae8aad72cb8c2fd6f9dc5043f85cd56739676241f602b9L879-R908) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-e1f01ceadfaf16c980ae8aad72cb8c2fd6f9dc5043f85cd56739676241f602b9L888-R917) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-e1f01ceadfaf16c980ae8aad72cb8c2fd6f9dc5043f85cd56739676241f602b9L904-R933)

**Template and Context Refactoring:**

* Refactored the web template context builder into `_build_render_context()` for shared use by both Flask routes and the Azure relay, and updated how QR overlay and message pages are injected into the template context. § 5.3 spells out four **re-lock criteria** for that future moment:
1. Slot field name (`admin.settings.panels` vs `admin.customPanels` vs extending `admin.actions`)
2. Component serialization across the server / client boundary (admin extensions are declarative JSON today)

### 2. Plugin quickstart — configSchema walkthrough (`docs/plugin-quickstart.md`)
