Closes #1944.

When `fd -x cd` (or any shell builtin) fails with "command not found", the error now explains that the command is a shell builtin and shows how to invoke it through a shell:

```
[fd error]: Command not found: cd. Note: cd is a shell builtin, not a standalone
program. To run shell builtins, invoke a shell explicitly,
e.g. fd -x sh -c 'cd ... "$1"' sh {}
```

Non-builtins still get the plain "Command not found: foo" message.

The builtin list covers POSIX and common bash builtins that don't have standalone executables. Commands like `echo`, `printf`, and `test` are excluded since they typically exist as `/usr/bin/` binaries and work fine with `-x`.

Changelog entry added.

author: goehringcory-lang
body: ## Summary The editorial site is a client-rendered SPA, so without intervention every URL serves the same homepage `` and an empty `#root`. That breaks social card previews on Slack/Twitter/Discord/iMessage, prevents non-JS crawlers (most AI bots, Bingbot under load) from seeing article-specific metadata, and means AI crawlers can't read the actual article prose — directly contradicting the AI-citation goal stated in `robots.txt`. This PR adds a Cloudflare Pages Function (`functions/_middleware.js`) that, on the edge: 1. **Rewrites the ``** for known routes — per-route ``, meta description, canonical, Open Graph, Twitter, and `Article`/`CollectionPage` JSON-LD. 2. **Rewrites the `<noscript>`** on article routes — fetches `/bodies/{slug}.jsx`, transforms the JSX-prose into plain HTML, and replaces the article-list fallback with the article's title, dek, byline, and full body. The existing runtime SEO logic in `app.jsx` still runs after hydration; the function just makes the static HTML correct from the first byte. ### What changed - **`functions/_middleware.js`** — new Pages Function. Maps known paths to per-route SEO data, rewrites the response, and on article routes also fetches + transforms the body into the noscript fallback. - **`articles.json` + `categories.json`** — data source for the function. Mirrors `data.js` (which stays the source of truth for the browser SPA). A note in `data.js` flags the duplication. - **`feed.xml`** — created. It's been referenced from `index.html` since launch but didn't exist. - **`apps/guide/index.html`** — `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">`. The PWA is buyer-only behind auth; Google shouldn't index it. - **`index.html`** — dropped `<meta name="keywords">` (Google has ignored it since 2009). - **`sitemap.xml`** — dropped `<changefreq>` and `<priority>` (deprecated as ranking signals). - **`_headers`** — serve `feed.xml` as `application/rss+xml` with the same short-cache treatment as sitemap/robots. ### How the body pre-render works The 13 article bodies are intentionally HTML-shaped JSX — no custom React components, no embedded expressions in prose, just `<p>`, `<h2>`, `<a>`, `<ul>`, `<blockquote>`, `<strong>`. The transform is four regex passes: extract content between `return ( ... );`, strip outer `<>`/`</>`, replace `className=` → `class=`, replace the one inline-style pattern (`style={{ fontSize: 14 }}`), and strip JSX comments. Validated end-to-end against four bodies including the longest (stargazing, ~18KB extracted clean). Body fetches are cached at the edge (`cacheTtl: 3600`) and the noscript content is invisible to JS-enabled users — no perceptible cost to readers. ### Not in this PR - Dropping in-browser Babel + dev React — would be a Core Web Vitals win but contradicts the explicit "no build step" ethos in `CLAUDE.md`. - Real 404 page, image responsive markup, BreadcrumbList JSON-LD — separate PRs. ## Test plan - [ ] Merge and wait for Cloudflare Pages to redeploy. - [ ] `curl -sL https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/articles/bears-spring-emergence | grep -E '<title|og:title|canonical|"@type":"Article"'` shows the bear article's title/canonical/JSON-LD, not the homepage's. - [ ] Same `curl` piped to `grep -A2 '<noscript>'` shows the bear article's title and prose, not the article-list fallback. - [ ] `/section/wildlife` shows the category title and a `CollectionPage` schema in the head. - [ ] Paste an article URL into Slack or Twitter's card validator — preview shows the article title, dek, and image (not Half Dome / homepage copy). - [ ] `curl -sI https://thetalusfieldjournal.com/feed.xml` returns 200 with `Content-Type: application/rss+xml`. - [ ] `curl -s https://guide.thetalusfieldjournal.com/ | grep robots` shows the noindex directive. - [ ] Spot-check in browser: with JS enabled, no visible change. With JS disabled (DevTools → Settings → Disable JavaScript), an article URL shows the full article prose instead of the article list. https://claude.ai/code/session_01RzwX6ePu9LZdEQnR2Sr48N

author: copilot
body:
## Summary

Even after #74, `spack spec zlib` still failed with:
```
==> Error: thread constructor failed: Resource temporarily unavailable
```

### Root cause

The fix in #74 only applied the serial `ProcessPoolExecutor` fallback when `_can_start_threads()` returned `False` **at shim load time**. However, in the Pyodide browser environment:

1. `_can_start_threads()` **succeeds** at load time (threads work initially)
2. Pyodide installs its own internal threads during startup (for I/O, etc.)
3. When `spack spec` runs and `ProcessPoolExecutor.submit()` lazily starts its internal manager thread, the thread pool is exhausted → `RuntimeError("thread constructor failed: Resource temporarily unavailable")`

Additionally, in WASM/Pyodide, process forking/spawning is **impossible** — so `ProcessPoolExecutor` can never run work in a child process regardless of thread availability.

### Fix

Added `_is_pyodide()` helper that detects the Pyodide environment by checking if the `js` module (Pyodide's exclusive JavaScript bridge) is importable. The section 16 condition now applies the serial `_SerialProcessPoolExecutor` fallback when **either**:
- (a) thread startup fails completely at shim load time, **or**
- (b) we're running in Pyodide/WASM (where process spawning is impossible)

### Changes

- **`shim_system.py`**: Added `_is_pyodide()` detection function; changed section 16 condition to `not _can_start_threads() or _is_pyodide()`
- **`tests/test_multiprocessing_shim.py`**: Added `TestProcessPoolPyodideFallback` class with 3 tests that simulate the Pyodide environment by installing a stub `js` module before exec'ing the shim

author: jslee02
body:
## Summary

- Replace manual `std::thread` ownership with `std::jthread` in threaded tests and the parallel-worlds benchmark.
- Use `std::stop_token` for the long-running signal raiser thread instead of a separate atomic stop flag.
- Keep thread work and test assertions unchanged while making joins scoped and exception-safe.

## Motivation / Problem

- These tests and benchmarks start finite worker threads and immediately join them manually.
- `std::jthread` is a C++20 fit here because it joins on scope exit, reducing cleanup boilerplate and avoiding leaked joinable threads if a test assertion or exception exits the scope early.
- The signal stress test had a separate stop flag only to terminate the raiser thread; `std::stop_token` expresses that ownership directly.

## Changes / Key Changes

- Convert worker thread containers from `std::vector<std::thread>` to `std::vector<std::jthread>`.
- Convert single worker threads in profiler tests to scoped `std::jthread`.
- Convert the signal test raiser to a `std::jthread` with `std::stop_token`.

body:
## Summary
This PR refactors the voting round gallery projection feature to use a dedicated `show_final_gallery_projection` field instead of reusing `show_results_to_voters`, and enables Supabase Realtime for the `seats` and `candidates` tables to support real-time updates in the admin interface and projection displays.

## Key Changes

- **Gallery Projection Logic**: 
  - Changed `toggleGallery()` to use `show_final_gallery_projection` instead of `show_results_to_voters` for controlling the final gallery display
  - Updated the condition check to remove the unnecessary `show_ballot_summary_projection` requirement
  - When activating the gallery, now explicitly disables `show_results_to_voters` and `show_ballot_summary_projection` to prevent stale projection data

- **Round Closure**:
  - Extended `closeVoting()` to set `round_finalized: true` and reset all projection-related flags (`show_results_to_voters`, `show_ballot_summary_projection`, `show_final_gallery_projection`) to `false`
  - Updated success toast message to guide users to activate the final gallery when ready

- **UI Updates**:
  - Updated `ControlsAside.tsx` to display the gallery toggle only when round is closed and finalized (simplified condition)
  - Changed the gallery status label from "Visible para votantes" to "Proyectándose" to better reflect the actual state
  - Updated button state binding to use `show_final_gallery_projection` field

- **Database**:
  - Added migration script `015-realtime-seats-candidates.sql` to enable Supabase Realtime publication for `seats` and `candidates` tables, enabling real-time synchronization for admin and projection features

## Implementation Details
The refactoring separates concerns by using dedicated fields for different projection modes rather than overloading `show_results_to_voters`. This prevents conflicts when toggling the final gallery and ensures the projection system displays the correct data at each stage of the voting process.

author: lofyz
body:
## Summary

Adds an AI-powered "blog copilot" surface to the stack: a single federated mutation `runPostAgent(prompt)` that dispatches into a Vercel AI SDK tool-calling agent in `libs/ai`. The agent has four tools (`createPost` / `updatePost` / `deletePost` / `listPosts`), all routed through the federated gateway, so the agent acts as the user's hands on the existing GraphQL surface. A `/blog-copilot` page in `apps/web` drives it with a single prompt input and reacts to the agent's action — created/updated → navigate to the post; deleted → back to the feed; nothing matched → inline notice.

End-to-end shape:

```
  /blog-copilot  ── RUN_POST_AGENT mutation ──▶  gateway
                       (cookie-forwarded)            │
                                                     ▼
                                       ai-subgraph (port 3002)
                                       BetterAuthGuard
                                                     │
                                                     ▼  CommandBus
                                          libs/ai (CQRS handler)
                                                     │
                                                     ▼  PostAgent
                                       VercelAiPostAgent (NVIDIA Llama)
                                                     │
                                       toolChoice: 'auto'
                                                     │
                       ┌─────────────┬──────────────┬─────────────┐
                       ▼             ▼              ▼             ▼
                  createPost    updatePost     deletePost    listPosts
                       │             │              │             │
                       └─────────────┴──────────────┴─────────────┘
                                            │
                                            ▼  POST + Cookie + WP JWT
                                      gateway → posts (WP)
```

## Capabilities

- **NEW** `ai-post-agent` — the federated mutation, the agent, the four tools, the auth/cookie/token forwarding contract, and the web form.
- **No spec-level modification** to `gateway-federation` — its requirements are generic about the subgraph set; adding `ai` is config.

## Architecture

- **`libs/ai`** is one DDD-layered library. The application layer depends on a `PostAgent` port; the infrastructure layer ships a Vercel AI SDK implementation. Future swap to LangChain + Apollo MCP (the brief's eventual direction) is a single `infrastructure/` change — `application/` and `domain/` are framework-free.
- **`apps/ai-subgraph`** is a thin Apollo Federation subgraph (NestJS, port 3002) that hosts the schema + guard + resolver and dispatches the CQRS command. The composition pattern leaves room for additional AI mutations (chat copilot, drafts, summarization) without polluting `users-subgraph` ("only for authentication" per the project's stated principle).
- **Gateway** stays thin: one line added to `IntrospectAndCompose.subgraphs` to register `ai`. The existing `CookieDataSource` already forwards both `cookie` and `authorization` to subgraphs, which is exactly what the agent needs (cookie for the user's identity at users-subgraph; the WP service token at the WP write hop).

## Provider config

Defaults to **NVIDIA NIM** (`build.nvidia.com`, free developer tier) using `meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct` — strong tool-calling, no paid API needed for the demo. Selectable via env: `AI_PROVIDER=nvidia | openai | anthropic`, `AI_MODEL`, `AI_API_KEY`, `AI_BASE_URL` (escape hatch for self-hosted vLLM/Ollama).

The chat-model factory uses `createOpenAI(...).chat(model)` for the NVIDIA branch because NVIDIA NIM only exposes `/chat/completions` — not the new `/responses` API the SDK targets by default in v3.

## Verification

- `pnpm openspec validate ai-post-agent --strict` ✓
- `pnpm nx run-many -t build,lint -p ai,ai-subgraph,gateway,web` ✓
- End-to-end smoke against the live stack:

| # | Smoke | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 7.1 | Boot + composition | ✓ Supergraph mutations include `runPostAgent` + WP CRUD. |
| 7.2 | CREATE | ✓ NVIDIA Llama → `createPost` tool → post #17 published, `action: "CREATED"`. |
| 7.3 | Visible in feed | ✓ * |
| 7.4 | UPDATE | ✓ Agent: `listPosts → updatePost`; content delta verified. |
| 7.5 | DELETE | ✓ `listPosts → deletePost`; subsequent `post(slug)` returns `null`. |
| 7.6 | NOOP | ✓ "I couldn't find a match." |
| 7.7 | Web page (auth) | ✓ HTTP 200, page rendered. |
| 7.8 | Web page (anon) | ✓ HTTP 307 → `/sign-in?next=%2Fblog-copilot`. |
| 7.9 | Mutation w/o cookie | ✓ `extensions.code = "UNAUTHENTICATED"`. |

\* Authorship caveat: with the current cookie + WP-token forwarding, WP authenticates via the JWT (`desafio-svc`), so `appUser` resolves to `Service Acct`. Pinning to the calling user requires a `users.find(id) → wp_user_id` lookup before each tool call and passing `authorId` in the WP input — captured as a follow-up in the design risk list.

## Drive-by fixes uncovered during smoke

Three small things surfaced and got patched in their own commits:

1. **Subgraph `typePaths` collision** — both subgraphs were using `'**/*.graphql'` (workspace-relative glob) and ended up serving each other's schemas, breaking composition with "Non-shareable field … resolved from multiple subgraphs". Scoped each glob to `apps/<name>/src/**/*.graphql`.
2. **NVIDIA endpoint mismatch** — `createOpenAI()(model)` defaults to `/responses`; NVIDIA NIM only has `/chat/completions`. Switched the NVIDIA branch to `.chat(model)`.
3. **WP write authentication** — Better Auth cookies don't authenticate to WP. The `gateway-fetch` helper now sends `Authorization: Bearer ${WP_GRAPHQL_SERVICE_TOKEN}` alongside the cookie; the gateway forwards both.

## Commits

12 commits, ordered for review:

1. `feat(ai)` domain layer (port + types + errors)
2. `feat(ai)` chat-model factory + gateway-fetch helper
3. `feat(ai)` four CRUD tools (create/update/delete/list)
4. `feat(ai)` VercelAiPostAgent (the agent loop)
5. `feat(ai)` CQRS command + handler
6. `feat(ai)` AiModule wiring + exports + deps
7. `feat(ai-subgraph)` new federated subgraph + tsconfig sync
8. `fix(users-subgraph)` scope typePaths glob
9. `feat(gateway)` compose ai subgraph
10. `feat(web)` /blog-copilot page + form + mutation + dashboard/home links
11. `chore` AI env vars in .env.example
12. `docs(openspec)` add ai-post-agent change

## Test plan

- [ ] Boot the full stack: `docker compose up -d`, `pnpm nx serve users-subgraph`, `pnpm nx serve ai-subgraph`, `pnpm nx serve gateway`, `pnpm nx dev web`. Confirm gateway logs successful composition with all three subgraphs.
- [ ] Set `AI_API_KEY` in `.env` to a NVIDIA `build.nvidia.com` key (free).
- [ ] Visit `/blog-copilot` as a signed-in user. Try a CREATE prompt ("Write a short post about Apollo Federation"). Confirm redirect to `/blog/<slug>` with the rendered post.
- [ ] Try an UPDATE prompt referencing a post by title; confirm the content changes on `/blog/<slug>`.
- [ ] Try a DELETE prompt; confirm the post disappears from `/blog`.
- [ ] Try a NOOP prompt that doesn't match anything; confirm an inline message and the prompt text is preserved.
- [ ] Visit `/blog-copilot` anonymously; confirm redirect to `/sign-in?next=%2Fblog-copilot`.
- [ ] `curl` the mutation without a cookie; confirm `errors[0].extensions.code === "UNAUTHENTICATED"`.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- **User-pinned authorship** — look up the calling user's `wp_user_id` and pass `authorId` in the WP `createPost`/`updatePost` input so generated posts attribute to the user instead of the service account.
- **Apollo MCP + LangChain** — the design's port-based seam makes this a single `infrastructure/` swap whenever we want to swap from native AI SDK tools to MCP-loaded tools.
- **Streaming + chat copilot** — the broader brief feature; this PR is the synchronous one-shot precursor.

author: richardpan
body:
Closes #40.

## What
Adds an OS tray icon (Windows `NotifyIcon` via the WPF + WinForms hybrid) and minimise-to-tray behaviour for the main window. Pairs with #41 single-instance work — left-clicking the tray icon routes through the same `ActivateMainWindow` helper.

## How
- `Services/Tray/ITrayIconService` + `NotifyIconTrayService` — Windows-only (`[SupportedOSPlatform("windows")]`), wraps `NotifyIcon` with a Show/Hide/UpdateAwaitingInputCount API and Activate/Open/Quit events. Generic `SystemIcons.Application` for V1 (branded icon = follow-up).
- `Services/Tray/TrayCoordinator` — subscribes to `SessionsViewModel.Sessions` (collection + per-card `Status` PropertyChanged) and pushes the count of `AwaitingInput` sessions into the tray tooltip. Forwards the three tray events to plain callbacks the host wires to its window/lifecycle.
- `App.xaml.cs` — registers the tray as a singleton, extracts `ActivateMainWindow` out of the single-instance pipeline so both consumers share it, intercepts `MainWindow.Closing` to honour `MinimizeToTrayOnClose`, and uses `_userRequestedQuit` so the tray's Quit menu skips the hide-on-close path.
- `AppSettings.MinimizeToTrayOnClose` (bool, default `true`) — additive add, no schema bump per the #43 policy.
- `csproj` — `<UseWindowsForms>true</UseWindowsForms>` plus `<Using Remove>` for `System.Drawing` / `System.Windows.Forms` to avoid `Application` / `Brush` ambiguity with WPF.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Tray icon appears while the app is running.
- [x] Closing the main window hides it to the tray (when the new setting is on).
- [x] Tray icon's left-click and Open menu restore + foreground the window.
- [x] Tray menu has a Quit item that actually exits the process.
- [x] Tooltip shows count of sessions awaiting input.
- [ ] Quit confirms when there are active sessions — **deferred to follow-up** to keep this PR focused; will file once this lands.

## Tests
13 new (10 `TrayCoordinator` + 3 `NotifyIconTrayService` smoke). Total **391 passing**, all green locally on the trifecta (build /warnaserror, test, format --verify-no-changes).

## Summary

Adds the PSE-96 Trash workflow for local recovery and purge safety.

## Linear issue

Closes: PSE-96

## Scope

What is included in this PR?

- Adds a database TrashRepository and feature TrashService for listing deleted containers/items/list items/attachments, restoring targets, and clearing Trash.
- Adds Electron IPC, preload API, renderer API client, app route/sidebar entry, and a Trash page with restore and backup-preflight clear controls.
- Adds repository/service/preload/smoke test coverage for delete → restore and clear-trash backup preflight.

## Out of scope

What is intentionally not included?

- Cloud sync, hosted retention, team trash, or remote storage.
- Broad schema changes or migrations.
- Physical attachment file deletion from disk during clear Trash.

## Product spec references

- docs/PRODUCT_SPEC.md: local-only object graph, safe local data ownership.

body:
### Motivation
- Generated `witness_manifest.json` entries were emitted as display/absolute or out-dir-prefixed paths, which fails the hardened `resolve_bundle_relative_path` that requires bundle-relative artifact names. 
- The intent is to ensure manifests produced by `demo` and agent runs are compatible with strict verification without weakening path confinement. 
- Preserve existing artifact hashing and bundle-hash semantics while making manifests resolvable under the stricter resolver.

### Description
- Changed runtime `WitnessManifest` construction in the demo drift path and the agent run path (`src/main.rs`) to emit fixed bundle-relative filenames for artifact fields (e.g. `meta_json: "meta.json"`, `agent_trace_json: "agent_trace.json"`, `tool_transcript_json: "tool_transcript.json"`, `drift_report_json: "drift_report.json"`, `hash_chain_txt: "hash_chain.txt"`, `chaos_profile_json: Some("chaos_profile.json")`, `witness_root_txt: Some("witness_root.txt")`).
- When `nix_provenance_json` is present it is serialized as the bundle-relative filename `"nix_provenance.json"` instead of an absolute/display path. 
- Artifact hashing and `bundle_hash` computation are unchanged and still computed from the same on-disk files prior to manifest serialization. 
- Did not alter `resolve_bundle_relative_path`, witness serialization format, witness-root algorithm, or weaken path confinement; change is limited to manifest field values (file: `src/main.rs`).

### Testing
- Ran `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --locked`, and all tests passed. 
- Ran `cargo run --locked -- demo drift --seed 1 --threads 1 --fault-profile ci --out-dir demo_out --clean` and it completed successfully. 
- Ran `cargo run --locked -- verify --witness demo_out/drift/baseline_faults` and `cargo run --locked -- verify --witness demo_out/drift/baseline_faults --recompute-witness-root`, both succeeded and reported matching bundle/witness roots. 
- Ran `cargo run --locked -- ordeal check --golden goldens/ordeal_witness_root.txt` and it matched the golden; the golden witness root did not change.

author: julymetodiev
body:
Two related improvements addressing audit-time friction in the "find related code" workflow.

find_related filters: VelesIndex::find_related now accepts filter_languages and filter_paths in the same shape as `search`. The historical "default to source chunk's language" stays in effect when both are None, so existing callers (CLI, gRPC, TUI) keep their behaviour without changes beyond the new None / None arguments.

The MCP find_related tool exposes lang / path / exclude args and threads them through filter::resolve_path_filter, so an agent can say "show me related code, but only under crates/veles-mcp/**" and have the candidate set restricted exactly that way.

refs dedupe: when a BM25 hit's chunk contains a definition's start line, the chunk is the same code the Definitions section already pointed at — drop it from the BM25 list. The handler now requests ~50% extra BM25 hits to compensate for dropped duplicates, so the post-filter result count is closer to the requested top_k.

author: mwelwa-cyber
body:
## Summary

Follow-up fix for #323. The Vex agent landed in main but two real-world bugs surfaced as soon as a teacher tried it:

1. **Vex graded a quiz with the visible typo "Nae the National Park marked A." as a clean pass.** Root cause: new quizzes save question stems as serialised Tiptap JSON (see `serializeRichField` in `src/utils/quizSections.js`). The modal's flattener used `richTextToPlainText`, which only handles HTML — so Claude received a wall of `{"type":"doc","content":[...]}` instead of the question stem and couldn't grade what it couldn't read.
2. **When Claude returned an unparseable response, the runner silently faked a pass** — all-zero scores, empty issues, and a green "No issues detected. This quiz looks ready to publish." That's worse than no check at all.

Reproduced from the editor: every category showed 0%, no issues, "Quiz looks good to publish."

## Fixes

- `src/utils/quizRichText.js` — new `extractRichTextPlain` helper that detects Tiptap JSON (object or stringified) and walks it to plain text, falling back to `richTextToPlainText` for HTML/plain strings.
- `src/components/quiz/QuizVerifyModal.jsx` — `flattenQuestionsForVerify` now uses `extractRichTextPlain` for question text, options, and expected answers. Modal renders an amber "AI response was unreadable" panel when `aiUnreadable: true`, replacing the misleading green "No issues detected" panel for that case.
- `functions/agents/runners/vex.js` — server-side defense in depth: structural-check `extractPlainText` also handles Tiptap docs. When Claude's response can't be parsed (no scores AND no issues AND no summary), runner returns `aiUnreadable: true` with an honest summary instead of pretending the quiz passed. System prompt tightened to explicitly require flagging obvious typos in question stems / options.

author: neilconway
body:
## Which issue does this PR close?

- Closes #22088.

## Rationale for this change

`LogicalPlanBuilder::infer_data` (the inference path for `VALUES` clauses without a target schema) hard-coded every inferred column's nullability to `true`, regardless of whether any row actually contained a NULL. This is inconsistent with how nullability is computed for other, similar situations (e.g., `SELECT 1`).

In addition to improving internal consistency (and theoretically allowing better query optimization), this also makes it easier to write tests for nullability-related behavior without using a scratch table.

## What changes are included in this PR?

* `LogicalPlanBuilder::infer_data` now tracks per-column nullability while iterating values, marking the column nullable iff any row's value expression returns `nullable() == true`. Note that this only changes behavior for `VALUES` without a schema; `INSERT INTO VALUES`, for example, already computed nullability.
* Add SLT tests for this behavior
* Update expected SLT tests where this change results in updating a schema. Note that some Parquet files are slightly smaller now, which caused byte-count metrics in a few places to change.


## Are these changes tested?

Yes, with new tests added.

## Are there any user-facing changes?

The inferred schema for `CREATE TABLE AS VALUES (...)` will now change, although if we also fix #22087 then the original behavior will be preserved.

### Motivation
- Prevent pickup/merchant/split chat cards from being created or merged when chat output is disabled or uses restricted visibility, which could leak private/blind pickups into public chat logs.
- Ensure existing chat cards are only updated if their whisper visibility matches the current output mode to avoid appending private data to an older public card.

### Description
- Added `_getOutputToChatMode`, `_getOutputWhisperRecipients`, and `_messageMatchesOutputVisibility` helpers to centralize output-mode and whisper-recipient logic in `src/API/chat-api.js`.
- Short-circuited `_outputPickupToChat`, `_outputSplitToChat`, and `_outputMerchantTradeToChat` to return early when output mode is off, preventing creation/updating of chat cards in disabled mode.
- Only attempt to merge incoming pickup/merchant messages with an existing chat message when the existing message already matches the expected whisper recipients, preventing visibility escalation.
- Consolidated whisper population and deduplication in `_createNewChatMessage` so newly-created messages get the correct GM/self/GM+user recipients.
- Added a regression test `tests/regression.test.mjs` that reproduces the reported scenario by providing an existing public pickup card and asserting that Private/Blind/Off output behave correctly, and adjusted test mocks to support the new logic.

### Testing
- Ran `npm test` which executed the repository tests including the new regression test and all tests passed.
- Ran `npm run build` which produced the module build successfully (Svelte/Vite warnings are unrelated to this change and pre-existed).

author: wxlpp
body:
## Outcome: spike fallback (option 1)

Issue #9 spike attempted **NSFocusRing system integration** on macOS via `NSViewRepresentable` + `drawFocusRingMask` + `window.makeFirstResponder(nsView)`. Compile + Swift 6 strict concurrency cleanly passed, but Round 1 Copilot review caught an **architectural correctness issue**:

> `window.makeFirstResponder(nsView)` STEALS first responder from the actual focused control (TextField / NSTextView / etc), breaking keyboard input and creating a focus tug-of-war with SwiftUI `@FocusState`.

This is not a Swift 6 concurrency bug; it's a fundamental incompatibility between AppKit's NSFocusRing model (the focused view MUST be first responder) and SwiftUI's `@FocusState` model (where first responder belongs to the focused content).

Per PRD Assumptions / epic Implementation Strategy fallback clause, took **option 1** of Copilot's three suggestions:

- macOS uses the same SwiftUI overlay implementation as iOS
- Accessibility Inspector will not identify the ring as system focus indicator (PRD SC #11 marked as "fallback, limitation documented")
- Visual focus indication preserved across both platforms; only the system-vs-custom semantic distinction is lost

## Diff

`Sources/CoreDesign/Modifier/FocusRingModifier.swift` only:

- File-header doc-comment now contains the full spike conclusion + Copilot's 3 suggested paths + the rationale for picking option 1
- The macOS-branch `TODO(issue #9)` marker in the View extension is replaced with a definitive comment ("does not attempt NSFocusRing integration; fallback path")
- No NSViewRepresentable code, no AppKit code (the file no longer needs `import AppKit`)
- Unchanged: the iOS `FocusRingModifier: ViewModifier` struct, the `.focusRing(...)` View extension API surface, the iOS `#Preview`

## Acceptance criteria status

- ✅ macOS branch is no longer a "TODO placeholder pending #9"; it's a documented final decision
- ✅ `swift build -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors` clean on host (macOS)
- ✅ `swift test` passes
- ⚠️ PRD SC #11 (Accessibility Inspector identifies system focus ring): **NOT met by design** — fallback path drops this requirement. Limitation captured in file header.

## Risks / follow-ups

- If a future epic needs system focus ring on macOS, options 2 (custom AppKit drawing without first-responder hijack) or 3 (constrain to non-interactive views) from Copilot's R1 review remain available.
- Pre-existing `MenuButton.swift` UIImpactFeedbackGenerator main-actor error on iOS build is unrelated to this PR; flagged for separate fix.

Closes #9.

author: michaela811
body:
Uploads on /post-create occasionally surfaced error when users navigated away mid-upload.

Wire an AbortController to the page lifecycle so navigation cleanly
cancels any active upload. Cancel errors are filtered via
axios.isCancel; real errors still surface unchanged.

When a friend request was already resolved, clicking Accept/Decline
on its lingering notification fired a 404 that is seen as a silent
"stuck" UI. The buttons did nothing visibly and no error toast
appeared either.

Add cache invalidation to the accept/decline mutations so successful
actions update the notifications list, and treat 404 responses as
"already resolved" rather than real errors. Both branches invalidate
['notifications'] (plus ['friends'] on accept) so the resolved row
drops out of the UI immediately.

README Update, more updates to come.

## Summary

- PR #201 fixed `captures.metadata → source_metadata` but the same function has a second `db.execute` against `pipeline_events` that referenced `started_at` (does not exist; actual column is `created_at`). Drizzle's catch block was swallowing the Postgres error and returning `[]` silently, so post-#201 deploy verification still showed empty `/api/v1/system/flows`.
- Schema pre-flight confirmed: `pipeline_events` has `created_at` (timestamptz), not `started_at`. All other SELECT fields (`capture_id`, `stage`, `status`, `duration_ms`, `error`) were correct.
- `PipelineFlowEntry.stages` interface updated to match (`started_at → created_at`).

author: greateggsgreg
body:
Fixes #691.

## Cause

`MethodBinding` and `OverloadMapper` hold a `PyObject target` but didn't release it on `tp_clear`, so the underlying CLR instance waited on the .NET finalizer chain to drop the refcount. They also shared the same C# `PyObject` instance across `mp_subscript` / `Overloads` paths, so disposing one wrapper corrupted the others.

## Fix

- `ExtensionType`: add virtual `OnClear()` hook called from `tp_clear`.
- `MethodBinding` / `OverloadMapper`: override `OnClear` to dispose `target`. (`targetType` left alone — disposing it broke unrelated subclass tests.)
- Each sharing site now passes `new PyObject(self.target.Reference)` so each wrapper owns its own INCREF'd reference.

## Tests

The three existing `*_does_not_leak_memory` tests cover the three sharing sites but their 0.9 MB/iter threshold was too loose — master was leaking ~600 KB/iter and still passing. Tightened to 0.1 MB/iter (104 KB).

## Verification (Python 3.14 GIL, linux-aarch64)

| | .NET 8 | .NET 10 |
|---|---|---|
| master | **FAIL** 765 KB/iter | **FAIL** 572-647 KB/iter |
| this PR | PASS -0.6 KB/iter | PASS -0.5 KB/iter |

## Summary

The first Cloudflare deploy of marginalia after #224 merged failed:

\`\`\`
✘ [ERROR] The directory specified by the \"assets.directory\" field in your configuration file does not exist:
  /opt/buildhome/repo/dist
\`\`\`

**Diagnosis:** The Atlas deploys via Cloudflare Workers (not Pages) — \`wrangler.jsonc\` at the repo root configures the Atlas worker with \`assets.directory: ./dist\`. When marginalia was set up as a sibling Workers project, the deploy step ran \`npx wrangler deploy\` from the repo root, which read the Atlas's wrangler.jsonc and looked for \`./dist\` at the repo root (which doesn't exist — only \`marginalia/dist\` does, and only after the marginalia build).

**Fix:** Add \`marginalia/wrangler.jsonc\` so wrangler reads marginalia's config when run with Workers Builds Root directory = \`marginalia\`. \`assets.directory: ./dist\` then resolves to \`marginalia/dist\`, which exists.

Static-only — no \`main\` field, no Worker code. SPA fallback handled natively via \`assets.not_found_handling: \"single-page-application\"\` (the public/_redirects file is kept for compat; either alone would work).

author: jumplink
body:
## Summary

Phase D-2 groundwork. First audit deliverable comparing the two WASM targets we need to bind for the Rust-crate runtime:

- **lightningcss-wasm**: NAPI on plain WASM. No WASI, no SAB, ~30 napi-wasm fns + 2 customs. High GJS viability.
- **rolldown wasm32-wasi**: NAPI on WASI + threads. Requires preopens, worker_threads, and `WebAssembly.Memory({shared:true})` — SAB is disabled in stock GJS, so the threaded variant is blocked.

Three escape paths for rolldown documented (single-threaded rebuild / upstream SAB / skip-WASM). Decision: try the single-threaded rebuild first, fall back to Vala+Rust FFI if that fails.

Also registers `refs/lightningcss` as a submodule (v1.32.0+2). Its `c/` subdir ships a `lightningcss_c_bindings` cdylib + cbindgen-generated header — significantly de-risks the FFI POC since we won't need to write a Rust shim from scratch.

- [x] Submodule registered, refs/lightningcss/c/lightningcss.h verified to expose the full transform API

author: pmrv
body:
## Summary

- New `Benchmarks (main)` workflow runs on push to `main` and uploads `benchmarks/results.csv` as a SHA-keyed artifact (`benchmark-<sha>`), retained 90 days.
- PR `Benchmarks` workflow resolves its merge base, looks up that commit's run-id via `gh run list`, and downloads the artifact with the stock `actions/download-artifact@v4` (using `run-id` + `github-token` for cross-run access). Falls back to recomputing on a `git worktree` if no baseline run exists.
- PR runs upload their head's results under the same SHA-keyed naming, so a follow-up push can pick up its HEAD~ artifact and the comment gains an extra `Δ vs HEAD~` column when HEAD~ is distinct from the merge base.
- New `benchmarks/compare_results.py` joins baseline/head/prev CSVs on `(topic, configuration, workload, function)` and emits a markdown delta table, flagging |Δ| > 5% with 🔴/🟢.

## Test plan

- [ ] Land to `main`; confirm `Benchmarks (main)` runs and uploads `benchmark-<sha>`.
- [ ] Open a PR off that commit with a deliberate slowdown, label `benchmark`; expect comment with merge-base short SHA, "baseline: cached", and slowed row flagged 🔴.
- [ ] Open a PR whose merge base predates this rollout; expect "baseline: recomputed" and ~2× runtime.
- [ ] Push a follow-up commit to a PR; expect `Δ vs HEAD~` column to appear.
- [ ] Single-commit PR (HEAD~ == merge base); expect no `Δ vs HEAD~` column.

## Summary
PR-Fun1.4 검증 시 발견된 두 issue 통합 fix.

## 진단

### Issue 1 — [SUGGESTIONS] click 부정확 query
- click handler 가 `pending_q` 매개체 사용 + main() 의 fall-through 패턴 (`q = q_input or clicked_q`) → carry-over 가능
- **fix**: 매개체 변수 분리 + main() 입구 즉시 처리

### Issue 2 — 피드백 UI 사라짐
- `_render_feedback` 코드는 살아있고 호출 위치 정상
- `if not query_log_id: return` 가드에서 즉시 종료
- **root cause 추정**: PR-S1 의 RLS SELECT 정책 (`to service_role only`) 이 anon INSERT 후 RETURNING 도 차단 → `ins.data` 빈 list → `ans.query_log_id = None`
- **fix**: DB 변경 X 가드레일 준수 → `query_masked` + 최근 5분 ts 윈도우 fallback 매칭. UPDATE 자체는 anon UPDATE 정책 (USING true) 통과해 실제 row 수정 가능 (RETURNING 만 차단).

## 변경 (`app.py` only)

### 작업 1 — `clicked_q` 매개체 분리
```python
# _show_example_questions / _render_suggestion_cards click
st.session_state["clicked_q"] = q
st.rerun()

# main() 입구 (chat_input early 호출 다음)
_clicked = st.session_state.pop("clicked_q", None)
if _clicked:
    _run_ask(sb, _clicked, cat, hotlines)
    st.rerun()
```
기존 `clicked_q = pop("pending_q")` fall-through 줄 제거. chat_input 처리부는 `q_input` 만.

### 작업 2 — 피드백 fallback 매칭
- **`_feedback_update` 헬퍼 신설**: `query_log_id` 우선, 없으면 `query_masked + ts >= now()-5min` 매칭
- `_record_feedback_click` / `_record_feedback_submit` 시그니처에 `masked_question` 인자 추가
- `_render_feedback` 가드: `query_log_id` OR `masked_question` 있으면 표시
- live answer + history replay 호출에 `masked_question` 전달
- `_push_history` meta 에 `masked_question` 저장

- core/chatbot.Answer 시그니처 무수정 (이미 `masked_question` 필드 존재)

author: harshagarwalnyu
body:
Fixes #36423

Currently, infinite render loop detection for passive effects (useEffect) is entirely wrapped in an if (__DEV__) block. In production builds, this check is stripped, causing infinite loops to run silently until the browser tab hangs or crashes. This prevents error boundaries from catching the issue and hides it from error monitoring tools.

This PR promotes the 
estedPassiveUpdateCount check out of __DEV__ and changes the console.error to an unconditional 	hrow new Error, matching the behavior of synchronous infinite loop detection.

author: copilot
body:
Adds a local-first analytics layer oriented around emotional usability and ecosystem health — not engagement maximisation. No PII, no user IDs in events, no external transmissions by default.

## Core engine (`src/lib/analytics.ts`)
- Anonymous session tokens rotating every 24h for privacy
- Event queue persisted to `localStorage`, flushed in-memory; extend to a backend endpoint at `VITE_ANALYTICS_ENDPOINT` if needed
- 27 named events covering navigation, directives, reports, proposals, rituals, journaling, workbooks, and onboarding
- Lightweight user state model deriving one of 8 states (`exploring`, `reflecting`, `deep_reading`, `ritual_tending`, `high_energy`, `low_energy`, `overwhelmed`, `unknown`) from session behaviour — used solely for pacing/UX adaptation, never manipulation

## React integration
- **`AnalyticsContext`** — exposes `track()`, `userState`, `isOptedOut`, `optOut()`, `optIn()`
- **`usePageTracking`** — fires `page_view` with dwell time on every route change; detects return visits via a persistent `has_visited` flag (not an inverted session expiry)
- **`useAnalytics`** — thin per-component hook

```tsx
const { track } = useAnalytics();
track('directive_complete', { lunar_phase: 'waxing_gibbous' });
```

## Observability dashboard (`/analytics`)
Internal page reading exclusively from the local queue — no network calls. Shows:
- Session state + behavioural breakdown
- Page distribution, event distribution (recharts)
- Onboarding funnel with step-completion bars
- Reflective completion timeline
- Live event log (last 50 events)

## Privacy controls
Analytics opt-out toggle added to Settings → Privacy. Opt-out clears the queue immediately and suppresses all future tracking for the session.

## Explicitly out of scope
Rage-click tracking, scroll depth, notification responses, engagement maximisation, or any external adtech integration.

author: laboef1900
body:
## Summary

Operator feedback: *"On top level of a project I can select assisted, manual or auto. In the settings of the project I can set plan_only, plan, analyze and full. It's a bit confusing."*

The two project settings control different concerns but were split across two pages with no shared framing — mode was editable only on `ProjectDetail`, `autonomy_level` only on the `ProjectsPage` cards — so they read like duplicate or competing controls.

The fix is **not** to merge them: they're genuinely orthogonal. `mode` shapes *what* the agent is asked to do (prompt + manager-review criteria); `autonomy_level` shapes *how freely* it can act (`can_use_tool` gates). Combinations like `analyze + auto` and `full + manual` are legitimate.

This PR groups both on `ProjectDetail.svelte`'s overview tab under labelled sections that name each axis's concern:

- **Work scope** (`mode`) — *"What the agent is asked to do"*
- **Execution policy** (`autonomy_level`) — *"How freely it can act"*
- **Project basics** — priority, branch, enabled toggle

Each option's dropdown label now carries a one-line summary (e.g. *"Manual — operator approves every edit and risky command"*), and the existing per-selection help paragraph stays underneath for the longer description.

`docs/configuration.md` gains:
- A "Two orthogonal axes" subsection at the top of Project config with a comparison matrix and three example combinations.
- A permissions table under Autonomy levels enumerating manual/assisted/auto inline (today the section just points to ADR-0001).

## Screenshot

Verified live on `http://localhost:5173/projects/1` (next-itsm) with `npm run dev` against the running dashboard backend. Three sections render cleanly with no console errors:

```
WORK SCOPE
  What the agent is asked to do on this project. Shapes the prompt
  teammates receive and the criteria the manager applies.
  [Plan Only — write plan, stop, wait for approval ▾]
  Teammates write a plan and stop. The manager approves, requests
  revisions, or rejects before any code is written. An approved
  plan_only run schedules a follow-up full run that implements it.

EXECUTION POLICY
  How freely the agent can act on the work scope above. Independent
  of mode — applies to every tool call regardless of whether the
  run is implementing, planning, or analyzing.
  [Assisted — edits auto-allowed, destructive commands ask ▾]
  Edits auto-allowed; destructive bash patterns still defer to the
  operator. The default for established repos. Every decision is
  recorded to the autonomy audit, regardless of level.

PROJECT BASICS
  Priority [High ▾]    Branch [main]    [●] Enabled
```

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` → 812 ms, no errors on changed files
- [x] Live render against running dashboard, project detail page loads three sections without console errors
- [ ] Sanity check: change autonomy on this page, confirm it round-trips via `PATCH /api/projects/{id}` and the inline selector on the Projects card view reflects the new value

## Out of scope

- The inline autonomy selector on `ProjectsPage` cards stays — it's a useful at-a-glance toggle for many projects. This PR just stops *requiring* you to leave the detail page to change it.
- A "preset picker" that hides both axes behind one combined dropdown was considered and rejected (loses combinations like `plan_only + auto`).

body:
While testing the original bury implementation, the action failed at runtime with `RuntimeError: unsupported action`. Investigation:

- Tried `bury`, `buryCards`, `buryNotes` against the running AnkiConnect (25.2.25.0) — all return `unsupported action`.
- Inspected upstream plugin source (25.2.25.0 and the latest 25.11.9.0): **no bury endpoint exists**. AnkiConnect only exposes `suspend` / `unsuspend`.
- The only way to manually bury via AnkiConnect is `setSpecificValueOfCard` with `warning_check=true`, mutating internal scheduler fields — too brittle to ship.

So the feature implementation is reverted and the README now states clearly that bury isn't available, pointing users at desktop/mobile Anki for that action.

Closes #14.

## Summary

### المشكلة الأصلية — انتهاء مدة العمل
الـ backend كان يُرجع `EditSession` بدون `exists`/`minutesLeft`/`modifiedPaths` فالـ frontend كان ينهي الجلسة فوراً.

### النقلة النوعية — خط إنتاج احترافي

#### 1. إصلاح الجلسة (Commit 1)
- `createdAt`/`lastActivity` timestamps + dual timeout (4h absolute / 1h idle)
- `keepSessionAlive` endpoint + frontend ping كل 30 ثانية
- `getSessionInfo` يُرجع `exists`/`minutesLeft`/`modifiedPaths` بشكل صحيح

#### 2. إعادة كتابة `rebuildAPK` بالكامل — 7 خطوات تنفيذية (Commit 2)
| الخطوة | العملية | التفاصيل |
|--------|---------|----------|
| 1 | حذف التوقيعات القديمة | `.SF` `.RSA` `.DSA` `.EC` `.MF` + `STAMP-CERT-SHA256` |
| 2 | APKTool rebuild | `--use-aapt2` ثم fallback بدونها |
| 3 | تنظيف APK المعاد بناؤه | حذف أي META-INF متبقي من ZIP |
| 4 | Keystore | تحميل أو إنشاء RSA-2048 |
| 5 | zipalign | محاذاة 4-byte + التحقق بـ `zipalign -c` |
| 6 | التوقيع | `apksigner` V1+V2+V3 (+ fallback jarsigner) |
| 7 | التحقق | `verifyAPK()` شامل |

#### 3. `verifyAPK()` — فحص ما بعد البناء
- التحقق من التوقيع (V1/V2/V3)
- التحقق من المحاذاة (zipalign)
- التحقق من سلامة ZIP
- التحقق من الملفات الحرجة (classes.dex, AndroidManifest.xml, resources.arsc)
- حكم نهائي: **قابل للتثبيت** أم لا

#### 4. قوالب تعديل Smali تنفيذية جديدة (`applyPatchTemplate`)
| القالب | العملية الحقيقية |
|--------|----------------|
| `removeAds` | حذف SDK إعلانات + `safeNeutralizeInvoke` لكل ad call |
| `bypassRoot` | `isRooted()/checkRoot() → return false` |
| `bypassSSL` | `checkServerTrusted() → return-void` + تعديل `network_security_config.xml` |
| `unlockPremium` | `isPremium()/isPro() → return true` + `getCoins() → MAX_INT` |
| `removeLicense` | تعطيل Google LVL |
| `modifyAPI` | استبدال API URL في كل الملفات |
| `removeTracking` | حذف Analytics/Firebase SDK |
| `bypassIntegrity` | تعطيل SafetyNet/tamper detection |

#### 5. تحسينات Frontend
- شريط حالة جلسة ملوّن + مؤشر تقدم
- 8 أزرار قوالب تنفيذية
- تقرير بناء مفصّل (حالة كل خطوة + مدة + تفاصيل)
- عرض نتائج التحقق (V1/V2/V3 + aligned + ZIP + installable)
- دعم بناء كل أنواع الملفات (ZIP لغير APK)

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human
- [ ] رفع APK → تحرير & بناء → التأكد من عدم ظهور \"انتهت الجلسة\"
- [ ] الضغط على قالب \"إزالة الإعلانات\" → التأكد من ظهور نتائج حقيقية (عدد الملفات المعدّلة)
- [ ] بناء APK → التأكد من ظهور تقرير البناء المفصّل مع كل الخطوات
- [ ] التأكد من أن APK الناتج يظهر V1+V2+V3 في تقرير التحقق
- [ ] تثبيت APK المعدّل على جهاز Android والتأكد من عدم وجود مشاكل تثبيت
- [ ] اختبار قالب \"تجاوز Root\" و \"تعطيل SSL Pinning\"

### Notes
- كل القوالب تنفّذ تعديلات Smali حقيقية عبر regex patterns على مستوى bytecode
- `signAPKFile` يحذف التوقيعات القديمة **مرتين** (من المصدر المفكك + من ZIP النهائي) لضمان عدم تعارض التوقيعات
- تم تطبيق إصلاح الجلسة على كل من `ReverseEngineer.tsx` و `ReverseEngineer-export.tsx`

Added fallback error handling for two common issues:

2. Camera access (`getUserMedia`) unavailable over `file://` protocol

- **tests.html**: Added a 3-second timeout fallback that detects if tests never executed and displays an actionable message directing users to run a local HTTP server
- **potatovision.js**: Added a check before requesting camera access to detect when `getUserMedia` is unavailable and provide a helpful error message instead of silently hanging

## Implementation Details
- The test fallback uses a simple timeout to detect the "running…" state persisting, indicating the ES module never loaded
- The camera check uses optional chaining (`navigator.mediaDevices?.getUserMedia`) to safely detect API availability
- Both changes provide specific guidance to users (running `python3 -m http.server` and opening `http://localhost:8000`)
- Error messages are user-friendly and actionable rather than cryptic browser errors

## Sammanfattning

Förbereder repot för publik release som **GitHub Template Repository**. Ingen funktionell ändring i AI-pipen — det här är artefakter, workflows och dokumentation runt koden.

Tre logiska commits (alla Conventional Commits så commitlint-grinden passerar):

1. `chore: add open-source artefacts and package metadata` — LICENSE (MIT), CONTRIBUTING, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, issue/PR-templates, .editorconfig, package.json-metadata.
2. `ci: add CI, commitlint, dependabot, and release-please workflows` — fyra workflows + lokal Husky-hook + release-please-konfig.
3. `docs: add badges, template usage, and contribution sections to readme` — visuella tillägg + "Använd som template"-sektion + "Bidra"-sektion.

## Vad är nytt

### Open source-artefakter
- **LICENSE** — MIT.
- **CONTRIBUTING.md** — komma-igång-guide, Conventional Commits-tabell, PR-flöde.
- **CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md** — Contributor Covenant 2.1 (defacto-standard).
- **`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`** — bug + feature templates + config med länk till Discussions.
- **`.github/pull_request_template.md`** — checklista som påminner om Conventional Commits + verifikationer.

### CI + underhåll

- **`.github/dependabot.yml`** — veckovisa updates för npm + github-actions, grupperade per stack.

### Commit-lint (100% efterlevnad — krav)
- **`.commitlintrc.json`** — extends `@commitlint/config-conventional`.
- **`.husky/commit-msg`** — lokal hook (snabb feedback). Aktiveras via `prepare`-script i `package.json`.
- **`.github/workflows/commitlint.yml`** — `wagoid/commitlint-github-action@v6` på PRs. Detta är den slutliga grinden — kan inte bypassas.

### release-please
- **`.github/workflows/release-please.yml`** — triggar på push till `main`.
- **`release-please-config.json`** — `release-type: node`, `package-name: aitoblog`. CHANGELOG-sektioner: feat, fix, perf, revert (synliga), docs/refactor (synliga), chore/ci/build/test/style (dolda).
- **`.release-please-manifest.json`** — initial baseline `0.1.0`.

### README
- **Badges** i toppen: CI-status, MIT-licens, Deploy to Cloudflare Pages-knapp.
- **"Använd som template"** — sektion som förklarar GitHub-template-flödet.
- **"Bidra"** — pekar på Conventional Commits-kravet och CONTRIBUTING.md.
- **Filstruktur**-diagrammet uppdaterat med `.github/`, `.husky/`, release-please.

### package.json
- Bumpat från `0.0.1` → `0.1.0` (matchar release-please-baseline).
- Ny metadata: description, license, repository, bugs, homepage, keywords, author.
- Nytt script: `prepare: "husky || true"` (silent fallback om Husky saknas i CI).
- Nya dev-deps: `@commitlint/cli`, `@commitlint/config-conventional`, `husky`.

## Verifierat lokalt

- `pnpm astro check` — 0 errors.
- `pnpm build` — bygger fortsatt grönt (`dist/index.html`, `dist/blog/2026-05-09-hello-world/`, `dist/rss.xml`).
- Commitlint-CLI: `echo "broken format" | commitlint` → felmeddelar med "subject may not be empty"; `echo "feat: test" | commitlint` → tystnar (= passerar).
- Husky-hook: `.husky/commit-msg` är executable och aktiverad via `core.hooksPath`.

## Inte verifierat (görs efter merge)

- Att GitHub Action-workflows faktiskt kör grönt (sker när PR:en triggar dem).
- release-please skapar sin första release-PR (sker när denna PR mergas till main).
- Commitlint-grinden validerar PR:s commits (sker när denna PR triggar workflowen — alla tre commits är Conventional Commits så det ska passera).

1. **Settings → "Template repository"** — markera checkboxen så andra kan "Use this template".
2. **About-panelen** — sätt description, homepage (om det finns en demo-deploy), topics (`astro`, `claude`, `cloudflare-pages`, `template`, `ai`, etc.).
3. **Första release-PR:n** — release-please skapar en `v0.1.0`-PR efter merge. Granska den och merge → tag `v0.1.0` + GitHub Release skapas automatiskt.
4. **Eventuell demo-deploy** (valfritt) — klona via "Use this template" till ett personligt repo, koppla Cloudflare Pages där. Dina blogginlägg lever i klonen, mallen i detta repo förblir ren.

body:
## Summary

Pivot do epic **Cockpit Saúde do Ecossistema** (US-COPI-095): ao invés de criar `/copiloto/admin/health` separada, **estendemos `/governance` Dashboard** que já é o cockpit de saúde gold-standard do projeto (charter `live`, [Cockpit Pattern V2 ADR 0110](memory/decisions/0110-cockpit-pattern-v2-canon-list-detail.md), em prod desde 2026-05-08).

3 fontes adicionadas: `failed_jobs` (Horizon), `jana_mensagens` 24h (custo IA Brain B), `jana_health_narratives` (PR #339).

## Why o pivot

Constituição V2 §5 SoC brutal + [ADR 0105](memory/decisions/0105-cliente-como-sinal-guiar-sem-mandar.md): princípio "não duplicar". `/governance` já mostra os MESMOS 6 checks do `jana:health-check` que o cockpit planejava agregar. Separar contextos sem cliente pedindo seria churn.

Decidido em chat 2026-05-09 com Wagner — opção (a) "estender governance" preferida sobre (b) "criar tela nova".

## Mudanças

- [`DashboardController.php`](Modules/Governance/Http/Controllers/DashboardController.php) — 3 queries graceful (`Schema::hasTable`) pra failed_jobs / jana_mensagens / jana_health_narratives. Cada uma retorna `null` ou `[]` quando tabela ausente, mantendo shape estável pro front
- [`Dashboard.tsx`](resources/js/Pages/governance/Dashboard.tsx) — 2 fileiras KpiGrid separadas por h2 de seção (`Constituição` cols=6 mantém · `Saúde do ecossistema` cols=3 novo) + grid lateral cresce 2-col → 3-col com card "Narrativas Brain A 24h"
- [`Dashboard.charter.md`](resources/js/Pages/governance/Dashboard.charter.md) — bump `charter_version: 1 → 2`, Mission expandida, Goals atualizados, related_adrs ganha 0114
- [`governance-dashboard-extension-visual-comparison.md`](memory/requisitos/Jana/governance-dashboard-extension-visual-comparison.md) — gate F1.5 mwart-comparative satisfeito (status `approved` por Wagner em chat 2026-05-09)
- [`DashboardExtensionTest.php`](tests/Feature/Modules/Governance/DashboardExtensionTest.php) — 8 testes Pest cobrindo as 3 fontes com janela 24h + degradação

## Como funciona o KpiGrid em 2 fileiras

```
─── H2 "Constituição" ────────────────────────────────────────────────
[ADRs pend] [Policies] [Skill apr] [Actors] [Audit 24h] [Compliance]    ← cols=6 (mantém)
─── H2 "Saúde do ecossistema" ────────────────────────────────────────
[Failed jobs 24h]  [Custo IA 24h]  [Última narrativa]                    ← cols=3 (novo)
```

Tones semânticos:
- **Failed jobs**: `success` (0), `warning` (>0), `danger` (>100)
- **Custo IA**: `success` (0), `info` (>0), `warning` (>5 BRL)
- **Última narrativa**: `info`/`warning`/`danger` espelhando severity do registro

Em ambiente sem `failed_jobs`/`jana_mensagens`/`jana_health_narratives`, KPI mostra `—` + description explicativa ("failed_jobs ausente" etc) — sem erro 500.

## Test plan

- [x] Cobre janela 24h, pricing canônico, degradação graciosa em 3 fontes
- [ ] Pós-merge prod biz=1 (Wagner): smoke `/governance` carrega 200, 2 fileiras KpiGrid renderizam, narrativas aparecem assim que PR #339 mergear e cron Brain A rodar
- [ ] Pós-merge: rodar Pest `CockpitPatternConformanceTest` pra confirmar que extensão não quebra audit do canon V2

body:
## Summary

Phase 3 of the implementation plan — every SonarCloud V1 endpoint Sift needs, wrapped behind a typed `SonarClient` that returns `Result<T>` for every method (errors as values, never thrown). Plus thin TanStack Query bindings whose `staleTime` values are pinned by ADR-008(a).

- **`tests/msw.ts`** — MSW v2 handlers serving the recorded fixtures from Phase 1; `tests/setup.ts` wires `setupServer` with `onUnhandledRequest: 'error'` so any stray live request fails loudly. Vary-by-query-param overlay for `/issues/search` (severities=BLOCKER → empty fixture).
- **`src/api/SonarClient.ts`** — class with constructor (region + token-getter) and one shared `get<T>()` helper that owns the status→Result mapping (401/403 with upstream message/404/429 with optional Retry-After/5xx/non-2xx/schema-mismatch → server_error; fetch reject → network_error). Each public method is then a URL builder + parser handoff.
  - `listOrganizations()` — happy + 401/403/404/429/5xx + network + malformed-body
  - `listProjects(orgKey, opts?)` — pagination, full status table
  - `listBranches(projectKey)`
  - `searchIssues(filters, opts?)` — comma-encoded V1 filters; null entries dropped from `resolutions`; ADR-007 over-cap detection at `paging.total > 10_000` (boundary stays `ok`)
  - `searchHotspots(filters, opts?)`
  - `getQualityGate(projectKey, branch)`
  - `getMeasures(projectKey, branch, metricKeys[])`
- **`src/api/queries.ts`** — pure option factories + hooks (`useOrganizations`, `useProjects`, `useBranches`, `useIssues`, `useHotspots`, `useQualityGate`, `useMeasures`). `STALE_TIMES` pinned to ADR-008(a) values; tests assert the table verbatim so drift here can't silently weaken the no-proxy-cache decision.
- **`vitest.config.ts`** — routes `src/api/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}` through the jsdom project so relative-URL fetch resolves against `window.location` (SonarClient calls `/api/sonar/v1/...` paths the proxy serves; in tests MSW intercepts at the same paths).

151 tests pass; `src/api/` line coverage 99.16% (target ≥90%); lint, typecheck, build all clean.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm lint`
- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm test` — 151/151 pass
- [x] `pnpm build`
- [x] `pnpm coverage` shows `src/api/` lines ≥ 90% (99.16%)
- [x] Every public SonarClient method has a happy-path test
- [x] Every public method has tests for every Result variant relevant to the endpoint (401/403/404/429/5xx/network/over_cap where applicable)
- [x] `searchIssues` has a dedicated test for the >10k cap (and one at the 10_000 boundary)
- [x] Filter encoding tests cover every `IssueFilters` dimension
- [x] Render-smoke test mounts each `useX` hook through `QueryClientProvider`

## Notes for review

1. **`filePathPrefix` is intentionally not encoded** to a SonarCloud V1 query param (no direct V1 equivalent exists). It's reserved for client-side post-filtering of results, documented in `encodeIssueFilters`. Worth confirming this is the intended behavior before Phase 8 wires the Issues filter sidebar.
2. **`region` is stored on `SonarClient` but not yet read.** The proxy decides region based on the SPA-supplied `?region=us` query param, and the SPA passes that separately when needed. If we want the client to forward `?region` automatically based on the constructor's `region`, that's a small follow-up — flagging rather than silently shipping.

## Summary

- **TSAN data race**: \`EpollReactor::m_callbacks\` accessed concurrently from caller thread (\`Connect()\` → \`Register()\`) and I/O thread (\`WaitAndDispatch()\`). Fixed by adding \`std::mutex m_mu\`; dispatch copies callback under the lock then invokes it without holding it. Extracted \`DispatchOneEvent()\` helper.

body:
feat(tests): close v0.2.1 carryover — bump coverage floor 70% → 80%

Workspace line coverage measured before this PR: 74.64%.
After: 80.20%. The CI floor in `.github/workflows/coverage.yml`
moves from 70 → 80 (the delta-vs-baseline cap stays at 2pp).

Where the new lines came from:

* `sotfs-cli/tests/sotfsctl_integration.rs` (new): 13 cases
  exercising every `sotfsctl` subcommand (mkfs / check / dump / prov)
  plus the arg-error and unknown-subcommand paths. Pulls
  `sotfsctl.rs` from 0% to 79%.
* `sotfs-cli/tests/dot_and_export.rs` (new): 18 cases for
  `sotfs-dot` (all 5 ops × before/after .dot files) and
  `sotfs-export-hunter` (snapshot mode to stdout and to file, all
  arg-error paths, the `--tail` "not implemented" path). Pulls
  `main.rs` from 0% to 100% and `export_hunter.rs` likewise.
* `sotfs-graph/tests/error_display.rs` (new): 3 cases that format
  every `GraphError` variant. Pulls `error.rs` from 9% to 100%.
* `sotfs-graph/tests/types_methods.rs` (new): 14 cases for the
  small accessors on `Permissions`, `Rights`, `Inode::new_*`,
  `Quota::check_*`, and `Edge::{id, src_node, tgt_node}`. Pulls
  `types.rs` from 66% to 100%.
* `sotfs-graph/tests/graph_api.rs` (new): 22 cases for
  `TypeGraph` accessors (alloc_*_id, contains_*, get_*, remove_*,
  insert_*, lookup_name, list_dir, resolve_path / resolve_parent,
  parent_dir, is_ancestor, dir_for_inode, prov_log {get, mut, take,
  enable, disable}, rebuild_dir_name_idx,
  check_dir_name_idx_consistency, clone_boxed, new_boxed). Pulls
  `graph.rs` from 71% to ~85%.
* `sotfs-ops/tests/export_full.rs` (new): 8 cases that exercise
  `to_dot` (default/full/minimal styles), `to_d3_json` (well-formed
  + escape semantics), `to_graph_hunter` (non-trivial graph), and
  `stats` against a populated fixture (4 files, 1 dir, 1 hard-link,
  1 symlink, 1 xattr). The test lives in `sotfs-ops/tests/`
  because the fixture is built via the DPO ops; sotfs-graph cannot
  cycle back on sotfs-ops.

Bug fixed during the coverage pass:

`sotfs-graph/src/export.rs::json_str` only escaped backslash and
quote, leaving control characters (newline, tab, CR, etc.) bare in
the produced JSON. POSIX permits these bytes in filenames, so
`to_d3_json` would emit invalid JSON for any filesystem that
contained one. Replaced the two-character replacer with a
character-by-character escaper that handles `\\`, `\"`, `\n`, `\r`,
`\t`, `\b`, `\f` and `\uXXXX` for any other C0 control. New
regression case in `export_full.rs::to_d3_json_escapes_special_*`.

Other small things:

- `sotfs-fuse/src/fs.rs`: not bumped here. FUSE callbacks need a
  real mount to exercise; that lives on the v0.2.4 roadmap as a
  separate item under integration testing. The 5% number on this
  file pulls the global average down by ~5pp; everything else is
  ≥ 80% and most ≥ 90%.

- coverage.yml comment: rewrote the threshold-gate explanation to
  reflect the new floor and what closed the gap.

Tests: `cargo test --workspace --release` — all green. Clippy
`-D warnings` — clean.

author: dlf-dds
body:
## Track G — bundle-import IPC contract + integration test

Implements `HANDOFF.md` Track G end-to-end. **Updated 2026-05-09** to adapt to Track B (PR #1) and Track E (PR #2) merging into main while this branch was open.

## CI status

| Check | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **`integration` (Tier-A — IPC contract, stub driver)** | **PASS** | Track G's own workflow. 11/11 tests, 17s. This is the gate Track G's acceptance lives behind. |
| `ci` (vet + test + build) | fail | **Pre-existing on main** — fails identically on the post-merge commit `5ef3fb0` ([run 25611409423](https://github.com/dlf-dds/goat-client/actions/runs/25611409423)). Root cause: `go vet ./...` walks into `internal/ui` which imports Fyne; the `ubuntu-latest` runner lacks `libx11-dev` + `libgl1-mesa-dev` + `pkg-config gl`. Track E's `ci.yml` needs an `apt-get install` step before vet; or, more cheaply, `go vet ./cmd/goat-clientd/... ./internal/ipc/... ./internal/daemon/...` to skip the GUI. Captain follow-up. |
| `release` cross-build (6 targets) | fail | **Pre-existing on main** — fails identically on `5ef3fb0` ([run 25611409424](https://github.com/dlf-dds/goat-client/actions/runs/25611409424)). Root cause: `release.yml` builds the Fyne GUI binary with `CGO_ENABLED=0`, which the OpenGL bindings reject (`build constraints exclude all Go files in .../go-gl/gl/v2.1/gl`). Track E + Track B composition issue. Captain follow-up: either `CGO_ENABLED=1` + per-target cross-toolchain (zig-cc / cosmocc / per-OS runner) for the GUI matrix, or matrix only the daemon. |

Track G does **not** introduce either failure. Verified by running both workflows against my PR head and against main HEAD — same failure mode on both.

## Conflict resolution (from initial merge-conflict state)

Track B's PR #1 landed the GUI-facing IPC contract on main first (`internal/ipc/types.go`, `internal/ipc/client.go`, `internal/ipc/stub.go`) and is consumed by `internal/ui/`. My initial Track G commit had used different type names. To avoid forcing churn on Track B's GUI:

- **Reset** `track/bundle-ipc-test` to `origin/main` and re-authored Track G on top.
- **Adopted** Track B's canonical names: `State`, `BundleInfo`, `StatusInfo`, `Diagnostics`, `Client` interface, `DefaultAddr`, `NewClient`. Track B's `internal/ui/` code compiles unchanged.
- **Extended** the contract with what the daemon-side state machine + integration tests need:
  - `State`: added `not_imported` (initial, pre-bundle) and `disconnecting` (transitional). Track B's `internal/ui/state.go` switch falls through to "disconnected" for unknown states, so the additions are GUI-safe.
  - `StatusInfo`: added `ActiveEndpoint` (the host:port currently in use, distinct from the configured `Endpoints` from the bundle).
  - `Diagnostics`: added `Reachability []EndpointReachability` for per-endpoint detail; aggregate `Reachable` / `ProbeError` fields Track B's GUI reads stay populated.
- **Rewired** `NewClient(addr)` to dispatch by scheme: `stub://` keeps Track B's in-process stub (kept verbatim as `internal/ipc/stub.go`), `unix://<path>` dials the real daemon over a Unix socket, `\\.\pipe\<name>` is a Windows named-pipe stub for Track A.
- **Trimmed** my CI workflow — Track E's `release.yml` already owns the cross-platform desktop matrix (Fyne requires CGO so a `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...` matrix wouldn't apply to the GUI binary). My `integration.yml` now only does the Tier-A integration-tag run + a realprotocol-skip-behavior compile check.

PR is now `MERGEABLE` per `gh pr view`.

## Summary

- **`internal/ipc/`** — daemon-to-GUI IPC contract: extends Track B's types, adds the wire layer (length-prefixed JSON-RPC), adds the daemon-side `Service` interface, adds the `Server` (transport-agnostic dispatch), adds the real `*rpcClient` implementation of `Client`, adds the Unix-socket transport. Windows named-pipe is a forward-compatible stub so cross-build stays green.
- **`internal/daemon/`** — `Service` that owns the tunnel state machine and dispatches IPC methods to two pluggable ports: `BundleVerifier` and `TunnelDriver`. Stub implementations live alongside; Track A swaps in real CBOR-+-Ed25519 verifier and netbird-fork-derived single-peer wg-cp0 driver behind the same interfaces, no IPC-contract change.
- **`cmd/goat-clientd/`** — daemon binary now actually runs an IPC server on `$HOME/.goat-client/sock`, handles SIGINT/SIGTERM, shuts down cleanly. Cross-builds for `linux/{amd64,arm64}` + `darwin/{amd64,arm64}` + `windows/{amd64,arm64}` with `CGO_ENABLED=0`.
- **`tests/integration/`** — 11 Tier-A integration tests (build tag `integration`) that build the daemon, spawn it on a short Unix-socket path, dial via `ipc.NewClient("unix://...")`, and assert state-machine + error-code behavior. Hermetic, ~2s wall-clock total.
- **`tests/integration/realprotocol_test.go`** — sibling Tier-B smoke (build tag `realprotocol`) that brings the wg-cp0 outer tunnel up against a live lab endpoint when `GOAT_LAB_BUNDLE_PATH` is set; skipped otherwise. Pattern lifted from goat-trunk's [Block 50G/I real-protocol e2e harness](https://github.com/dlf-dds/DesertBreadBird/blob/main/docs/design/real-protocol-e2e-validation.md).
- **`.github/workflows/integration.yml`** — Tier-A integration tests + realprotocol-skip compile check on every push and PR. Distinct from Track E's `ci.yml` (always-fast vet/test/build) and `release.yml` (cross-platform release matrix).
- **`.gitignore`** — `.claude/` + `.iso-mode.env` (per-session worktree state from `/iso enter`) + Go build artefacts. Mild scope creep flagged; captain may revert into a separate housekeeping PR if preferred.

## Test plan

- [x] `go vet ./...` green
- [x] `go build ./...` host-native green (Fyne `-lobjc` is a linker warning, not a fatal — the binaries link cleanly)
- [x] Cross-build green on `linux/{amd64,arm64}` + `darwin/{amd64,arm64}` + `windows/{amd64,arm64}` for `cmd/goat-clientd ./internal/ipc/... ./internal/daemon/... ./internal/bundle/...` (`CGO_ENABLED=0 -trimpath -buildvcs=false`). Track E's `release.yml` owns the GUI cross-build.
- [x] `go test -tags integration -count=1 -v ./tests/integration/...` — **11/11 pass in ~2s** locally
- [x] `go test -tags realprotocol -count=1 -v ./tests/integration/...` — skips cleanly when no env vars set
- [ ] CI confirms above on `ubuntu-latest` (workflow run on this PR)
- [ ] Once Track A lands real bundle + tunnel: realprotocol test green against `wg-cp0.lab-sandbox.goat`

## Coordination notes for the captain

- **Contract this PR defines for Track A**: the `ipc.Service` interface (5 methods, mirroring Client), the wire `Request` / `Response` envelope + length-prefixed framing, the stable error-code constants (`ErrCodeBundleInvalid`, `ErrCodeBundleNotImported`, `ErrCodeAlreadyConnected`, `ErrCodeNotConnected`, `ErrCodeTunnelFailed`). Track A's daemon must satisfy `ipc.Service`; the integration tests are the regression guard.
- **Contract this PR defines for Track B**: extends Track B's `Client` interface compatibly. Track B's `internal/ui/` code compiles + runs unchanged. Once this PR lands, Track B can swap from the in-process stub to the real RPC client by changing one line in `internal/ui/app.go` (or `internal/ui/tray.go`) — pass `"unix://"+path` to `ipc.NewClient` instead of bare/empty.
- **Stub bundle format** (`internal/daemon/stub_verifier.go`): `"GCB0"` 4-byte magic + 4-byte big-endian metadata length + JSON `BundleInfo` + opaque payload. Track A's real CBOR + Ed25519 verifier replaces this; the integration tests will need a fixture-format swap at that point (small, mechanical — `EncodeStubBundle` is the only test-side consumer).
- **Out of track scope** (per HANDOFF): real CBOR/Ed25519 parser → Track A; netbird-fork single-peer wg-cp0 driver → Track A; Windows named-pipe transport → Track A; Fyne GUI consumer → Track B (already shipped); cross-platform release matrix → Track E (already shipped).
- **Decision needed before merge?** None. Captain can squash-merge whenever

author: arthurhrc
body:
## Summary

The dual-API split (\`Paragraph\` for fluent chains, \`AddParagraph\` for style configuration) collapses to a single builder.

\`\`\`go
doc.Paragraph(kardec.Text(\"body\"))                       // works as before
doc.Paragraph(kardec.Text(\"body\")).WithStyle(myStyle).LineHeight(1.4)  // no .Done() needed
doc.Paragraph(kardec.Text(\"a\")).Heading(2, kardec.Text(\"next\"))      // chain continues
\`\`\`

### Mechanics

- \`Document.Paragraph\` returns \`*ParagraphRef\`. The ref embeds \`*Document\` so unrelated doc methods continue to chain through field promotion.
- Style overrides mutate the just-appended block in place via interface-value round-trip (read from slice, mutate, write back).
- \`AddParagraph\` and \`ParagraphBuilder\` remain as deprecated aliases pointing at the unified ref. Removed at v1.0.

### Migration

Tests / call sites that captured the chain result in a \`*Document\` variable and passed it to a function expecting \`*Document\` need \`.Document\` once:

\`\`\`go
out, err := render.Bytes(doc.Document)  // was: render.Bytes(doc)
\`\`\`

Sed-fixed across the affected test files in this PR.

## Test plan

- [x] \`go test ./...\` — full suite green
- [x] New ParagraphRef tests cover: chain back to doc, retroactive WithStyle, Align/Justify/LineHeight, AddParagraph alias

author: ssoggytacoman
body:
🛡️ Sentinel: [HIGH] Fix JDBC URL injection vulnerability

🚨 **Severity:** HIGH
💡 **Vulnerability:** The `MySQLManager` constructs its JDBC connection URL string by directly concatenating user-defined properties (`host`, `dbName`, `sslMode`) from the configuration without any validation or sanitization.
🎯 **Impact:** If an attacker can control the configuration parameters, they could append arbitrary JDBC parameters to the connection string. In MySQL, this can lead to remote code execution (e.g., via `autoDeserialize`) or arbitrary file read (e.g., via `allowLoadLocalInfile`) vulnerabilities upon initialization, depending on the driver version.
🔧 **Fix:** Introduced `requireValidJdbcParam` in `SqlSafety` using a strict alphanumeric and hyphen regex `^[a-zA-Z0-9_.\\-]+$` to validate the configuration parameters before appending them to the JDBC URL.
✅ **Verification:** Run `./gradlew test` and verify that the plugin builds and starts correctly with valid MySQL configurations.

author: aerocristobal
body:
Generalizes STORY-002's AXPress wrapper into a perform_ax_action tool that dispatches any standard AX accessibility action and lets agents discover the supported-action list for any element without first walking the full accessibility tree.

Production:
- AXActionEnumerator wraps AXUIElementCopyActionNames behind the bridge for testable action discovery; new AXActionEnumerating protocol for DI
- AXElementInteractor gains generic perform(_:on:); performPress is now a one-line delegation to perform("AXPress", on:) — STORY-002 callers observe no behavior change
- AXApplicationBridge protocol gains copyActionNames(_:); the real impl swallows kAXErrorNoValue / .attributeUnsupported / .actionUnsupported as empty arrays and surfaces other AXErrors via AXResolutionError
- PerformAXActionTool orchestrates resolver → enumerator → interactor: validates at-least-one-locator, applies the same locator precedence and AND-filter post-validation as click_element, branches on whether action was provided (omitted → discovery; provided → whitelist gate → per-element supported-actions check → dispatch). All rejection paths are guaranteed to skip AXUIElementPerformAction
- Whitelist of 8 standard actions (AXPress, AXIncrement, AXDecrement, AXConfirm, AXCancel, AXShowMenu, AXRaise, AXPick); allow_custom=true opt-in for app-defined actions like AXShowAlternateUI
- AccessibilityModule registers perform_ax_action with readOnlyHint: false and destructiveHint: true (broader action surface than click_element, including AXCancel / AXConfirm / arbitrary custom)

Tests (28 new, 276 total green):
- PerformAXActionTool 92.86% line coverage, AXActionEnumerator 100%, AXElementInteractor 87.18% (DoD ≥85% on all three)
- All 5 BDD scenarios + 8 standard actions in the outline mapped to XCTest per STORY-001/002 pattern; story-003-ax-action-performer.feature shipped as living documentation
- 11 dedicated assertions verify interactorSpy.performCallCount == 0 across every error path: missing locator, omitted action, empty action, whitelist reject, allow_custom-but-unsupported, resolver not_found, resolver resolution error, enumerator error, post- validation mismatches (role / title / label / description)
- AXActionEnumeratorSpy added; MockAXApplicationBridge gains copyActionNames + per-element elementActions override map; MockAXUIElement gains supportedActions; AXElementInteractorSpy gains generic perform(_:on:) recording
- ToolRegistrationTests / ToolRouterTests counts updated (2→3 for AccessibilityModule, 66→67 for ToolRouter); STORY-002's ClickElementToolTests + AXElementInteractorTests still green

Discovery mode is the canonical contract from Open Q1: omit `action` to receive { ok: true, supported_actions: [...] } as a non-error response. The whitelist + allow_custom design from Open Q2 catches typos like AXNonsense early without blocking legitimate third-party custom actions. destructiveHint: true is unconditional per Open Q5.

Justified deviation from story §7: MCPError.actionNotSupported is not added — the tool returns the snake_case error code and supported list inline in its JSON response, matching how click_element translates AXNotFoundError to element_not_found. MCPError remains reserved for non-AX system errors per existing codebase convention.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>Kha-kis/arr-dashboard (artifactory.local.hejsan.xyz/docker/khak1s/arr-dashboard)</summary>

### [`v2.18.6`](https://redirect.github.com/Kha-kis/arr-dashboard/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#2186---2026-05-09)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/Kha-kis/arr-dashboard/compare/v2.18.5...v2.18.6)

##### Fixed

-   **Sonarr hunt requests skipping while Radarr worked normally (closes [#​438](https://redirect.github.com/Kha-kis/arr-dashboard/issues/438)).** The queue-threshold pre-flight check counted *every* queue entry against the default threshold of 25 — including items in `completed` (downloaded, waiting for import), `failed`, `warning`, and other stuck states that don't actually consume download-client capacity. Sonarr's queue accumulates these (one entry per episode plus stuck imports), so the threshold was easily exceeded and every hunt skipped. Radarr (one entry per movie, faster import lifecycle) rarely hit this. Live verification on a real Sonarr 4.0.16 instance reproduced the bug exactly: 31 stuck `completed` items, 0 actively downloading — every hunt skipped before fix, hunts proceed after.
    -   `checkQueueThresholdWithSdk` now passes `status: ['queued','downloading','paused','delay']` to `client.queue.get` on Sonarr/Radarr/Lidarr so the threshold reflects items genuinely competing for download slots. Readarr's arr-sdk `QueueResource.get` enumerates known fields and silently drops unknown keys, so the filter cannot be applied there — Readarr's behavior is unchanged from pre-fix and the message is labeled "Queue" (vs "Active queue") to keep the wording honest.
    -   **Connectivity failures now surface as errors, not silent throttle.** The catch branch previously returned `status: "skipped"` with the same shape as a healthy threshold-skip, so an offline Sonarr or rotated API key would silently stop hunting with no notification (the scheduler's `HUNT_FAILED` dispatch only fired from thrown errors, not returned ones). The function now returns a discriminated outcome (`pass` / `threshold-exceeded` / `check-failed`); the caller maps `check-failed` to `status: "error"`, and the scheduler now dispatches `HUNT_FAILED` for returned errors as well.
    -   **Fail-safe on malformed queue responses.** A reverse-proxy returning HTML, a future SDK field rename, or any response missing `totalRecords` previously coalesced to `0` and proceeded as if the queue were empty. Now treated as `check-failed` with an explicit "unexpected response shape" message.
    -   **UI**: the skip/error message is shown inline in the collapsed activity row (instead of only after expanding) with a `title` tooltip for full text on hover, so operators see *why* a hunt was skipped at a glance.

</details>
