author: copilot
body:
This PR adds a repository-native handover convention so any model can resume a feature without human stage narration. It standardizes how current stage, prior context, and next task are derived from repo state.

- **Handover prompt standard (`methodology/implementation/HANDOVER.md`)**
  - Adds a copy/paste prompt block with a single placeholder: `{{UC-XX-slug}}`.
  - Requires strict read order (`AGENTS.md` → `STAGES.md` → `DELIVERY.md` → `HANDOVER.md` → `templates/usecase.md`).
  - Defines deterministic current-stage diagnosis from `features/{{UC-XX-slug}}/stages/` by first empty/missing `output/` artefact stage.
  - Requires reading prior stage outputs + `features/{{UC-XX-slug}}/RESUME.md`, then stating feature/current stage/next task and waiting for human confirmation.

- **Per-feature resume state artifact (`RESUME.md`)**
  - Adds worked example: `features/UC-00-login/RESUME.md` (feature complete state).
  - Adds bootstrap template: `templates/feature-skeleton/RESUME.md` with the required fields populated as `TBD`.

- **Policy updates**
  - `AGENTS.md`: adds explicit **RESUME rule** — after each approved gate, overwrite `features/{{slug}}/RESUME.md` before gate commit.
  - `methodology/implementation/DELIVERY.md`: adds note that `RESUME.md` is required per gate and included in per-gate commits.

Example prompt core introduced in `HANDOVER.md`:

```text
Then locate the current stage by inspecting `features/{{UC-XX-slug}}/stages/` in chronological order. The current stage is the first stage directory that has no `output/` files, or has an `output/` directory with no artefacts.
...
Then read `features/{{UC-XX-slug}}/RESUME.md` for fine-grained state...
...
Then wait for explicit human confirmation before doing anything else.
```

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>


## Problem

There is no standardised way for any model to pick up a feature mid-flight. The human currently has to manually describe where the feature is, what was rejected, and what the next task is. This should be self-orienting from the repo state.

## Changes required

### 1. `methodology/implementation/HANDOVER.md` — new file

A generic orientation prompt template that a human copies and gives to any model. It must:

- Tell the model to read these files in order before doing anything:
  1. `AGENTS.md`
  2. `methodology/implementation/STAGES.md`
  3. `methodology/implementation/DELIVERY.md`
  4. `methodology/implementation/HANDOVER.md` (this file — so the model understands the convention)
  5. `templates/usecase.md`
- Tell the model to locate the current stage by inspecting `features/{{UC-XX-slug}}/stages/` — the current stage is the first stage directory that has no `output/` files or has an `output/` directory with no artefacts
- Tell the model to read all prior stages' `output/` artefacts in chronological order to build full context
- Tell the model to read `features/{{UC-XX-slug}}/RESUME.md` for fine-grained state (corrections, rejections, deferred concepts) that is not visible from folder structure alone
- Tell the model to state out loud: which feature it is working on, which stage it has diagnosed as current, what the next task is — and then **wait for human confirmation** before doing anything
- Remind the model of the standing rules:
  - Gate behaviour: stop after every stage output is produced and wait for explicit human approval before proceeding
  - Commit cadence: one commit per gate approval on the feature branch, message format `feat(UC-XX): Stage NN — <artefact name>`
  - Branch name: `feat/UC-XX-<slug>`
  - Never write artefacts directly to `main`
  - After each gate approval, overwrite `features/{{slug}}/RESUME.md` before committing

The fill-in section the human provides should be minimal — just the feature slug. Everything else the model derives from the repo.

The file should include a ready-to-use prompt block (fenced, copyable) that the human pastes to the model, with `{{UC-XX-slug}}` as the only placeholder.

### 2. `features/UC-00-login/RESUME.md` — new file (worked example)

A worked example `RESUME.md` for the existing UC-00-login feature (which is the completed worked example in the repo). It should show the format an agent writes after each gate. Fields:

- `Feature:` — the UC slug
- `Branch:` — the feature branch name
- `Last completed stage:` — e.g. `Stage 05 — verify`
- `Gate outcome:` — e.g. `Approved`
- `Corrections at last gate:` — any corrections made, or `None`
- `Deferred concepts:` — any concepts explicitly deferred, or `None`
- `Next stage:` — e.g. `None — feature complete and merged`
- `Next task:` — e.g. `None — feature complete`
- `Notes:` — any other context a fresh model needs

Since UC-00-login is complete, all fields should reflect that.

### 3. `templates/feature-skeleton/RESUME.md` — new file (skeleton template)

A blank `RESUME.md` template in the feature skeleton, pre-populated with empty field values so the agent knows the format when it creates a new feature folder. Same fields as above, all values set to `TBD` or empty.

### 4. `AGENTS.md` — add one new rule

Add a rule to the existing agent rules (in the gate/commit section if one exists, otherwise after the last gate rule):

> **RESUME rule:** After each gate is approved by the human, overwrite `features/{{slug}}/RESUME.md` with the current feature state (last completed stage, gate outcome, corrections, deferred concepts, next stage, next task). Do this before running the `git commit` for that gate.

### 5. `methodology/implementation/DELIVERY.md` — add one sentence

In the branch lifecycle section (added by a prior PR) or in §3 (CI surface) — add a note that `RESUME.md` is a required output of each gate and is included in the per-gate commit.

## Constraints

- Match the existing tone and formatting of all files exactly.
- Do not touch any `stages/` CONTEXT.md files or any existing `output/` artefacts.
- Do not modify `features/UC-00-login/` artefacts other than adding the new `RESUME.md`.
- The `HANDOVER.md` prompt block must be self-contained — a human should be able to copy it and give it to any model with only the feature slug filled in.


The following is the prior conversation context from the user's chat exploration (may be truncated):

User: For continuous delivery hygene (which should be noted in a doc of the repo), should a branch already be created for this work and what should be the scope of each branch before it gets merged back into main? Should it be stage by stage or potentially feature by feature (going through all the prior stages?)

Assistant: Good hygiene question, and the answer matters because the stages have very different natures.

---

### Recommended branching scope: **feature per branch**

Branch name convention: `feat/UC-01-register`

The branch lives from the mome...

</details>

body:
Supermarket reviews were saving/displaying the wrong author name (email prefix fallback) and appearing to disappear after page refresh. This change ensures the canonical user full name is persisted on insert, keeps the review list in sync after submission, and hardens seller ID usage so reviews attach to the correct profile.

- **Review insert payload correctness**
  - Normalize route param handling for `id` and guard against missing `supermarket_id` before submit.
  - Persist reviewer name from `user._raw.user_metadata.full_name` into `user_name` (and continue writing `buyer_name` for compatibility).
  - Continue inserting with explicit `supermarket_id` and `buyer_id` to avoid mis-attribution.

- **Post-submit UI synchronization**
  - Trigger `router.refresh()` after successful `supermarket_reviews.insert(...)` so the UI reflects persisted server state immediately.

- **Display-name fallback alignment**
  - Update review normalization to resolve author name in this order: `profiles.full_name` → `review.user_name` → `review.buyer_name` → default label.

```ts
const metadataFullName = user._raw?.user_metadata?.full_name;
const realName = metadataFullName || user.displayName || user.email || 'משתמש';

const reviewData = {
  supermarket_id: id,
  buyer_id: user.uid,
  user_name: realName,
  buyer_name: realName,
  is_anonymous: reviewIsAnonymous,
  rating: reviewRating,
  comment: reviewComment,
};

const { data: inserted, error } = await supabase
  .from('supermarket_reviews')
  .insert(reviewData)
  .select()
  .single();

if (!error) router.refresh();
```

author: iskhakovt
body:
Closes #198.

## Summary

- Adds `restricted boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false` to `profile_classes`. Default preserves today's open-by-default behaviour for every existing class.
- Service composes a `{ not: { tags: ["profile_class:r1", …], match: "any" } }` leaf over restricted classes the profile hasn't opted into. `match: "any"` (not `any_strict`) — only memories carrying one of those tags are excluded; untagged legacy rows pass through.
- **Speaker auto-include is structural, not opt-in**: a profile *always* sees its own writes, regardless of how the operator configured `memory_scope.profileClasses`. The class leaf the Service emits is structurally `scope.profileClasses ∪ {profile.profileClass}`. Applies symmetrically to both the `any_strict` opt-in leaf (when scope is set) and the `NOT` restricted-exclusion leaf (when restricted classes exist). Matches the convention in every personal-data system surveyed — email's Sent folder, Drive owner-implicit-read, PostgreSQL RLS's `USING (owner = current_user)` idiom.
- Today-fast-path preserved: null scope + zero restricted classes still goes through the same `opts ?? {}` short-circuit.
- Telegram surface: `/classes restrict <name>` / `/classes unrestrict <name>`, restricted markers in:
  - `/classes list` — `(restricted)` inline + sentence legend
  - `/profile list` — `[class=intimate!]` + `(! = restricted)` legend at list level
  - `/profile scope` and `/status` — `classes: general, intimate (speaker) (! = restricted)` (auto-include rendered explicitly so the operator's view matches the effective filter; both surfaces conditionally fetch the registries — `/status` skips the round-trip when scope and speaker are both null)
- `/classes rm` is independent of `restricted` — the FK-RESTRICT contract still gates deletion of in-use classes regardless of the flag.

## Behaviour notes

- Marking a class `restricted` has no retroactive effect on already-tagged Hindsight memories — same forward-only semantics as `/compartments rm`.
- Pre-existing PR-#180 deployments that intentionally configured `scope.profileClasses` to exclude the speaker class will now have the speaker class auto-included. The auditor / write-only pattern is expressed via `profile.profileClass = null` (write untagged) plus `memory_scope.profileClasses = […]` for what to read — don't conflate "what tag to stamp on writes" with "speaker identity in the recall filter."

## Architecture

- `createService` gains two adjacent positional args (`speakerClass: string | null`, `restrictedClassNames: ReadonlyArray<string>`) right after `memoryScope`.
- The orchestrator (`handle-message.ts`) loads the restricted-class list once per turn via `listProfileClasses(userId)` keyed on the **conversation user** — not `profile.userId`, since an org profile speaks for the conversation user and restricted-class semantics follow the user's own registry. Per-turn round-trip; future-cache breadcrumb left in the comment.
- `ConversationStatusSummary.profile` gains a `profileClass: string | null` field so `/status` can surface the speaker auto-include via `formatScope`.
- `formatScope` accepts an optional `speakerClass` arg and renders `(speaker)` annotation when the class isn't already in the explicit list.
- `buildIsolationLeaves` (renamed from `buildScopeLeaves`) — the symbol now matches the doc-comment, which always described it as the isolation filter; the rename reflects that scope-leaves and the restricted-NOT leaf are both emitted from the same function.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` clean
- [x] `pnpm lint` clean (3 pre-existing warnings unrelated)
- [x] `pnpm test` — 2847 passed (48 new tests across 3 commits)

New unit coverage:
- **Service NOT-leaf** (8 cases): null scope + restricted; today-fast-path; speaker auto-include; composition with compartments/trust; explicit opt-in dropping the leaf; full opt-in suppressing NOT entirely; retain unaffected; reflect symmetry.
- **Service `any_strict` speaker auto-include** (4 cases): adds speaker when not in list; doesn't duplicate when present; no-op when speakerClass null; composes with NOT leaf for combined restricted+explicit-scope case.
- **Store** (4 cases): `createProfileClass` defaults `restricted: false`; `setProfileClassRestricted` flips on/off idempotent + unknown-name → `updated:false` + works while a profile references the class.
- **Transport** (3 cases): `setRestricted` happy path, `profile_class_not_found`, `identity_rejected`.
- **Telegram `/classes`** (4 cases): restrict/unrestrict happy paths, no-name usage, `profile_class_not_found` surfacing, list-with-legend annotation.
- **`/profile scope` conditional fetch** (4 cases): skips `profileClasses.list` when `scope.profileClasses` unset; fetches and marks restricted classes with `!`; confirmation echoes the legend on set; surfaces fetch error.
- **`/profile list` registry-loading** (2 cases): loads both registries and annotates restricted profile classes; degrades gracefully on registry-list error.
- **`/status` registry-loading** (4 cases): renders `!` markers when scope sets profileClasses; renders speaker `(speaker)` annotation alongside `!`; skips fetches when scope and speaker are both null; degrades gracefully on registry error.
- **handle-message wiring** (2 cases): end-to-end recall payload contains the right NOT leaf when restricted classes exist with speaker auto-include; today-fast-path preserved when no class is flagged restricted.
- **`formatScope` / `renderProfileList`** (10 cases): restricted markers + combined custom + restricted legends; speaker `(speaker)` annotation; no-duplicate when in list; null speaker leaves classes unannotated; class-level legend at list level when no `formatScope` call provides one; `*` vs `!` collision avoidance.

body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|
| [mirror.gcr.io/freikin/dawarich](https://redirect.github.com/Freika/dawarich) | patch | `1.7.6` → `1.7.7` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>Freika/dawarich (mirror.gcr.io/freikin/dawarich)</summary>

### [`v1.7.7`](https://redirect.github.com/Freika/dawarich/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#177---2026-05-09)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/Freika/dawarich/compare/1.7.6...1.7.7)

##### ⚠️ Breaking changes

**Prometheus metrics backend migrated to Yabeda.**

Dawarich now uses the Yabeda monitoring framework instead of `discourse/prometheus_exporter`. Self-hosters who scrape Prometheus metrics from Dawarich should update their configuration.

If Sidekiq is unreachable during a scrape, web returns its own metrics only and
logs a warning. Prometheus sees a momentary gap in `sidekiq_*` rather than a
failed scrape.

**Scrape target** (requires HTTP basic auth with `METRICS_USERNAME` / `METRICS_PASSWORD`):

- Web: `http://dawarich_app:3000/metrics`

**Custom `dawarich_archive_*` metric names are unchanged.** Dashboards and alerts built on these metrics continue to work.

**Infrastructure metric names have changed.** If you have dashboards built on `ruby_*`, `active_record_*`, or similar metrics emitted by `prometheus_exporter`, you must update them:

| Category                                             | Before                                      | After                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| HTTP requests (total)                                | `ruby_http_requests_total`                  | `rails_requests_total`                                      |
| HTTP request duration                                | `ruby_http_request_duration_seconds`        | `rails_request_duration`                                    |
| Sidekiq job count                                    | `ruby_sidekiq_jobs_total`                   | `sidekiq_jobs_executed_total`                               |
| Sidekiq failed jobs                                  | `ruby_sidekiq_failed_jobs_total`            | `sidekiq_jobs_failed_total`                                 |
| Sidekiq job duration                                 | `ruby_sidekiq_job_duration_seconds`         | `sidekiq_job_runtime_seconds`                               |
| Sidekiq queue latency                                | `ruby_sidekiq_queue_latency_seconds`        | `sidekiq_queue_latency`                                     |
| Sidekiq queue backlog                                | `ruby_sidekiq_queue_backlog_total`          | `sidekiq_jobs_waiting_count`                                |
| Sidekiq process count                                | `ruby_sidekiq_process_count`                | `sidekiq_active_processes`                                  |
| Puma workers                                         | `ruby_puma_workers`                         | `puma_workers`                                              |
| Puma backlog                                         | `ruby_puma_request_backlog`                 | `puma_backlog`                                              |
| Puma thread pool capacity                            | `ruby_puma_thread_pool_capacity`            | `puma_pool_capacity`                                        |
| ActiveRecord pool                                    | `active_record_connection_pool_connections` | `activerecord_connection_pool_size`                         |
| Process/GC (e.g. `ruby_rss`, `ruby_heap_live_slots`) | emitted                                     | not emitted by default; add a custom Yabeda group if needed |

**Removed environment variables:**

- `PROMETHEUS_EXPORTER_HOST`, `PROMETHEUS_EXPORTER_HOST_SIDEKIQ` — no longer needed. Metrics are served in-process by each application.

**Retained environment variables:**

- `PROMETHEUS_EXPORTER_ENABLED` — still the single on/off switch.
- `METRICS_USERNAME`, `METRICS_PASSWORD` — unchanged.
- `PROMETHEUS_EXPORTER_PORT` — port the in-process Sidekiq metrics exporter binds to (default 9394).

**New optional environment variable:**

- `SIDEKIQ_METRICS_URL` — internal URL the web container uses to fetch Sidekiq metrics (default `http://dawarich_sidekiq:9394/metrics`). Override on Dokku, Kubernetes, or any deployment where the worker container's hostname differs from the docker-compose default.

**Prometheus scrape config example:**

```yaml
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: dawarich
    metrics_path: /metrics
    basic_auth:
      username: prometheus     # set via METRICS_USERNAME
      password: prometheus     # set via METRICS_PASSWORD
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['dawarich_app:3000']
```

##### Fixed

- Fixed monthly stats failing with a "Stats update failed" notification when the month's distance exceeded the int4 limit (2,147,483,647 m ≈ 2.15M km). Affected months stayed stuck on the prior value until recalculated. [#​1996](https://redirect.github.com/Freika/dawarich/issues/1996)
- 500 error on the imports page. [#​2683](https://redirect.github.com/Freika/dawarich/issues/2683)
- Insights weekly pattern now refreshes after monthly stats change, instead of showing a stale snapshot until the next monthly digest job runs. [#​2478](https://redirect.github.com/Freika/dawarich/issues/2478)
- Points with no reverse-geocoding result (ocean, wilderness) are now marked as attempted instead of being re-queued every nightly run; use "Start Reverse Geocoding" to retry after switching providers. [#​2271](https://redirect.github.com/Freika/dawarich/issues/2271)
- Activity detection now falls back to displacement when the tracker reports 0 m/s, so OwnTracks Significant Change mode and similar low-power setups stop misclassifying real movement as stationary. Run **Map v2 → Settings → Recalculate tracks & stats** to apply to existing tracks. [#​2390](https://redirect.github.com/Freika/dawarich/issues/2390)
- Redis no longer balloons (multi-GB) when browsing photos with Immich or Photoprism connected. Photo thumbnails are no longer copied into the server-side Redis cache; the browser caches them directly via `Cache-Control` instead. [#​1609](https://redirect.github.com/Freika/dawarich/issues/1609)
- Drag-selecting a region on the map now includes visits attached to your saved Areas (Home, Work, etc.), instead of silently dropping area-only visits from the visit tray. [#​2420](https://redirect.github.com/Freika/dawarich/issues/2420)

</details>

author: hamer1818
body:
## What ran successfully on the previous PR

Run [25613885430](https://github.com/hamer1818/TulparLang/actions/runs/25613885430) actually produced numbers end-to-end on commit `5c48f90`:

- `loopsum:Tulpar AOT=1.8 ms`, `fib:Tulpar AOT=28.2 ms` (vs `gcc -O2` at 0.6 / 18.1 ms — runner is fast).
- `Tulpar listen=15 951 rps`, `Tulpar listen_evented=16 764 rps`.
- `Tulpar listen_async=0 rps`, `Tulpar listen_pool=0 rps` ← real Tulpar bugs the now-fixed barrier deadlock no longer hides.
- `Python ThreadingHTTP=98 rps` ← suspect (way slower than the Windows seed). Real number from this CI runner; investigation is separate work.

## What this PR fixes

The final step blew up:

```
remote: error: GH006: Protected branch update failed for refs/heads/main.
remote: - 3 of 3 required status checks are expected.
```

Branch protection on `main` requires `build-linux` / `build-macos` / `build-windows` to be green before any push lands. The bot's `GITHUB_TOKEN` can't bypass that — which is correct policy, you don't want a workflow sneaking past the build gate.

So the bot now uses the **same merge flow as every other change**: push to a bench branch, open a PR, enable auto-merge with squash. After the build checks pass on the bench branch, GitHub squashes it into `main` automatically.

## How the loop guard still works

The PR title is `ci(benchmarks): refresh results from CI run [bench skip]`. When auto-merge squashes, the squash commit on `main` uses the PR title by default — so `[bench skip]` lands in the commit message. The `workflow_run` trigger filter at the top of `bench.yml`:

```yaml
if: |
  github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
  (github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' &&
   !contains(github.event.workflow_run.head_commit.message, '[bench skip]'))
```

…sees `[bench skip]` and refuses to fire bench.yml again. Loop closed.

## Side fix in update_readme.py

Previous header sentence was hard-coded to `Tulpar's listen_async serves X× the throughput of Node`. With listen_async at 0 rps in CI, that printed `0.0× the throughput of Node` — meaningless. Now we pick the fastest *working* Tulpar listener for that sentence (so a partial failure still produces a sane headline), and we omit the sentence entirely if every Tulpar listener fails.

The 0-rps rows for `listen_async` / `listen_pool` stay visible in the table — that's a real Tulpar regression worth seeing, not something to paper over.

## Permission delta

Added `pull-requests: write` for `gh pr create` and `gh pr merge --auto`. `contents: write` stays for the bench-branch push. Direct main push is no longer used.

## Test plan

- [x] `pyyaml.safe_load(bench.yml)` clean
- [x] `py -m py_compile benchmarks/update_readme.py` clean
- [x] Synthetic JSON with 0-rps `listen_async` + `listen_pool` rows: headline sentence picks `listen_evented` (the fastest non-zero), table preserves the 0 rows
- [ ] **First post-merge run**: bench should land via PR. Watch for: PR opens automatically, auto-merge enables, squash commit on main carries `[bench skip]`, next bench.yml fires and skips.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary Adds a `setup_verifiers_tracing()` function that monkey-patches the core `Environment`, `MultiTurnEnv`, and `ToolEnv` classes at runtime to inject Braintrust tracing. This is an alternative to the existing drop-in replacement classes in the experimental folder — users just call one function at the top of their environment file and all subclasses automatically produce traces. **Usage:** ```python from verifiers.envs.experimental.braintrust_tracing.integration import setup_verifiers_tracing setup_verifiers_tracing() ``` **What gets patched:** - `Environment.generate` — wrapped to auto-generate unique run-level tags per eval run for filtering in Braintrust (calls original) - `Environment.get_model_response` — wrapped to add model_request spans (calls original) - `Environment._run_rollout_state` — replaced to add rollout + scoring spans - `Environment._run_group_states` — replaced to add group + per-rollout child spans - `MultiTurnEnv.rollout` — replaced to add setup/turn/timeout spans - `ToolEnv.call_tool` — wrapped to add tool_call spans (calls original) - `ToolEnv.env_response` — replaced to pass `state=` to `call_tool` for span context Patching is idempotent (guarded by `__verifiers_bt_patched__` class marker). Zero overhead when `BRAINTRUST_API_KEY` is not set. ### Updates since last revision - **Added `generate()` wrap for run-level tags**: Each `generate()` call now auto-generates a unique `run--` tag via `_bt.set_run_tags()` and attaches it to every trace in that run. Tags are cleared after the call completes. This enables filtering/grouping by eval run in the Braintrust UI. Previously, `set_run_tags()` was only called from the experimental `environment.py` drop-in class and was missing from the monkey-patching path. - **Fixed critical MRO inheritance bug in `_is_patched`**: Changed from `getattr(cls, _PATCH_MARKER, False)` to `cls.__dict__.get(_PATCH_MARKER, False)`. The previous implementation followed Python's MRO, so after patching `Environment`, the inherited marker caused `_patch_multiturn_env()` and `_patch_tool_env()` to silently skip — meaning turn-level, tool-call, and setup spans were never installed. - **Removed dead code**: Removed unused `_orig_run_rollout_state`, `_orig_run_group_states`, and `_orig_env_response` captures that were saved but never called. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] **`_run_rollout_state`, `_run_group_states`, `MultiTurnEnv.rollout`, and `ToolEnv.env_response` are full method replacements, not wrappers.** Any future changes to the core methods won't be picked up by the patched versions. Verify the reimplemented logic matches the current core methods exactly (e.g. compare `_traced_run_rollout_state` against `Environment._run_rollout_state` in `environment.py`). - [ ] **Subclass overrides bypass patched methods.** If an environment subclass (e.g. `MiniBrowseEnv`) overrides `call_tool` or `env_response`, it must explicitly pass `state=state` to `super().call_tool(...)` for tool_call spans to appear. Verify any subclass overrides propagate state correctly. - [ ] **No automated tests for the integration.** Run an actual eval with `setup_verifiers_tracing()` and verify: (a) traces appear in Braintrust with nested span hierarchy (rollout → turn → model_request / tool_call → scoring), (b) each eval run gets a unique tag visible in the Braintrust UI for filtering, and (c) tool call spans have correct timing/duration. - [ ] **`_bt._INSTANCE = None` directly mutates a private module-level singleton** to force re-init when `api_key`/`project` are passed. Verify this doesn't race with concurrent access. ### Notes - Based on PR #10 which added the experimental Braintrust tracing folder (drop-in replacement classes + `braintrust_tracing.py` helpers). This PR adds the monkey-patching layer on top. - The `generate()` wrap is a safe wrapper pattern (just sets/clears tags around the original call), unlike the replaced methods which reimplement logic. - The MRO bug fix was critical — without it, only `Environment`-level patches would have been applied, while `MultiTurnEnv` and `ToolEnv` patches would have been silently skipped. author: shacollision
body:
## Summary

Adds the `Collection` variant to `PubkyAppPostKind` plus a typed `PubkyAppCollectionContent` envelope so a collection post can carry a `name`, optional `description`, and an ordered list of post URIs in `attachments`. No new homeserver path; no new top-level type.

**Stacked on top of #115** (the v0.4.5 forwards-compat shim). Reviewers: please review only the commit range above #115 — the v0.4.5 PR is independent. This PR will be retargeted from `feat/spec-v0.4.5-postkind-unknown-shim` to `main` once #115 merges.

## Spec changes

- `PubkyAppPostKind::Collection` placed before `Unknown` so the `#[serde(other)]` catch-all still works.
- `FromStr`, `Display`, both WASM kind-getters wired for the new variant.
- `PubkyAppCollectionContent { name, description }` struct, parsed inside `validate` but never re-serialized as a top-level homeserver object.
- **Forward-compat by design**: NO `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`. Future additive envelope fields (e.g. `cover_image`) must not break older parsers.
- Three new limits (`collection_content_max_length=2_000`, `collection_items_max_count=100`, `collection_item_uri_max_length=300`).
- Kind-gated `validate` early-branch: forbids parent and embed, parses the envelope, validates name (1..=100), description (..=500), attachment count (..=100), per-URI length (..=300), protocol allowlist. Existing kind-switch tuple is untouched for the six legacy kinds.
- VERSION bumped to 0.5.0.

## Locks v1 envelope shape

The envelope ships with **only `name` and `description`**. Deferred from v1:

- No `is_listed` / privacy flag — anything in `/pub/` is public.
- No `is_locked` — Paykit / locks are future work, and may end up as a post-level attribute (across all kinds) rather than buried in the collection envelope.
- No follow-collection primitive, reserved-label registry, or per-item curator commentary.

author: wasthatrudy
body:
## Problem

Multi-trace search (`?traceID=a,b,c`) silently drops any traceID the backend can't return. The query API answers with `{ data, errors: [{msg, traceID}] }` so the per-trace failure is on the wire, but `searchDone` in `reducers/trace.ts` only iterates `payload.data`, so failed IDs never make it into `state.traces` or `state.search.results` and the UI shows no indication. `fetchMultipleTracesDone` in the same file already ingests `payload.errors`, so this is essentially a parity gap.

## Fix

Extend `searchDone` to walk `payload.errors`, store each entry as `{id, error, state: ERROR}` in the trace map, and push the failed IDs into `search.results` so downstream selectors see them. `stateTraceXformer` in `SearchTracePage/index.tsx` now splits the IDs into successful traces and errored ones, exposing a new `traceErrors` prop that flows into `SearchResults`. The list view renders an error row per failed ID alongside the successful results, using a small new `ResultItemError` component rather than overloading `ResultItem`. Empty-state handling is updated so a search that returns only errors shows the error rows instead of "No trace results."

The trace-diff cohort path (`fetchMultipleTraces`) already handled errors and is left alone. `rawTraces` (used for the JSON download) continues to contain only successful results.

## Testing

- Reducer test in `trace.test.js` for a `searchDone` payload that mixes `data` and `errors`.
- `mapStateToProps` test in `SearchTracePage/index.test.jsx` asserting the selector returns errored IDs in `traceErrors` and excludes them from `traces`.
- `SearchResults/index.test.jsx` renders error rows for each `traceErrors` entry, including the case where no successful traces are present.
- Unit test for `ResultItemError` covering the label, trace ID, and optional message.

`npm run lint`, `npm run tsc-lint`, `npm test`, `npm run build` green locally on Node 24.

Fixes #51

body:
## Summary

- Add `k8s-deployment-security-context` ADR guard check enforcing ADR-006-R2 against both base manifest snapshots (`platform/k8s/gcp/base/`) and helm-template-rendered output of the authoritative chart at `platform/charts/shifter` (per ADR-007). Per pod: `seccompProfile RuntimeDefault`. Per container/initContainer (effective context, honoring pod-level inheritance): `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, `capabilities.drop: ['ALL']` with no `capabilities.add` key, `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`, `runAsNonRoot: true`, `privileged` not `true`, container-level `seccompProfile.type` (when set) `RuntimeDefault`, positive integer `runAsUser`/`runAsGroup` (booleans rejected since Python's `bool` is a subclass of `int`).
- Wire the check into ADR-006-R2 (`docs/adr/index.yaml`) and the ADR guard's `ci` level, plus a dedicated `adr-guard-k8s` pre-commit hook (`language: python`, `additional_dependencies: pyyaml>=6.0`) scoped to `platform/k8s/gcp/base/*.{yaml,yml}` and `platform/charts/shifter/`. The system-Python `adr-guard-fast` hook stays dependency-free.
- Install CI dependencies hermetically per job in `.github/workflows/_quality.yml`: PyYAML pinned to 6.0.2 (`--no-deps --target $RUNNER_TEMP/py-deps`, `PYTHONPATH` on the run step) and Helm pinned to v3.15.4 (downloaded under `$RUNNER_TEMP`, SHA256-verified against the published checksum before extraction, `$GITHUB_PATH`-prepended). No `--user` installs, no sudo, no mutable host state on self-hosted runners.
- Remove the now-redundant `ADR-006-R2` exception from `docs/adr/exceptions.yaml`. Originally filed when the manifests lacked security contexts; all seven base deployments and the chart helpers in `platform/charts/shifter/templates/_helpers.tpl` have since been hardened to 1000/1000 for app/guacd and 1001/1001 for guacamole-client. The unrelated ADR-006-R3 NetworkPolicy exception remains.
- Robustness: missing chart directory, missing values file, empty/missing `containers` list, and malformed `spec`/`spec.template`/`spec.template.spec` mappings all produce actionable violations rather than silent passes or crashes. Violation paths stay repo-relative (values file or chart path) so existing exception globs in `docs/adr/exceptions.yaml` continue to match.

Maintainer decision Q-P1-A1 says Apple Developer Program is unavailable for v0.1.0, so this PR implements ad-hoc signing only. It intentionally does not notarize, staple, or enable hardened runtime; those remain v0.2 follow-ups.

author: abhigyanpatwari
body:
## Summary

Closes #1466.

Cursor 2.4 (released 2026-01-22) shipped generic `preToolUse`/`postToolUse` hooks with matchers `Shell|Read|Write|Grep|Delete|Task|MCP:<tool>`. The current `gitnexus-cursor-integration/hooks/hooks.json` still uses the 2.3-era `beforeShellExecution`, so graph augmentation only fires when the agent runs `rg`/`grep` via shell — `Read` and `Grep` (the agent's far more common tools) get no graph context.

This PR brings Cursor parity (and slight superset) with the Claude Code hook coverage:

- **`gitnexus-cursor-integration/hooks/hooks.json`** — single `postToolUse` entry matching `Shell|Read|Grep`, invoking the new Node script.
- **`gitnexus-cursor-integration/hooks/gitnexus-hook.cjs`** (new) — cross-platform Node hook ported from the bash + `jq` script. Mirrors safety patterns from `gitnexus/hooks/claude/gitnexus-hook.cjs`:
  - `path.isAbsolute(cwd)` validation
  - `.gitnexus/` discovery with linked-worktree fallback (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir`)
  - Global-registry exclusion (`isGlobalRegistryDir` heuristic)
  - `npx.cmd` on Windows, `--` end-of-options marker (#200), `.slice(0, 200)` debug truncation
  - Graceful failure (`status === 0`, no broken pipe to Cursor)
  - Per-tool pattern extraction:
    - `Grep` → `toolInput.query` (also `pattern` / `regex` aliases)
    - `Read` → file basename stripped to identifier chars (≥ 3 chars)
    - `Shell` → existing rg/grep arg parser
  - Emits `{ "additional_context": "..." }` (Cursor 2.4 shape), not Claude's nested `hookSpecificOutput`.
- **`gitnexus-cursor-integration/hooks/augment-shell.sh`** (deleted) — bash + `jq` pipeline doesn't run on Windows and only covered Shell.
- **`gitnexus/test/unit/cursor-hook.test.ts`** (new) — 33 regression tests. Coverage:
  - File presence + legacy `augment-shell.sh` removal
  - `hooks.json` wiring (matcher, command, version, no leftover `beforeShellExecution`)
  - Source-level invariants: no `shell: true`, `npx.cmd`, `path.isAbsolute(cwd)`, `.slice(0, 200)`, `additional_context` (not `hookSpecificOutput`), pattern length ≥ 3, end-of-options marker, `.gitnexus` gating, linked-worktree resolution
  - `extractPattern` coverage per tool (Grep / Read / Shell)
  - Behavioral early-exit tests: empty stdin, invalid JSON, relative cwd, unindexed cwd, unknown tool name, non-search Shell commands, 2-char query, basename with no identifier chars, missing file path, case-insensitive tool name matching
  - Output parser sanity (well-formed JSON, empty stdout, malformed JSON)
- **`README.md` / `gitnexus/README.md`** — editor-support table now reads `**Cursor** | Yes | Yes | Yes (postToolUse) | **Full**` instead of `— | MCP + Skills`.
- **`gitnexus/src/cli/augment.ts`** + **`gitnexus/src/core/augmentation/engine.ts`** — doc-string `Cursor beforeShellExecution` → `Cursor postToolUse`; engine doc tool list expanded to `grep/glob/read/search`.

### Design notes

- **`postToolUse` only**, not also `preToolUse`. Augmentation is observational (the agent sees enriched context after the tool ran), not gating, so the second matcher is dead weight.
- **Read pattern = file basename** (stripped to identifier chars), not the raw file path. Engine uses BM25 over symbol names, so the basename is a higher-signal token than `src/auth/handler.ts`.
- **`codebase_search` left unhandled.** Cursor's docs (https://cursor.com/docs/agent/hooks) don't list it as a matchable tool name. Per the issue's open question, semantic-search miss is acceptable — `Read`/`Grep`/`Shell` already cover the dominant paths.

### Risk

Low. Change is isolated to `gitnexus-cursor-integration/` plus four doc-string / README cells. The augment CLI and `core/augmentation/engine.ts` API are unchanged — neither cares which harness called them. Cursor users on 2.3 will silently lose hook augmentation; users on 2.4+ gain `Read`/`Grep` coverage on top of the existing `Shell` path.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/cursor-hook.test.ts` — 33 / 33 pass in ~0.6s
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/hooks.test.ts test/unit/cursor-hook.test.ts` — 120 / 120 pass (new tests + existing Claude hook tests)
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — 0 errors
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx eslint test/unit/cursor-hook.test.ts ../gitnexus-cursor-integration/hooks/gitnexus-hook.cjs src/cli/augment.ts src/core/augmentation/engine.ts` — 0 issues on touched code
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx prettier --check ../gitnexus-cursor-integration/hooks/{hooks.json,gitnexus-hook.cjs} test/unit/cursor-hook.test.ts src/cli/augment.ts src/core/augmentation/engine.ts` — clean
- [x] Manual smoke: piped synthetic JSON for Grep / Read / Shell rg / Shell ls events through the new hook — exits 0, no spurious output for non-search calls
- [x] Pre-commit hook (lint-staged + typecheck) passes locally

## Out of scope

- `gitnexus-cursor-integration/` README — file doesn't exist; Cursor users currently copy `hooks/`+`skills/` directly. If install docs land later, they should reference `gitnexus-hook.cjs` not `augment-shell.sh`.
- `setup.ts` — does not currently install Cursor hooks (only MCP config + skills); unchanged here.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Low risk: changes are isolated to Cursor integration wiring/docs plus a new hook script and regression tests; main risk is hook behavior differences across Cursor versions or tool-input field variations causing missed augmentation.
> 
> **Overview**
> Upgrades the Cursor integration from the legacy `beforeShellExecution` bash hook to a Cursor 2.4+ `postToolUse` hook that augments **`Shell`/`Read`/`Grep`** tool results with GitNexus graph context.
> 
> Adds a cross-platform Node hook (`gitnexus-hook.cjs`) with safer pattern extraction, `.gitnexus`/worktree detection, and Windows `npx.cmd` handling, deletes the old `augment-shell.sh`, and introduces unit tests to lock in the hook/manifest contract.
> 
> Updates the top-level docs and `gitnexus/README.md` to mark Cursor hooks as **full support** with manual install instructions, and adjusts related docstrings in `augment.ts` and the augmentation engine.
>

author: mrbildo
body:
## Summary

Frontend half of card #220 — backend evidence model landed in PR #162 (`3deb083` on `release/install-runway`).

- New `StaticSitePanel` and `ExecutablePanel` probe panels.
- Soft-nudge box on the Executable panel when the binary looks like a self-contained .NET publish (Bill ruling #2 — single panel, informational, never side-by-side with `dotnet-runtime`).
- `AppCreatePage` handles `suggestedStrategy='notApplicable'` as a free-string literal (Bill ruling #1) — surfaces evidence as a hint without auto-filling any strategy field.

## Files changed

- `frontend/src/probes/StaticSitePanel.tsx` + test — index.html presence, HTML file count, capped asset size (renders `200 MB+` at backend cap), nested-asset layout indicator.
- `frontend/src/probes/ExecutablePanel.tsx` + test — binary name + size, `1 of N candidates` hint when multiple .exe candidates, soft-nudge box gated on `data.isManagedDotnet`.
- `frontend/src/probes/probe-registry.ts` + test — register both new panels (7 panel types total).
- `frontend/src/api/types.ts` — `StaticSiteProbe` + `ExecutableProbe` added to the `ProbeEntry` discriminated union. `DetectStrategyResponse.suggestedStrategy` tightened to a `SuggestedStrategy` string-literal union including `notApplicable`.
- `frontend/src/pages/AppCreatePage.tsx` — `notApplicable` branch surfaces evidence as a hint without auto-fill.
- `frontend/src/lib/format.ts` + test — new `formatBytes` helper for human-readable byte display (1024-base, KB/MB/GB suffix).

## Soft-nudge copy

The Executable panel's nudge box renders only when `data.isManagedDotnet === true`:

> **Looks like .NET.** Re-registering this app as `dotnet-app` enables ASP.NET Core defaults (health checks, environment variables, port injection).

Styled as a `wm-bg-inset` box with a 2px cyan left border — informational, not a warning. Gracefully invisible when the flag is false.

## Backward compat

Additive — the existing `dotnet-runtime`, `dotnet-dependencies`, `node`, `react`, `typescript` panels and their AppType bindings are untouched. The curator's AppType-aware filtering (suppressing Node panels under `static-site`, etc.) is a backend-side change shipped in #162; the frontend renders whatever the curated `probes` array contains.

## Verification

- `npm run build` — tsc + Vite, 0 errors.
- `npm run lint` — Biome, 129 files, 0 errors.
- `npm run format:check` — clean.
- `npm run test` — 347 tests pass (321 baseline + 26 new: 10 StaticSitePanel + 8 ExecutablePanel + 2 probe-registry + 6 formatBytes).

## Test plan

- [ ] Register a self-contained .NET single-file publish as `executable` and verify the soft-nudge appears on the app detail page.
- [ ] Register the same binary as `dotnet-app` and verify the nudge does NOT appear (the dotnet-runtime panel renders instead).
- [ ] Register a static-site directory and verify the StaticSitePanel renders with the expected counts/sizes.
- [ ] Browse to a `static-site` directory in the create form and verify `notApplicable` surfaces as a hint without populating the discovery strategy field.

The previous PR #25 ("align typescript with angular build peer range") only pinned the Angular packages; the TypeScript major was left at 6.0.3 in `package.json`, which is what `npm ci` rejected. This PR completes the alignment and prevents the next Renovate bump from re-introducing the conflict.

- Make `flet-geolocator.Geolocator` actually work end-to-end on web and stop silently swallowing errors on desktop:
  - `get_last_known_position()` now returns `Optional[GeolocatorPosition]` instead of crashing with `TypeError: argument after ** must be a mapping, not NoneType` when no fix is cached.
  - `get_current_position()` no longer hangs forever on web — added a Dart-side `Future.timeout` workaround for the upstream [`geolocator_web` 4.1.3](https://pub.dev/packages/geolocator_web) `inMicroseconds`/`inMilliseconds` timeout typo, and picked sensible web defaults (`time_limit: 30s`, `maximum_age: 5m`) that scope only to single-shot calls (the position stream is left alone).
  - Fixed the Dart side reading `args["settings"]` when Python sends `args["configuration"]`, which silently dropped the configuration on every `getCurrentPosition` call.
  - The position stream is now gated behind a registered `on_position_change` / `on_error` handler, and cancels the previous subscription on `update()` so configuration changes don't leak listeners or trigger CoreLocation prompts at random times.
  - Platform exceptions (`LocationServiceDisabledException`, `PermissionDeniedException`, `PermissionDefinitionsNotFoundException`, `PermissionRequestInProgressException`, `PositionUpdateException`, `TimeoutException`) are translated into actionable error messages via a private `_GeolocatorException` whose `toString()` drops the default `Exception:` prefix, so Python sees `RuntimeError("Location request timed out.")` rather than `RuntimeError("Exception: ...")`.
- Updated the example to wrap each `geo.*` call in `try/except RuntimeError` so failures land in a `SnackBar` instead of escaping to the global app-error banner, and to handle `None` from `get_last_known_position`.
- Added a docs section for the web cache window (`maximum_age` default + override) and a macOS troubleshooting note for the recurring `POSITION_UNAVAILABLE` failure mode (`sudo killall locationd`).
- Bumped `packages/flet/pubspec.yaml` to `0.85.1` and added CHANGELOG entries (root and `packages/flet/`) following the 0.83.1 precedent.

## Test plan

- [ ] Native macOS: Request Permission → Get Permission Status → Get Current Position returns a fix and renders a snackbar.
- [ ] Native macOS: Get Last Known Position returns either a position or "No last known position available." (no crash).
- [ ] Web (Chrome / Edge / Safari) on `localhost`: Get Current Position returns a fix when the browser can reach `locationd`; surfaces a snackbar with `Location request timed out.` (not a hang) when the OS pipeline is wedged.
- [ ] Web: position stream stays subscribed only when `on_position_change` is set; toggling the configuration cancels the previous subscription instead of leaking it.
- [ ] Permission-denied path: snackbar shows `Could not get current position: Location permission denied: ...` instead of a global error banner.
- [ ] Rebuild the Flutter web client (`client/build/web/`) and the desktop runner before regression-testing — Dart-side changes don't take effect otherwise.

## Summary by Sourcery

Improve flet-geolocator reliability and error handling across web and desktop and prepare the 0.85.1 release.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent get_last_known_position from crashing when no cached position exists by returning an optional position value instead.
- Ensure get_current_position on web times out with a clear error instead of hanging indefinitely and respect web-specific configuration settings.
- Route configuration correctly from Python to the Dart geolocator calls and gate the position stream behind registered handlers to avoid leaks and spurious prompts.
- Normalize platform geolocation exceptions into user-friendly error messages surfaced to Python as RuntimeError.

Enhancements:
- Update the geolocator example app to wrap geolocation calls in error handling and surface issues through snackbars and logs.
- Introduce sensible default web cache and timeout behavior for single-shot geolocation requests and document these behaviors and macOS troubleshooting steps.
- Guard desktop settings-opening calls on web by returning a boolean result instead of doing nothing.

Build:
- Bump the flet Dart package version to 0.85.1 and add coordinated changelog entries for the core project and Dart package.

Documentation:
- Document web geolocation cache-vs-fresh behavior and configuration, and add macOS troubleshooting guidance for POSITION_UNAVAILABLE failures.

author: shosho-chang
body:
Closes #511.

## Summary

Ships ADR-024 Slice 3 — the deterministic Promotion Preflight that takes a normalized `ReadingSource` (#509) and returns a frozen `PreflightReport` value-object describing language, evidence-track status, approximate size, structural risks, and a recommended next action. Pure-deterministic, no LLM, no KB write, no UI, no vault mutation. EPUB / markdown inspectors read variant bytes via an injected `blob_loader: Callable[[str], bytes]` — production callers and tests provide their own loader.

## What changed

**Add:**

- `shared/schemas/preflight_report.py` — Pydantic schema. Closed-set Literal enums (`PreflightAction` 5 values, `PreflightReason` 11 values incl. `inspector_error`, `PreflightRiskCode`, `PreflightRiskSeverity`). `extra="forbid"` + `frozen=True` on every model. Two hard invariants via `model_validator(mode="after")`: (1) `recommended_action == "proceed_full_promotion"` requires `has_evidence_track == True`; (2) `error is not None` requires `recommended_action == "defer"`.
- `shared/promotion_preflight.py` — `PromotionPreflight` service. `__init__(blob_loader, registry=None)`; `run(reading_source) -> PreflightReport`. EPUB inspector via `xml.etree` + `zipfile` (no BeautifulSoup, no new deps); markdown inspector via local `_strict_extract_frontmatter` helper. Variant selection: `has_evidence_track=True` → `role="original"`, else `role="display"`; defensive `None` return with defer-path inspector_error report on invariant violation. Action policy implements Brief §4.2 mapping table top-down with first-match-wins. Narrow exception tuples in inspectors (`_LOADER_FAILURES`, `_EPUB_BODY_FAILURES`); programmer errors propagate.
- `tests/shared/test_promotion_preflight.py` — 19 named tests (22 collected with parametrize). Tests inject in-memory dict-backed `blob_loader` callables; ebook tests build hermetic EPUB blobs via `make_epub_blob(EPUBSpec(...))`.

## V2 corrections applied (Brief §0)

- **Correction 1**: `partial_promotion_only` is intentionally absent from `PreflightAction`. T15 reflectively asserts `typing.get_args(PreflightAction)` does not contain it. `has_evidence_track=False` defaults to `defer` (long content) or `annotation_only_sync` (short / weak-structure); never auto-routes to `partial_promotion_only`.
- **Correction 2**: EPUB inspector receives bytes via injected `blob_loader`, never via `book_storage`. T14 subprocess gate asserts `shared.book_storage` is not in `sys.modules` after `import shared.promotion_preflight`. `ReadingSource.source_id` is never parsed — only `variant.path` is consumed (per #509 N3 contract). The `ReadingSourceRegistry` type-hint is imported under `TYPE_CHECKING` so the registry module (which itself imports `book_storage`) does not get pulled into the runtime import surface.

## Codex review (2026-05-09)

Verdict: **REWORK** (1 P0 + 5 P1 + 4 P2). All P0 + P1 findings addressed in fix-up commit `6cddf0a`.

| ID | Severity | Status |
|---|---|---|
| F1 — `error` field has no model_validator forcing `error is not None ⇒ defer` | P0 | **FIXED** in `6cddf0a` — second model_validator added; new test asserts ValidationError for error+non-defer combinations |
| F2 — Row 1 emits `frontmatter_minimal` reason for all inspector failures | P1 | **FIXED** in `6cddf0a` — added `inspector_error` to PreflightReason Literal; Row 1 dispatch uses it; T9 updated to assert reason; new reason-presence cross-check test |
| F3 — Row 4 OR vs AND | P1 | **NOT FIXED** — codex misread Brief §4.2 row 4 which explicitly uses OR (`weak_toc OR no_chapters_detected`); the implementation matches the spec |
| F4 — Variant selection raises ValueError on malformed RS | P1 | **FIXED** in `6cddf0a` — `_select_variant` returns `Optional[SourceVariant]`; `run()` catches `None` and emits defer-path inspector_error report with WARNING log; new regression test |
| F5 — Bare `except Exception` in inspectors | P1 | **FIXED** in `6cddf0a` — narrow tuples `_LOADER_FAILURES = (OSError, FileNotFoundError, KeyError, ValueError)` and `_EPUB_BODY_FAILURES = (BadZipFile, ParseError, KeyError, OSError, UnicodeDecodeError)`; programmer errors (TypeError, AttributeError, KeyboardInterrupt) propagate |
| F6 — Markdown frontmatter parser swallows YAMLError | P1 | **FIXED** in `6cddf0a` — local `_strict_extract_frontmatter` helper lets YAMLError propagate; malformed YAML now surfaces as inspector_error; new regression test |
| F7 — `weak_toc` severity inconsistency | P2 | **NOT FIXED** — the severity grading is intentional design (chapter_count==0 emits severity=medium; chapter_count<MIN emits severity=low). Captured as design clarification, not a bug |
| F8 — T11 LLM gate missing `google.genai`, `claude_code_sdk`, `pydantic_ai` | P2 | follow-up: prefix list can be widened in a future hardening pass |
| F9 — T12 misses bare `import agents` | P2 | follow-up: `m == "agents" or m.startswith("agents.")` extension |
| F10 — Missing edge-case parametrize (variant collision, row precedence, boundary values) | P2 | follow-up: precedence + boundary parametrize enrichment |

## Test plan

- [x] **T1** `test_preflight_high_quality_ebook` — has_evidence_track=True, 3 chapters, ~6k words → `proceed_full_promotion` + `reasons=["ok"]`.
- [x] **T2** `test_preflight_high_quality_inbox` — has_evidence_track=True, ~5k words, 3 sections → `proceed_full_promotion`.
- [x] **T3** `test_preflight_bilingual_only_inbox_defaults_to_defer` — bilingual-only inbox, ~5k words → `defer` + `missing_evidence_track` + `low_confidence_lang`; `primary_lang_confidence == "low"`.
- [x] **T4** `test_preflight_no_original_uploaded_defaults_to_defer` — ebook with no_original_uploaded, large body → `defer` + `missing_evidence_track`; lang confidence stays high.
- [x] **T5** `test_preflight_short_no_evidence_routes_to_annotation_only_sync` — inbox no-evidence, ~600 words → `annotation_only_sync` + `missing_evidence_track` + `very_short`.
- [x] **T6** `test_preflight_short_content_skips` — ~150 words → `skip` + `reasons=["very_short"]`.
- [x] **T7** `test_full_promotion_requires_evidence_track` — Pydantic `model_validator` rejects `recommended_action="proceed_full_promotion"` + `has_evidence_track=False`.
- [x] **T8** `test_preflight_lang_normalization_high_confidence` — parametrized over `en / en-US / zh-Hant / zh-CN` with `evidence_reason=None` → all `primary_lang_confidence="high"`.
- [x] **T9** `test_preflight_inspector_error_falls_back_to_defer` — `blob_loader` raises `OSError` → `defer` + populated `error` field + `reasons=["inspector_error"]` + WARNING logged.
- [x] **T10** `test_preflight_no_kb_write` — preflight against tmp_path vault produces zero filesystem mutation.
- [x] **T11** `test_preflight_no_llm_client_import` — subprocess import-gate confirms `anthropic` / `openai` / `google.generativeai` not in `sys.modules` after `import shared.promotion_preflight`.
- [x] **T12** `test_preflight_no_fastapi_or_thousand_sunny_imports` — subprocess import-gate confirms `fastapi` / `thousand_sunny` / `agents.*` not pulled in.
- [x] **T13** `test_no_enumeration_api_exposed` — reflective `dir(PromotionPreflight)` contains no `list_*` / `iter_*` / `enumerate_*` members (Brief §0 scope decision).
- [x] **T14** `test_preflight_no_book_storage_import` — subprocess import-gate confirms `shared.book_storage` not pulled in (Correction 2).
- [x] **T15** `test_preflight_no_partial_promotion_only_in_action_enum` — reflective `typing.get_args(PreflightAction)` excludes `"partial_promotion_only"` (Correction 1); confirms exact 5-value set.
- [x] **Codex F1** `test_preflight_report_error_implies_defer_invariant` — Pydantic `model_validator` rejects error+non-defer combinations (skip / annotation_only_sync / proceed_with_warnings).
- [x] **Codex F2** `test_preflight_reason_includes_inspector_error` — `PreflightReason` Literal contains `inspector_error`.
- [x] **Codex F4** `test_preflight_variant_selection_failure_routes_to_defer` — malformed `ReadingSource` (has_evidence_track=True without `ori

author: jpfulton-fultonengineeringservices
body:
## Summary

This is the **0.15.0 release PR** — what started as a single new endpoint grew into a broad hardening pass on the auto-budget startup probe, structured logging/observability improvements, and an ONNX model file cache. Ten release-candidate tags were cut before stabilisation.

---

## New Feature — `POST /v1/embeddings:both`

Produces dense **and** sparse embeddings for each input in a **single** ONNX `session.run()` per chunk. BGE-M3's transformer backbone runs exactly once; both output heads are derived from the same forward pass at near-zero marginal cost.

- **FP32 (`BAAI/bge-m3`):** model graph exposes `sentence_embedding` and `token_embeddings` as separate named outputs — one `session.run()` emits both.
- **FP16 / INT8 (`Xenova/bge-m3`):** single `last_hidden_state` output; server derives dense (CLS pooling) and sparse (SPLADE projection) from the same tensor.

Numerically equivalent to calling `/v1/embeddings` + `/v1/sparse-embeddings` sequentially, within FP rounding tolerance, but halves transformer compute for ingestion pipelines that need both representations. Path follows [AIP-136](https://google.aip.dev/136) custom-verb convention (`:`).

**New Rust surface:** `EmbedPool::both(texts)`, `Both` job variant, `embed_both` in `src/embedder.rs`, `DualRequest` / `DualResponse` / `DualEmbeddingData` types, `both_embeddings` Axum handler, route registered in `src/main.rs`, plus alias routes for percent-encoded path (`/v1/embeddings%3Aboth`).

---

## Auto-Budget Probe Hardening

The startup workspace probe accumulated a series of correctness bugs discovered across rc1–rc8 production deployments. All are now fixed:

| Fix | Root cause |
|-----|-----------|
| **Sequential worker spawning** | `/proc/self/statm` is process-wide; parallel ORT session init made each worker's `post_load_rss` include peers' in-flight allocations, inflating `per_worker_workspace` and breaking the OLS fit. Workers now load one at a time (leader first). |
| **Median aggregation** | `fetch_max` of per-worker RSS deltas amplified single-worker outliers from page-cache settling or arena jitter. Median is robust to one outlier. |
| **ECS Bottlerocket cgroup-v2 path-walk** | On Bottlerocket without `--cgroupns=private`, `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max` resolves to the host root (`"max"`). `detect_available_memory()` now reads `/proc/self/cgroup`, extracts the unified-hierarchy path, and walks ancestors until it finds a numeric limit. |
| **Absolute RSS guard** | Reads `current_rss` before each probe shape and skips the shape if `current_rss + 4 × chunk_cost > 87.5% × cgroup_limit`, preventing the ORT arena from accumulating past the container ceiling mid-sweep. |
| **Arena warm-up** | ORT lazily allocates ~1 GiB of arena bookkeeping on the first `session.run()` per session, adding a constant offset to all per-shape RSS deltas and burying the workspace signal. A `(1, 64)` warm-up call is discarded before measurements begin. |
| **`OwnedSemaphorePermit` for probe serialisation** | `tokio::spawn` returns synchronously. A permit bound to a local variable in the spawning function was dropped immediately (before the task started), leaving the semaphore un-drained. Changed to `Arc<Semaphore>::acquire_many_owned` so the permit moves into the closure and lives for the full probe. |
| **Restored 7-shape probe set** | The shape set was reduced to avoid OOM. With the three independent safety layers above (arena warm-up, conservative `fits()` gate, absolute RSS guard) the full 7-shape set is safe. The dynamic `(1, max_seq)` shape serves as the high-seq quadratic anchor. |
| **rc8: negative-`a` clamp** | Between seq=2048 and seq=4096, ORT switches from a fused attention kernel (no `[B,H,S,S]` matrix) to the standard path (~7.9 GB workspace jump). The two-coefficient quadratic `y = a·BS + b·B·S²` cannot describe this step function — OLS drives `a_raw` to ~-109 KB/token to fit the near-zero low-seq points alongside the ~7.9 GB high-seq point. Pre-rc8, `fit_cost_model` returned `None` on negative `a_raw`, fell back to conservative defaults that under-budgeted by 12×, and the bin-packer accepted oversize batches that ORT then OOM'd on. Fix: when `b_raw > 0` but `a_raw < 0`, clamp `a_raw` to 0; the `.clamp(4096, …)` floor raises it to 4 KiB/token. `chunk_cost(1, 8192) ≈ 8.8 GB` correctly exceeds the per-worker budget; bin-packer rejects oversize batches. |

### Probe Coefficient Cache

Fitted coefficients are written to `{cache_dir}/probe-coefficients.json`, fingerprinted by `version × model × max_seq × arch`. On warm starts the server reloads them in milliseconds, skipping the ~120 s probe sweep. Cache writes use atomic `write → rename` via a `.tmp` file.

### Lock-Free Cost Model Handoff (`arc-swap`)

The probe runs in a Tokio background task. Workers serve requests immediately on conservative defaults and pick up the fitted coefficients lock-free through `Arc<ArcSwap<CostModel>>` after the probe completes. No reader lock is held on the hot path.

---

## Structured Logging & Observability

| Addition | Detail |
|----------|--------|
| `BGE_M3_LOG_FORMAT` | `json` / `text` / `pretty` / auto (TTY-detect). JSON is the default in non-TTY environments; required for CloudWatch Logs Insights. |
| `BGE_M3_HEARTBEAT_SECS` | Periodic background log event (default 60 s) with `rss_mb`, `live_workers`, `loaded_workers`, `queue_depth`, `available_permits`, `probe_status`. Set `0` to disable. |
| Per-request `EmbedStats` | Each worker captures `tokenize_ms`, per-chunk `inference_ms`, `chunk_count`, `max_chunk_seq` and forwards them via the reply channel. Handler logs one structured INFO event per request with full timing breakdown. |
| TraceLayer tuning | `/health` and `/v1/models` demoted to DEBUG; embedding routes stay at INFO — suppresses load-balancer noise. |
| `probe_status` in `/health` | New field in the `tuning` object: `disabled`, `running`, `complete`, `failed`, or `cache_hit`. Exposed as `ProbeStatus` enum (`#[repr(u8)]`) in `src/state.rs`. |
| JSON current span | `tracing-subscriber` configured with `with_current_span(true)` for JSON output, correlating log events to active spans. |

---

## Additional Configuration — `BGE_M3_INTRA_THREADS`

Controls the number of intra-op threads per ORT session (i.e. per `session.run()` call). Default `1` keeps per-worker RSS predictable for the workspace probe. Raise to `floor(num_cpus / workers)` on under-utilised hosts to drive CPU from ~25% to ~100% under load. Re-run (or invalidate) the probe cache after changing.

---

## ONNX Model File Cache

Model ONNX files are cached to disk on first download. Subsequent runs reuse the cache, avoiding `hf-hub` fetches. `tempfile` crate added for atomic cache writes in tests.

---

## Documentation

- **`docs/startup-probe.md`** (new, comprehensive): theory primer for the workspace probe — transformer workspace decomposition, OLS conditioning at `MAX_SEQ_LENGTH=8192`, column normalisation, persistent cache, lock-free coefficient handoff, safety properties.
- **`docs/hf_tei_gaps.md`** (new): Hugging Face TEI capability gaps vs. this server.
- `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/health-state-machine.md`, `docs/request-flow.md`: updated to reflect probe background execution model, ArcSwap, and new endpoint.
- Removed stale decision docs: `docs/decisions/long-context-security.md`, `docs/decisions/pr9-review-findings.md`, `docs/decisions/pr9-re-review-findings.md`.

---

## Other Changes

- **Dockerfile**: `build.rs` added to the dependency-cache `COPY` layer (was missing, causing full rebuilds when `build.rs` changed).
- **Dependency bumps**: `rand` 0.9.2 → 0.9.4, `openssl` 0.10.75 → 0.10.79 (Dependabot).
- **New dependencies**: `arc-swap = "1"`, `tempfile = "3"` (dev).

author: chris-wolfgang
body:
## Summary
Four review findings flagged on the downstream template-sync PR
[Chris-Wolfgang/ETL-FixedWidth#88](https://github.com/Chris-Wolfgang/ETL-FixedWidth/pull/88), addressed at the canonical source so every Wolfgang.* repo benefits on its next sync.

1. **\`git ls-remote\` exit code check.** A network/auth failure produces empty stdout, which the script was treating as "branch missing" and routing into the bootstrap path. Now: check \`\$LASTEXITCODE\` immediately and abort, so a transient failure cannot accidentally clobber an existing \`gh-pages\` branch.
2. **Token no longer embedded in remote URL.** Replaced \`https://x-access-token:\${TOKEN}@github.com/...\` with a global \`http.extraheader\` carrying basic auth. The token is no longer visible via \`git remote -v\`, future error-log changes, or per-repo \`.git/config\`.
3. **\`Remove-Item -LiteralPath\`.** Both cleanup calls now pass \`-LiteralPath\` so a path with wildcard meta-characters cannot glob-expand.
4. **Scoped \`\$LASTEXITCODE\` restore.** Replaced unconditional \`\$global:LASTEXITCODE = 0\` after cleanup with capture-before / restore-after so cleanup noise still cannot fail the step, but a real deploy failure is preserved.

## Test plan
- [x] YAML syntactically validated locally
- [ ] PR CI green
- [ ] After merge, re-sync into [Chris-Wolfgang/ETL-FixedWidth#88](https://github.com/Chris-Wolfgang/ETL-FixedWidth/pull/88) (and pick up via the next template sweep for other repos)

author: emutis21
body:
## Who this is for

Anyone running several missions at the same time — a sales person researching three accounts in parallel, an operator drafting two emails while a long research task runs in another mission.

## The problem

Each mission has a model picker under the chat input — the little "Sonnet / Opus / Haiku" selector that controls which AI is doing the work.

Users want fast and cheap (Haiku) for short replies, and deeper but slower (Opus) for hard research. The picker LOOKED like it was per-mission, but it wasn't: switching it on one mission silently changed it on every other mission too.

Esteban Jaramillo flagged this in the beta-users WhatsApp group on Friday. Felipe confirmed it's a bug:

> "Es un bug. La manera en que debería funcionar es que cada vez que abras una misión, debajo de la barra de texto, puedes elegir el modelo."

## What's different now

The picker is honestly per-mission:

- Pick Opus on mission A → mission B is unaffected.
- Switch to Haiku on mission B → mission A still on Opus.
- Quit Houston and reopen → each mission remembers what you left it on.

If saving the choice ever fails (rare — would need disk to be unreachable), the user gets a visible toast instead of silent inconsistency, in line with the beta-stage error policy already documented in CLAUDE.md.

## Why it matters for the user

The picker is the only knob between "fast and cheap" and "deep but slow". Power users were either accidentally running their cheap work on Opus (burning tokens) or their hard work on Haiku (getting weaker answers) without realising. The bug had a direct cost-and-quality impact every time they switched contexts.

## How it was verified

- Repro confirmed on macOS desktop build: two missions side by side, model switched, restart, each mission held its choice.
- Engine unit test (`per_mission_model_isolation`) covers the isolation guarantee.
- App typecheck, locale validation (en/es/pt), and full engine test suite green.

author: n-ichimura
body:
## Summary

Phase 4a of [`docs/plans/annot-html-document.md`](https://github.com/ingcreators/annot/blob/main/docs/plans/annot-html-document.md). Adds the foundation for in-place document editing: contentEditable on heading + paragraph blocks, a per-block hover toolbar (delete / move up / move down), and snapshot-based undo / redo via a new `DocumentHistory` class. Bold / italic / underline shortcuts work for free via the browser's default contentEditable handling (Ctrl+B / Ctrl+I / Ctrl+U → execCommand).

**Phase 4b** (next PR) adds the slash menu, insert above / below in the block toolbar, contentEditable on the remaining text-bearing blocks (list items, callout / quote inner paragraphs, figcaption), and any further auto-commit polish.

## New surface

- `<annot-doc-shell editing>` — switches the shell into editing mode. Heading + paragraph blocks become contentEditable; every block gets a hover-shown `<annot-doc-block-toolbar>`.
- `shell.commit()` — folds in-progress DOM edits into the document model and pushes a history snapshot. Idempotent.
- `shell.undo()` / `shell.redo()` (+ `canUndo()` / `canRedo()`) — public methods for hosts; also wired internally to Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y while the shell has focus.
- `doc-changed` CustomEvent — dispatched on commit / block-action / undo / redo with `{ document, reason }`.
- New `<annot-doc-block-toolbar>` Lit element (light DOM, hybrid CSS) — delete, move up, move down with property-bound `canMoveUp` / `canMoveDown`.
- New `DocumentHistory` class (Tier A, pure-Node) — snapshot stack with 200-entry default limit + `replaceCurrent` for future coalesced typing.

## Implementation note — ContentEditable + Lit

Lit's template parts use comment-marker nodes inside elements to patch dynamic content. ContentEditable interactions (e.g. `innerHTML =` replacements, which `execCommand` triggers internally for some commands) can rip the markers out, leaving the next render to throw "ChildPart has no parentNode". The shell sidesteps this by rendering **empty** contentEditable elements in the Lit template and populating their bodies imperatively in `updated()`. Read-only mode keeps the existing `unsafeHTML(block.inlineHtml)` template path unchanged — Phase 3's tests remain green untouched.

## Tests (23 new, 60 total in the doc surface)

- `annot-doc-history.test.ts` (7) — pure-Node: stack semantics, undo / redo cursor walking, redo-tail truncation on push, identical-reference no-op push, configurable limit + head-trimming, `replaceCurrent`.
- `annot-doc-block-toolbar.test.ts` (3) — happy-dom: button rendering, action dispatch, disabled-state propagation.
- `annot-doc-shell.test.ts` (+13) — editing mode wraps blocks + sets contentEditable on heading / paragraph only; block-toolbar delete / move up / move down mutate the document + emit `doc-changed`; deleting the only block preserves a placeholder paragraph (article never empty); undo / redo via methods AND keyboard shortcuts; setting `document` externally resets the history; `commit()` folds DOM edits; debounced input commits to history after the configured idle window.

## Stories

- New `Editing mode` story on `<annot-doc-shell>`.
- 4 stories on `<annot-doc-block-toolbar>` (Default / First-block / Last-block / Singleton).

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm -r typecheck` — green across all 12 packages.
- [x] `pnpm test` — 1966 passing (1943 pre-existing + 23 new in this PR).
- [x] `pnpm --filter @ingcreators/annot-host-ui exec biome check src` — 0 findings.
- [x] `pnpm --filter @ingcreators/annot-host-ui build` — green (65 KB ESM).
- [x] `packages/web/src/storybook-coverage.test.ts` — passes (every LitElement still has a co-located `*.stories.ts`).

author: gmarisi
body:
### Motivation

- Provide a Python-first scaffold of the AQuA2 (Activity Quantification and Analysis) workflow so MATLAB batch settings and AQuA2-like pipelines can be ported incrementally.
- Offer a lightweight, dependency-minimal implementation of the core detection stages (preprocessing/dF, active voxel detection, spatiotemporal labeling, and feature extraction) to enable stepwise module parity with upstream MATLAB code.
- Include a simple desktop GUI and file/CSV loaders to make the port usable for interactive inspection and export of AQuA2-style outputs.

### Description

- Add project metadata and a console entry point via `pyproject.toml` and expose `aqua3.app:main` as the `aqua3` script.
- Implement a PySide6 GUI in `src/aqua3/app.py` with Data, Detection, and Export tabs and controls wired to a `ProjectState` and `AnalysisConfig` model.
- Add `AnalysisConfig` and `ProjectState` dataclasses in `src/aqua3/model.py` with AQuA2-compatible field names and backward-compatible aliases for common parameters.
- Implement batch-CSV parameter parsing (`src/aqua3/config.py`), TIFF stack I/O and exports (`src/aqua3/io.py`), and a modular AQuA2-inspired detection pipeline (`src/aqua3/pipeline.py`) that includes baseline estimation, dF computation, median filtering, noise estimation, active voxel detection, flood-fill event labeling, and per-event feature extraction.

### Testing

- Run `pytest -q` against the new unit tests in `tests/test_model.py`, which exercise `ProjectState` round-trip serialization, `AnalysisConfig` aliases, `coerce_parameter_value`, and `load_aqua2_batch_parameters` behavior, and all tests passed (4 passed).

- Models `FinancialEntry`/`BankAccount`/`ChartOfAccount` não existem (reais: `Titulo`/`TituloBaixa`/`ContaBancaria`)
- Services (`BaixaService`, `FluxoCaixaService`, etc) não existem
